title: The district-heating, electric-heating and idealised-heater controllers become explicit state machines (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (dual-circuit generators beside the boiler): DistrictHeatingController (generic_district_heating.py), ElectricHeatingController (generic_electric_heating.py) and IdealizedElectricHeaterController (idealized_electric_heater.py): space heating and hot water through the diverter valve's modes, the heating season, hysteresis. Follows the boiler pilot directly, since they share its dual-circuit pattern (dual_circuit_system.py).

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Staged plan: a later stage that enlarges a kept subject books nothing for the increment
description: Found while implementing renovisorissues #53 (hisim-is7w), 2026-09-26. StagedEvaluator._charged_subjects charges an enlarged subject its size increment ((new-old)/new), but _staged_inputs registers the earlier stage's purchase of the same subject as an ExistingAsset with replaced_by_asset_classes=[] (the subject is in the later stage's facts), so the later stage's own evaluation sees the subject as KEPT (installation_verdict), books no year-0 entries, and share x nothing = 0. Reproduced on the synthetic stages: PV 5 kWp bought in stage 1, 8 kWp in stage 2 (from_year 2): charged {'PV': 0.375} for stage 2, and the plan's timeline carries only the stage-1 INVESTMENT of 5000. A reader's quote for such a stage's measure (investment_overrides) is accepted by the staged command (the subject is charged) and then books nothing either. Decide: price the increment (evaluate the enlarged subject as a new purchase and keep the share), or refuse/declare it.
close_reason: fix/staged-instalments: a later stage that enlarges a kept subject buys the increment as its own purchase (subject#increment_stage<k>)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decision (cmf, 2026-09-28): price the increment. The later stage buys the increment as a new purchase (size difference at the database price for that size, escalated to its from_year; a reader's quote replaces it), with its own life and replacements; the earlier purchase keeps ageing.

title: Stop publishing hand-copied measure-option bounds that contradict the request schema
description: Source: PR #807 review follow-up (the fix agent's finding, 2026-09-24). ProbeSet.OPTION_BOUNDS is published as each measure option's minimum/maximum (capabilities.Aggregation._options) and is hand-copied from the house fields each option writes into; the request schema declares no bounds on options ($defs.measure.options is a free anyOf), so nothing can be derived. Three entries contradict the fields they copy: u_value_in_watt_per_m2_per_kelvin publishes minimum 0.1 where the target is exclusiveMinimum 0; number publishes (1, 2) where the target is the enum [1, 2]; installation_year borrows construction_year's range. Decide: an explicit option -> target-field map so option bounds are read from the target field's schema bounds (and enums as values[]), or bounds declared in measures.yaml by the contract owner (GitLab ask), or stop publishing option bounds.

title: Window opening is an option of the energy system and of a RenoVisor calculation request, not only a field inherited from the twin
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-18, on #1010 (the occupants open the windows only more than 0.01 K above the cooling set temperature).

Today: HiSim's building has the switch BuildingConfig.enable_opening_windows (building.py checks it before calling occupants_open_the_windows). The recorded energy-system files set it explicitly (true in almost all of the 34 files that name it, false in one). The RenoVisor translator does not set it at all: no field of the calculation request maps to it, so every RenoVisor calculation inherits the twin's value (true), and a user cannot say whether the occupants air the rooms in summer.

Wanted:
- HiSim: window opening is a documented option where a user states it, i.e. the energy-system file's building entry (and the describe/schema output), with its default stated once and its effect explained (the occupants open the windows when the room is more than 0.01 K above the cooling set temperature and the outside is cooler; this lowers cooling demand and summer overheating).
- RenoVisor: an optional field in the calculation-request contract (agreed with the frontend side on renovisorissues before it is used), mapped by the translator to enable_opening_windows, recorded in mapping_report.json; absent means today's behaviour. Update the capability probes and the translation map.

Done when a request can switch window opening off, the result changes accordingly (degree-hours above the cooling set temperature, cooling demand), and both the HiSim option and the request field are documented.

title: Build the PDF report once at the end instead of once per report section
description:
Source: the profile of hisim-gehf (PR #981, 2026-10-14). Every report section calls `ReportGenerator.close()`, which rebuilds the whole PDF (164 pages with all options): six builds of about 135 s each, about 14 of the all-options run's 15 minutes. title: Feed-in escalation counts from year 1, so the rate jumps at year 21
description: Source: #52 spec review, 2026-09-26. The feed-in rate is held nominal for its 20 guaranteed years, then should rise with escalation.feed_in; the engine applies (1 + feed_in)^(y - 1) counted from year 1, so at year 21 the rate jumps by 20 years of escalation at once when feed_in != 0. Count from the end of the guarantee (hisim/economics/calculators/energy.py ~317-324) and fix the spec's §6.1 sentence.
close_reason: Not a bug (owner decision 2026-10-14, PR #980 closed unmerged). The shared economics spec (renovisorissues specs/economics-hisim-spec.md §6.1, from #52) defines the feed-in rate after its 20 fixed years as the year-1 rate × (1 + feed_in)^(y − 1): once the guarantee ends the plant gets the rate that has moved since year 1 (e.g. a lower market value with a negative feed_in), so the step in year 21 is the model, not an error. feed_in is caller-stated, default 0, allowed > −1. The year-0 price shift of feed-in revenue stays as the spec says.

title: Measure the part-load open points against the 60 s reference: missed restarts, the heat pump's COP above 63 degC, cycling losses
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §10 (owner, 2026-10-09).

The part-load approach leaves three effects to be measured against the 60 s reference and remedied only if they matter: (1) heating restarts missed inside a coarse step (a controller off on T0 does not restart when draws cool the store during the step); (2) the heat pump's COP above about 63 degC evaluated at T-bar only (remedy: COP along the node's curve within the step); (3) cycling losses for fractions below 1 (EN 14825 Cd for heat pumps, part-load efficiency for boilers). Each remedy applies above the threshold only, so 60 s stays the reference.

title: Decide the LCOH denominator's source so levelized_cost_of_heat stops being null on RenoVisor documents
description:
Source: ~/shared_todos/todos.md H2 (frontend, engine v20260920-1)

Observed: plan.totals.levelized_cost_of_heat_in_euro_per_kwh is null in both stage slots of the staged economics document, on every RenoVisor calculation.

Root cause: LCOH = NPV annuity / annual_heat_demand_in_kwh (calculators/aggregation.py); a missing or zero denominator omits the KPI. The denominator reaches the engine only through the declared EconomicContext (bridge _merge_context, non-negative scalars) - the simulation extract never sets it. The RenoVisor translator builds the EconomicContext BEFORE the simulation runs (run.py attaches it beside the parameters), so it cannot know the heat demand, and it states none. The engine then omits the KPI rather than dividing by an invented figure - correct per cost-spec, but the frontend wants the number.

The simulation does produce a candidate: the Building component's "Theoretical heating demand" KPI (kWh, from the TheoreticalThermalBuildingDemand channel, building.py get_kpi_entries).

Decision needed (owner):
1. Semantics: is the LCOH denominator the building-side theoretical (useful) heat demand or the generator-side delivered heat? cost-spec says "annual useful heat demand".
2. Placement: engine-side extract (bridge reads the Building KPI, declared context still overrides) benefits every run and keeps the seam promise; renovisor-side attach after the run would be two-phase and stale for re-pricing.

Done when: the denominator's source is decided, implemented, and a staged run on the mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both stage slots (or the decision is "stay null" and the frontend is told so).
close_reason: Decided with Noah 2026-09-23: the LCOH divides by the useful heat the simulation measured (Building TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand + SimpleDHWStorage ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW), extracted engine-side into economic_inputs.json and annualized with simulated_period_fraction; a declared EconomicContext.annual_heat_demand_in_kwh still wins. The mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both evaluations.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Answered the frontend's duplicate report renovisorissues #33 (2026-09-23): fixed on feat/lcoh-denominator, live once the next image after that PR ships.

title: Staged: a stage that replaces an earlier stage's purchase writes it off as new (age at plan year 0, not at its own from_year)
description:
Source: hisim-dutz/hisim-nl6j work (worktree agent-y0, feat/year-zero), 2026-09-26.

Each stage k is evaluated over the whole horizon from plan year 0, and what it charges is shifted by
from_year_k. When stage k replaces an asset an earlier stage j bought (installation_year
plan_year_zero + from_year_j, origin STAGE), resolve_replaced_asset measures the replaced asset's
age at plan year 0: max(0, year0 - (year0 + from_year_j)) = 0. The replacement actually happens at
plan year from_year_k, when the asset is from_year_k - from_year_j years old. So the sunk cost
(written-off book value, decision-neutral, reported) is the full like-for-like price, and the
anyway-cost test sees the whole service life remaining, so no anyway credit is due even when the
earlier purchase is near the end of its life. Before the year-0 anchor the same case measured
year0 - (weather_year + from_year_j), right only by accident.

The first-replacement schedule of such an asset is now unfloored (ExistingAsset.age_for_replacement),
this path was left floored on purpose. Fix idea: resolve the replaced asset's age at the charging
stage's own from_year (year0 + from_year_k) for a STAGE asset, and pin it with a hand-computed test.
close_reason: a later stage's replacement of an earlier stage's purchase writes it off at its real age (ExistingAsset.stated_age_in_years, fix/year-zero-review)

title: Survey HiSim's hot-water components for the LCOH's useful-heat table
description:
Follow-up of PR #812 (hisim-4p86, the LCOH denominator is the useful heat the run measured).

`adapter.UsefulHeatSources` lists two sources of useful heat: the Building's
TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand (rooms) and SimpleDHWStorage's ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW (hot water).
A run with a Building and no listed hot-water source divides the system cost per unit of heat by the
rooms' heat alone; the bridge logs a warning and the plausibility panel carries a WARN row
(`useful_heat_without_hot_water`) saying so.

Survey HiSim's components that deliver domestic hot water without a SimpleDHWStorage — combi boilers,
electric (instantaneous or stored) water heaters, heat-pump DHW paths, solar-thermal DHW, generic DHW
storages, the UTSP/LPG hot-water profiles — and for each name the output that states the heat drawn
(column, unit, sign convention). Then add the rows to `adapter.UsefulHeatSources` (kind HOT_WATER, sign
INTO_THE_HOUSE or LEAVING_THE_SOURCE), with the binding test in tests/test_economics_bridge.py.
Watch for double counting where a setup contains both a tank and a device that also states the drawn heat.

title: Price thermal storage with a fixed part and a scaling law, separately for buffer vessels and hot-water cylinders
description: Source: renovisorissues #48 investigation, owner decision 2026-09-26 (beads only for now). devices_IE.json prices THERMAL_ENERGY_STORAGE at 12/16/22 EUR per liter, strictly linear (no scaling exponent, no fixed installation cost; AI estimate); DE is 10/14/18. That fits a 150-300 l cylinder, not a 900-1,000 l buffer (market: roughly 0.5-2.9 kEUR installed for 1,000 l; a 1,000 l buffer sells for ~1.2 kEUR as a product). Replace with a fixed part plus a scaling exponent (the engine supports both, catalog_entries.py ~180-203), separate rows for buffer vessels and DHW cylinders (depends on their separate asset classes), from sourced IE/DE data.

title: The KPI 'Total electricity production' is 1000 times too small in electrolyzer_with_renewables (68.4 against 68,381 kWh delivered)
description:
Source: PR #1034 (CSV loader time column), found while measuring electrolyzer_with_renewables on 2026-10-16. In a one-week January run of electrolyzer_with_renewables at 900 s, the general KPI 'Total electricity production' reads 68.4 while the transformer reports 68,381 kWh delivered (after #1034's averaging: 180.5 vs 180,546 kWh): a factor of 1000, likely a W/kW or Wh/kWh mix-up in how that KPI sums the production outputs of this setup. The same factor appears before and after #1034, so it is older.

Fix: find where 'Total electricity production' is computed (hisim/postprocessing/kpi_computation/), check the unit of every production output it sums for this setup (transformer, CSV loader), and correct the conversion; check the other setups' production KPIs for the same mistake. Golden: the electrolyzer's goldens will move if the 60 s value is affected too (check).

Done when: the KPI equals the transformer's delivered energy in kWh for this setup, a test pins it, and any golden move is explained.
close_reason: electrolyzer-production-kpi-units: KpiPreparation.filter_results_according_to_postprocessing_flags summed every flagged column as W, but the transformer publishes its ELECTRICITY_PRODUCTION output in kW. Each flagged power column is now converted from its declared unit into W (W x1, kW x1000) and each stored-energy column into Wh (Wh x1, kWh x1000); any other unit is refused. Measured at 60 s: one week 180.5 -> 180,546.0 kWh, July week 168.6 -> 168,588.8 kWh, each equal to the transformer's 'Electrical energy delivered' (180,546.027 and 168,588.781 kWh); 'Grid injection of electricity' moves the same way (180.546 -> 180,546.027, 168.589 -> 168,588.781). Only the electrolyzer's three goldens move; no other golden setup flags a kW output. Pinned by tests/test_kpi_preparation.py::TestElectricityKpisReadTheDeclaredUnit.

title: The hplib heat pump's default minimum running and idle times of 3600 s each look far longer than a compressor's anti-short-cycle times
description:
MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig: cycling_mode True, minimum_running_time_in_seconds 3600, minimum_idle_time_in_seconds 3600. Owner, 2026-10-18: 'no real machine would shut down for an entire hour'. Typical anti-short-cycle times of heat-pump compressors are on the order of 10 to 20 minutes (to be sourced).

Options: (a) keep 3600 s and cite a source; (b) lower both to a sourced typical value, which moves every heat-pump golden at 60 s. Recommendation: (b), with a source per hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.11.

Related: hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.11 (every heat-pump default cites its source), hisim-component-physics-4g9.61 (RunTimeGuard helper).
notes: 2026-10-19, measured on midyear-pr3-lpg-utc (#1029): the 3600 s idle time makes the hot-water chain's tap heat depend on the step length. household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, 1 to 28 January: at 60 s the space-heating run ends at 19:00 on 13 January, the tank falls below 40 °C at 19:05 and the heat pump rests until 20:00, so the evening draws go unmet down to 27.5 °C; at 900 s the stop and the hot-water request fall into one step and the heat pump switches modes without stopping. Unmet hot water 3.63 kWh at 60 s against 1.04 kWh at 900 s, tap heat 235.23 against 237.82 kWh (1.1 %). tests/test_dhw_chain_time_resolution.py marks that comparison a strict xfail (KNOWN_DIVERGENCES); a shorter idle time may make it pass, and the entry then goes. 2026-10-19, midyear-pr6-solar-thermal-sun (#1032): with the collector on the weather's sun the same window gives unmet hot water 2.56 kWh at 60 s against 1.02 kWh at 900 s, tap heat 236.30 against 237.84 kWh (0.65 %), so the comparison passes and #1032 removes the xfail. The step-length dependence of the idle time remains.

title: SH buffer control oscillates and underheats at coarse timesteps once the storage conserves energy
description:
Found while implementing hisim-component-physics-4g9.16 (2026-09-27, worktree agent-stor, branch fix/storage-energy).

Once the water storages conserve energy (4g9.16, option B), the space-heating buffer shows the dynamics the old mass-mixing update damped away. The generator controllers (GenericBoilerController.modulate_power: full power 5 K below the set flow temperature, linear to minimum at the set temperature; the HPLib SH controller's on/off hysteresis) act on the buffer temperature only, with no feed-forward of the distribution system's draw, and the distribution system's request is one step old. With a small buffer (20 l/kW gas: 170 kg, M c = 0.2 kWh/K) the buffer swings:

- DE household_gas_building_sizer, full year: 900 s period-2 oscillation of +-2 K around the set flow temperature; 3600 s a period-3 limit cycle of 14..32 degC, and during DHW-priority hours the buffer empties to the indoor-air floor. Heat delivered to the building 12236 -> 12193 kWh (900 s), 12243 -> 10579 kWh (3600 s, -13.6 %); degree-hours more than 1 K below the heating set temperature 2.2 -> 96.7 (900 s), 3.2 -> 4681 (3600 s).
- RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib), 900 s: degree-hours 57 -> 291 (comfort rating 4 -> 2): during long DHW runs the buffer now drains to the indoor temperature at the real rate.

Options: feed-forward of the distribution system's request into the boiler modulation (P = request + M c (T_set - T0) / dt); a larger buffer or sizing rule; or sub-stepping. Owner decision needed; numbers and traces in the 4g9.16 report.
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-16 (Noah), from the review of #1006 (roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §12, S9 amended): stage D asserts the delivered space heat within 1 % of the 60 s run only at 900 s, for the gas, pellet, heat-pump and heat-pump + solar thermal twins. The gaps at 3600 s are recorded, not asserted, and tracked here with the comfort at coarse steps, since both are the same underheating: delivered heat against 60 s -1.01 % (gas), -0.24 % (pellets), -1.99 % (heat pump), -1.15 % (heat pump + solar thermal); degree-hours 192.8, 11.3, 109.3 and 93.7 (full year 2021, the stage-D top with pull requests 7 and 8).

title: Building takes the largest b_Transmission of an element's sub-elements, so walls to unheated spaces count as outside walls
description: information.py _element_u_value_and_adjustment_factor area-weights the TABULA sub-elements' U-values but takes max(b_Transmission_*) as the element's adjustment factor. 42 wall sub-elements of the generic rows (001-003) have 0<b<1 with area>0 (walls to unheated spaces); they are counted with b=1, overstating their heat loss. Fix: conductance = sum_i U_i*A_i*b_i per sub-element (or an area-weighted U*b), which changes Building results for those rows (goldens re-blessed with owner approval). title: The radiator circuit's pump stops outside the heating season by default; passive cooling through the radiators becomes a configuration switch
description:
Source: owner request 2026-10-20, after the July-week check of household_heatpump_building_sizer (60 s, 2021): "the radiator cooling should be a configurable switch. in most houses they turn off the circulation pumps in the summer."

Today: outside the heating season the heat distribution controller switches the radiator circuit to its cooling state (-1) whenever the building has a cooling demand, and the circulation pump keeps running its design flow (0.27 kg/s in this setup). The heat pump does not cool, so the buffer, at about 26-27 C, acts as a heat sink: the circuit takes up to 0.9 kW out of the room and puts it into the buffer (30 % of July's minutes, 14 kWh over the year). It is energy-balanced but not what a typical house does.

It also makes the room air alternate from one minute to the next: the circuit decides on the room's start-of-step air temperature (TemperatureIndoorAirAtStartOfStepInCelsius). A cooling step takes the air below the buffer's temperature, so the next step sees no cooling potential and delivers 0 W, which lets the air jump back up: e.g. 4 July 17:03-17:06, -824 W / 0 / -894 W / 0 with the room air at 26.67 / 27.54 / 26.71 / 27.51 C. The radiator also exchanges as much heat as its flow allows (outlet brought all the way to room temperature), with no limit from its size.

Do: a configuration switch on the heat distribution (or its controller) that says whether the circulation pump runs outside the heating season. Default off (the pump stops in summer, as in most houses); on keeps today's behaviour for systems that really cool through their emitters. When it is on, the circuit's cooling must not alternate from step to step (a dead band, or a decision on the step's own temperature).

Done when: with the default, no setup moves heat through its radiators outside the heating season, and the room air no longer alternates in July; with the switch on, the cooling is steady; the goldens are re-blessed once (the July-week and full-year pairs of setups with a radiator circuit behind a buffer move slightly).

title: The pellet and wood-chip boilers cycle about once a minute in space heating: their minimum run and idle times act on the controller's mode, not on the burner
description:
Source: the fix of hisim-component-physics-4g9.63 (PR #979, 2026-10-14). With the pump limit in place the on/off boilers (pellet, wood chips; the `on_off` controller) book the right heat, but the burner now fires and stops roughly every minute while the controller stays in its space-heating mode: `GenericBoilerController`'s minimum run and idle times act on the mode (space heating / hot water / off), not on the burner's firing. A real wood boiler runs for tens of minutes once lit and has a minimum burn time. Owner (Noah, 2026-10-14): P1.

Fix: the minimum run and idle times (or a burner-level minimum firing time) act on the burner's on/off state, so an on/off boiler modulates by cycling at a realistic rate; measure starts per day and the year's fuel before/after on the pellet and wood-chip twins; related to hisim-component-physics-4g9.17 (minimum runtime rounding at coarse steps) and hisim-component-physics-4g9.40 (device protection belongs in the device).

Done when: the pellet and wood-chip twins' burners start at a realistic rate (state the target per day), a test pins the minimum firing time, and the golden moves are explained.

A burner held lit sends its heat to the space-heating buffer. Year 2021 at 60 s: pellets 233 -> 10.1 starts/day (mean burn 1.4 -> 32 min), wood chips 232 -> 5.8 (1.4 -> 61 min); field target 500-3000 starts a year (17 monitored biomass boilers, Schmidl et al. 2016). Fuel pellets 16617 -> 16820 kWh, wood chips 16565 -> 17147 kWh; delivered heat unchanged; gas twin bit-identical (128 of 128 columns). Test: test_a_wood_burner_burns_its_minimum_firing_time_and_rests_its_minimum_pause.

What changed upstream that HiSim's frozen catalogue (`hisim/renovisor/request.py` CatalogueTable)
and the translator have to follow:

1. **`material` options carry no `values` any more.** The option is declared (`name`,
   `access_level`) and its values are generated from the `materials.yaml` rows whose `measures` key
   names the measure; the values are the rows' `asp_id`s. HiSim reads the material as an object
   (`asp_id` + properties) and checks only the conductivity, so validation is unaffected, but the
   frozen table's ENUM lists ("EPS", "XPS", "EPS Foam", ...) no longer mirror the file.
2. **Three measures gained a `material` option:** `cavity_wall_insulation`,
   `basement_internal_insulation`, `top_floor_ceiling_insulation`. These are exactly the three
   `FixedMaterials.BY_MEASURE` stands in for (`hisim/renovisor/constants.py`), so the fixed table
   and its `approximated` notes go: a request names the material like for every other layer. The
   table's two ids are stale anyway (`eps_beads_cavity` -> `eps_beads`,
   `stone_wool_flexible_insulation_blankets` -> `stone_wool`).
3. **`change_room_temperature.new_room_temperature` is now `new_room_temperature_in_celsius`**
   (the unit-suffix fix of C1 item 4). Touches `apply.py`, the capability range table in
   `capabilities.py`, the frozen table, tests and the translation map.
4. **`openapi.yaml` was split:** `HomeInventoryInput` moved to a new `homeinventory.yaml`, referenced
   relatively. The vendored `openapi.yaml` is non-authoritative; decide whether to vendor both files
   side by side (they are meant to ship together) or drop the non-authoritative copy.
5. **The `building_components` vocabulary is gone from `materials.yaml`.** HiSim's `placement`
   values (`external_wall_external`, `basement_ceiling`, ...) were that vocabulary; they keep working
   as HiSim's own names (economics `EnvelopeAssets.BY_PLACEMENT`, subsidy conditions), but no
   upstream list anchors them now. Say so where they are defined.

Also note: `calculation-request.md` §3 (table at lines 345-356, the material column) and §12
still describe the old option values and `measure_material_values`; that is the contract
owner's text, reported, not edited here.

openapi decision is taken), the frozen table equals it, `FixedMaterials` is gone, the option rename
is followed everywhere, capabilities and the translation map are regenerated, and
tests/renovisor pass.

title: Report an increasing/decreasing monotone declaration that is flat on every base, so a vacuous contract is visible
description:
Found in the review of PR #899 (2026-10-08).

Evidence: heating/gas_condensing_boiler's monotone entry `heating_threshold_in_celsius` -> `Total Gas consumption (energy)` of Boiler, direction increasing, is flat on the 1 January test day. Every heating limit of the range 10-22 °C lies above the day's mean outside temperature, so each base gives one value at all four sweep points (measured 128.8, 92.6 and 184.9 kWh from the bases s000, s001 and s002). hisim/energy_system/assemblies/testing/checks.py (`check_monotone`, `offending_pair`) accepts equal steps for increasing and decreasing, so the entry passes while checking nothing. D24 calls monotone "the cheap test that catches wrong-sign physics"; a sweep that never moves cannot catch it.

PR #899 added a moving sweep to the gas boiler (`power_in_watt` -> `Standby heat loss of Hot water storage` of Buffer: 0.2, 1.3, 2.0, 2.6 kWh), so that contract is no longer vacuous, but the harness still does not report a flat declaration. #900's four boilers (oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen) copy the same flat threshold entry.

To decide: fail or warn, and where the aggregation lives (each base's sweep is its own pytest test today, so "flat on every base" needs the results of all of one declaration's sweeps). A sweep flat on one base stays allowed, since a KPI may saturate there.

Done when: an increasing or decreasing declaration whose KPI is equal at every point on every base is reported with its assembly, parameter and KPI.

Source: renovisorissues #120, the github_runners agent's analysis of 2026-10-16.

The self-hosted runners lose a job offered while they switch from their busy poll to their idle one after a job ends; GitHub then cancels the job with "not acquired by Runner of type self-hosted even after multiple attempts" (31 jobs on 2026-10-15). This is actions/runner#4728; its fix, actions/runner PR #4729, has one approval and no release yet, and runner 2.338.0 still has the bug. .github/workflows/rerun-not-acquired.yml re-runs such jobs once their run finishes. The runners update themselves, so done when a runner release contains PR #4729, the runners run it, a few days of CI show no "not acquired" job, and the workflow file is deleted.

title: Boilers, the solar collector and devices without minimum run times get run-time and start estimates above 600 s, like the heat pump (hisim-ef6u part 1b)
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-19 on hisim-ef6u part 1 (the heat pump goes first).

Gaps found by the implementation agent: (1) gas, oil and hydrogen burners, the collector pump and a heat pump with cycling off have no minimum run/idle times, so the starts estimate dt / max(t_run_min/tau, t_idle_min/(1-tau)) divides by zero; the natural estimate there is one start per step in the cycling range (ratio below p_min); (2) the boiler and the collector publish no run time or starts today, so adding them adds KPIs (a bless); (3) the gas boiler's minimum times live in its controller (1800/1800 s), which the boiler cannot read without breaking the black-box rule: either the controller publishes them as a port or the boiler gets its own.

title: Give duplicated households distinct profiles in USE_LOCAL_LPG mode, where the guid reaches only the cache key
description:
Source: validation of the review of PR #880, 2026-10-08 (Claude session with Noah).

With `data_acquisition_mode: USE_LOCAL_LPG`, duplicated households in one UtspLpgConnector all get the same
profile. The connector gives each duplicate its own guid "to make sure that each lpg request delivers a
unique profile" (`vary_guids_for_lpg_utsp_requests_if_config_household_is_a_list_and_contains_duplicated_household_types`),
but only the UTSP path passes the guid on (`get_profiles_from_utsp(..., guid=...)`).
`get_profiles_from_local_lpg(lpg_households=...)` takes only the households, so locally the guid changes
the cache key and nothing else (hisim/components/loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py, around lines
720-770 and 1030-1060 on main as of 2026-10-08).

Consequence: a multi-apartment building of one household type gets N identical profiles, so the load
peaks of its apartments line up exactly. That overstates simultaneity and peak power compared with the
UTSP mode or real buildings. The existing scaling test (2 identical households = 2 x 1 household) relies
on this today.

To decide: how local pylpg varies a duplicate (a random seed derived from the guid, or the guid passed to
the calculation), and what the scaling test asserts afterwards (sums scale, profiles differ).

Done when: duplicates in USE_LOCAL_LPG mode get distinct, reproducible profiles; a test pins that two
duplicates differ and that a re-run with the same guids is identical.

title: The hplib heat pump runs its space heating without its minimum thermal power after the first hot-water step: hot_water() sets minimum_thermal_output_power to 0 and never restores it
description:
Source: found by the hydronics implementation agent on 2026-10-19 (while working on hisim-ef6u); confirmed on main: hisim/components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py, MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib.hot_water() sets self.minimum_thermal_output_power = 0.0 (a hot-water step modulates down to no minimal power); nothing sets it back to the configured minimum_thermal_output_power_in_watt (default 1800 W, read in __init__). Every later space-heating step calls hplib with minimal_thermal_power_in_watt=0, so from the first hot-water step of a run on, space heating also modulates below its minimum.

Fix: pass the hot-water minimum (0 W) only to the hot-water calls instead of overwriting the attribute (e.g. an argument of the hplib call), so space heating keeps the configured minimum. Measure before/after at 60 s (heat-pump twins with hot water): SH electricity, SPF, cycles/starts, run lengths.

Owner decision 2026-10-19: P1, its own PR after the mid-year chain (#1033/#1034), blessed in the same round as hisim-b5u7 (#1079). Moves the 60 s goldens of every heat-pump setup with hot-water preparation.
close_reason: Fixed on branch hplib-sh-minimum-power (PR #1087): every hplib request takes its minimal thermal power as an argument; hot water passes HOT_WATER_MINIMAL_THERMAL_POWER_IN_WATT (0 W), space heating and cooling the configured minimum_thermal_output_power_in_watt, so a hot-water step no longer leaves 0 W behind. Measured, full year 2021: the building-sizer heat-pump setups (household_heatpump_building_sizer at 60 s and 900 s, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer at 60 s) are bit-identical before/after, because their sized machines (~5 kW lowest hplib output) never go below 1800 W; no golden should move. The bug bites heat pumps below ~2.7 kW: a 60 m2 refurbished SFH (DE.N.SFH.05.Gen.ReEx.001.003, 2.2 kW machine) had 54 % of its 60 s space-heating steps below the minimum (lowest 1433 W), 0 % after; SH electricity 386.7 -> 389.1 kWh, SH SPF 4.433 -> 4.409, CounterOnOff 1000 -> 1015; at 900 s SH SPF 4.605 -> 4.591, full-load SH power below minimum 55 % -> 0 %.

title: Where a hot-water tank's and a buffer's standby losses go is configurable: outdoors (unheated cellar, today) or into the heated zone
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-19, on Q-F of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md: the original assumption was that tanks often stand in the cellar and their standby heat is indeed lost, but this should be configurable.

Today: SimpleHotWaterStorage and the DHW tank compute their standby loss against a fixed ambient temperature and the heat leaves the system.

Wanted: a configuration field naming where the tank stands (unheated space, today's default; or inside the heated zone). Inside the zone, the tank's ambient is the room temperature it reads as a published port and its standby loss becomes an internal heat gain of the building (ROOM_HEAT in the Sankey spec), so it lowers the heating demand in winter and adds to overheating in summer.

Done when: the field exists with today's behaviour as default (no result moves), a test shows a tank in the heated zone hands its standby loss to the building, and the Sankey draws it accordingly.

title: A modelling guide states how HiSim models physics: energy conservation at every port, sign conventions, the 60 s reference, failing versus clamping at limits, and sources for parameters
description: Complements system_docs/component_design_principles.md (who computes what) with how to model correctly. Points, each from the hydronics work: (1) sender and receiver book the same energy at a port (stage B, m*c*dT), and every component that moves energy closes its balance in a test (epic hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo); (2) sign conventions, which HiSim mixes today (e.g. TotalElectricityToOrFromGrid); (3) 60 s is the reference, every coarse-step model is measured against it with a documented tolerance (part-load spec); (4) when a component may clamp silently and when it must fail, generalising RenoVisor's 'fail loudly, except for what is written down'; (5) every default parameter cites its source (standard, datasheet, measurement). Do it after the principles review of the heat-pump and gas systems (~/hisim/principles-review/report.md), which may add points. title: Docstrings and comments in hisim/ stop citing specs, as coding_style.md §6 requires
description:
Source: system_docs/documentation_map.md (hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.6) and the review of #996, 2026-10-15.

coding_style.md §6 says a docstring never cites a spec or roadmap document ("see spec §8.4"); it states the rule itself. About 150 lines of Python under hisim/ still cite one (git grep -nE 'roadmap/[a-z_/-]+\.md|_spec\.md' -- 'hisim/*.py': energy_system 47, components 38, postprocessing 13, economics 11, renovisor 9, config 9), 36 of them roadmap/cost_spec.md; #996 only rewrote their paths when it moved the documents. The notes of the cost database JSON files (about 100) are data provenance, not docstrings, and stay. Done when each citation in a docstring or comment is replaced by the rule it stands for, or deleted where the code already says it; one pull request per package keeps the reviews small.

title: A guide states how a change that alters results is made, and which names are public interfaces
description: 'golden' appears 0 times in AGENTS.md. Rules to write: a change that alters results lists the KPI deltas in its PR description; golden references are blessed only through the CI workflow golden-update.yml, never locally; refactoring commits stay free of result changes; the tolerance policy is hisim-declarative-systems-b3b.6. Output names, KPI names, config field names and the energy-system YAML schema are contracts with RenoVisor, the webtool and the recorded twins: a rename needs a re-bless and a note to the RenoVisor side (renovisorissues). Open example: the KPI 'Unmet DHW heat demand' (rename plus re-bless, or a documented exception). Deliverable: a section in AGENTS.md or system_docs/results_and_interfaces.md. Proposal 3 of 6 from 2026-10-10.
close_reason: system_docs/results_and_interfaces.md states how a result-changing change is made (separate refactoring commits, KPI deltas, CI-only bless, tolerance policy) and which names are public interfaces and how one is renamed; linked from AGENTS.md. The 'Unmet DHW heat demand' example stays an open owner question (Q1 there).

title: Rename the KPI 'Unmet DHW heat demand' in one pull request with every reader, a re-bless and a heads-up
description:
Source: system_docs/results_and_interfaces.md, §4, the rule on KPI names (bead hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.3, its open example).

The KPI 'Unmet DHW heat demand' (hisim/components/simple_water_storage.py, introduced by hydronic stage C, #909) is in 26 golden files; hisim/renovisor/ does not read it. AGENTS.md has stated since #919 that a KPI name is a display label beside its mandatory unit field and is not renamed for the units rule. Options: (a) keep the name and confirm that exception as the rule for all KPI names; (b) rename it now and record the rename as results_and_interfaces.md §5 says (all readers, re-record twins, re-bless through golden-update.yml, heads-up on renovisorissues if the RenoVisor side reads it). The recommendation was (a), because the unit already sits in the KPI's unit field and a rename costs a re-bless of 26 goldens for a label.

Owner decision 2026-10-15: rename the KPI. It is not part of the guideline PRs. The rename is one pull request, as system_docs/results_and_interfaces.md §5 says: the KpiEntry name in hisim/components/simple_water_storage.py and every reader (tests, energy-system files, RenoVisor bindings if any), re-recorded twins, a re-bless of the goldens through golden-update.yml (the name is in 26 golden files), and a heads-up issue in renovisorissues (from:hisim, to: each package that reads it). The new name is chosen in that pull request.
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-16 (Noah): the exception of AGENTS.md for KPI names stays in force for every other KPI name, because renaming them breaks the goldens and the RenoVisor side, and AGENTS.md now uses "Grid injection of electricity" as its example. This rename is not covered by that rule; its pull request states its own reason for renaming "Unmet DHW heat demand".

title: Decide whether the parameter-source rule of the modelling guide applies to existing presets and constants
description:
Source: system_docs/modelling_guide.md, §5, which states the answer (bead hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.2).

The modelling guide (§5) requires every default parameter -- a preset value, a class constant with a physical or technical meaning, a hard-coded set point -- to cite its source (standard, datasheet, measurement, literature or a dated owner decision); SolarThermalSystemController.SWITCH_ON_TEMPERATURE_DIFFERENCE_IN_KELVIN is the example. Many existing presets and constants cite none. Options: (a) one bead per component family to add the sources; (b) a value gets its source only when it is next touched (the boy-scout rule, coding_style.md §2 rule 2). Recommendation: (b) plus (a) for the components RenoVisor runs (boilers, heat pump, district heating, solar thermal, building), whose defaults reach users' results.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-15: the source rule applies to all existing presets and constants now. modelling_guide.md §5 states it without an exemption; one bead per component family lists the unsourced presets, constants and config defaults: hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.11 (heat pumps), .12 (boilers and heat sources), .13 (district heating), .14 (electric heating), .15 (solar thermal), .16 (PV), .17 (battery), .18 (storages and the hydronics library), .19 (building), .20 (heat distribution, heating curve, night setback), .21 (air conditioners), .22 (cars and EV charging), .23 (energy management systems), .24 (hydrogen, fuel cells and CHP), .25 (weather, occupancy and data sources). The survey found none in the meters.

title: Decide whether 1 % is the default tolerance of a coarse-step model against the 60 s reference
description:
Source: system_docs/modelling_guide.md, §3, which states the answer (bead hisim-agent-rules-h2ib.2).

Every coarse-step model is measured against the 60 s run with a documented tolerance (modelling guide §3), but each spec sets its own: hydronic stage C's done-when is 1 % (hisim-hydronics-fxix.4), the dynamic distribution loop's criterion 1 % on delivered heat and the bill (hisim-hhj2), and tests/test_dhw_chain_time_resolution.py allows 1 % at 900 s and 1.5 % at 3600 s for the generators' hot-water heat. Options: (a) 1 % on annual energy figures by default, another value only when the spec documents and justifies it; (b) no default, every spec sets its own. Recommendation: (a), since every spec so far has chosen 1 % and a default saves the question for each new model.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-15: 1 % is the default tolerance of a coarse-step model (900 s, 3600 s) against the 60 s run unless a spec states and justifies another. Written into modelling_guide.md §3 and the testing guide.

title: The car charge controller becomes an explicit state machine (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (car charging): L1Controller (hisim/components/controller_l1_generic_ev_charge.py): at home or away, below or above the set point, charging from the station or from surplus, the 1.1 kW threshold.

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Assemblies: compose an energy system from tested, parameterised fragments with interfaces, named instances and tag-selector inputs (roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/assemblies_spec.md)
description: Owner discussion 2026-10-02: the energy-system format and the RenoVisor's switch-only rule do not scale to several PV arrays and batteries (renovisorissues #83, at least 4 arrays), seven DHW system types (#85) and the hydronic tanks. Design: ASSEMBLY files (components, internal wiring, parameters, interface of required / conditionally required / optional-with-fallback ports), imported once or as named instances, expanded in pre-processing; tag-selector inputs for dynamic components (meter, EMS); carrier providers as supply assemblies, a missing provider fails. First approach, to be refined; open decisions D1-D11 in the spec. PR #872 (one added slot) closed.

title: Pin a meter's carrier and fuel constants from its provider so a file with two energy_carrier providers can be sized
description:
Decided (owner, 2026-10-08, review of PR #899; spec §5.1, the §13.1 cut table and D30 amended): in v1 a meter's carrier, and a fuel meter's heating value and density, follow its class's law from the file's one `energy_carrier` provider, as in the twins, which write no line for it (D28). Pinning them from the provider, which the earlier §5.1 wording asked for, is cut from v1 and tracked here.

Evidence:
- hisim/components/gas_meter.py: `CARRIER_LAW = Size.ENERGY_CARRIER`, the law of `gas_loadtype` (around :68 and :84 on main as of 2026-10-08).
- hisim/components/fuel_meter.py: the same `CARRIER_LAW` on `fuel_loadtype` (around :59 and :74), plus the heating-value and density laws.
- The providers of the `energy_carrier` fact: `GenericBoiler` (generic_boiler.py, around :242 and :257) and `generic_district_heating` (`DistrictHeatingConfig.ENERGY_CARRIER`, around :135 and :148).
- hisim/config/engine.py (around :360): a scalar read binds by the bare-fact rule only when `len(candidates) == 1`, else `_unbindable_error`. So a second `energy_carrier` provider of ANY value is refused at sizing: a second burner of the same fuel, or a boiler beside a district heating connection.
- Step 3 already checks the fuel constants of a provider's consumers in the expansion (EF-7Z). Two burners with equal constants therefore pass that check and then fail at sizing (EF-4B).

Gate implication: the twins write no carrier line on the meter, so a carrier pinned from the provider and written as a config line differs from every twin. Pinning needs either an intended difference in the twin gates or an omit-when-equal rule (write the line only where the law would not give the same value, as D28's G9 does for parameters).

Due: before the first file with two `energy_carrier` providers: a gas boiler beside a gas cooker (step 6), a boiler beside district heating, or a hybrid.

title: Test the solar thermal assembly's collection when its composed file and gate arrive with hydronic stage C
description:
Evidence (owner review of PR #905, 2026-10-08): the test contract of energy_systems/assemblies/heating/solar_thermal.assembly.yaml cannot fail on the collector's physics. The isolation run is the fixed test day, 1 January in Aachen at 900 s; at most 53 W/m² reach the collector plane, the collector never gets 10 K above the cylinder, so the solar pump never starts. The contract's only monotone sweep is the investment cost over area_in_m2 (797 EUR per m², 1594 to 15940 EUR over 2 to 20 m²), and its expect entry is 0.0 kWh of heat delivered at the defaults. The bounds hold trivially for every output that only moves while the pump runs. What the contract tests is the assembly's build, its bounds and its pricing, not collection.

What an effective test needs: a run in which the pump starts, either an isolation day with sun (the harness has one fixed test day for every assembly, and the owner does not want the harness changed for this) or the full-year golden of the assembly's composed file, whose summer covers collection. Until then the collector's physics is covered by the goldens of the two solar twins (household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer).

Due: with hydronic stage C (hisim-hydronics-fxix.4), which brings the solar composed files and their gates (spec §13 step 5). Then add a monotone sweep or an expect entry on the heat the collector delivers, measured on a run with sun, and check that it can fail.

comments.text: Workable now (2026-10-13): hydronic stage C (hisim-hydronics-fxix.4), which this bead waited for, merged in #909 (b9a32aa1) and is closed, so the bead is no longer blocked. The solar composed files and their gates (spec §13 step 5) are not on the stack yet: review-guards has no household_*solar_thermal*.composed.energy_system.yaml. The effective collection test (a run with sun, a monotone sweep or expect entry on the collector's heat that can fail) is added with them.

title: The building's thermal mass carries its step-average temperature into the next step instead of its end temperature, so it keeps only half its net heat per step
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-19 (rated P0).

Location: hisim/components/building/building.py, Building.i_simulate after calc_crank_nicolson (ISO 13790 5R1C, annex C). The step computes the thermal mass's end-of-step temperature T_m,t (C.4, calc_next_thermal_mass_temperature_in_celsius) and the step average T_m = (T_m,t-1 + T_m,t)/2 (C.9) that the surface and air equations use, and then stored the AVERAGE as the next step's start: self.state.thermal_mass_temperature_in_celsius = thermal_mass_average_bulk_temperature_in_celsius.

Mechanism: the state moves only half the way C.4 says, so the mass keeps half the net heat that flows into it each step and the other half disappears from the model; the mass reacts as if about twice as heavy. Example (first 15-min step of the one-day snapshot, C_m = 20.0 MJ/K): the mass loses 3.71 MJ, C.4 gives 22.000 -> 21.815 degC, the average is 21.907 degC and the next step started from 21.907 degC, booking 1.85 MJ and dropping 1.85 MJ.

Measured (full year 2021 at 60 s, local LPG, twins household_heatpump / gas / heatpump_car _building_sizer; before = main f7366908): per-step residual C_m*dT_state - Q_net,mass 4,636 / 3,320 / 4,656 kWh/yr in absolute value (exactly half the heat through the mass), net +19.4 to +19.7 kWh/yr, up to 60 Wh in one minute; after the fix < 4e-9 kWh/yr. Daily thermal-mass swing +70 to +74 % (HP 1.23 -> 2.10 K), cool-down time constant of the house 45 -> 27 h. Degree-hours above 26 degC +43 to +46 % (HP 168 -> 241 K*h), max indoor 30.3 -> 31.4-31.7 degC, open-window hours +31 %, theoretical cooling demand +30 %; degree-hours more than 1 K below the set temperature +18 to +60 % (9-19 K*h). Space-heating heat delivered +1.0 / +1.5 / +1.3 %, gas +1.0 %, heat-pump electricity -0.3 / +0.6 %, grid import +1.1 / +0.6 %. Heat-pump compressor hours +0.7 / +0.3 %, starts -1.5 / -0.2 %, peak electrical power unchanged; peak 15-min heat to the building -0.5 / +4.7 / +6.7 %. Report: agent-tmp/thermal-mass-runs/report.md (2026-10-19).

Fix: carry T_m,t (next_thermal_mass_temperature_in_celsius) in the state; the average stays what the same step's surface and air equations use and what TemperatureMeanThermalMass publishes. tests/test_building_thermal_mass_energy_balance.py checks the per-step balance (fails on main in 96 of 96 steps). Golden references move for every setup with a building; the bless follows after the owner has seen the numbers.
close_reason: building-thermal-mass-end-state: the state carries the end-of-step temperature T_m,t; the per-step thermal-mass balance closes (residual 4,636 -> <1e-8 kWh/yr in the heat-pump twin), pinned by tests/test_building_thermal_mass_energy_balance.py

title: A stated heat-pump power or battery size that is not finite or not above 0 builds and runs: the components refuse it when they are built
description:
Source: review of PR #978 (explicit sizes), findings R1/R5 (review-evals/review978_evaluation.md); owner decision of 2026-10-15: guard in the components.

A number in a config: block switches a sizing law off, and nothing replaced the law's implicit domain. A heat-pump power (MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig.set_thermal_output_power_in_watt) of 0, -8000 or NaN configured, built and ran; hplib scaled its fit to it and the buffer beside the machine followed it (0 l, a negative volume). The bslib battery refused a negative capacity only through BslibChargingParameters; a capacity of 0 (ZeroDivisionError in bslib's first step) and any inverter power (0 W never charges, -5000 W charges 5000 W when offered 3000 W) were not refused.

Done when: the heat pump refuses a non-finite or non-positive set thermal power, and the battery a non-finite or non-positive capacity or inverter power, when they are built, with a ValueError naming the field, the unit and the value; tests fail without each guard; no shipped energy system changes. No upper bound unless a physical or datasheet bound can be named.
close_reason: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib.refuse_an_impossible_thermal_power and Battery.refuse_an_impossible_size refuse the values when the component is built; tests in test_more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py and test_advanced_battery_bslib.py fail without them; record_all_setups --check passes. No upper bound: hplib's database spans 2.4 to 69.9 kW but its generic fit scales linearly with the power, and bslib's generic systems scale linearly with both sizes, so no physical or datasheet bound applies.

title: The components' time_correction_factor is a reciprocal step length named a correction factor
description:
Found while removing the charts' time_correction_factor_in_hours (hisim-nyk7), 2026-10-18.

hisim/components/example_component.py sets self.time_correction_factor = 1 / seconds_per_timestep, and hisim/components/generic_heat_pump.py calls set_time_correction() (with a commented-out self.set_time_correction(self.time_correction_factor)). The value is the reciprocal of the step length in 1/s, but its name says neither that nor its unit; a reader has to look up what it corrects.

Done when: each use is renamed to what it is, with its unit in the name (for example timesteps_per_second), or removed where nothing reads it, and the docstrings say what the value is.

title: The boiler has no auxiliary electricity and no standby loss, so a stated label seasonal efficiency adds back only F(1) and HiSim burns 1 (gas) to 4 (oil) points too much fuel
description: Source: owner decision B of 2026-10-20 on hisim-component-physics-4g9.66. The label's eta_s is eta_son - F(1) - F(2) - F(3) - F(4) (Commission communication 2014/C 207/02 point 4.4; 2015/1189 Annex IV point 4). HiSim scales the curve to eta_son = eta_s + F(1) (3 %) because GenericBoiler draws no auxiliary electricity (burner fan, oil pump, controls: F(2)), has no standby heat loss (F(3); IWU 2002 eq. 2-2 gives q_B,70) and no ignition burner (F(4)). On real fiches F(2) + F(3) is 1.2 points (Hoval UltraGas 20), 3.2 (Buderus Logano plus GB125-22) and 4.2 (Hoval MultiJet 12), so a stated eta_s makes HiSim burn that much more fuel, and the house's electricity lacks the burner's auxiliary consumption. Options: model auxiliary electricity and standby loss in the boiler (an electricity input and a loss port), then add back F(2)-F(4); or add typical F(2)/F(3) per type from fiches. Done when the bias is gone or the owner keeps it.

title: D25 for chains without a buffer: the circuit flows when the room thermostat calls for heat and the generator books against that flow, so the gas boiler stops booking 10.6 % more space heat than the radiators deliver
description:
Source: the hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.12 investigation, 2026-10-20 (report /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/9uoo12/report.md); P1 by owner decision.

gas_boiler_household (energy_systems/, the only golden setup with a boiler and no buffer), full year 2021: the boiler books 12536.8 kWh of space heat at 900 s, the heat distribution system delivers 11204.9 kWh (+1331.9 kWh/yr, 10.6 % of the booked heat; +1325.7 at 60 s, +1364.1 at 3600 s). The boiler books m_b = P / (c * lift), about 0.29 kg/s while firing; the distribution system pumps its design flow, 0.27 kg/s, on the same circuit: two flows on one circuit, an implicit junction.

Scope (owner decision 2026-10-20, option b: D25 split out of hisim-pnw7 as this P1 bead): D25, who pumps follows from the circuit, reworded: the heat-distribution L1 controller decides whether the circuit flows, on the room thermostat (hisim-component-physics-4g9.37, which this depends on); the generator decides only how hot (the curve's supply set point) and books against the circuit's one flow; PositionHotWaterStorageInSystemSetup in the distribution system goes (the heat pump's and the storage's own enums are hisim-hydronics-fxix.15). The pipe-water node and the part-load mode above 600 s stay in hisim-pnw7 (P3). Caveat: the prototype closed the books only with node + D25 together (gas for space heating -4.4 % at 900 s); if D25 alone does not close them per step, the implementation measures that and, if needed, brings the pipe-water node for this chain along.

Done when: in gas_boiler_household the heat the boiler books equals the heat the distribution system delivers plus the pipe water's change of energy, per step, at 60 / 900 / 3600 s; goldens re-blessed.
notes:
2026-10-22, remeasured on main 9b092df16 (after #1093), report /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/4awa/report.md: the gap is now +3,700 kWh/yr (33.0 %) at 900 s (boiler 14,905 kWh against 11,205 delivered), about the same at 60 and 3600 s. Cause: the boiler's pump is sized for 5 K at maximal power and the controller's full-power band is the same 5 K, so a firing boiler always runs at its largest flow, P_max * eta_full / (c * 5 K) = 0.359 kg/s, whatever the load; the floor heating's design flow is load / (c * 7 K) = 0.27 kg/s. #1093 raised eta_full and so the gap. With radiators (15 K design lift) the same file overstates gas by +125 %. The circuit audit (/home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/circuits/report.md) found no other circuit with two pump owners in any recorded system.

Owner decisions 2026-10-22:
- a2 first, as its own PR under this bead: the distribution system keeps pumping its design flow and the boiler gets an optional flow input; wired to the distribution system's flow, it heats that flow (supply = return + P/(m c), throttled at its maximum supply temperature) and books m c dT with it. Scratch: gap 0.001 / 0.02 / 0.09 % at 60 / 900 / 3600 s, 0 forced steps, gas -25 %, building and comfort unchanged, every other system bit-identical. D25 is amended for boilers: a boiler without a buffer is a heater on the distribution system's flow, like a substation without a pump; and D1 gets the exception that a boiler on such a flow holds a power, not a lift.
- With zero flow the boiler does not fire (a flow switch).
- R2: receivers' flow inputs mandatory wherever their temperature input is (own bead and PR).
- R1: a build-time rule refusing a pumping circuit end whose flow nobody reads, on top of #1109: hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.20.
After a2 this bead keeps the per-step closure (one-step lag, |gap| 427 kWh/yr at 900 s), the thermostat-driven flow (hisim-component-physics-4g9.37) and the removal of the distribution system's position enum; re-rate it then.

title: Below about 8 kW the IWU 1990s gas condensing boiler's full-load efficiency lies below the 92/42/EEC floor by more than the 0.005 tolerance
description: Source: the implementation of hisim-component-physics-4g9.66 (2026-10-20). IWU 2002 Tab. 2 gives the 1990s gas condensing boiler 0.92 at 70 °C and 20 kW (NCV); eq. 2-1 moves it by 0.015 per decade of kW, the directive's floor (91 + log Pn) by 0.01, so the row meets the floor only from 79 kW and stays within the owner's tolerance of 0.005 (decision A) only from about 8 kW: at 4 kW it is 0.9095 against 0.9160. The floor test checks 10 kW and up. A boiler sized below 8 kW with a stated year in the 1990s gets this curve. Options: keep (IWU's row lumps low-temperature and condensing boilers at 70 °C, and 1990-1997 boilers predate the directive); floor the curve at the directive's value; or stop the size law below a minimum size. Recommendation: keep, stated in the spec.

title: Model solar priority in the controllers: the collector charges above the backup's target, optionally holding the backup back, instead of both stopping at 60 degC
description:
Source: owner discussion 2026-10-10 on the part-load prototype (PRs #915-#918, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md) and hydronic stage C (#909, roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5, §5.3, §5.5, D4).

## Problem

In the setups with a solar collector and a backup (household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, and RenoVisor requests with solar_thermal_system), the solar collector and the backup charge the same hot-water cylinder to the same temperature. Neither controller knows about the other:

- **Solar controller** (SolarThermalSystemController, hisim/components/solar_thermal_system.py):
  - the pump switches on when the collector is warmer than the cylinder by its switch-on lift. That is decided on the cylinder's step mean, an owner exception to D4 from stage C;
  - the pump stops when the cylinder was above its 60 °C aim at the start of the step (decided on T0). On the step mean that stop has no fixed point: 21507 forced steps a year at 60 s.
- **Backup controllers** charge to about 60 °C as well:
  - GenericBoilerController: warm-water aim 60 °C, hysteresis 10 K, supply capped at 70 °C;
  - MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW: t_max − 0.5 K, plus the energy manager's raise of up to +10 K on PV surplus;
  - ElectricHeatingController: aim 60 °C, hysteresis 15 K.

So at 60 s both run at the same time whenever both are on, until the cylinder reaches about 60 °C. The backup keeps the cylinder near 60 °C, and the collector often has nowhere to put its heat. Solar yield is therefore probably modelled too low even at 60 s. Real systems separate the two by control:

- **Different temperatures:** solar charges the cylinder up to its maximum (typically 80-90 °C, below a safety limit); the backup only tops up to a lower target (typically 55-60 °C), usually with its sensor in the upper part of the cylinder.
- **Solar priority:** the backup is held back while the collector delivers, or is expected to, with a minimum-temperature guard so the tap stays served.
- **Sensor heights:** they only matter once the cylinder is stratified (hisim-hydronics-fxix.1).

## Owner decision (2026-10-10)

Priority between solar and backup is a **control strategy** and belongs in the **controllers, not in the physics**.
- The part-load mechanism (hisim-naze and the part-load spec) does not encode any priority: generators on the same store whose controllers are on with the same target share one part-load fraction, iterated against the store's end temperature.
- The prototype's "solar first" rule (the backup counting the solar inflow as running anyway) is to be removed from the physics.
- Because the controllers behave the same at every step length, the 60 s run stays the reference that coarse runs reproduce, whatever strategy the controllers implement.
- Order: do this AFTER the part-load iteration lands, so its effect is measured against an unchanged mechanism.

## Options to evaluate (the owner wants a good solution, not a fixed one)

1. **Raise the solar stop above the backup target:**
   - a configurable solar maximum (e.g. 80-85 °C) in SolarThermalSystemControllerConfig, with presets;
   - the backup keeps 60 °C;
   - the cylinder's mixing valve at the tap (stage C, §4.3) already serves the tap from a hotter cylinder;
   - standby losses rise, which is realistic.

   Check: the cylinder assembly's contract bounds, the generators' maximum supply temperatures, and the energy manager's raise interplay.
2. **Backup inhibition while the solar pump runs**, with a minimum-temperature guard (e.g. do not let the cylinder fall below 45 °C). Watch for fixed points: decide on T0 or on values that do not move within the iteration (D4); a decision on the step mean that its own effect changes can cycle, as the solar stop did.
3. **Both (1) and (2).**
4. **Later, with a stratified cylinder (hisim-hydronics-fxix.1):** sensor heights for backup (top) and solar (bottom).

## Constraints and pitfalls from earlier work

- Controllers decide on the start-of-step temperature T0 (D4). The only exception is the solar pump's switch-on on the step mean. A stop or inhibition decided on the step mean can lose its fixed point.
- Stage C caps every backup's hot-water supply at its controller's set temperature and at its maximum supply temperature (§5); the cylinder conserves energy exactly per step.
- Since hisim-component-physics-4g9.23 the simulator warm-starts every step. The energy manager's knife edge (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28, hisim-component-physics-4g9.31) still causes forced steps in heat-pump houses.
- The units-in-names rule (AGENTS.md) applies to every new field and output.

## Effects to expect and handle

- The 60 s results of the two solar twins change: re-bless the goldens in CI with golden-update.yml.
- RenoVisor solar requests change: post a heads-up issue on renovisorissues before merge.
- Reference values from stage C, to compare against:
  - gas + solar twin, full year at 900 s: collector 389 kWh;
  - RenoVisor mockup with solar_thermal_system: reported solar heat 197 kWh.
- Re-record the twins if a controller config field is added, and check the solar assembly (heating/solar_thermal) parameters and bounds.

## Done when

- The chosen strategy is configurable through controller config fields with presets, named with units.
- Collector yield, backup fuel or electricity, and unmet hot water at 60 s are reported before and after, with a physical justification of the new defaults.
- The part-load runs at 900 s and 3600 s still agree with the new 60 s reference within 1 %.
- Goldens are blessed in CI and the heads-up is posted.

comments.author: noah

The solar controller's maximum storage temperature is a class constant, SolarThermalSystemController.MAXIMUM_STORAGE_TEMPERATURE_IN_CELSIUS = 80 °C, not a config field; the full-tank stop releases 3 K below it and the pump's part-load target is 80 °C. The backups keep 60 °C. The pump's part-load target of 80 °C and the solar assembly's target bound (40 to 80 °C) hold again: the collector's part load (#917, hisim-hydronics-fxix.11) was parked from 2026-10-12 and is back below #941 and #942 since 2026-10-14 (owner: "Bring back #917 first"); while it was parked neither existed, and a 20 m² collector at 3600 s ended a step above 90 °C.
