title: No path in a run depends on the current working directory: cache directories, weather, LoadProfileGenerator and input files are resolved once, at the start of a calculation, against a defined anchor, and logged
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-21, after the hisim-ksja PR (#1102), which refuses relative paths only where they come from outside (HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES, RenoVisor's --cache-dir) and left CacheLocations alone.

A relative cache path (cache_dir_path, HISIM_CACHE_DIR, the occupancy config's cache_dir_path) is resolved against whatever the current working directory is when a cache file is written: the repository root for the CLI, system_setups/ for a setup run from there, tests/ in CI, the container's working directory for RenoVisor. The same value then names different directories: silent cache misses, cache files in the repository or the CWD (which the write guard refuses, with an unobvious cause), and a write-guard registry (absolute, hisim/write_guard.py:194) that may disagree with where the writer writes if the CWD changes.

Do: CacheLocations resolves every relative entry to an absolute path once, when the calculation starts (os.path.abspath against the CWD at that moment), registers the absolute path with the write guard, and logs the absolute cache directories it will use. Relative paths keep working, deterministically. A test: a relative entry is resolved once and a later chdir does not move it.

Widened by the owner, 2026-10-21: not only the cache. Every path a run reads or writes (cache directories; weather files and their source_path; LoadProfileGenerator binaries, workspaces and predefined profiles; CSV loader files; energy-system and simulation-parameter files and the files they reference; result directories) is resolved to an absolute path once, at the start of the calculation (CalculationScope.open), against a defined anchor: the referencing file's directory for paths written in a file, the package (hisim/inputs) for shipped inputs, and the CWD at start only for paths given on the command line, never against the CWD later. HiSim has six code paths that open a calculation (hisim_main for setups and energy-system files, the energy-system executor, the RenoVisor run, the economics CLI, scripts/runner.py) plus direct calls from tests; all go through CalculationScope, which is the one place to do it. Consolidating the entry points themselves is hisim-declarative-systems-b3b.21 (and hisim-ylxf).

Do: inventory every path-valued config field and environment variable (grep for path, dir, file, directory in configs and os.environ reads), anchor each as above, and add a test that runs one twin day from two different CWDs (repository root and tests/) and gets identical results and the same cache files.

Done when: no run's behaviour depends on the CWD (the two-CWD test passes), every resolved path is logged at the start of the calculation, and the cache part above is done.

title: Caching correctness and the cache service
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md, roadmap/cache_service_spec.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8

Everything about how HiSim caches computed inputs: the six components that use
`hisim.utils.get_cache_file`, the producer-keyed cache service (phase 1 landed for weather, PV
series and building solar gains), the legacy caches that still key on configuration alone, the
non-bit-exact PV CSV round trip, the pylpg serialisation workaround, and the cache service's own
open questions.

title: Read the building-sizer cache directories from the environment instead of cluster paths
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 4

All `system_setups/household_*_building_sizer.py` hard-code FZJ cluster paths, still on main
(checked 2026-09-20):
`cache_dir_path_simuparams = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/hisim_inputs_cache/"` and
`cache_dir_path_utsp: Optional[str] = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/lpg-utsp-cache"`.

On any machine that is not the cluster these paths silently do not exist and caching is disabled
-- every run recomputes LPG profiles and weather inputs, which dominates runtime for short
simulations. The RenoVisor use case runs one simulation per request, so cold caches hurt every
single request.

Suggested fix: read the cache directories from environment variables (e.g.
`HISIM_UTSP_CACHE_DIR`, `HISIM_INPUTS_CACHE_DIR`) or from `SimulationParameters`, with the
cluster paths as documented defaults. One shared helper instead of a copy in each of the eleven
setups.

Related: `roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md` names the two
`/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/` existence probes as environment couplings a recording has to pin;
and the RenoVisor container needs a declared cache-directory list anyway.

Testing: a setup-level test that sets the env var to a temp dir and asserts the occupancy config
picks it up; run one of the fast marker tests twice and assert the second run hits the cache.

title: The LoadProfileGenerator runs once per household and year: the cache holds the year's minute profile, and every window and time resolution is cut and averaged from it on read
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-26 (Noah): P1, it wastes a lot of time.

Problem: the LoadProfileGenerator connector (hisim/components/loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py) caches the profile after it was put onto the run's clock (lpg_local_time), cut to the run's window and averaged to the run's step. So the key (utils.build_cache_key_string -> SimulationParameters.get_unique_key) names start, end, seconds_per_timestep, timesteps and a non-default part-load threshold, and every new window or resolution misses. A miss runs the LoadProfileGenerator for the whole calendar year again (lpg_request_days, owner decision 2026-10-19), although the minute profile it produces is the same: HiSim reads only the one-minute files (Results/SumProfiles.HH1.<load>.csv, the bodily-activity and flexibility jsons, the car series) and averages them itself. Measured on the CI runners at the first 900 s golden run (#1151): 280 to 520 s per household for each building-sizer setup, once per (window, resolution) pair; the 60 s week and the 60 s year each paid it too. The request also sets CalcSpec.ExternalTimeResolution to the run's step, so at 900 s the LPG writes SumProfiles_900s.* files nobody reads.

Done when: the LoadProfileGenerator runs at most once per household configuration and requested year (the effective configuration it was produced from, so Fault D of roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md stays closed). The cache holds that year's raw minute profile (all series the connector reads), keyed by the effective household configuration, the data-acquisition mode and the requested days, and by nothing of the run's window, step or part-load threshold. Putting it on the run's clock, cutting the window and averaging happen on every read, with the same arithmetic as today, so every result stays bit-identical: golden-check and golden-year pass without a re-bless, at 60 s and 900 s. ExternalTimeResolution is no longer the run's step (one minute, or left out if the LPG then writes no extra files). A test shows that a 60 s week, a 60 s year and a 900 s year of one household start the LoadProfileGenerator once (the executor mocked or counted), and that the profile served from the cache equals the one computed cold. Old entries simply miss once; the cache-entry metadata and its validation (pylpg_flakiness F5) cover the new entries. The UTSP path follows the same rule where it caches the same data.
close_reason: Done on branch lpg-year-cache. The occupancy's cache entry holds the LoadProfileGenerator's minute profile of one request (an LpgMinuteProfile per household: activity levels, the electricity, warm-water and device-heat sums per minute as the files state them, the start time, the flexibility and car files) as JSON, keyed by minute_profile_key_material: the effective household configuration's cache_key_view (acquisition mode included), ":lpg_minute_profiles" and the requested days, nothing of the run's window, timestep or part-load threshold; the .meta records the same material (F5). The clock, the window and the averaging run on every read (minute_values_of, series_of_the_run) with the arithmetic of before. ExternalTimeResolution is "0:01:00" for every run, the value a 60 s run always sent. Verified locally: the CHR01 local-LPG series of a 60 s week, a 900 s week, a July 60 s week, a 900 s year and a 60 s year are bit-identical to the base commit's (five base generator runs of 109 to 229 s against one branch run of 117 s, then 0.7 to 1.0 s per build); all_kpis.json of household_gas_building_sizer one_week_60s and one_week_900s and household_heatpump_car_building_sizer one_week_900s are byte-identical to the base commit's, and six golden pairs at 60 s and 900 s (week, July week, 900 s year) pass the CI tolerance, the second to sixth reading the cached year. tests/test_lpg_minute_profile_cache.py counts one generator run for a 60 s week, a 60 s year and a 900 s year. Follow-up: hisim-caching-hi1.11.

title: utils.get_cache_file and build_cache_key_string have no production caller left, and portalocker is no longer imported
description:
Source: hisim-caching-hi1.10 (the occupancy's minute-profile cache, 2026-10-26).

The LoadProfileGenerator connector was the last production caller of hisim.utils.get_cache_file (and through it build_cache_key_string): it now looks its entries up with utils.get_cache_entry and its own key material, which names no simulation parameters. Both functions are only called by tests now (tests/test_utils.py, test_caching_local.py, test_caching_client.py, renovisor/test_cache_directories.py, test_cache_key_portability.py), and the coding style keeps nothing in a shared module without a production caller. The connector was also the last module importing portalocker (its old cache writer held a lock around an atomic write); requirements.txt and the [mypy-portalocker.*] sections of mypy.ini and mypy_moderate.ini still name it.

Done when: get_cache_file and build_cache_key_string are deleted or have a production caller again, their tests are moved to get_cache_entry and ConfigBase.cache_key_view, and portalocker is dropped from the requirements and the mypy configurations (or a remaining user is named).

title: Run the cold-versus-cached protocol over all six caching components
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13 ("Every component that caches, not just this one")
and section 10 ("How to verify a fix")

The worst fault of the pylpg investigation (Fault D, section 6) is a caching pattern: a key taken
from what the caller asked for, contents produced by what the code actually did. Nothing about it
is specific to load profiles, so the verification protocol belongs to every cached component, and
each needs its own answer to one question -- can this cache ever be filled with something other
than what its key describes?

Six components use the shared helper `hisim.utils.get_cache_file`:
`loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py` (occupancy profiles; Faults A-D, the only one that
rewrites its own configuration), `generic_pv_system.py` (a year of AC power ratios; second
confirmed defect, see the CSV round-trip issue), `weather.py` (weather series; feeds nearly every
setup), `building/building.py` (building physics), `solar_thermal_system.py` (collector output)
and `generic_car.py` (car profiles; its data originates from the occupancy, so Fault D can reach
it second-hand).

What the sweep should produce, for each of the six in that order: run the protocol, and record
whether run 1 and run 2 agree bit for bit. Where they differ, establish which of the two is right
-- the cached or the computed value -- because that decides whether the fix is in the writer or
the reader. Then answer, per component, whether every input that changes the result is part of
the key. A cache whose key omits a relevant input is Fault D wearing a different hat.

PV is expected to fail today, which makes it the first thing to measure rather than a surprise to
discover.

title: Stop the PV cache round-tripping float64 through CSV text
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13, "The PV cache does not round-trip exactly"; with
the consequence recorded as roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-32

`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/pv_system.py` writes its cache with `database.to_csv(...)`
(:514) and reads it back with `pd.read_csv(...)` (:485) -- a text round trip of float64 data. So
a cached PV run and an uncached one are not the same run.

P3's parity work already ran into it: giving both sides of a comparison one cache directory let
the second run read the first run's PV output back out of the CSV, which both masked a real
configuration difference and invented a false one. That was worked around there by giving each
side its own empty cache; it is not fixed. F-32 generalises it: any A/B comparison of two HiSim
runs on one machine has this hazard.

Done when: the PV cache round-trips bit-exactly (parquet, npy, or a full-precision text format),
and the cold-versus-cached protocol passes for PV.

title: Key the solar thermal and car caches on their producer code, not configuration alone
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8 (fixed for three producers), closing paragraph;
roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 12 (the survey)

Phase 1 of the cache service landed three producers that key on their own code:
`hisim/components/weather/calculation.py` (`weather_series`),
`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/calculation.py` (`pv_series`) and
`hisim/components/building/solar_gains.py` (`building_solar_gains`). Each key is a fingerprint of
the producer module's source and of every `hisim` module in its transitive import closure, plus
the third-party versions in it and the calculation's DTO.

Two legacy caches still key on configuration and simulation parameters alone:
`solar_thermal_system.py` (pvlib solar positions, so a pvlib upgrade is what would be invisible)
and `generic_car.py` (an LPG export resampled by our own `resample_meters_driven`). Both are
future producers; the survey in section 12 of the cache spec lists them.

Why it matters, from F-8: before the producers, a physics change (the zenith clamp of #628, which
moves 33 KPIs on a cold cache) was invisible to the golden gate, because CI restores
`hisim/inputs/cache` from the previous run and the restore key hashes only the files that decide
where an entry is filed, not the ones that decide what is in it.

Done when: both caches are producer-keyed and an edit to either producer misses the cache.
close_reason: Branch producer-keys: the solar-thermal sun position (hisim/components/solar_thermal_sun_position.py) and the car's driving profile (hisim/components/generic_car_profile.py, with the LPG conversion moved to hisim/components/lpg_local_time.py) are producers keyed on their code; tests prove an edit to either producer, or to the conversion, misses a real cache directory. No golden moves (one week: 19 of 22 identical, the other 3 differ identically on the base branch; full year of the 4 collector and car pairs identical). The LoadProfileGenerator connector's cache still keys legacy-style on post-conversion profiles; PR3 (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.5) must make it follow the conversion.

title: Delete the whole-calculation pylpg lock once the cache service removes the need for it
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 9, F13 ("shipped in #611, and meant to be deleted")

Since F12 did not end the sqlite contention and the remaining shared route was never found, the
lock F10 introduced is held for the length of a calculation, so local LPG runs serialise. Of the
twenty-two system setups four run local profiles, so eighteen keep their parallelism and four
take turns -- and those four were contending with each other in any case.

The document is explicit: this is a workaround for a defect in a third-party binary, and it
should be deleted rather than maintained. The cache service (PR #584) removes the need to
generate the same profile repeatedly at all, which is the real answer; when it lands, the
serialisation goes with the need for it. The lock's docstring says so too, so whoever finds it
does not mistake it for design.

Done when: the cache service makes repeated generation unnecessary and the whole-calculation lock
is removed, keeping F10's install lock.

title: Find the shared path by which two pylpg calculations still reach one sqlite database
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 14, open question 4

With F12 in place each calculation runs its own executable beside its own `profilegenerator.db3`,
and one still died with `database is locked`. Some path -- an absolute location compiled in, a
temp directory, a user-profile location -- is shared and was not found. F13 serialises around it.

The document records it as "recorded rather than pursued": the question only matters if the
serialisation ever has to be lifted before the cache service makes it moot.

needs-triage: this is an investigation with no owner and a named reason not to do it. Close it
with the F13 lock removal if the cache service lands first.

title: Answer the four open questions of the cache service spec
description:
Source: roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 13, "Open questions"

1. Blob size cap and total quota -- needs measured sizes of the largest current `.cache` files
   (UTSP full-year minutely results are the likely maximum).
2. Does the internal endpoint require read auth? Recommendation: no -- friction for zero gain
   inside the institute network.
3. Which weather subset stays bundled in the repository for offline-after-install use?
4. Should the RenoVisor container prewarm at build time (bigger image, instant start) or at first
   start (small image, slow first request)? Recommendation: build time for weather datasets,
   first-start for opportunistic entries.

Related: the deferred cache writes of section 12 (PV non-predictive, building and solar thermal
fill their cache late) go with the producer migration.

title: Move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs so it stops masquerading as input data
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Separate tracked
reference data from generated cache"; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C26

`hisim/inputs/` holds about 319 MB of git-tracked reference data; on a working copy it reaches
1.7 GB because generated caches live in the same tree. Move the cache out of `hisim/inputs/`, and
consider distributing the reference data as a versioned package or download.

Payoff now: clone size, and -- the operational half -- cache from one branch stops masquerading
as input data in another, which is a known source of false "pre-existing" test failures.

C26 says the same from the container side: `hisim/inputs/cache/Building_<hash>.cache` is on disk
on main right now, and the cache's location must be an explicit declared directory, not the
working tree.

Done when: no generated cache lives under `hisim/inputs/`, and the default location is declared.

title: One shared producer-copy test helper instead of a ProducerCopy class in each of the five producer test files
description:
Source: review of #987 (review-evals/review987_evaluation.md, findings R7 and R8)

Each producer test file defines its own `ProducerCopy`: a copy of the real producer module in a package a test may edit, so the code fingerprint is measured on the real code. `tests/test_weather_producer.py`, `tests/test_building_solar_gains_producer.py` and `tests/test_pv_series_producer.py` had one before #987; #987 added `tests/test_car_profile_producer.py` (which also copies the LPG time conversion and rewrites the producer's import of it) and `tests/test_solar_thermal_sun_position_producer.py`, which #1032 deleted with the producer it tested. The `write`/`source`/`load`/`code_fingerprint` bodies are the same in the four left; `test_pv_series_producer.py` already has a form parameterized by root and module.

A change to how the probe evicts its modules from `sys.modules` or computes the closure root has to be repeated four times, and the copies already differ in detail.

Done when: one helper module under `tests/` provides the probe (one or several copied modules, with the import rewrite as an option), and the four files use it.

title: tests/ci_durations.json is refreshed from measured CI times: several groups take 2-3 times their weight and three units have none
description:
Source: found 2026-10-21 by the subagent of hisim-fjh6 (PR #1104, which added only the four stage-D groups), from the ci-durations-* artifacts of main runs 39444700707, 39448024896, 39459943731. Stale weights: the dhw-chain time-resolution groups took 154-228 s in CI against 81-154 s; tests/test_heat_pump_flow_booking.py 192 s against 65 s; the two test_p3_parity_participants_* modules about 304 s against 185-187 s; no weight at all for tests/test_space_heating_buffer_twins.py (129 s), tests/test_boiler_space_heating_balance.py and tests/test_multiple_pv_arrays.py. Stale weights unbalance the shards and lengthen the slowest one.

Do: refresh every entry from the artifacts of several recent main runs with `python tests/ci_split.py refresh` (it keeps the larger figure), and consider a periodic refresh (e.g. in the ci-usage workflow or a weekly job) so it does not go stale again.

Done when: every test unit has a measured weight within ~20 % of recent CI times.

title: CI takes 32 min per push on 20 shared GitHub slots while the institute's 20 self-hosted runners sit idle
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27 (ci-usage run 36305724420, tests run 36303671417, golden-check run 36303671424, golden-year run 36305904351), requested by Noah because CI keeps getting longer.

A push to a pull request takes 32 min until every check is green, and on a busy day considerably longer. Measured on the main push of 2026-09-27 07:37 UTC:

| workflow | wall | jobs | bound by |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| tests | 32.3 min | 9 | `pytest (base)`: 31.2 min, 7,277 tests in one process |
| golden-check | 11.2 min | 24 | 22 matrix jobs, 6 to 254 s of simulation each plus ~1 min fixed overhead, queued up to 5.7 min |
| golden-yaml-check | 10.8 min | 24 | the same 22 setups again as recorded twins |
| quality | 4.9 min | 6 | prospector 4.8 min |
| the rest | <= 3.1 min | 4 | |

Three structural facts under those numbers:

1. **Every push fires 67 jobs, and the organisation is on the GitHub Free plan: 20 concurrent jobs for the whole org.** Every job runs on GitHub-hosted 4-core runners (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, runner group "GitHub Actions") at ~25% CPU. The 20 self-hosted runners the institute operates are idle: no workflow names them. On 2026-09-11/12 (5,000 jobs a day) the median wait for a golden-check runner was 15 min, the 90th percentile 36 to 40 min.
2. **The base shard grew sixfold in three weeks**: 4.8 min (2026-09-05), 12 min (2026-09-20, staged economics), 22.8 min (2026-09-26, path verification), 31 min (2026-09-27). extendedbase went from 2.4 to 11 min on 2026-09-15 with two `test_p3_parity` EMS-sizer tests at 220 s each.
3. **Inside the 30-minute base shard** about 10 min are six rebuilds of the RenoVisor capability document (~100 s each in CI), about 10 min are the 36 `test_verify.py` tests at ~18 s each, and an estimated 7 min are the stray-file guard's two `git status --untracked-files=all` calls per test (14,500 per run). The tests themselves take about 3 min.

Order of payoff: the base-shard content (no infrastructure), then the golden matrices, then xdist inside the shards, then the self-hosted runners. Together the tests workflow drops from 32 to about 7 min (bounded by two single tests, see the child issue), the golden gates from 11 to 17 min down to about 4 min, and a push from 67 jobs to about 25, which is what stops the queueing on busy days.

The `ci-usage` job summary ("holding a runner without using it", "jobs that got slower") is the instrument to watch the effect on.

title: Build the RenoVisor capability document and translation map once per test session instead of six times
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417, `pytest (base)` slowest-durations block; parent epic.

The base shard rebuilds the RenoVisor capability document six times per run, about 100 s each in CI (446 probes through validate, apply and translate):

- `tests/renovisor/test_capabilities.py`: the module-scoped `document` fixture (103 s setup), and `TestTheDocument::test_two_builds_of_one_state_are_byte_identical` builds it again (99 s).
- `tests/renovisor/test_map.py`: the module-scoped `page` fixture renders the map, which builds the document (98 s setup); `test_rendering_twice_produces_the_same_page` and `test_writing_it_somewhere_else_leaves_the_committed_one_alone` render again (99 s each).
- `tests/renovisor/test_report.py`: `TestHiSimCommit::test_the_capability_document_stays_valid_without_a_commit` builds it once more (98 s).

To do: build the document and the rendered page once per session (a session-scoped fixture in `tests/renovisor/conftest.py`, or a process-level memo on `CapabilityDocument.build()` / `TranslationMap.render()` that the determinism tests reset explicitly). The three "two builds are identical" tests then compare the shared build with one deliberate second build, not one second build each. The report test that patches the commit lookup needs the build to happen under its patch, so that one keeps its own build or patches before the session fixture is first used.

Done when: the base shard's `--durations` block shows one ~100 s capability build, the byte-identity tests still compare two independent builds, and `tests/renovisor/test_map.py` still fails when the committed page is stale. Expected saving: about 8 min of the base shard.
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Shorten the four single tests that bound the tests workflow once the shards run in parallel (220 to 328 s each)
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417 (`--durations` blocks of the utsp, extendedbase2 and extendedbase shards); parent epic.

After the shards run in parallel, four single tests bound the tests workflow:

| test | shard | call time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `tests/test_lpg_connector_scaling_with_local_lpg.py::test_occupancy_scaling_with_local_lpg` | utsp | 328 s |
| `tests/test_hisim_main_python.py::test_initialize_from_python_with_module_config` | extendedbase2 | 297 s |
| `tests/test_p3_parity.py::test_the_table_still_spells_the_participant_targets_the_ems_sizers_actually_grow[household_electric_heating_building_sizer]` | extendedbase | 220 s |
| the same for `household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer` | extendedbase | 218 s |

The local-LPG test deliberately runs pylpg from cold to prove the local install delivers (roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md F1), so it cannot use the inputs cache; it could run a shorter simulated period or a smaller household set if the scaling assertion stays meaningful. The `test_hisim_main_python` test runs a full setup through `hisim_main`; check what it needs to prove and whether a week suffices (its sibling without optional arguments takes 144 s for the same reason). The two parity tests belong to the temporary P3 rig, which P6 deletes (hisim-declarative-systems-b3b.22); if that is soon, leave them.

Done when: no single test in the suite takes longer than 120 s, or each one above 120 s has a comment saying why the period cannot be shorter.

title: Memoise HiSimCommit._git and ProbeSet.build(): two git subprocesses per probe and a 2 s probe-set build per verify test
description:
Source: profile of `ProbeRunner.run()` on main (90640d87) on 2026-09-27; parent epic.

Two costs recur once per probe and once per verify test:

- `hisim/renovisor/report.py` `HiSimCommit._git` runs `git -C <root> rev-parse --short HEAD` as a subprocess, and `HiSimCommit.of()` is reached twice per probe through `MappingReport.to_json`. Over 40 probes: 18.6 s with the real git call, 14.7 s with it stubbed; on the older tree the two subprocesses were 12.3 of 26.9 s. The commit does not change during a process.
- `ProbeSet.build()` takes 2.3 s and is called by every `test_verify.py` test through the `_probes` helper (36 tests), and by every `CapabilityDocument.build()`.

To do: memoise both for the life of the process (`functools.cache` on `_git`, or a class-level slot keyed on `ROOT`; a cached, frozen probe tuple for `ProbeSet.build()`). `tests/renovisor/test_report.py` patches `subprocess.run` and the environment to exercise the three lookup routes, so the memo has to be resettable (`cache_clear()` in those tests, or a fixture that clears it).

Done when: one `git rev-parse` per process in a probe run and one probe-set build per process; `test_report.py`'s commit-lookup tests still pass by resetting the memo. Expected: about 20% off every probe run and about 80 s off the verify tests.
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Share one translation artefact cache across tests/renovisor/test_verify.py (36 tests at 18 s each)
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417 (`pytest (base)` slowest-durations block); parent epic.

`tests/renovisor/test_verify.py` has 36 tests at 18 to 47 s each in CI, about 10 min of the base shard. Each test builds its own `VerificationRunner`, whose `ArtefactCache` translates the anchor and the probe's request from cold, and most tests ask for the same handful of named probes (AZIMUTH, SCOP, THICKNESS, ...).

To do: share one `ArtefactCache` (or one runner) across the module through a module-scoped fixture, so the anchor and each named probe are translated once; tests that deliberately break a probe or patch the translator keep a fresh runner. Depends on the memoised `ProbeSet.build()` and `HiSimCommit._git` (sibling issue) for the rest of the per-test cost.

Done when: the verify tests together take under 2 min in CI and every test still exercises its own verdict (a shared cache must not let one test's refusal leak into another's).
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Replace the per-test git status stray-file guard (14,500 subprocesses per base run, unsafe under xdist)
description:
Source: `tests/conftest.py` `guard_against_stray_files` (autouse, function scope); CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; parent epic.

The stray-file guard runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` before and after every test: 14,500 subprocesses per base run. Measured locally (Windows, warm) at 410 ms per call, so 36 trivial tests take 31 s; in CI the "others" shard shows 131 sub-second tests taking 10 s, which puts the two calls at roughly 60 ms per test, about 7 min of the base shard. It is also the one thing that makes the suite unsafe under pytest-xdist: workers' status calls would see each other's files in flight.

To do: keep the guarantee (no test leaves a file git would track) at a cheaper granularity. Options, in order of preference:
1. module scope: one status before and after each module, the failure names the module (attribution to the test is then a local re-run of that module);
2. session scope with a per-worker snapshot, so xdist workers compare against their own start state;
3. keep function scope only for tests that declare they write outside `tmp_path` (a marker), the rest run under the module guard.
Whichever is chosen, the `_result_dir` exclusion and the diagnostics in `_stray_file_diagnostics` stay. The write guard from #837 (every file a run writes lands in its result directory or the cache) already covers what the runtime writes, so the per-test check is now guarding test code, not HiSim.

Done when: fewer than 1,000 git status calls in a base run, the guard still fails a test (or its module) that drops a file into the tree, and nothing in it depends on the worker being alone in the checkout. Blocks the xdist issue.
close_reason: stray-file guard at module scope: ~418 git status calls per base run instead of ~14,700 (ci/stray-guard-module)

title: Run every pytest shard with pytest-xdist on the runner's four cores, coverage through pytest-cov
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; resource-monitor lines of tests run 36303671417 (every shard 23 to 26% of 4 cores); parent epic.

Every pytest shard is one process on a 4-core runner. With the stray-file guard reworked (blocking issue), run each shard with `pytest-xdist`: `-n 4 --dist loadfile` (a module's tests stay on one worker, which keeps module fixtures and the LPG-profile cache behaviour as today). Expected from today's durations: base from ~6 min (after the content fixes) to 2 to 3 min; extendedbase from 11.5 to about 4 min (the two 220 s `test_p3_parity` tests then run side by side); system-setups from 5 to 2 min. The tests workflow is then bounded by two single tests at 5 to 6 min (see the sibling issue on those tests), about 7 min instead of 32.

Details to settle:
- coverage: `coverage run --parallel-mode -m pytest -n 4` does not follow xdist workers; switch to `pytest-cov` (`--cov=hisim --cov-report=` plus `COVERAGE_FILE`), which starts coverage in each worker and writes the parallel data files the `combine coverage` job already merges. Add `pytest-xdist` and `pytest-cov` to `requirements.txt` so the test image carries them (the image rebuilds on that file).
- the inputs cache `hisim/inputs/cache` is written atomically already (`scripts/record_all_setups.py` runs four children against it), so concurrent workers are safe there; the results directory is per test via `ResultPathProviderSingleton` and `tmp_path`, check the 15 test files that set the provider themselves.
- memory: the shards peak at 2 to 6 GiB per process (`pytest (extendedbase)` 6 GiB); 4 workers of extendedbase would exceed the 16 GiB runner, so give that shard `-n 2` or move the heavy tests apart. The resource monitor prints the peak per job.

Done when: every shard runs with more than one worker, `combine coverage` still produces the same report, and the workflow's wall time is under 10 min on a quiet runner.
close_reason: done by #850 (2ef5d6fb): shards run with pytest-xdist and pytest-cov

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Implemented on ci/xdist (uncommitted): workers per shard in the matrix: base 4, buildingtest 4, system-setups 4, extendedbase 2, others 2; extendedbase2, postprocessingoptions and utsp 0 (one module / one test each, so --dist loadfile cannot spread them; extendedbase2 and utsp also peak at 11.3/11.5 GB cgroup). Deviation from the Done-when: those three shards stay single-process. extendedbase stays bounded by test_p3_parity.py (~540 s in one module under loadfile); splitting its two 220 s parametrised cases into their own modules (or hisim-ci-speed-60sv.10) is what would let -n 2 overlap them. Local base run: 6:05 sequential -> 2:09 with -n 4; coverage same file set and statements, 82 more lines hit under xdist (cold per-process caches).

title: Collapse the 48 golden matrix jobs into a few multi-pair jobs that run four pairs at once and the YAML twin alongside
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, golden-check run 36303671424 and golden-yaml-check run 36303671382 (jobs API step timings); parent epic.

`golden-check` and `golden-yaml-check` are 22 matrix jobs each, one per week pair, plus discover and summary. Per job the simulation is 6 to 254 s (sum 1,895 s), while the fixed cost is about a minute: container init 20 to 27 s, checkout 5 to 30 s, package install, `hisim-cache` save 14 to 16 s. That is 44 runner-minutes of overhead per push, 36% of the two workflows' runner time, and the jobs wait up to 6 min for one of the 20 slots, which is what makes the workflows take 11 to 17 min for 4 min of work. Each job uses one of 4 cores.

To do:
1. `scripts/golden_check.py` already runs every pair when `--setup`/`--param` are absent; give it `--jobs N` like `record_all_setups.py` (subprocess per pair, results collected into the one `ComparisonReport`) so one job runs several pairs at once.
2. `scripts/golden_matrix.py`: emit shards instead of pairs (`--shards 4` balances the pairs by their last measured duration or by a weight in `golden_config.json`), each matrix cell a list of pairs.
3. Run the recorded YAML twin (`--mode yaml`) in the same job right after the Python setup: same container, same inputs cache, the two workflows become one with 4 to 5 jobs. Keep the workflow name `golden-check` or update `golden-year.yml`'s `workflow_run.workflows` list and `scripts/ci_prereqs_done.sh`, which name the prerequisites.
4. Memory sets the parallelism: week pairs peak at 1.2 GiB (four per runner), full-year pairs at 6 GiB (two per runner), so `golden-year` goes from 8 jobs to 4 with the same wall time, and `golden-update.yml` follows the same shape.
5. `hisim-cache` scope becomes the shard, so a pair that moves between shards recomputes its LPG profiles once; acceptable.

Done when: a push fires about 8 golden jobs instead of 48, the week tier finishes in under 5 min on a quiet runner, a diverging pair still fails the summary and still uploads its deviation report, and the golden-year gate still fires.
close_reason: done by #848 (70fa71c8): golden gates run their pairs in a few shards

title: Publish the labels, specs and Docker availability of the 20 self-hosted runners (needs org admin)
Run the tests shards, the golden matrices and the freshness gate on the self-hosted runners
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; Noah confirmed the institute's 20 self-hosted runners are idle; parent epic.

Once the runner labels and specs are known (blocking issue), point the heavy workflows at the fleet: the `tests` shards, the golden matrices and `energy-system-freshness`, leaving the small jobs (`quality`, `docs-build`, `worked-examples`, the golden-year gate) wherever they are cheapest. Self-hosted runners are not counted against the plan's 20 concurrent jobs, so this removes the queueing on busy days outright, and machines with more than 4 cores allow a higher xdist worker count.

Things to carry over:
- `container:` jobs need Docker on the runner; the `git config --global --add safe.directory` step stays.
- `actions/cache` works on self-hosted runners but stores in GitHub's cache (10 GB per repo); if the fleet shares a disk, the `hisim-cache` action could restore from it instead.
- `.github/actions/resource-monitor` reads cgroup v2 `memory.peak` and `cpu.stat`; check that it still reports on the fleet (the `note` line says when it could not), and `RegressionRules` in `scripts/ci_usage_report.py` assumes 16 GB for the "near the limit" flag, which must become per-runner.
- a self-hosted runner keeps state between jobs: results directories and the inputs cache under the workspace persist, so a job must not depend on a clean checkout beyond what `actions/checkout` guarantees (the freshness gate records into a throwaway directory already).
- `golden-year.yml`'s fork guard already keeps fork pull requests off the token-carrying job; a self-hosted runner must never run a fork's code, so the fleet's runner group should be restricted to non-fork events, or the heavy workflows keep the same guard.

Done when: the heavy jobs show the fleet's runner name in the jobs API, the queue time in the ci-usage report drops to seconds on a busy day, and the resource monitor still prints a peak-memory line for them.

title: Path filters so documentation-only pull requests skip the simulation gates
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; parent epic.

Every push runs the simulation gates even when it touches nothing they can see. Add `paths-ignore` to `tests.yml`, `golden-check.yml`, `golden-yaml-check.yml` and `energy-system-freshness.yml` for `docs/**`, `roadmap/**`, `**/*.md`, `.github/ci-monitoring.md` and the beads file, and `paths` to `docs-build.yml` so it runs on `docs/**`, `hisim/**` and `requirements.txt` (its header explains why a change under `hisim/` can break the build). Mind the branch protection: a required check that does not run because of a path filter blocks the merge, so either the required checks list changes with it or each filtered workflow keeps a trivial job that reports success (GitHub's documented pattern).

Done when: a documentation-only pull request fires under 10 jobs and can still be merged.

title: The solar thermal controller becomes an explicit state machine (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (solar thermal): SolarThermalSystemController (solar_thermal_system.py): the differential controller (on at +7 K, off at +3 K), the full-tank stop that restarts 3 K below the aim, the 80 C maximum, the speed-controlled pump's part load.

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Component physics defects and fidelity gaps
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md, roadmap/p3_random_findings.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md

Defects and fidelity gaps in the component models and the simulator core, collected while
building the RenoVisor translator (`roadmap/simulation_issues.md`, 2026-07-05) and while running the
declarative migration. Fidelity items are measurable: everything the translator cannot express
shows up as `ignored`/`approximated` in its mapping report.

title: Guard the window U-value division so a TABULA row with zero window area cannot crash
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 2 ("Same division pattern for windows -- latent crash"), with the
follow-up of item 1

The window U-value is the area-weighted average `(u1*a1 + u2*a2) / (a1 + a2)`. A TABULA row with
`A_Window_1 == A_Window_2 == 0` crashes identically to the door case of item 1.

State of the code (checked 2026-09-20): item 1 is fixed --
`hisim/components/building/information.py` gives the door element
`keep_u_value_when_reference_area_is_zero=True`, and the guard skips the division when the
reference area is zero while preserving the pinned `(u * area) / area` float round trip that
shifts the last mantissa bit for 164 TABULA codes. Item 3 is fixed too
(`_thermal_bridging_conductance_in_watt_per_kelvin` uses a local value instead of writing 0.1
back into the shared dataframe). The window element declares two area columns and no such guard,
so item 2 is the one still open.

Follow-up once fixed, from item 1: `hisim/renovisor/tabula.py::_is_usable` still requires
`door > 0 and window > 0`. The `door > 0` half is already unnecessary; the `window > 0` half
becomes unnecessary with this fix, at which point the band substitution and the expectations in
`tests/renovisor/` can go back to the exact bands.

Testing: cover via a synthetic `buildingdata_ref` row with both window areas zero, and assert a
normal German code's U-value is unchanged.
close_reason: done by #795 (c7b51bce): the window U-value survives zero window areas

title: Derive the country-specific ArcheTypeConfig defaults instead of inheriting German ones
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 14

`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/archetype_config.py` defaults to
`weather_try_region: int = 6`, Aachen coordinates, a German postal code and a DE building code.
Non-German archetypes inherit German defaults for every field the caller does not set, and
nothing warns about the mismatch (a TRY region has no meaning for Dublin). The RenoVisor
translator overrides what it can, but any new field added with a German default silently degrades
non-DE runs.

Suggested fix: make the country-specific fields `Optional[...] = None` and derive them from
`weather_location` / `building_code` when unset; log which defaults were applied.

Testing: construct an IE archetype without the optional fields and assert no German TRY region is
used downstream.

title: Stop the DHW storage temperature running away at 3600 s timesteps
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 15 -- observed crash, listed in the document's own priority 1

Running `household_gas_building_sizer.py` (via the RenoVisor translator, config
`IE.N.SFH.04.Gen.ReEx.001.001`, full year 2019) at `seconds_per_timestep=3600` aborts with
"The water temperature in the DHW water storage is with 98.32 degC way too high or too low."
The same configuration proceeds normally at the default 900 s. The DHW charging control overshoots
when one timestep spans a whole hour (a full hour of heating power is committed before the
controller sees the new temperature): the components are stable at 15 min but not at 1 h, and
nothing validates the timestep range a setup supports.

Why it matters: coarse resolutions are the natural lever for fast batch and screening runs
(RenoVisor previews, building-sizer iterations). Today they fail late -- after component setup
and possibly hours into a batch -- rather than being either supported or rejected upfront.

Suggested fix, either or both: (1) make the DHW storage / heat-source controller timestep-aware,
scaling the hysteresis band or limiting charging power so one timestep cannot overshoot the
target band (`P_max ~ storage_capacity * dT_band / dt`); (2) have setups declare a supported
timestep range and fail fast in `SimulationParameters` validation with a clear message instead of
mid-simulation.

Testing: regression test running the gas building-sizer setup for a winter week at 900 s, 1800 s
and 3600 s, asserting the DHW temperature stays within bounds; if option 2 is chosen, assert the
clear early error instead.
close_reason: The range check read an intermediate convergence iterate; moved to i_doublecheck (fix/dhw-runaway)

title: Make the EMS restore a copy of its state rather than a reference
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states" and "Independent repairs surfaced by the
analyses" (out of scope there, named as a prerequisite for checkpointing)

`hisim/components/controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:665`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restores the state."""
        self.state = self.previous_state

That assigns the reference, not a clone, so after the first restore `self.state` and
`self.previous_state` are the same object and every later `i_save_state` and `i_restore_state`
pair is a no-op on a shared object. Siblings that get it right use `self_copy()` (see
`heat_distribution_system.py:398`).

The epic records why it matters beyond correctness in the convergence loop: `i_save_state` is a
convergence scratchpad, not a checkpoint contract, and this is one of two live bugs proving it;
both have to be fixed on their own merits before checkpoint handover (the seeded-restart tier of
the mid-year oracle) is discussable.

Done when: the restore clones, and a test forces an extra convergence iteration and asserts the
outputs are identical (the epic's M6-shaped state-leak check).
close_reason: Obsolete since #921 (339ec168): EMSState is a frozen one-field dataclass (controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:89-102), and i_save_state / i_restore_state copy it with dataclasses.replace (:738-744), so state and previous_state are never one object and an alias cannot leak a mutation. The extra-pass check this bead's done-when asks for is TestSurplusHysteresis.test_the_band_keeps_the_decision_of_the_previous_step_not_of_the_previous_pass (tests/test_controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:1157). Found in the evaluation of the review of #921 (2026-10-13).

title: Make the heat-distribution controller restore its mode instead of self-assigning
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`hisim/components/heat_distribution_system.py:1180`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restore the previous state."""
        self.controller_heat_distribution_mode = self.controller_heat_distribution_mode

The self-assignment restores nothing: whatever the controller did during a rejected convergence
iteration is kept. There is no `previous_...` attribute saved in `i_save_state` to restore from,
so the fix is to save and restore one.

The second of the two live `i_save_state` defects the mid-year analyses surfaced; both are
prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

Done when: the mode is saved and restored, and a forced extra iteration leaves the outputs
identical.

title: Split the building's initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius from the comfort floor
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius` doubles as the permanent window-opening comfort floor
in the building's free-cooling rule -- a field named "initial" that is silently a model
parameter. The epic names it as the one blocker to untangle before any building-side seasonal
default: changing the initial temperature for a mid-year window would change the comfort rule for
the whole run.

Done when: the two meanings are separate fields, the free-cooling rule reads the comfort one, and
the goldens confirm no behaviour moved at the current values.

title: Calibrate the hplib heat pump to a stated standardized SCOP instead of the Generic fit
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21; numbers below from an EN 14825 bin-method check over the
hplib database on the same day (script not kept, method described here so it can be redone).

The RenoVisor twins heat with `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib`, whose COP is hplib's linear curve fit
`COP = p1*T_source + p2*T_flow + p3 + p4*T_ambient` evaluated every timestep, with `model="Generic"`
(hplib's regression over its whole air/water or brine/water group). There is no way to make the
machine match a stated seasonal COP. A user knows the manufacturer's standardized SCOP (EN 14825,
average climate, at W35 or W55), so the machine should be calibrated to that figure, and the house,
climate, flow temperature and controller then produce the realized seasonal performance factor as
they do today.

Findings behind the design (2026-09-21 check):
- hplib's database carries no SCOP column, only the fit coefficients and the reference point.
- Running the EN 14825 bin method (average climate hours per outdoor-temperature bin, part load
  linear from full at -10 C to zero at 16 C, flow temperature falling from 52 C at A-7 to 30 C at
  A12 for W55 and from 34 C to 24 C for W35, inverter modulation at constant COP down to hplib's
  25 % clamp, backup rod at COP 1 above capacity) over the fit gives Generic air/water SCOP 3.40 at
  W55 and 4.74 at W35; the 366 real air/water rows span 2.95..3.65 (W55, 5th..95th percentile),
  interquartile 3.22..3.42. The device spread is narrow; realized performance is dominated by
  flow temperature and climate, which HiSim already simulates.
- Matching to the nearest database device is rejected: many devices share one SCOP with different
  temperature slopes and some fits are extrapolation artefacts (one row computes 5.57 at W55 but
  3.73 at W35, physically impossible). Calibrate the Generic fit instead.

Design:
1. Component: two optional fields on `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig`, `standardized_scop:
   Optional[float]` and `scop_application: Optional[ScopApplication]` (Enum W35 | W55, class scope,
   no module constants). Both set or both None; one without the other is a configuration error.
2. Calibration factor k = standardized_scop / bin_scop(generic fit, application, group). COP is
   linear in its coefficients, so every COP the component takes from hplib is multiplied by k and
   the electrical power divided by k; thermal power is unchanged. hplib itself is not modified; the
   factor is applied in `get_cached_results_or_run_hplib_simulation` (or right after it) to COP and
   P_el, including the DHW branches, the heating-rod branch (cop <= 1) left as hplib returns it.
   The EER/cooling path is not scaled (out of scope, say so in the docstring).
3. The bin method lives in a small class in the component module or `hisim/components/` helper
   (e.g. `StandardisedSeasonalCop` with the bin table as a ClassVar tuple, the two flow-temperature
   lines and the sizing convention Pdesign = P_th_ref(A-7/W52) / 0.88 as named class constants with
   the source EN 14825 named in the docstring). It must be deterministic and cheap (26 bins, one
   hplib call each) and run once in `i_prepare_simulation`.
4. Ground source (group 2): same method with the brine source at 0 C in every bin and the same
   flow-temperature lines; the ambient term still uses the bin temperature.
5. Translator (`hisim/renovisor/translate.py`): when the generator is a heat pump and the request
   carries `scop` + `scop_application`, write both onto the hplib config (new `Targets` entries),
   mapping-report `used`; when only one of the two is present, refuse with a `heating.scop.*`
   problem code (fail hard, no guessing); `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` on a heat pump house
   stays listed as not applicable. The economics context (`hisim/renovisor/economics.py`) publishes
   the SCOP as the heat pump subject's technical attribute so subsidy conditions can read it
   (remove the "No SCOP" comment block there).
6. Capability document: field probes for the two new leaves.

Tests (targeted files only, never the full suite):
- bin_scop(Generic air/water, W55) is 3.40 +- 0.05 and W35 4.74 +- 0.05 (pins the method).
- After calibration to 3.0 at W55 the bin method over the calibrated component returns 3.0 +- 0.01.
- A one-day run with standardized_scop set has P_th identical to the uncalibrated run and P_el
  scaled by 1/k in every heating timestep.
- Translator: request with both fields -> config carries them, report `used`; request with one
  field -> exit 2 with the problem code; boiler house with the percent field unchanged.
- Economics: the heat pump subject's attributes carry the SCOP.

Depends on the spec update (the maintainer's bead) because the field names and the W35/W55 enum
must be final before the translator side is written; the component side (steps 1..4) can be built
first against the config alone if the agent wants to start early.
close_reason: Done: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig gains standardized_scop_en14825_w35/_w55; StandardizedSeasonalCop rates hplib's fit by EN 14825 (Generic air/water 3.40 at W55, 4.74 at W35); ScopCalibration solves one factor per stated rating so the calibrated fit rates exactly at them, interpolated in outlet temperature between the rating lines' heat-weighted mean outlets (28.9 / 40.7 C, decision 2026-09-23; real-data check is hisim-x2mu), applied to every heating call before caching (P_th unchanged, compressor electricity / k, rod untouched, cooling untouched). The translator writes a kept heat pump's pair onto hplib; a heating_system measure removes it with the old generator. Economics publishes nothing (physics only, renovisorissues !11), superseding design step 5's attribute.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Design update from contract PR #10 (2026-09-22): the inventory states the SCOP as a pair, heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 and heatpump_scop_en14825_w55, either may be null. Adapt design step 1: config fields standardized_scop_w35 / standardized_scop_w55 (Optional[float]) instead of standardized_scop + ScopApplication. Step 2: with both given, calibrate against both bin SCOPs (e.g. a factor per rating point, interpolated linearly in flow temperature between 35 and 55 C, held constant outside); with one given, a single factor as designed. Still blocked by hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.27 for the request-schema field names.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Tracked for the other agents on GitLab: https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/iek-3/groups/urbanmodels/renovisorissues/-/work_items/8 (the SCOP field this is blocked on)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23: the request fields are final (#8, renovisorissues !9): house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 / _w55, either may be absent; W55 <= W35 is guaranteed by the request checks; the pair places the unit at house.heating.flow_temperature_in_celsius. Only the existing pump carries them; a new pump from the heating_system measure keeps the generic fit. When this lands, remove the two not_implemented_yet entries hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.27 adds.

title: Make the water storages conserve the energy their heat generators book
description:
Found while root-causing hisim-component-physics-4g9.11 (2026-09-27).

`SimpleWaterStorage.calculate_mean_water_temperature_in_water_storage`
(hisim/components/simple_water_storage.py ~375) updates both storages (SimpleDHWStorage and
SimpleHotWaterStorage) as `T_new = (M*T0 + sum m_i*T_i)/(M + sum m_i)`, where `m_i = mdot_i * dt`. This
mixes temperatures by mass, but it does not conserve energy. The heat generator books
`m*c*(T_sup - T0)`: GenericBoiler thermal output, gas demand, and the storage's own
ThermalEnergyFromHeatGenerator output. The vessel, however, gains only `M*c*(T_new - T0) = M/(M+m)` of
that. The rest vanishes, and the vanished share grows with dt and with small lifts, because the boiler
sets `m = P/(c*dT)`.

Measured on the RenoVisor translation of an IE detached house built 1960 (TABULA
IE.N.SFH.04.Gen.ReEx.001.001, mockup-1 envelope, gas, no measures), full year 2019:

| dt | DHW boiler heat | vessel gain | lost | DHW drawn + standby | SH boiler heat | HDS draw |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 900 s | 7680 kWh | 3982 | 48 % | 2854 + 281 | 44778 | 39258 |
| 1800 s | 10015 | | | 2854 + 278 | 48988 | 39271 |
| 3600 s | 14120 | 3630 | 74 % | 2854 + 280 | 57500 | 39290 |

The gas bill therefore depends on the resolution: DHW gas 8.5 / 11.1 / 15.7 MWh and SH gas 61 / 66 / 75
MWh at 900 / 1800 / 3600 s. Even at 900 s the DHW gas is roughly 2.4 times the physical demand. The
median charging step at 3600 s has m/M = 2.9 (the tank volume passes through the boiler about three times
per step).

Every generator that feeds these storages shares this: GenericBoiler, MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib,
DistrictHeating, ElectricHeating and SolarThermalSystem.

The fix is the physically correct form of the bead's option (1). Make the update energy-conserving, with
`T_new = T0 + sum m_i*(T_i - T0)/M` (or the exact well-mixed solution `1 - exp(-m/M)`, with the generator
booking what the vessel actually took). Cap the per-step delivery so the vessel cannot pass the supply
temperature: `Q_max = M*c*(T_sup - T0)`, i.e. `P_max = M*c*dT/dt`. The generator must be told what was
accepted, or it must compute it itself.

This moves every golden and KPI that includes a SimpleWaterStorage, including at 900 s, so the owner has
to decide on it.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text:
Measured 2026-09-27 (origin/main faa88f3b, full years, per-step balance from hooks on the converged call; scripts and pickles in scratchpad egap/). Balance per storage: R = generator's own booked heat (GenericBoiler ThermalOutputEnergyDhw/Sh; HPLib ThermalEnergyDHW/SH) - booked draw (DHW: m_d*c*(T_warm-T_drain) = -ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW; SH: HeatDistribution ThermalPowerDelivered*dt) - standby (loss_W*dt) - M*c*(T_end-T0). Identity R = sum m_g*c*(T_new-T0) [R_gen] + secondary term [DHW m_d*c*(T_new-T_warm); SH m_h*c*(T_new-T_to_hds)] + booking-vs-flow (HDS inlet, HP c): holds to 1e-14 kWh per step in every run. Return temperature told to the generator = T0 exactly (heat exchanger present in all cases).

Residual R (R_gen) as % of booked heat:
| case | dt | DHW R kWh (%) | DHW R_gen (%) | SH R kWh (%) | SH R_gen (%) |
| RenoVisor mockup baseline (IE.N.SFH.05 gas) | 900 | 4747 (60) | 3566 (45) | 4459 (9.5) | 3612 (7.7) |
| RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib) | 900 | 5667 (66) | 5104 (59) | 5541 (17) | 5050 (15) |
| household_gas_building_sizer (DE) | 300 | 1565 (33) | 451 (9.6) | 361 (2.8) | 273 (2.1) |
| same | 900 | 2419 (44) | 1361 (25) | 855 (6.5) | 633 (4.8) |
| same | 3600 | 5537 (64) | 4545 (52) | 2572 (17) | 1771 (12) |
R_gen -> 0 roughly linearly in dt. The DHW secondary term (~1.0-1.2 MWh/yr, dt-independent) is a second defect: the draw takes m_d at tank temperature T_new but books it at 40 C (no mixing valve), so it survives dt -> 0.

KPI first order (residual / per-step efficiency or COP): gas baseline -8.7 MWh gas (R_gen only) to -11.4 MWh (full R) of 73.4 MWh = -11.8..-15.5 %; at 0.11 EUR/kWh -950..-1250 EUR/a; CO2 -1.7..-2.3 t of 15.5 t/a. HP package: -2.2..-2.5 MWh of 8.2 MWh HP electricity (-27..-30 %), upper bound -780..-870 EUR/a at 0.35, -0.62..-0.69 t CO2 of 2.41 (grid share <1 because of PV).

Side findings: the mockup baseline crashes at 1800 and 3600 s (DHW > 90 C raised on a non-converged iterate; hisim-component-physics-4g9.11) and cannot run at 300/600 s (weather array one/two short; new hisim-j2mh).

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decision (cmf, 2026-09-27): fix with option B (vessel updates on booked energy: T_new = T0 + (Q_gen - Q_draw - loss)/(M c), delivery capped at M c (T_supply - T0), accepted heat fed back to every generator) plus the DHW mixing valve (m_hot = m_d (T_warm - T_cold)/(T_tank - T_cold)). Option A evaluated separately. Announce on renovisorissues when the fix lands.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Reopened 2026-10-01: the fix on PR #864 (accepted-heat back-channel) is not merged (owner: no interim fix); solved again by epic hisim-hydronics-fxix (roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md).

close_reason: Done in hydronic stage D, branch stageD-5-buffer-node: the space-heating buffer is a start-of-step node (owner decision 2026-10-15), every circuit booked on its start temperature, the balance closed on every step; the hot-water tank conserves since stage C. Full year 2021, predefined occupancy, booked space heat stack top -> start-of-step buffer: gas twin 11267.3 -> 11164.2 kWh at 60 s, 11908.8 -> 11124.5 kWh at 900 s; pellets 11838.7 -> 11312.3 and 16353.4 -> 11367.6 kWh; heat pump 13091.8 -> 12461.5 and 15696.7 -> 12403.9 kWh; heat delivered to the building unchanged within 0.3 %. tests/test_space_heating_buffer_twins.py checks the closure and both circuits on every step.

title: Enforce the boiler controller's minimum runtime and resting time, and stop them rounding to zero at coarse timesteps
description:
Found while root-causing hisim-component-physics-4g9.11 (2026-09-27). hisim/components/generic_boiler.py:

1. `GenericBoilerControllerState.activate()` / `deactivate()` are never called, so `activation_time_step`
   and `deactivation_time_step` stay 0 forever. `enforce_minimum_run_and_idle_times` therefore never
   enforces a minimum runtime or resting time after the start of the simulation. The only effect is a
   start-up lockout: the controller is forced OFF for timesteps < minimum_resting_time_in_timesteps.
2. `minimum_*_in_timesteps = int(seconds / seconds_per_timestep)` rounds down. The default 1800 s
   becomes 2 steps at 900 s, 1 at 1800 s and 0 at 3600 s. The start-up lockout therefore vanishes at
   hourly resolution. This is exactly what let the controller act on the zero-initialised storage
   temperature at timestep 0 in hisim-component-physics-4g9.11 (the 3600 s crash; 900/1800 s were protected by the
   lockout). The same `seconds / dt` conversion exists in generic_chp/controller.py:346 and
   generic_heat_pump.py:455.
3. Related: in DHW or SH mode the boiler's supply temperature is `temperature_delta + T_in`, where
   `temperature_delta` is the controller's output from the previous iteration and `T_in` is the storage's
   current output. At timestep 0, `stsv` starts at zero, so the first iterate gets a 70 K lift on top of
   60 degC, i.e. a 130 degC supply. The loop corrects it; an output of target supply temperature instead
   of a delta would not have the mismatch.

Fixing (1) or rounding (2) up changes results at 900 s, so the owner has to decide on it.

title: Evaluate and test option A for the water storages: generator books against the end-of-step (implicit) return temperature
description: Owner (cmf, 2026-09-27): hisim-component-physics-4g9.16 is fixed with option B (the vessel updates on booked energy, delivery capped, accepted heat fed back). Option A must still be evaluated and tested properly, because the mixing in the storage tank is crucial for heat pumps in particular: the return temperature a heat pump sees sets its COP. Option A: the storage reports its end-of-step temperature as the return to the generator (and the supply to the heat distribution); the generator books m*c*dT from there; conserves energy at convergence. Evaluate against B on the RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib) and a plain HP setup at 300/900/3600 s: COP, electricity, iteration counts, oscillation at coarse dt, stratification (the mixing-factor path of a storage without heat exchanger). Measurements of the gap: hisim-component-physics-4g9.16 comments, scratchpad egap/.

title: At 3600 s a whole hour goes to hot water and empties the space-heating buffer: split a timestep between space heating and hot water
description: Owner (cmf, 2026-09-27): accepted for now after hisim-component-physics-4g9.16/hisim-6ehm (option B + draw feed-forward). DE gas house full year: 222 degree-hours below set at 3600 s (1.8 at 900 s), all within 2 steps of a hot-water hour when the DHW tank is below 45 C (the hot-water charge is never interrupted there) and the 170 l buffer empties; the distribution system's request lags one step. Fix: time-share a step between SH and DHW (fractional operation) for coarse timesteps, or size the buffer. Traces: scratchpad stor/.

title: Let a caller specify battery and heat-pump sizes instead of always auto-sizing
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 5

`EnergySystemConfig` (`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/system_config.py`) only has
`use_battery_and_ems: bool`; the battery is always auto-sized, and the heat pump is always
auto-sized from the building's heating load. RenoVisor users pick concrete sizes (battery
5/10/15 kWh, heat pump 6/8/10/12 kW) -- the translator marks these `approximated` and lets the
setup size them.

Suggested fix: add optional `battery_capacity_in_kilowatt_hours: Optional[float] = None` and
`heat_pump_thermal_power_in_kilowatt: Optional[float] = None` (None = keep auto-sizing, fully
backward compatible); in the setups, pass an explicit value through to `advanced_battery_bslib` /
`more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib` when present.

Note that under the declarative path the equivalent is a sparse `config:` override on the twin,
which the parametriser already applies -- so check whether the translator's route makes the
`EnergySystemConfig` change unnecessary before doing it.

Testing: extend the setup tests with a config carrying explicit sizes and assert the component
configs received them; keep one auto-sizing test as regression.
close_reason: No size was dropped and no EnergySystemConfig field is needed. The battery: since contract 882a8c1 apply.py battery_system writes capacity_in_kwh/power_in_watt into house.battery and translate.py _battery (Targets.BATTERY_CAPACITY/BATTERY_INVERTER) pins both sized Battery fields in the twin, reported used; a test now follows them through the sizing kernel unchanged. The heat pump: the request contract (measures.yaml heating_system, schema house.heating) has no power field, so a stated size is refused as key.unknown, never auto-sized silently; carrying one needs a contract change first (renovisorissues), after which the translator writes it onto set_thermal_output_power_in_watt the same way. The declarative route covers every other caller: a sparse config: override pins both sizes, the buffer follows the heat pump (tests/test_energy_system_explicit_sizes.py, energy_systems/README.md). The imperative EnergySystemConfig path has no consumer that needs explicit sizes, so it stays auto-sizing and its docstring points to the file.

title: The hplib heat pump's water flow carries up to 0.5 % more heat than its thermal power, so a storage accepts more than the pump books from its own model
description: Found in the #864 review (2026-09-30): at converged steps of household_heatpump_building_sizer (one week, 60 s) the flow m c (T_out - T_in) from hplib's mass flow and outlet temperature carries up to ~0.5 % more than hplib's P_th. AcceptedHeat.booked therefore does not cap the booked power at the generator's own (a cap broke the storage energy balance by 8-13 Wh per step), and the heat pump's accepted share can exceed 1 by that margin. Make the flow and P_th consistent in MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib (derive one from the other), then cap booked power at own in AcceptedHeat.booked. Owner decision needed on which of the two is authoritative (hplib's P_th/COP vs the flow).
close_reason: Resolved by D2 in hydronic stage B (hisim-hydronics-fxix.3): hplib's mass flow and outlet temperature are authoritative and the heat pump books the heat that flow carries from the unrounded return, so the flow and the booked P_th agree on every step to float precision; the up to 0.5 % excess (and the up to 1.5 % shortfall: hplib's 0.1 K rounding and its 4200 J/(kg K)) is gone. The cap in AcceptedHeat.booked belonged to #864, which is closed unmerged and whose accepted-heat back-channel the spec drops (§9.3); nothing on main books accepted heat, so no cap is needed.

title: Circuit laws for the hydronic ports: an owner publishes its outlet-vs-inlet curve so a node solves the step exactly in 2-3 iterations (if pure (m, T) ports get slow or biased)
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-01: the generator-storage coupling is redesigned in the temperature domain with PURE (m, T) ports — mass flow, supply and return temperature only; energy only derived as m c dT; no accepted-heat back-channel (PR #864's design rejected as an interim fix). This bead keeps the alternative analysed the same day, for when iteration counts or accuracy become a problem.

ALTERNATIVE: circuit laws. Each circuit owner publishes, besides m, its outlet-vs-inlet curve in temperatures only: T_out(T_in) = T_in + clamp(T_target - T_in, -max_drop(T_in), +max_lift(T_in)), max_lift = a + b*T_in (K, K/K; boiler: P_max/(m c), b = 0; heat pump: tangent of hplib's P_th(T_in)/(m c) at the current return estimate, b < 0). The water-holding node (mixed vessel, or HDS pipe water without a buffer) integrates C dT/dt = sum_i m_i c (T_out,i(T) - T) - UA (T - T_amb) exactly, piecewise-exponential across the kinks (<= 2 per circuit, each crossed once), and publishes per circuit the realized step means T_sup and T_ret; owners book Q = m c dt (T_sup - T_ret). The balance closes by construction; a heating-only source can never push the vessel above its T_target; cooling falls out (colder target). For a non-linear curve (hplib) the tangent is re-drawn at each iterate: Newton-like, quadratic convergence.

WHY PURE PORTS CONVERGE TO A BIASED ANSWER: the generator sends one supply temperature computed at the guessed return; the node must treat it as constant over the step. A heat pump holds its lift, not its supply temperature, so the node models the wrong reaction (with a fixed supply, every K the tank warms cuts the delivered heat by m c = 670 W/K instead of the heat pump's ~135 W/K). The iteration converges to the answer consistent with that assumption — converged = self-consistent, not correct.

TOY NUMBERS (300 kg tank at 35 degC, 6 kW draw, HP 0.16 kg/s, P_th = 9000*(1 - 0.015 x - 0.0004 x^2), x = T_in - 35; reference = 200k Euler sub-steps):
- 3600 s: reference mean 38.749, end 41.962, heat 8429 W (HP 9.0 -> 7.9 kW). Pure ports: 17 iterations, supply frozen at 51.82, mean 39.369 (+0.62 K), end 41.712, heat 8341 W (11.3 -> 6.8 kW). Law (single tangent): 3 iterations, mean 38.768 (+0.019 K, curvature over a 7 K swing).
- 900 s (the RenoVisor resolution, hisim/renovisor/simulation.py:74): reference mean 36.040, end 37.046, heat 8854 W. Pure ports: 8 iterations, mean 36.101 (+0.06 K), end 37.040, heat 8847 W (< 0.1 %).
- Design-draft measurements (agent, 300 kg buffer, 10 kW boiler, HDS 6 kW): plain fixed point boiler holding 55 degC 3/8/15 iterations at 60/900/3600 s; power-limited boiler 4/11/41; district heating -> HDS without buffer (30 kg pipe water, 900 s) 24 iterations and end 43.66 degC vs exact 44.18; law + exact node 2 iterations in all cases. Plain fixed-point contraction theta = 1 - (1 - e^-a)/a, a = sum(m) dt / M: tends to 1 for long steps or small vessels.
- Simulator limits (hisim/simulator.py:322-324): controllers frozen (force_convergence) after 10 tries, run aborted after 100; tolerance 1e-4 absolute on every output (hisim/component.py:189-195).

WHEN TO PICK THIS UP: iteration counts near 10 (frozen controllers) at 900 s or 3600 s, runtime problems from iterations, setups without a buffer (generator -> HDS) converging slowly, or visible bias at large steps / at regime switches inside a step (thermostat taking over, tap mixing valve below 40 degC, heat pump at max outlet temperature). The law is a pure temperature-domain extension of the pure ports (adds T_target and K, K/K parameters per circuit), so it can be added later without redesigning the ports.

title: Every time step's convergence iteration starts from an all-zero vector instead of the previous step's converged values
description:
hisim/simulator.py:628 creates stsv once and the loop at :631-638 never reassigns it (the reset line is commented out, and its comment claims the opposite of what the code does); process_one_timestep clones the incoming vector (:388-389). So in pass 1 every component reads 0 from every output that sits later in file order: the iteration's starting point depends on component order, the heat pump carries a 'storage sends zero' workaround (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:3357-3362), and no step converges in fewer than 3 passes. Expected fix if confirmed: stsv = resulting_stsv after each step (warm start), remove the workaround; results change slightly; hydronic spec D7 (no simulator change) to be amended.

VERIFY FIRST (owner, 2026-10-03): confirm with a minimal reproduction that this is a defect and what it changes before fixing anything. Found by a read-only analysis of the convergence loop after measuring that component order changes one week's KPIs by 0.1-7 % (analysis: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-cmf-HiSim/8a0b0959-06ba-4050-82c1-5ca9a7a47108/scratchpad/order/convergence_analysis.md; measurement artefacts in the same directory). Citations against origin/main 0921f9bd.
close_reason: Done in the simulator warm-start PR: Simulator.run_all_timesteps now hands each step's converged values to the next step (stsv = resulting_stsv), so only step 0 starts from zeros; the misleading comment is corrected, tests/test_simulator_warm_start.py pins the warm start, and the heat pump's DHW zero guard stays as a documented step-0 guard until the controller restore fix (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Relinked from the #909 review (finding M4, 2026-10-10), against hydronic-stage-c 0cce1839: the zeroing now sits in hot_water() (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:1408, self.minimum_thermal_output_power = 0.0), and it has a second consequence. The hplib cache key (CalculationRequest in cached_hplib_result, around :2045) holds t_in_primary, t_in_secondary, t_amb, mode and operation_mode but not p_th_min, while heatpump.simulate is called with p_th_min=minimal_thermal_power_in_watt (:2063). A grid point first computed before the first hot-water step is cached with p_th_min = 1800 W, one first computed after it with 0 W, and both are reused for the rest of the run. Results therefore depend on whether a grid point was cached before or after the first hot-water step, not only on the restore defect described above. Fix both together: restore the minimum (or keep it in the saved state) and put p_th_min into the cache key.

title: After a forced step the heat pump's space-heating controller keeps its start-of-step mode, while the plant ran the mode it held: the next step skips the hysteresis band
description:
After 10 tries (simulator.py:415-416) controllers skip their computation (e.g. more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2835, :3351; heat_distribution_system.py:1194) but restore_state has already reset their internal state, so stsv keeps pass 12's output while the controller's memory is the start-of-step state; the plant (heat pump :1496, storages, EMS :823, battery) keeps computing on the frozen outputs and advances its own timers (:1953). Measured on the heat-pump twin, one week at 900 s: 32 forced steps (original order) / 30 (reordered) = ~8 h per week; every step with more than 7 passes is a limit cycle the freeze ends (histogram 14-15 passes). At step 44 the frozen state heats at 10.3 kW with the buffer above its switch-on point and an HDS flow temperature not derivable from its own inputs. Root cause of the cycles: the EMS surplus sign test (:765, :782) includes the heat pump's own draw, so 'on' is never a consistent state. Expected fix if confirmed: controllers decide on start-of-step values (hydronic D4 extended to the EMS, surplus from exogenous + start-of-step quantities with hysteresis), skip restore for frozen components, and a forced-step counter with target 0.

VERIFY FIRST (owner, 2026-10-03): confirm with a minimal reproduction that this is a defect and what it changes before fixing anything. Found by a read-only analysis of the convergence loop after measuring that component order changes one week's KPIs by 0.1-7 % (analysis: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-cmf-HiSim/8a0b0959-06ba-4050-82c1-5ca9a7a47108/scratchpad/order/convergence_analysis.md; measurement artefacts in the same directory). Citations against origin/main 0921f9bd.

The heat pump DHW controller's step-0 guard (a DHW tank temperature of 0 replaced by the previous value, MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW.i_simulate) is removed together with the controller restore fix, as the owner decided on 2026-10-09 when the simulator warm start (hisim-component-physics-4g9.23) kept it.
