The outputs still moving on the eleventh pass of a forced step are the same in both orders (3 days at 60 s, 187 and 344 forced steps): the building's theoretical demand, the heat-distribution controller's flow temperature, the hot-water controller's target (the raise), the heat pump's power and the energy manager's grid balance. So this loop, the raise switching on the heat pump's own draw, is what remains of the heat-pump twins' forced steps; the hot-water electricity at 60 s moves 1158.3 -> 1119.6 kWh with the order.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-11, energy-manager loop (branches remove-fixed-point-acceleration, ems-battery-limits, ems-pv-surplus-only, dhw-charge-creep, below #914): the raise's on/off loop that made most of this bead's forced steps is mostly removed at its source. A: the battery publishes its charging limits for the step and the energy manager computes the battery's charging share from them instead of from its answer to an earlier pass (the stale answer read as a fake surplus or deficit, 98 % of the forced steps). C: only PV surplus keeps a raise; a discharging battery no longer counts. Heat-pump twin, full year 2021 at 60 s, predefined occupancy: 89020 forced steps without the acceleration -> 72060 with A -> 3469 with A + C (900 s: 8677 -> 6827 -> 2134); with the warm start (#914) on top 4390 at 60 s. B (a hold when the decision cycles) is open as hisim-component-physics-4g9.51. D of the design (consistent forced passes: controllers keep what they published) does not reduce forced steps (with A it doubled them at 60 s); it stays here for this bead's remaining aspect: under force_convergence controllers skip their computation after restore_state reset them, so controller and plant carry different states in the forced steps that remain. Narrowed to that aspect.

notes:
From the fxix triage of 2026-10-19 (hisim-hydronics-fxix.26 closed into this bead): in the heat-pump twins no part-load ratio moves after pass 10; what keeps moving is the energy manager, the meter and the hot-water side. Forced steps on main (full year 2021, local occupancy): heat pump 60 s 3562, 900 s 1881, 3600 s 832; gas 60 s 0, 900 s 88, 3600 s 559 (mostly a building <-> distribution loop).

Verified 2026-10-20 on main 49b04e38c (report /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/4g928/report.md). Only the heat pump's space-heating controller (MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating) is inconsistent: i_restore_state resets controller_heatpumpmode to the start of the step on every pass, and under force it only holds its outputs, so it commits the start-of-step mode while the plant ran the last free pass's State_SH. 185 mismatches a year at 900 s, 319 at 60 s (heat-pump twin); each restarts the heat pump early (example step 641: restart at 29.9 C instead of coasting to 22.2 C). The energy manager, the heat-distribution controller and the plant timers are consistent on main (the description's claims about them, and its step-44 example, are stale). Effect of removing it: <= 0.02 % (900 s) / 0.31 % (60 s) on annual energies; the gas boiler controller has the same pattern with 0 mismatches.
Owner decisions 2026-10-20: P3 (was P1). Fix option B: the controller gets a start-of-step and an end-of-step mode, the pattern of the energy manager and the heat-distribution controller (an unforced pass writes the end mode, restore leaves it, save makes it the next start), plus a unit test that after a forced step the committed mode equals the published State_SH; the boiler controller may get the same. Not option A (a simulator rule skipping restore under force). The parity noise (12 vs 13 free passes, up to 1 % at 60 s) is accepted until design G (note on 4g9.51). hisim-component-physics-4g9.24 stays a separate change, parked until 4g9.51.

title: GenericBoiler's maximal_thermal_power_in_watt is the maximal fuel input, so a boiler sized to the heating load delivers only about efficiency x load
description: Where: hisim/components/generic_boiler.py. GenericBoiler.i_simulate (lines ~688-708) burns control_signal * maximal_thermal_power_in_watt (maximum_power_used_in_watt, also the fuel energy) and delivers that times real_combustion_efficiency, which runs between eff_th_min = 0.60 and eff_th_max = 0.90 (GenericBoilerConfig, lines ~207-208). The sizing law MAXIMAL_POWER_LAW (lines ~189-195, scale_thermal_power ~104-122) sets that field to the building's heating load, or 2.5 kW per apartment for DHW, whichever is larger, plus 10 % when the boiler serves SH and DHW. So the field named thermal is the fuel input, and a boiler sized by the law delivers at most about 0.9 x the heating load (plus the 10 % margin): it is undersized by the efficiency. Found in the review of PR #900; the assemblies' power_in_watt descriptions now say fuel input (wording only). Open questions: rename the field (to a fuel-input name) and/or divide the law by the maximal efficiency so the delivered heat covers the load. Either changes every boiler twin's goldens (gas, oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen, and the setups that use GenericBoiler), so the fix gets its own PR with a golden re-bless. Since #979 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.63) the boiler's pump reads the field too: BoilerPump.sized_for sizes the pump's largest flow from maximal_thermal_power_in_watt * eff_th_max, the maximal heat the burner gives today; a fix of this bead keeps the pump sized from the boiler's maximal heat, whatever the field then means (review of #979, finding R12).

title: Make the heating setpoint configurable so RenoVisor's targetTempC can be mapped
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 6 (listed in the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

Building-sizer setups hard-code `building_set_heating_temperature_in_celsius = 20.0` (and 25.0
for cooling), e.g. `household_heatpump_building_sizer.py` lines ~122-124. The user-chosen
living-room setpoint (12-28 degC in the RenoVisor UI, default 21) is ignored; every simulation
heats to 20 degC. Setpoint strongly affects heating demand (rule of thumb ~6 %/K), so this is one
of the biggest fidelity gaps for "your house today" baselines.

Suggested fix: add `set_heating_temperature_in_celsius: Optional[float] = None` to
`ArcheTypeConfig`; setups use it when present, falling back to the current constants.

Related: challenges.md C15 records that the `change room temperature` measure writes two fields
-- the building set-point and the HDS controller set-point (M11).

Testing: setup test asserting the building config receives the configured setpoint; an
integration assertion that a higher setpoint yields higher annual heating demand. Translator: map
`targetTempC` to the new field and flip its report status to `used`.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP. new_room_temperature stays on the not-implemented whitelist and greyed out; every twin heats to the recorded 20 degC for the MVP.

title: ElectricHeating delivers the building's full demand in space-heating-only steps, ignoring maximum_electric_power_w
description:
Evidence: hisim/components/generic_electric_heating.py, ElectricHeating.i_simulate. The HeatingMode.SPACE_HEATING branch (lines 427-444) sets thermal_power_sh_delivered_in_watt to the Building's TheoreticalHeatingDemand and the energy to TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand whenever the demand is positive, with no reference to config.maximum_electric_power_w. The parallel branch, HeatingMode.SPACE_HEATING_AND_DOMESTIC_HOT_WATER_IN_PARALLEL (lines 467-513), caps space heating at maximum_electric_power_w minus the DHW power (available_electric_load_in_watt, line 497, min() at 504-511). The electric outputs equal the thermal ones (direct resistive heating), so the same holds for the electricity drawn.

Consequence: with parallel_space_heating_and_dhw_option true (household_electric_heating_building_sizer and energy_systems/assemblies/heating/electric_resistive.assembly.yaml), every step without hot-water demand runs SPACE_HEATING and is uncapped. A stated maximum_electric_power_w below the building's demand has no effect in those steps, so the delivered heat and the electricity drawn are overstated. AUTO sizing hides it: the law sets the power to the building's heating load, which the demand rarely exceeds.

Fix: cap the SPACE_HEATING branch as the parallel branch does (power at min(demand, maximum_electric_power_w), energy at min(energy demand, maximum_electric_power_w * seconds_per_timestep / 3600)), then re-bless the electric-heating goldens (household_electric_heating_building_sizer week and year) and re-check the heating/electric_resistive monotone and expect figures. Found in the review of PR #904; owner decision 2026-10-08: its own PR, not #904.

title: The energy manager switches its temperature raise on a +-5e-12 W surplus, so a 1e-13 K flip in a storage loops forever; fix it at the source (hysteresis or a threshold) and remove the tank's 1e-9 K deadband
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), commit 858f5012; roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §6 (owner, 2026-10-09).

L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.modify_set_temperatures_for_components_in_case_of_surplus_electricity (hisim/components/controller_l2_energy_management_system.py) raises the building, buffer and hot-water set temperatures when available_surplus_electricity_in_watt > 0, the surplus left after the battery is dispatched. When the battery balances the house exactly, that surplus is float noise: measured +-5e-12 W at step 758 of household_heatpump_building_sizer (full year 2021 at 900 s, predefined occupancy profile) and at step 10674 of household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer. A converged DHW tank whose step mean flips between two neighbouring floats (about 1e-13 K apart at 70 °C) moves the heat pump's hot-water electricity by 5e-12 W, the sign flips, the raises toggle 0 <-> 10 K (building 0 <-> 2 K), the building's demand toggles with them, and the simulator aborts after 100 tries.

Stopgap in stage C (owner, 2026-10-09): SimpleDHWStorage publishes the same float once its step mean moves by at most PUBLISHED_MEAN_DEADBAND_IN_KELVIN = 1e-9 K. Fix at the source: a threshold or a hysteresis on the surplus the energy manager switches on (or deciding on start-of-step values, hisim-component-physics-4g9.28), then remove the deadband and its spec sentence and show the heat-pump twins' years at 900 s complete without it. Related to hisim-component-physics-4g9.28 (the energy manager's on/off loops at force_convergence): the same switching rule, here at zero surplus rather than at the heat pump's own draw.
close_reason: The energy manager decides with a 0.01 W hysteresis around zero surplus; the heat-pump twins' years complete without the simulator's 1e-9 deadband, which is removed (branch ems-surplus-hysteresis).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10 (hydronic-stage-c, guideline review F2, owner decision): the 1e-9 K deadband left the tank. The simulator now holds any output a component declares accelerated within 1e-9 of the value it stood at (hisim/fixed_point_acceleration.py, SecantAcceleration.DEADBAND); the tank declares its two step-mean outputs. Removing the deadband after the energy-manager fix now means deleting held_value's use there; the full-year measurements (spec §6) show the heat-pump twins abort without it.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Fixed on branch ems-surplus-hysteresis (between #912 and #914), owner decision 2026-10-10: a hysteresis. L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.raises_set_temperatures (pure, transition-table test) raises above +0.01 W surplus after the battery, not below -0.01 W, and keeps the previous step's decision within the band (edges included). The previous decision is the manager's frozen EMSState, read from the saved state and advanced only in i_save_state. Band: 1e9 x the +-5e-12 W float noise and 10 x the ~1e-3 W a converged surplus can move under the simulator's 1e-4 tolerance; inside it at most 0.01 W goes to or from the grid whichever decision is kept (at most 88 Wh a year at any step length).

The simulator's 1e-9 deadband (SecantAcceleration.DEADBAND, held_value, StepAcceleration.hold) and its spec sentence are removed; under forced convergence the simulator no longer touches the accelerated outputs. The secant acceleration stays (without it the gas twin at 900 s has 52 forced steps instead of 0, the heat-pump-and-solar twin 5.08 instead of 4.77 passes at 900 s and 6.33 instead of 5.20 at 3600 s).

Full year 2021, predefined occupancy, on #912's head (no warm start), mean passes / forced steps:
(a) no deadband, no hysteresis: heat pump aborts at step 22058 (60 s), 1414 (900 s), 158 (3600 s); heat pump + solar at 22101, 1232, 979.
(b) no deadband, hysteresis: all six complete. Heat pump 6.21 / 89091 (60 s), 7.39 / 8550 (900 s), 8.79 / 3038 (3600 s); heat pump + solar 4.38 / 3467, 4.77 / 1540, 5.20 / 554.
With the deadband and no hysteresis (#912 as is): heat pump 7.37 / 8396 (900 s), 8.79 / 2980 (3600 s); heat pump + solar 4.80 / 1725, 5.19 / 553.

title: Refuse thermalpower_dhw_is_constant=true when the hot-water controller is built, for every storage position, or remove the field
description: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHWConfig.thermalpower_dhw_is_constant (with p_th_max_dhw_in_watt) asks the hplib heat pump for a constant hot-water power. Since hydronic stage B (PR #908) the heat pump books the heat its flow carries, so with a parallel storage it refuses the flag at runtime, at the first hot-water step (ValueError naming thermalpower_dhw_is_constant), and in the fixed-flow mode (a series storage or none) it silently ignores it. No file in the repository sets it. Wanted: refuse true when the controller is built, for every storage position, so the configuration fails before the simulation starts and the fixed-flow mode no longer ignores it. Option: remove the field and p_th_max_dhw_in_watt altogether (config schema, the energy-system recorder, the controller's ThermalPowerHPForDHWConst outputs and the heat pump's matching inputs).
close_reason: Removed on hydronic-stage-c (#909, guideline review finding F9, owner 2026-10-10): thermalpower_dhw_is_constant and p_th_max_dhw_in_watt, the controller's two outputs, the heat pump's two inputs, their default connections, the refusal and the controller's print are gone; schema regenerated. No setup or energy-system file set the option.

title: The boiler's total fuel KPI sums two separately rounded parts and differs from its meter's by up to 0.1 kWh
description:
`GenericBoiler.get_cost_opex` (hisim/components/generic_boiler.py, around :890-912) rounds the space-heating and the hot-water fuel to 0.1 kWh each and books their sum as "Total <carrier> consumption (energy)"; the meters round the one total once (GasMeter to 0.1 kWh, FuelMeter to 0.01 kWh). Every step agrees, but the two totals can differ by up to 0.1 kWh, and the boiler's volume, mass, cost and CO2 KPIs follow from the doubly rounded total.

Measured on hydronic-stage-c (one day, 900 s): the gas, oil and hydrogen composed files burn 76.531 + 10.635 = 87.166 kWh; the boiler reports 76.5 + 10.6 = 87.1, the GasMeter 87.2 and the FuelMeter 87.17. Pellets: boiler 201.0, FuelMeter 201.07 on 201.069 burned. GenericDistrictHeating and GenericElectricHeating round their two parts the same way (district heating on the test day: 56.3 + 5.5 = 61.8, the FuelMeter 61.77).

Fix: sum the unrounded series, round the total once (and each part for its own KPI). This moves KPI values in the goldens by up to 0.1 kWh, so it needs a golden re-bless; the assembly test of the gas house (tests/assemblies/test_assembly_crossing.py) already compares the meter per step on the unrounded results.

title: Controllers become explicit state machines: a state Enum, a transition table and a pure next-state function, with table-generated tests, transition coverage and Hypothesis invariants; pilot on the boiler controller
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (system_docs/coding_style.md, 'Design patterns' and 'Testing state machines'). A small generic helper (e.g. hisim/state_machine.py): states as Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), recording of the transitions taken. Tests: every table row and the boundary values of each condition (hysteresis edge, minimum run time exactly reached), a coverage check that every declared transition was taken and no undeclared one, a Hypothesis RuleBasedStateMachine checking invariants (minimum run and rest times never cut short, never two modes, off obeyed after the minimum run time), match plus typing.assert_never for exhaustiveness, the state diagram generated from the table. Hypothesis is not yet a dependency; add it to the test requirements. Pilot: GenericBoilerController's modes and hysteresis. Its minimum run and rest times (which only act at the start of the run today, review finding F7) move into the boiler physics by owner decision 2026-10-10 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.40) and are tested there with the same method. Then the single heat-pump controller (hisim-component-physics-4g9.41) and the heat distribution controller.

title: The heating curve becomes an L2 component that sends the supply set point to the generators' L1 controllers
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Owner decision 2026-10-10. Today HeatDistributionController computes HeatingFlowTemperature from the outdoor temperature (heat_distribution_system.py:1060), and the heat pump's SH controller (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2893-2906) and the boiler controller (generic_boiler.py:1466-1480) read it as their set point: an L1 reading another L1, which table A of the principles does not allow. The owner chose a dedicated L2 component (not L1-to-L1 reads, not a shared helper) that owns the heating curve and sends the supply set point as a signal to every generator L1. The HDS controller keeps only the valve/thermostat role.
close_reason: Done on branch heating-curve-l2 (on #942, with #922's kind base classes below): HeatingCurveController (hisim/components/heating_curve.py, an L2ControllerComponent) owns the heating curve and publishes SpaceHeatingSupplyTemperatureSetInCelsius and HeatingSeason; the heat pump's space-heating controller, the boiler controller and the district-heating controller read both from it. HeatDistributionController keeps only its valve (next_valve_mode, valve_state), and its valve mode now advances only in i_save_state. The simulator evaluates an L2 controller that reads another L2 controller after it, so the curve applies the energy manager's raise in the same pass, as the heat distribution controller did. Week goldens: all 22 pairs equal to #922's within 1e-9.

title: The heating threshold moves into the heating-curve L2 component, and every component that needs it reads it from there
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Owner decision 2026-10-10, its own bead. Today the outdoor temperature above which space heating stops exists in several copies: HeatDistributionControllerConfig derives it from the building (HEATING_THRESHOLD_LAW: 16 degC up to 50 W/m2, 18 up to 80, 20 above; heat_distribution_system.py:866-882); the heat pump's SH controller reads that fact (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2739); GenericBoilerControllerConfig has a plain field with default 16.0 (generic_boiler.py:1163-1165) that the gas twin pins to 18.0, equal to the HDS value only because the twin was recorded for that building. A renovated house at <=50 W/m2 would get 16 degC in the HDS controller and 18 in the boiler: the boiler keeps the buffer hot while the valve is shut. Also: summer_heating_condition raises when the daily mean equals the threshold exactly (heat_distribution_system.py:1277-1296, more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:3220-3244). Target: one owner (the heating-curve L2), everyone reads it from its output.
notes: 2026-10-14: #931 removes the exception the close reason names: the electric heater's controller reads HeatingSeason from the heating curve as well (the curve's preset direct_room_heating pins the emitter type in a house without a heat-distribution controller), and its threshold and specific-heating-load fields are gone. The heating curve is now the one owner of the threshold in every twin.
close_reason: Done on branch heating-curve-l2: the threshold law (16/18/20 °C by the specific heating load) is HeatingCurveControllerConfig.HEATING_THRESHOLD_LAW, the curve publishes HeatingSeason (1 on a day at or below the threshold), and the heat distribution controller, the heat pump's space-heating controller, the boiler controller and the district-heating controller read it; the boiler's plain 16.0 field, the copies in the heat pump's and the substation's configs and the sizing fact set_heating_threshold_outside_temperature_in_celsius are gone. A day mean exactly at the threshold is in the heating season (the old summer_heating_condition raised). Exception: the electric heater heats the rooms directly and has no heating curve; its controller keeps its own threshold field sized by the same law (owner question in the PR). The recorded boiler twins pinned 18 °C, the building's value, so they do not change; basic_household_only_heating and household_gas_solar_thermal ran their boilers at the old default 16 °C beside an 18 °C heat distribution and now use 18 °C.

title: The room thermostat moves out of the building and heat-distribution physics into the heat-distribution L1 controller; the building publishes its room temperature and receives heat through an emitter law
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Finding F1, P1 by owner decision. Building owns the room set points (building/config.py:70-71) and adds the energy manager's BuildingTemperatureModifier (building.py:697-699); it publishes TheoreticalThermalBuildingDemand, a what-if heat from its own 5R1C model with a 10 W/m2 probe (building.py:385-391, :2013-2077); HeatDistribution delivers exactly that demand (heat_distribution_system.py:556-620) and picks heating or cooling from its sign; HeatDistributionController switches on the same value, keeps a sized copy of the set point (:887-889) and applies the modifier a second time (:1312-1320). Breaks principles 2-4: physics decides how much heat the room gets, the interface is a model-form value, two owners of the set point, an L2 signal reaches physics. Any other building or emitter model must reproduce 'theoretical demand'. Fix: the HDS L1 controller is the thermostat (owns the set points, commands valve/flow), the energy manager signals that controller only, HeatDistribution computes heat from an emitter law (pipe/floor model at :503-554 as a start), the demand stays a report output. Changes goldens; large.

title: The energy manager keeps to the L2 role: it signals only L1 controllers, the battery gets an L1, it sums its own balance from physics ports, and it decides on values fixed within the step
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Finding F3, P1 by owner decision. L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem writes the surplus into the battery's LoadingPowerInput (controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:707-713; no battery L1), sends BuildingIndoorTemperatureModifier to Building physics (:784-797), computes the grid balance the meter bills (:842-890), and switches its modifiers on a surplus computed from the same iteration's heat-pump and battery electricity (:780-806); the hot-water tank's deadband (simple_water_storage.py:2039-2048, hisim-component-physics-4g9.31) and the DHW controller's tolerance (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:3373, :3583-3586) exist only to absorb that. i_save_state keeps a reference, not a copy (:670-677). Owner decisions: nothing reads a meter, so the energy manager sums its own balance from the physics ports for its decisions; L2 signals go to L1 controllers only. Fix: battery L1 taking an incentive; modifiers to L1s. Owner decision 2026-10-10: the energy manager keeps deciding on the values of the current iteration; making controllers decide on start-of-step or previous-step values (proposed principle M2) was rejected as harmful, because the iterations exist so that components react to each other within the step, which matters most at coarse steps. The flip-flop the deadband (hisim-component-physics-4g9.31) and the DHW controller tolerance absorb needs a remedy that keeps same-iteration coupling (e.g. hysteresis on the surplus, or holding the decision under force_convergence). Changes goldens.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-11: the decision part is addressed by A + C (branches ems-battery-limits, ems-pv-surplus-only): the battery publishes MaximumChargingPowerInWatt and MinimumChargingPowerInWatt from its start-of-step state, the energy manager computes the battery's charging share from them, and a discharging battery no longer keeps a raise. Rejected by the owner on 2026-10-11: E (a band sized by the heat pump's power) and F (deciding without the raise-induced draw, a what-if quantity); the simulator-side hold (B as first designed) was withdrawn, B is open as hisim-component-physics-4g9.51. G (a continuous incentive the heat pump's L1 controller decides on with its setting power) is the long-term design, not planned now. Remaining here: the battery's L1 controller, the modifiers to L1 controllers only, the meter-independent balance.

title: ElectricityMeter bills from the energy manager's net balance: consumers not wired to the energy manager are missing, and production and consumption are mislabelled
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Finding F9, P1 by owner decision. In both twins the meter's only input is L2EMSElectricityController.TotalElectricityToOrFromGrid (tag ELECTRICITY_PRODUCTION, weight 999; default connection electricity_meter.py:481-512), PV minus the consumers wired to the energy manager, signed. ElectricalInputPowerForCooling and ElectricalInputPowerBrinePump of the heat pump are not energy-manager inputs and are never billed (0 in the current HP twin); ElectricityProduction carries the net balance and ElectricityConsumption is always 0. Owner decision 2026-10-10: a meter reads physics ports only, and nothing reads a meter. Fix: the meter reads every physics electricity port (by port role, not by class) and computes the bill itself.
close_reason: Branch meter-reads-physics-ports: the ElectricityMeter reads every electricity port by its role, not by class (ElectricityMeter.default_connections_for: an IN port as consumption, an OUT port as production, a negated port with its sign turned) and computes import and export itself; it reads nothing of the energy manager, and every place that resolves default connections asks DynamicComponent.default_connections_for. The building-sizer setups connect the meter automatically, the twins, grouped twins, composed files and the grid test partner follow. ElectricityConsumption and ElectricityProduction carry the real totals (heat-pump twin, first January week at 60 s: consumption 0 -> 281.3 kWh, production -159.8 kWh net -> 121.5 kWh; gas twin 0 -> 109.3 kWh, 8.3 net -> 117.6 kWh). The heat pump's cooling and brine-pump ports are metered (unmetered list now empty); no KPI moves beyond 1e-9 relative in either twin, since both ports are zero in the air-source twin (also in a July week). Test: tests/test_electricity_meter_ports.py, test_a_consumer_the_energy_manager_does_not_read_is_billed.

title: Make boiler seasonal efficiency and design flow temperature configurable
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 9 (the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

The gas/oil/pellet/wood setups use fixed component defaults, and `heat_distribution_system.py`
handles the flow temperature internally. RenoVisor's expert fields
`heating.seasonalEfficiencyPct` (e.g. an old oil boiler at 78 %) and `heating.flowTempC` are
dropped. Baseline fuel consumption for old boilers is therefore optimistic, which understates the
savings of switching away from them.

Suggested fix: an optional efficiency override wired to the boiler component configs; an optional
design flow temperature wired to the heat-distribution controller (also improves heat-pump COP
realism, item 5).

Testing: setup test that a lower efficiency raises annual fuel energy proportionally.

title: Minimum run and idle times are device protection: the boiler's move from its controller into the boiler, where they actually take effect
description:
Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Findings F5 and F7. Owner decision 2026-10-10: minimum run and idle times are device protection (anti-short-cycle), enforced by physics like a maximum supply temperature. The heat pump already enforces them in physics (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:1645-1670). The boiler keeps them in GenericBoilerController, where they never take effect: activate()/deactivate() (generic_boiler.py:1243-1252) are never called, so the enforcement (:1627-1642) only acts during the first minimum period of the run, and the state is not saved or restored (:1497-1503). Move them into GenericBoiler, with state saved and restored, and tested with the state-machine method (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34). Changes boiler goldens (pellet, wood chip and other on/off presets cycle freely today). Keep the existing behaviour of rounding a minimum time down to whole steps (owner decision on #900).

Update 2026-10-14 (hisim-75mt, branch burner-firing-times): GenericBoiler now keeps its burner's own minimum firing time and minimum pause (BurnerTimes per fuel, class constants: pellets 30/15 min, wood chips 60/30 min, gas/oil/hydrogen none), with its state committed in i_save_state and restored in i_restore_state, acting on whether the burner burns. What remains here: GenericBoilerControllerConfig.minimum_runtime_in_seconds / minimum_resting_time_in_seconds, which act on the controller's mode and still only take effect during the first minimum period of a run; the pellet and wood-chip twins still set them.
close_reason: Duplicate of hisim-component-physics-4g9.68 (2026-10-25): the boiler's own BurnerTimes were done in hisim-75mt; what remained here, the controller's minimum run and idle times, is investigated there (fix or delete).

title: The heat pump gets one L1 controller for the whole device (off, space heating, hot water as one state machine) instead of two controllers with the priority decided in physics
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10. MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib has two L1 controllers (MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating, MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW), and the physics picks hot-water priority when both ask (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py module docstring and :1639-1642): physics deciding, against principle 3. Like the boiler controller, which handles both services with its DiverterValve, one heat-pump controller owns the modes as one state machine (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34) and decides the priority; the physics only executes. Folds in hisim-component-physics-4g9.28 (DHW controller writes its previous state in i_simulate). Changes goldens possibly.

title: Three small fixes from the component review: the heat pump's minimum output in hot-water mode, the heat-distribution controller's restore, and the controllers' buffer sensor
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Owner decision 2026-10-10: one small PR. (F4) MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib sets self.minimum_thermal_output_power = 0.0 in hot-water mode (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:1754) and never restores the configured 1800 W; the hplib cache key CalculationRequest (:2672-2690) omits p_th_min. Use a local value per mode and add p_th_min to the key (no golden change for the HP twin: its lowest hplib output is 4595 W). (F6) HeatDistributionController.i_restore_state assigns the mode to itself (heat_distribution_system.py:1178-1180); restore from previous_controller_heat_distribution_mode (goldens may change in steps where the demand crosses zero). (F12) The heat pump's SH controller (:2923-2936) and GenericBoilerController (generic_boiler.py:1417-1431) read SimpleHotWaterStorage.WaterTemperatureToHeatGenerator, a port temperature that becomes the step mean in stage D; rewire both, default connections and recorded twins, to the sensor output WaterMeanTemperatureInStorage (same value today).

title: Three copies to remove: the boiler controller's hard-coded 60 degC hot-water aim, the water density literal 0.992, and the storage ambient temperature defined twice
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Finding F11 b-d (not chosen for the small-fix PR on 2026-10-10). (b) GenericBoilerController sets warm_water_temperature_aim_in_celsius = 60.0 in __init__ (generic_boiler.py:1306): make it a config field. (c) 0.992 kg/l appears in SimpleHotWaterStorage (simple_water_storage.py:1200) and the occupancy KPI (loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py:2261) beside hydronics' WATER_DENSITY_KG_PER_M3 = 992.0: read it from one place. (d) The ambient temperature of the buffer (simple_water_storage.py:1215, comment says 17 degC basement, value 20.0) and of the DHW tank (:1364) are separate 20.0 values: one place, a config field. No golden change.

title: Remaining minor findings of the component review: weather through the SimRepository, dead and duplicated code, unit-less names, and a crash on an exact threshold
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Findings F10, F14, F15. (F10) PV and Building read the weather's whole-year arrays from the SimRepository (weather/weather.py:368-387; pv_system.py:577-656; building.py:832-955) instead of their wired inputs; another weather source with other keys breaks both. (F14) Both heat-pump air inputs use Weather.DailyAverageOutsideTemperatures (day-night COP swing lost; intent unknown); boiler OFF branch publishes TotalFuelConsumption while EnergyDemand* is 0 (generic_boiler.py:767-777), unused temperature_delta_in_celsius (:210); Building opens windows and overwrites the reported air temperature without changing its thermal state (building.py:680-694); dead warm-water input branch in UtspLpgConnector (:543-592), a KPI recomputing DHW heat with the tank's constants (:2255-2275); three PositionHotWaterStorageInSystemSetup enums that must agree (heat_distribution_system.py:54-75, simple_water_storage.py:63-75, more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:74-97; spec D25). (F15) I/O and config names without units (ThermalPowerDelivered, TemperatureOutputSH, MassFlowOutputSH, LoadingPowerInput, TheoreticalThermalBuildingDemand, PVSystemConfig.azimuth/.tilt, ...) and temperature differences named _in_celsius (GenericBoilerConfig.temperature_delta_in_celsius, SH controller offsets, energy-manager offsets): renaming I/O needs a recorder/YAML migration. Split into own beads when worked on.

title: Public "SH" names spell out SpaceHeating: ports, outputs and controller classes, with a migration of the energy-system files and goldens
description: The coding style (system_docs/coding_style.md §5, PR #919) forbids "sh" for space heating. PR #908 renamed every internal snake_case name in the heat pump module and its tests; the public names stay because they are addresses: ports and outputs such as ElectricalInputPowerSH, ThermalOutputPowerSH, MassFlowOutputSH, TemperatureOutputSH, OnOffSwitchSH, SetHeatingTemperatureSH, State_SH, the class MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSH (22 files incl. 10 energy-system files, system setups, assemblies and the RenoVisor roadmap), the golden KPI keys (Input_MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib_ElectricalInputPowerSH_*), and the sh names in other components (generic_gas_heater, generic_electric_heating, generic_district_heating: *_sh_channel, thermal_power_sh_delivered_in_watt). Done when no public or internal name uses SH/sh for space heating, the energy-system files and twins are re-recorded, the goldens are re-blessed with the renamed keys, and the RenoVisor backend is told if a name it reads changes. Do it together with the dotted-path migration that the file splits of more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py and simple_water_storage.py need (hydronics review, #909).

title: Four component classes mix kinds and have only the closest kind declared: the heating curve sits in the heat-distribution L1 controller, the idealised electric heater controls itself, the sum builders and the night setback fit no kind
description:
Source: the simulator's kind ordering (branch kind-classes, which replaces #922; hisim-hydronics-fxix.16), the kinds table of system_docs/component_design_principles.md §A.

Every component class now inherits one kind base class (DataSourceComponent, L2ControllerComponent, L1ControllerComponent, PhysicsComponent, MeterComponent in hisim/component.py) and the simulator evaluates a pass in the order data source, L2 controller, L1 controller, physics, meter. Four classes mix kinds; each inherits the closest kind:

1. HeatDistributionController (L1): it switches the distribution pump of its one device (L1), and it computes the heating curve's supply set temperature that the heat pump's and the boiler's controllers read. A set point several L1 controllers share comes from an L2 controller (§A), so the heating curve belongs in an L2 component of its own.
2. IdealizedElectricHeater (physics): it delivers exactly the building's theoretical demand, so the decision of its missing controller is inside the device. Either it gets an L1 controller, or it is documented as an ideal heat source with no control.
3. SumBuilderForTwoInputs, SumBuilderForThreeInputs, CalculateOperation (physics): arithmetic nodes between ports, no device and no decision. Physics is the closest kind (they pass port quantities on); a meter would be wrong wherever a component reads them. A kind of its own, or removal where a port can be read directly, is the choice.
4. NightSetbackController (L2): a time-of-day set-point shift with no inputs, so a data source by its inputs and an L2 controller by its role; both come before every L1 controller, so the evaluation order is the same either way.

Related, already filed: the room thermostat inside the building and the heat distribution (hisim-component-physics-4g9.37), the energy manager commanding the battery directly (hisim-component-physics-4g9.38), the heat pump's priority between its two controllers decided in physics (hisim-component-physics-4g9.41).

Done when each of the four is split or its kind is confirmed by the owner.
close_reason: Closed with the owner's decisions of 2026-10-10: (1) the heating curve is the L2 component HeatingCurveController, an L2ControllerComponent (hisim-component-physics-4g9.35); (2) IdealizedElectricHeater is split into IdealizedElectricHeaterController (an L1ControllerComponent, asks for the building's theoretical demand) and the heater (a PhysicsComponent, delivers what it is told); (3) SumBuilderForTwoInputs, SumBuilderForThreeInputs and CalculateOperation keep inheriting PhysicsComponent, and (4) NightSetbackController keeps inheriting L2ControllerComponent, as the owner confirmed. Branch heating-curve-l2.

title: bslib keeps its recharge hysteresis as per-pass state, so a battery near full answers each pass from the previous pass's flag
description:
Source: energy-manager loop design (2026-10-11), finding 2; branch ems-battery-limits.

bslib's ACBatMod keeps its recharge hysteresis (`_threshold`, set once the battery is full, cleared when the state of
charge falls below `SOC_h`, 0.98 for SG1) as an attribute it rewrites in every `simulate` call. HiSim's Battery
restores only its state of charge between passes, so within a step every pass after the first charges or not
according to the flag the previous pass left behind, not the one the step started with. That breaks principle 5
(i_simulate depends on inputs and saved state only) near a full battery.

Since ems-battery-limits the Battery records the flag after each pass in BatteryState.recharging_is_blocked and
publishes its maximum charging power from the start-of-step value, so the energy manager's share is consistent; the
bslib model itself still answers from the per-pass flag, so its realized power can differ from the published limit in
the passes where the flag flips. The iteration-safety test in tests/test_advanced_battery_bslib.py keeps the state of
charge away from full for that reason.

Fix: set the bslib flag from the saved state before each `simulate` (writing a private attribute, behind the
BslibChargingParameters adapter), or move the battery onto a model of HiSim's own (see the bslib accessor bead).
Changes results near a full battery only.
close_reason: Not reachable: bslib 0.7 sets _threshold only when a step ends above a state of charge of 1 (bslib.py:285), and the battery never passes 1, because avoid_overcharging caps the AC power at what fills the battery and the minimum charging power stops it short of full. Probe 2026-10-13 (SG1 10 kWh / 5 kW, and S2, the one non-generic AC system bslib ships, 8.99 kWh / 3.57 kW; 60, 900 and 3600 s): charging at 1 MW from 0.5 for 2000 steps ends at 0.999848 / 0.997726 / 0.990890 (SG1) and 0.999930 / 0.998948 / 0.995805 (S2); start states from 0.98 to 1.0 offered -100 W to 20 kW, and a 20,000-step random walk, never set the flag. The DC-coupled S3, S4 and INV1 give NaN charging parameters and are refused at construction since branch review-guards. The Battery keeps reading the flag as the adapter's defensive half, and its docstrings now say that bslib sets it only above a state of charge of 1. Found in the evaluation of the review of #928 (M1).

title: The battery reads bslib's private attributes for its charging limits; bslib needs an accessor or the battery a model of its own
description:
Source: energy-manager loop design (2026-10-11), decision A; branch ems-battery-limits.

The Battery publishes its charging limits for the step (MaximumChargingPowerInWatt, MinimumChargingPowerInWatt). bslib
has no public accessor for the parameters behind them, so BslibChargingParameters reads the private attributes
`_E_BAT`, `_P_AC2BAT_IN`, `_P_AC2BAT_MIN`, `_SOC_THRESHOLD` and `_threshold` of ACBatMod. A bslib update that renames
them breaks the battery silently or loudly. The limits are also exact only for bslib's generic systems (no peripheral
consumption, no stationary deviation, no standby consumption); every system in the repository is SG1.

Options: (a) ask bslib upstream for a public method returning the AC charging range for a given state of charge and
step (HTW Berlin, github.com/...bslib); (b) replace bslib by a small battery model of HiSim's own (capacity, rated
power, minimum power, efficiency, recharge hysteresis as state), which also fixes the per-pass hysteresis bead;
(c) keep the adapter and pin the bslib version in requirements. Recommendation: (b) when the battery gets its L1
controller (hisim-component-physics-4g9.38), else (c) now.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-11: keep bslib; no model of HiSim's own is planned. bslib is already pinned exactly (requirements.txt: bslib==0.7), and BslibChargingParameters.of_battery is the one place that reads its private attributes, so a version bump must check them there.

title: The air-conditioned house forces 6.5 % of its minutes: the AC controller's modulation and the indoor temperature contract by only 0.55 per pass
description:
Source: energy-manager loop design (2026-10-11), finding 3 (scratchpad loop/accmp.py, acrun.py).

The air-conditioned house (system_setups/air_conditioned_house.py) has a slow loop: the AC controller modulates from
the indoor temperature, which the building computes from the same minute's cooling or heating power. The error
contracts by about 0.55 per pass with alternating sign and needs about 17 passes for the 1e-4 tolerance, so 6.5 % of
the minutes are forced, in the added order and in the kind order alike.

The prototype fix (declaring the modulation an accelerated output, which brought the two evaluation orders within
1e-8) is no longer available: the simulator's acceleration was removed on 2026-10-11 (branch
remove-fixed-point-acceleration). Fix at the cause instead: the controller decides its modulation on a value the
step's iteration does not move (the building's start-of-step indoor temperature, as the hot-water controllers decide
on the tank's start temperature), or the building and the AC solve their coupling within one component. Also remove
the controller's last_committed_state pass memory, which is state written in i_simulate (principle 5). Changes the
air-conditioned house's goldens.
close_reason: The cause is gone since #948 (0abf96e9): AirConditionerController decides on the state committed at the end of the previous step, so every pass of a step sends the same signal, and the pass memory last_committed_state no longer exists. Measured 2026-10-13 on branch review-guards (stacked on #931): air_conditioned_house, the golden's one_week_60s parameters (first week of 2021, 60 s), 10,080 steps, 0 forced (was 6.5 %), every step converges in 2 passes.

title: Add per-element U-value overrides for roof, wall and floor to the building config path
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 7; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C12, C13 and Q10

`BuildingConfig` has `window_u_value_in_watt_per_m2_per_kelvin` and `door_u_value_...` overrides
(and `hisim/components/building/information.py` honours a configured U-value per element through
`EnvelopeElement.configured_u_value_field`), but `ArcheTypeConfig` has no envelope fields and the
setups never set them. RenoVisor sends detailed envelope data (per-element construction /
insulation ids and expert U-value overrides); the translator can only express "how renovated is
it overall" via the TABULA refurbishment variant (.001/.002/.003), a three-step scale.

Suggested fix, incremental: (1) add optional per-element U-value overrides (roof, wall, floor,
window, door) to `ArcheTypeConfig` and pass them into `BuildingConfig` in the setups -- the
building component already supports window/door overrides, so extend it to roof/wall/floor;
(2) later, a derivation table (construction + insulation + added mm of material -> U-value) so
measures translate into concrete post-retrofit U-values.

Challenges Q10 settles the precedence: the inventory wins per element, TABULA otherwise, and the
report says which. C13 flags one thing to check while doing it: the floor's transmission factor
becomes a fixed 0.5 when a floor U-value is configured -- check that against a suspended floor
over a ventilated crawl space.

Testing: building-component test comparing heating demand with and without an override; setup
test that the override reaches `BuildingConfig`.
close_reason: Completed: the v2 translator writes facade, roof, floor, window and door U-values from the request into the Building config (hisim/renovisor/translate.py; tests/renovisor/test_translate.py::test_every_element_u_value_lands_on_the_building), merged as #778

title: Without the simulator's acceleration the gas twins force 52 and 62 steps a year at 900 s: a boiler charge's first passes start kilowatts away from a 1e-4 W tolerance
description:
Source: branch remove-fixed-point-acceleration (owner decision 2026-10-11: remove the simulator's acceleration).

Without the secant acceleration the gas twins force steps at 900 s: household_gas_building_sizer 0 -> 52 forced steps a
year (mean passes 5.014 -> 5.021), household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer 11 -> 62 (5.147 -> 5.153); the heat
pump + solar twin's mean passes rise 4.77 -> 5.08 (1540 -> 1740 forced). Measured on main 339ec168 (= #921), full year
2021, predefined occupancy.

Cause (trace of 40 forced gas steps, e.g. steps 215, 1694, 2136): no slow loop. In each forced step the boiler starts a
hot-water charge; on the first pass the tank sees no boiler heat, on the second 2.6 kW, then 7.0, 7.59, 7.686 kW, and
the residual contracts by 0.14-0.15 per pass (tank ThermalPowerFromHeatGenerator, ThermalEnergyFromHeatGenerator,
ThermalEnergyIncreaseInStorage). From 7.7 kW to the simulator's absolute 1e-4 tolerance takes ~10 contractions, so the
step needs 12-13 passes and is forced at pass 11, by then within about 1e-3 W of its fixed point. The forced result
differs from the converged one by less than 1e-3 W.

This is the tolerance, not a component: the 1e-4 tolerance is absolute and applies to watt and watt-hour outputs too
(hydronic coupling spec §6 already noted it). Options, owner decision because they change convergence rules for every
system: (a) accept the forced steps (their error is below 1e-3 W); (b) a relative tolerance for power and energy
outputs, e.g. 1e-8 of the value or 1e-4 absolute, whichever is larger; (c) raise the forced-convergence limit from 10 to
about 15 passes. Recommendation: (a) now, (b) when the forced-step counter (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28) is the gate.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-11: accepted. No slow loop: a boiler charge starts 7.7 kW from its final value and the error shrinks to a seventh per pass; the absolute 1e-4 W tolerance needs 12-13 passes, so the step is forced within about 1e-3 W of its end. A relative tolerance or more passes would change convergence for every system.

title: The energy manager cannot tell from its own port inputs that a step has no consistent raise decision; decide how the remaining forced steps are handled
description:
Source: energy-manager loop design (2026-10-11), decision B as redesigned by the owner on 2026-10-11 ("the energy
manager itself recognises from its own inputs that no consistent decision exists, then keeps the previous minute's
decision; no simulator part").

Finding: this cannot be decided from the energy manager's own inputs without a what-if quantity. In the steps that
cycle (M1 of the design), unraised the house exports a little (median 59 W: the battery full, at its limit or below its
~200 W minimum) and raised the heat pump draws 0.7-2.8 kW more. Within one pass the manager sees one of the two states:
the surplus with the raise it decided, the heat pump's draw under that raise, the battery's limits. To know that the
other decision would flip the sign it needs the heat pump's draw under the other set temperature: a what-if quantity of
another component (principle 2), which the owner rejected as option F. Recognising the flip from its own earlier pass
(it decided "on", saw a deficit, decided "off", saw a surplus) is pass memory written in i_simulate (principle 5).

Options:
(a) No B. Branches ems-battery-limits + ems-pv-surplus-only alone: heat-pump twin, full year 2021 at 60 s, 3469 forced
    steps (0.66 % of the minutes; 72060 with A alone, 89020 on the removal branch), 2134 at 900 s; with the warm start
    (#914 on top) 4390 at 60 s. Every year completes, the golden full-year pair included.
(b) The simulator detects a period-2 cycle on the outputs of the L2 controllers (by kind) and sets a hold signal the
    energy manager obeys (implemented and measured on 2026-10-11, then withdrawn by the owner): 23 forced steps at
    60 s, 1872 at 900 s on #921 with the acceleration still in place.
(c) A band sized by the heat pump's current electrical power (option E of the design, rejected before): keeps the
    previous decision while the surplus magnitude is below the heat pump's draw; from port quantities, but it also
    lags real decisions.
(d) The long-term design G: the energy manager sends a continuous incentive and the heat pump's L1 controller decides
    with its own setting power, so no on/off decision of the L2 controller has to be consistent.
Recommendation: (a) now, (d) as the planned design; (b) only if the forced steps must go before (d).
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-11: no B now. A (#928) and C (#929) stay; the remaining ~0.7 % forced minutes a year are accepted, every year completes. The long-term design, a continuous incentive turned into a setting by the heat pump's own controller, is the new feature bead under hisim-component-physics-4g9. C's comfort side effects are the new task bead.
notes: 2026-10-20 (owner, from the 4g9.28 verification): which half of the energy manager's raise 2-cycle a forced step freezes depends only on whether the simulator forces after 12 or 13 free passes. That alone moves the heat-pump twin's annual energies by up to 0.5 % at 900 s and 1 % at 60 s and its forced steps by 39 % at 60 s (3528 -> 2149). Accepted as the noise floor until design G removes the cycle; do not read such moves as physics changes.

title: A hot-water charge near the heating-rod switch creeps by milliwatts per pass until the simulator aborts: hplib's jump at COP 1 was interpolated into a 25 kW/K ramp
description:
Source: energy-manager loop design (2026-10-11), finding 1; #914's full year at 60 s aborting at step 2439 (CI bless run
38120592182 and locally).

A hot-water charge near the raised 70 °C target crept by milliwatts per pass and the simulator aborted after 100
passes: the heat pump's hot-water power rose 4,966 -> 7,550 W over 90 passes (mass flow 0.238 -> 0.361 kg/s, return
60.76 -> 60.89 °C, COP 1.009 -> 1.0007), every output with the same per-pass ratio 0.875. Seen on #914 at step 2439
(after the raise cycled for ten passes and forced convergence switched the simulator's acceleration off) and in two
prototype years of the energy-manager loop design (steps 507638 and 470001).

Cause: the pair heat pump <-> hot-water tank. hplib switches to its heating rod alone where its COP falls to 1, and its
thermal power jumps there (8 kW air-water machine at 0 °C outside: 4.8 kW at COP 1.003 below a return of 64.1 °C, the
rod's 8.1 kW above). The heat pump interpolated hplib linearly between 0.1 K grid points of the return, which turned
the jump into a ramp of about 25 kW/K; the tank's step mean answers a watt with about 3.5e-5 K at 60 s; the product is
the observed contraction of 0.875 per pass, so from a 2.6 kW error the loop needs about 130 passes.

Fix (branch dhw-charge-creep): between two grid points on either side of the switch the heat pump asks hplib at the
return itself, so the jump stays a jump; a higher return gives more heat and a higher tank return, and the iteration
settles on one side within a few passes. Verified: #914's head as it was (436f2139) with only this change completes
the golden pair household_heatpump_building_sizer:full_year_60s (python mode) instead of aborting at step 2439; on the
new chain (acceleration removed, A, C, fix) the heat-pump twin's year at 60 s takes 3461 forced steps instead of 3469.
close_reason: The heat pump asks hplib at the return itself where the 0.1 K grid interpolation would straddle the heating-rod switch (branch dhw-charge-creep); #914's full year at 60 s completes.

title: The energy manager offers the PV surplus to each flexible device in priority order and the device's L1 controller reports what it takes, instead of a hard set-temperature raise
description:
The energy manager decides its set-temperature raise as on/off from the PV surplus after the battery (#928, #929). In about 0.7 % of the minutes a year (3,469 at 60 s in the heat-pump twin, 4,359 with the warm start) no consistent decision exists. Without the raise the house exports a few watts, so the manager raises; with it the heat pump draws 0.7–2.8 kW more and the export disappears, so the manager drops it again. The simulator forces these steps.

Within the design principles the manager cannot hold its decision: it would need the heat pump's draw under the other set temperature (a what-if value from inside another component, principle 2) or a memory of its own earlier passes (principle 5). See hisim-component-physics-4g9.51, decided 2026-10-11: accept the forced steps now, and plan this design.

Design: the manager publishes a continuous incentive, the PV surplus it offers in W, instead of a hard raise. The heat pump's own L1 controller turns the offer into its setting, for example a set-temperature lift or a power that grows with the offer. A smooth signal has no knife edge to flip across, so the cycle disappears without any pass memory.

Done when the heat-pump twins converge without the energy manager's forced steps and the raise logic lives in the device's own controller.

Design confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-17 (offer-and-take cascade; replaces the continuous-incentive sketch above). The manager hands out the surplus in priority order. Each flexible participant is offered the surplus left BEFORE its own share: production minus uncontrolled consumption minus the takes of the participants ranked above, never a value that contains its own response. It reports what it takes (its draw covered by the offer), and the remainder is offered to the next participant. No offer depends on its receiver's decision, so the chain is feed-forward and settles in about N + 1 passes for N participants; the manager itself makes no on/off decision. One offer per device: a heat pump with space-heating and hot-water circuits (today ranks 2 and 3 of one compressor) gets one offer and splits it internally. Each flexible participant has an L1 controller that turns its offer into its operation (hisim-component-physics-4g9.38): the heat pump lifts its set temperature on a reference that does not move with that decision (a configured power such as its rated electrical power in lifted operation, or the offer minus its base draw taken from its saved start-of-step state), with hysteresis or minimum run times between steps; the battery gets a charge controller that takes the remainder or covers the deficit; the car stays as today. The building gets no modifier from the manager; a lift of the room set temperature, if kept, comes from the heat pump's or the heating curve's controller. Bookkeeping falls out: each participant's grid draw is its draw minus its take, so the consumers' pseudo-dispatch outputs go. Holding under force_convergence (2026-10-17) stays as a backstop for loops inside a device's own physics. Changes goldens.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-14, #941 (the differential solar controller), traced in household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer at 60 s, full year 2021, predefined occupancy: steps needing 12 or more passes rose from 211 (old head c146a57a) to 371; 110 are common, 101 only old, 261 only new. In every flagged step of both heads the outputs still changing in the last four passes belong to the ElectricityMeter, this manager, the battery, the heat pump and its space-heating controller, the building and the buffer; no output of the solar collector, its controller or the hot-water tank changes after the third pass in any of them. The passes alternate between the raise on (DomesticHotWaterStorageTemperatureModifier and SpaceHeatingWaterStorageTemperatureModifier 10 K, heat pump drawing 950 to 2380 W, grid +1 to +16 W) and off (0 K, heat pump 0 W, grid -16 to -39 W, the PV surplus) until the forced pass, e.g. steps 5014 (4 Jan 11:34), 127133 (30 Mar 06:53), 245072 (20 Jun 04:32) and 408415 (11 Oct 14:55). The new collector delivers 13 % more heat and its pump runs 1022 instead of 626 hours, which moves the tank, battery and heat pump onto other minutes of this knife edge; the cycle itself is this bead's.

title: Check why the unraised heat-pump house falls below its room set point and misses hot water more often since only PV surplus keeps the raise
description:
Since only PV surplus keeps the energy manager's set-temperature raise (#929, decision C of hisim-component-physics-4g9.51), a battery no longer discharges to keep the house pre-heated. The raise share falls from 38.8 % to 31.7 % of the year and grid import by about 7 %. Two side effects (heat-pump twin, measured 2026-10-11):

- unmet hot water rises from about 2.3 to 4.6 kWh a year (out of about 3,000 kWh tapped);
- in the one-week golden runs the hours below the 20 °C room set point rise by up to 114 %, worst case 10.5 K·h a week.

Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-11 to be checked later: are the normal set points, the hot-water set temperature or the heating curve set so that the unraised house is comfortable on its own? The raise was meant to store PV surplus as heat, not to cover a comfort gap.

Done when the cause of the under-temperature hours is known and either fixed or recorded as intended.

title: The simulator forces a step when its iteration stops making progress, not after a fixed ten passes
description:
The simulator forces a step after a fixed pass count (`iterative_tries > 10` in `Simulator`, unchanged since the 2021 release). That count cannot tell a slow but converging loop from a cycle.

Measured 2026-10-11 (full year 2021, predefined occupancy; the unmerged diff is kept at scratchpad passlimit_year/limit20.diff of that session):

| twin | step | limit 10 | limit 20 | limit 15 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| heat pump | 60 s | 89,020 forced / 6.16 passes / 365 s | 89,614 / 7.88 / 451 s (+24 %) | aborted at step 505,182 |
| heat pump | 900 s | 8,677 / 7.53 / 34 s | 7,989 / 9.72 / 43 s (+24 %) | 5,302 / 7.18 / 32 s |
| gas | 900 s | 52 | 0 | 1 |
| gas + solar | 900 s | 62 | 11 | 13 |

- Boiler hot-water charges contract by about 1/7 per pass from kilowatts to the 1e-4 tolerance; they need 13 passes and are forced at 10 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.50).
- The heat pump's forced steps are cycles; a higher count only runs them longer.
- A different count leads the heat-pump twins to different states: at 20 the heat pump + car week moves its car grid electricity 14.4 → 6.1 kWh (−58 %), and 15 aborts the 60 s year. Those results depend strongly on where forcing starts (see hisim-component-physics-4g9.28, hisim-component-physics-4g9.53).

Owner decision 2026-10-11: keep 10 for now. Design, once the heat-pump cycles are reduced (energy manager hisim-component-physics-4g9.53; the evaluation order in #922): force a step when the change between passes stops shrinking (for example the largest output change does not fall below a set fraction of the one before over two passes), with a hard cap. The simulator still never alters or holds an output; it only decides when to stop. Expected: the boilers converge, cycles are forced as early as today or earlier.

Done when the rule is measured on the heat-pump, gas and solar twins (forced steps, mean passes, wall time, goldens) and the owner has decided.


Owner, 2026-10-17: no progress-based abort or force rule that tracks residuals per pass. `is_close_enough_to_previous` already dominates runtime, so any per-pass bookkeeping costs every pass of every run for a benefit in rare steps. The pass limit instead scales with the step length (100 passes per 60 s, at least 100), computed once per run (PR pass-limit-scales-with-step).

title: The heat-pump-and-car setup aborts a full year at 60 s with More than 100 tries: the hot-water heat pump and the battery's charging power drift together without converging
description:
Source: golden-full-year-all (every energy system gets a full-year golden, owner decision 2026-10-11), local full-year runs of household_heatpump_car_building_sizer through scripts/golden_update.py --setup household_heatpump_car_building_sizer --param full_year_60s.

The setup cannot complete the year 2021 at 60 s, so it is the one setup without a full-year golden (it keeps its week golden; golden_config.json restricts it to the week until this is fixed).

- On main 6c95e544: aborts at time step 470159 (2021-11-23 11:59) with 'More than 100 tries'. The changed values move by about 1 W per pass in one direction (a slow drift, not a 2-cycle): MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib ElectricalInputPowerDHW 5276.46 -> 5277.62 W, L2EMSElectricityController ChargingPowerForBattery_6 -3607.78 -> -3608.94 W, ElectricityMeter ElectricityFromGridInWatt 3606.57 -> 3607.78 W, DHWStorage ThermalPowerFromHeatGenerator 5300.37 -> 5301.53 W.
- On ems-battery-limits 54a76341 (PR #928, the battery publishes its charging limits): aborts earlier, at time step 41609 (2021-01-29 21:29), same family: heat pump in hot-water mode at about 7083 W, Battery AcBatteryPowerUsed -7559.90 -> -7560.15 W, ChargingPowerForBattery_6 -7560.15 -> -7560.37 W, grid about 0.25 W.
The week golden (first week of January) never reaches either step. The energy manager hands the battery the residual the heat pump leaves and the heat pump's DHW power follows the grid balance, so each pass moves both by the same small amount; force_convergence does not stop it before the 100-pass limit.

Done when: the full year at 60 s completes, and the setup's 'horizons' restriction leaves scripts/golden_config.json together with the setup's name in tests/test_golden_matrix.py (the full-year golden then comes from the next bless). Related: hisim-component-physics-4g9.38 (the energy manager's L2 role), hisim-component-physics-4g9.55 (forcing a step that stops making progress).
close_reason: The heat pump + car setup cannot finish a year on main (aborts 23 November, more than 100 tries) and on #928 alone (aborts 29 January): the heat pump's hot-water power and the battery's charging share drift together by about 1 W per pass. From #929 (only PV surplus keeps a raise) on, the year completes: 530 s on #929, 420 s on the stack top (measured 2026-10-11). #928 and #929 are merged together; the car setup gets its full-year golden in #943.

title: The air conditioner's controller cannot hold its set points: a 5 K band with power scaled to its far edge keeps it running for days, and its mode depends on the previous pass
description:
Source: #914's full-year bless (golden-update run 38167674763, bless PR #946, 2026-10-11), local full-year runs of system_setups/air_conditioned_house.py at 60 s.

With the warm start (#914) the air-conditioned house's full year goes from 311 to 2615 h below 20 °C and from 251 to 2924 h above 24 °C; the unit's electricity rises from 7068 to 9185 kWh. The controller (AirConditionerController, preset_standard) keeps heating up to 20 + 5 = 25 °C and cooling down to 24 - 5 = 19 °C once started, and scales its power by the distance to that far edge, so the power fades just before the edge and the unit never stops: the house sits near 19 °C all summer and near 26 °C in March and December. The cold start before #914 hid it. A 1 K band alone stops the sticking but the unit then droops (winter near 18 °C, summer peaks at 28 °C), because the power scales with the distance from the set point it holds.

The house also barely converges: 8.5 passes per step on average before #914, 11.6 with it, 13.7 with a 1 K band (limit 10, so most steps are forced). last_committed_state is overwritten on every pass and never restored, so the controller's decision depends on the previous pass, not only on the previous step.

Owner decision 2026-10-12: fix the controller in a small PR between #930 and #914 (hold the set points, 1 K hysteresis, keep the minimum on/off times, decision depends on the previous step only); #914 is re-blessed on top of it.
close_reason: The controller samples the indoor air once per step and decides on the state committed at the end of the previous step (no pass memory); it holds 20 degC heating / 24 degC cooling by ramping its power with the distance from the held set point (1800 s to full power per K; owner accepted 2026-10-12), 1 K hysteresis, 30/15 min minimum times kept, stops only from its 10 % minimum power (soft stop) and ramps at most 450 s per step (both amended in after the sizing fix #950, owner decision 2026-10-12). Branch ac-controller-setpoint on #950 (unit sized to 0.8 of the heating load), air_conditioned_house full year 2021: at 60 s 76.7 K*h below 20 degC and 68.4 K*h above 24 degC (0 % / 10 % of it at full power), min/max room 17.7 / 25.3 degC, AC electricity 5304 kWh, grid 5327 kWh, 2.83 passes per step cold and 2.68 warm, 0 forced steps, 96/127 heating/cooling starts; cold and warm start identical. At 900 s 122.9/105.7 K*h, 49/76 starts; at 3600 s 316.8/293.2 K*h, 39/72 starts; 0 forced at every resolution. Old controller on the same sizing: 444/1 K*h, 6537 kWh, 10.4 passes, 70 % forced; before the sizing fix, old controller cold 311/251 K*h, 7068 kWh, 7.9 passes, 44 % forced, and warm (#914) 2615/2925 K*h, 9185 kWh, 10.5 passes, 67 % forced.

title: The simple air conditioner's controller switches within a step on the same step's temperature, so about 1 % of its steps are forced and the warm start shifts its year
description:
Source: the measurements for #948 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.57, 2026-10-12), system_setups/simple_air_conditioner_household_building_sizer.py, full year 2021 at 60 s.

SimpleAirConditionerController decides on and off within a step on the indoor air temperature of the same step. The building's air node answers the unit's power within that step, so the decision can flip between passes: 5,537 forced steps a year with a cold start, 3,302 with #914's warm start, and the warm start moves the year from 10.5 to 6.0 kWh and from 0 to 12.5 K·h above 25 °C.

Owner decision 2026-10-12: bead it, fix later. The fix is the one #948 gave AirConditionerController: sample the indoor air temperature once per step and decide each step on the state committed at the end of the previous step, so every pass sends the same signal.

title: The air conditioner sized to a building picks the catalogue unit nearest the full heating load, then runs 0.8 of it, so its price is that of a larger unit
description:
Source: the sizing fix of hisim-h84t (branch ac-sizing, 2026-10-12), system_setups/air_conditioned_house.py.

AirConditionerConfig.for_building_load selects the catalogue unit whose heating capacity is nearest the design heating load and scales it to CAPACITY_SHARE_FOR_BUILDING_LOAD (0.8) of that load. The investment cost is the selected unit's price, so it belongs to a unit nearer the full load than the one simulated: in the air-conditioned house the Panasonic (4,899 €) is chosen; the unit nearest 0.8 × load would be the Mitsubishi (4,528 €) at a scale factor of about 1.05. Selecting the unit nearest share × load makes the investment cost follow the simulated size.

Owner decision 2026-10-12: bead it, keep the sizing PR to the corrected law.

title: Make ventilation and airtightness configurable (n50 and heat recovery)
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 8; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C15 (M3) and Q15

`hisim/components/building/` handles infiltration and ventilation internally; the setups only set
`enable_opening_windows = True`. RenoVisor's `air_sealing` measure (target n50 air-change rate)
and `ventilation` measure (MVHR with 75-92 % heat recovery) have no counterpart, so deep-retrofit
packages are under-represented (only via the TABULA variant bump).

Suggested fix: expose an infiltration rate (n50 or air changes per hour) on
`BuildingConfig`/`ArcheTypeConfig`, and add a mechanical-ventilation-with-heat-recovery option
(effective ventilation heat loss reduced by the recovery efficiency).

Challenges Q15 decided the three optional `BuildingConfig` fields (infiltration, shading, air
change / heat recovery) are not built for the MVP; `OUTSIDE_SHADING`,
`SHALLOW_AIR_TIGHTNESS_MEASURES`, `DIY_SEALING_OF_AIR_LEAKS` and `VENTILATION_SYSTEM` stay
`NoEffect` and are reported. This issue is the post-MVP work that closes them.

Testing: heating demand decreases monotonically with lower n50 and with higher heat-recovery
efficiency; the energy balance stays closed (`i_doublecheck`).

title: A TwoPointSwitch helper holds the two-point hysteresis that about nine L1 controllers copy, as a part each controller holds, not a base class
description:
Source: the kind base classes (branch kind-classes, replacing #922; owner decision 2026-10-12: shared controller behaviour is a helper part held by the controllers that need it, not inherited from L1ControllerComponent).

About nine L1 controllers implement the same two-point switch on their own: on below a lower threshold, off above an upper one, the previous state kept in between, saved in i_save_state and restored in i_restore_state. On main: AirConditionerController (air_conditioner.py, hysteresis_in_kelvin), SimpleAirConditionerController (simple_air_conditioner.py), GenericHeatPumpController (generic_heat_pump.py), MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating and MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py, next_state), GenericBoilerController, DistrictHeatingController and ElectricHeatingController (hysteresis_water_temperature_offset, partly through DiverterValve in dual_circuit_system.py), and the example SimpleController (controller_l1_example_controller.py). The solar controller gets one with #941 in the part-load stack. Each copy names its thresholds, its committed state and its save/restore differently, and the bugs found so far were in that copied state handling (pass memory instead of step memory, hisim-component-physics-4g9.57).

Wanted: one small class, TwoPointSwitch, with switch-on and switch-off thresholds in the unit of the quantity it watches (e.g. temperature_in_celsius), its committed state, and save/restore methods the controller calls from its own i_save_state / i_restore_state. A controller holds one instance per switched service (composition); L1ControllerComponent stays without state. Pure and table-tested on its own.

Done when the controllers above use it, their tests and the golden references are unchanged (or the differences are explained), and the copies are gone.

title: A RunTimeGuard helper holds the minimum run and idle times that the hplib heat pump, the air conditioner and other controllers count on their own
description:
Source: the kind base classes (branch kind-classes, replacing #922; owner decision 2026-10-12: shared controller behaviour is a helper part held by the components that need it, not inherited).

Minimum run and idle times are counted separately in several classes, each with its own timers and units: the hplib heat pump (MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib with HeatPumpRunTimers, minimum_running_time_in_seconds / minimum_idle_time_in_seconds in on_off_after_minimum_times, which also keep a hot-water run (signal 2) going after the hot-water controller asks to stop), the air conditioner's controller (AirConditionerController, activation_time_step / deactivation_time_step against minimum_runtime_s / minimum_idle_time_s), the boiler controller (GenericBoilerController.enforce_minimum_run_and_idle_times), the CHP controller (L1CHPController) and the generic heat pump. Per system_docs/component_design_principles.md §A, minimum run and idle times protect the device, so the device enforces them, and a controller may hold stricter times of its own.

Wanted: one small class, RunTimeGuard, with minimum_run_time_in_seconds and minimum_idle_time_in_seconds, the step at which the device last switched, and two questions (may it stop, may it start at this step), with save/restore methods its holder calls. Held by the physics component for device protection and, where a controller has stricter times, by the controller; neither kind base class gets state. Pure and table-tested on its own.

Done when the classes above use it, their tests and the golden references are unchanged (or the differences are explained), and the separate counters are gone.

title: The electric car's charge controller has no consistent decision in a step: it decides on the state of charge its own charging produces and charges with the surplus left after itself, so forced convergence and the evaluation order pick its result
description:
Source: trace of #922's golden move (2026-10-12, /home/noah/hisim/loop-design/trace_922_heatpump_car.md), household_heatpump_car_building_sizer at 60 s, main 737f7801 against #922 e009a45e.

Three defects in controller_l1_generic_ev_charge.L1Controller (line numbers of 737f7801):
1. The 0.4 set-point rule (:371-372) reads CarBattery.StateOfCharge (:436), which the battery writes after this step's charge (advanced_ev_battery_bslib.py:290). In the step where one minute of charging crosses 0.4 no consistent answer exists: charging lifts it above 0.4, which stops the charging, which leaves it below 0.4.
2. The energy manager sends the car the surplus left after the car's own charging (controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:781-808, consumer branch), and the controller charges with it as if it were the surplus offered to it (:376-381). The iteration c <- S - c has slope -1 and never converges.
3. Under force_convergence the controller replays processed_state (:431-432), written inside i_simulate (:447): design principle 5. The result of a forced step is the phase pass 12 happened to hit, and the evaluation order sets that phase.

Effect, one_week_60s: 332 forced steps on main, 1,157 on #922 (EV cycle 299 / 1,121). First material divergence at step 1201 (1 Jan 20:01): command 11,000 W on main, 0 W on #922; on #922 the car then sits parked below its set point for 12.6 h. Car grid electricity 16.04 (main) against 3.40 kWh (#922), house battery charging 38.1 against 23.9 kWh. full_year_60s: 36,770 forced steps on main, 99,288 (18.9 % of the minutes) on #922; car grid 310.8 against 317.7 kWh. A patch of both decisions (start-of-step state of charge, the offered surplus) made the two orders agree within 0.02 % on the car.

Owner decision 2026-10-12: fix it in its own small PR under #922; the energy manager sends the car the offered surplus, as it does for the house battery, and the car's grid KPI books realized draw minus offer.
close_reason: Branch ev-charge-offer (under #922). CarBattery publishes StateOfChargeAtStartOfStep and the controller decides its set-point rule on it; the energy manager sends the car the surplus offered to it and books the car's grid electricity as max(0, realized draw - max(0, offer)); the controller keeps no state and has no forced-convergence replay. one_week_60s, setup order / #922 order: car charged 23.00 / 22.97 kWh, car grid 3.50 / 3.50 kWh, house battery charged 19.41 / 19.39 kWh, grid import 214.28 / 214.15 kWh, forced steps 96 / 75 (before 332 / 1,157), none of them a car-only cycle; the orders first differ at step 2093, where #922's order lets a transient set-temperature raise latch a hot-water charge (hisim-component-physics-4g9.24, hisim-component-physics-4g9.53). full_year_60s: forced steps 7,299 / 8,334 (before 36,770 / 99,288), car grid 150.7 / 151.3 kWh (before 310.8 / 317.7), grid import 2,081.6 / 2,082.7 kWh, below 20 degC 157.6 / 159.5 K*h (before 158.2 / 180.4). The heat pump house without a car is unchanged (full_year_60s KPIs identical to main's golden). Unit tests: the crossing step has one answer and converges unforced in both orders; the offer and the car grid KPI arithmetic.

title: The pellet and wood-chip boiler twins book 51.7 MWh of space-heating heat a year for 11.0 MWh delivered to the building, with a mean space-heating mass flow of about 958 kg/s
description:
Source: the part-load measurement of 2026-10-12 (scripts and results in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-noah-hisim-HiSim/cf9e9bc6-6afe-4da8-812d-f80aeff8be7b/scratchpad/plmeasure/, summary s11.md item 7), household_pellets_building_sizer and household_wood_chips_building_sizer twins, full_year at 60 s.
