The boilers book 51.7 MWh of space-heating heat a year while the heat distribution delivers 11.0 MWh to the building, and the mean space-heating mass flow is about 958 kg/s, which no single-family heating circuit carries. Measured on main and on #922 alike, so it is not an effect of the evaluation order or of part load. Fuel demand, costs and emissions of these twins follow the booked heat, so live results are wrong.

Done when the boilers' space-heating heat closes against the heat delivered plus the buffer's losses and change of content (within the tolerance of hisim-hydronics-fxix.5's buffer balance) and the mass flow is a physical circuit flow, at 60 s, with a test that fails on the old booking.
close_reason: The boiler's pump has a largest flow (GenericBoilerConfig.minimal_lift_at_maximal_power_in_kelvin, 5 K; branch boiler-pellet-booking): a lift below the rise the commanded heat gives at that flow is raised to it. Cause: GenericBoiler.fired_circuit sized the flow to the controller's lift, m = P_th / (c lift), and the on/off controller asks for full power on a lift of a few mK while the buffer sits at its set temperature; the buffer's mixing law took in only M / (M + m dt) of that heat. Year 2021 at 60 s, before -> after: pellets booked 51683.8 -> 11838.7 kWh for 11016.4 kWh delivered, mean SH flow 958.6 -> 0.065 kg/s (max 225722 -> 0.369), SH fuel 57426.5 -> 13154.1 kWh; wood chips 51557.2 -> 11791.2 kWh for 11012.3 kWh, 1026.1 -> 0.064 kg/s, fuel 57285.8 -> 13101.3 kWh; gas twin bit-identical (128 of 128 columns). Booked against delivered + buffer loss + content change: pellets +4.62 %, wood chips +3.81 %, gas +0.87 %; the rest is the buffer's mixing law, closed per step by hydronic stage D (hisim-hydronics-fxix.5). basic_household_only_heating (12 kW, 1 kW minimum) also moves: booked 49624.8 -> 48915.9 kWh, max flow 725 -> 0.52 kg/s.

title: Review every storage's starting value and start it at about 50 % of full charge, so runs do not begin with empty or full storages
notes:
Branch storage-start-half (stacked on #988), 2026-10-14: every storage states one start value as a class constant and the state classes lost their contradicting defaults. Half charged: DHW tank 60 -> 35 °C (half way from the 10 °C mains to the 60 °C aim), hydrogen tank 400 kg (config field starting_fill, removed) -> 250 kg = INITIAL_FILL_FRACTION 0.5 of min..max, example storage 0 -> 25 kWh, car battery 0.5 (unchanged, dataclass default 0 removed). Owner decision open on two, each stated once at its old value: (1) space-heating buffer 35 °C (dataclass default 25 removed) -- its half-charged value depends on the emitter (floor 28-35 °C -> 31.5, LT radiator 45-55 -> 50, radiator 55-70 -> 62.5), which the buffer does not know; options: a sized field from Size.HEAT_DISTRIBUTION_SYSTEM_TYPE, one constant for the fleet-default floor heating (31.5), or keep 35. (2) house battery SOC 0: a 0.5 start makes the "Battery losses" KPI (charged - discharged, ignoring stored energy at start and end) negative and the self-sufficiency check refuses the storage/battery assembly runs; fix that KPI first (subtract the stored-energy change), then start at 0.5. Measured: the one-week goldens of the 13 setups with a DHW tank move by the tank's +7.2 kWh recharge; year totals +7-8 kWh (0.04-0.05 % of gas). Close when the two decisions land.

Owner decisions 2026-10-15: buffer keeps 35 °C; the Battery losses KPI is fixed first (branch battery-losses-kpi), then the house battery starts at 0.5; the DHW tank starts at 50 °C, half its usable charge between the 40 °C tap temperature and the 60 °C aim.
close_reason: Branch storage-start-half (on battery-losses-kpi): every storage states one start value as a class constant, state-class defaults removed. House battery and car battery SOC 0.5, hydrogen tank 250 kg of 500 (starting_fill removed), DHW tank 50 °C, example storage 25 of 50 kWh, buffer 35 °C (owner decision). Tests pin every value.

title: The car battery's losses KPI ignores the stored energy, as the house battery's Battery losses KPI did
description: Found 2026-10-15 while fixing the KPI "Battery losses" (branch battery-losses-kpi). CarBattery.get_component_kpi_entries reports "Total losses of car battery" as charged minus discharged energy, and get_cost_opex books the same figure as consumption, without the change of the stored energy. The car battery starts at a state of charge of 0.5, so a car that ends the run fuller than it started reports the energy it holds as lost. First check what AcBatteryDischargingPower covers (driving energy as well, or only discharge to the house), then subtract the stored-energy increase as the house battery now does (KpiHelperClass.compute_storage_losses_in_kilowatt_hour). Done when: the car battery's losses subtract the stored-energy change, with a test that fails on the old formula.

title: Boiler efficiency rises with burner power (0.60 at minimum to 0.90 at maximum), so a condensing gas boiler runs at 0.73 in space heating: replace the law with a sourced part-load curve
description:
Source: hydronic stage D part-load probe (2026-10-15) and the research of 2026-10-15. Owner (Noah, 2026-10-15): P1, parked until the open PR stack is merged; the efficiency curve is not changed before then. A draft spec with every source is kept outside the repository (loop-design/boiler_part_load_efficiency_spec_draft_2026-10-15.md, and the local branch boiler-part-load-efficiency, commit ccc63799).

GenericBoiler's combustion efficiency rises linearly with burner power from eff_th_min 0.60 to eff_th_max 0.90 (BurnerModulation.efficiency_at), so a condensing gas boiler runs at 0.73 in space heating (gas twin, 60 s golden) where datasheets give 0.95-0.98 (GCV), and firing a fraction of a step at full power burns 9-19 % less gas than modulating (stage D probe). The spec proposes a sourced curve per type: two test points (100 % and 30 % load; Ecodesign 813/2013 and 2015/1189, EN 303-5, IWU 2002, datasheets of Viessmann Vitodens 200-W, Froeling PE1 Pellet, Hargassner Eco-HK) plus a return-temperature gain of 0.30 points per kelvin for condensing boilers (BRE SAP S10TP-12). It needs the owner before any PR because RenoVisor's stated seasonal efficiency maps onto eff_th_max/eff_th_min by a rule the shared contract states (calculation-request.md section 3.6). Q1: replace both fields by one optional seasonal_efficiency that scales the curve to 0.85 eta_30 + 0.15 eta_100 (recommended; closes hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.29), keep both with a new meaning, keep the old law as an override (not recommended), or list the stated value as not_implemented_yet meanwhile. Q2: the calorific basis of the frontend's figure (the draft recommends NCV, converted for condensing boilers; the coordinator's view: GCV, because the energy-label seasonal efficiency and the 0.85/0.15 weighting are defined on GCV; or ask the contract owner). Q3: hydrogen has no published curve (recommended: the gas row as a stated estimate). Q4: the oil default, 1990s low-temperature boiler (recommended) or an installation-year row. Expected effect (estimated from the 60 s goldens, not run): gas and oil fuel about -20 %, pellets and wood chips a few percent lower; every boiler golden and every RenoVisor boiler result moves (heads-up needed). Test points proposed: condensing gas (GCV) 0.877 at 100 % / 0.978 at 30 %; oil (NCV) 0.932 / 0.920; pellets (NCV) 0.947 / 0.911; wood chips (NCV) 0.939 / 0.914; hydrogen as gas (estimate).

Done when: the owner has decided Q1-Q4 in the spec, the law is implemented with tests that fail on the old law, the five twins are measured at 60 s and 900 s, and the boiler goldens are blessed.
notes:
Owner decisions 2026-10-20 (supersede Q1-Q4 of the description):
- Q1: the optional seasonal efficiency is used exactly to scale the curve: the stated value is the Ecodesign seasonal space heating efficiency eta_s of the energy label (Regulation (EU) 813/2013 for gas/oil, 2015/1189 for solid fuel; GCV, with the corrections the regulations subtract), and the curve is scaled so that 0.85 eta_30 + 0.15 eta_100 minus those corrections reproduces it. The two fields eff_th_max / eff_th_min go. The shared contract (renovisorissues specs/calculation-request.md section 3.6) still maps the value to eff_th_max = value/100; that row must change on renovisorissues before the PR merges (draft the change; post only with the owner's go).
- Q2 follows from Q1: the stated value is on the gross calorific value (the label's basis).
- Curve shape (replaces the single-product datasheets of the draft for gas and oil): IWU, Diefenbach, Loga, Born, Grossklos, Herbert (2002), 'Energetische Kenngroessen fuer Heizungsanlagen im Bestand', Tab. 2 (eta_k,70 at 70 C, 20 kW) and Tab. 3 (eta_30% at the type's mean boiler temperature, 20 kW), NCV, means of the Stiftung Warentest series and field data, by type (gas/oil condensing, low-temperature, standard, solid fuel) and decade (70s/80s/90s), with the size law eta = eta_20kW - 0.0195 + 0.015 lg Pn (eq. 2-1) and the standby loss q_B,70 (eq. 2-2). https://www.iwu.de/fileadmin/publikationen/energie/werkzeuge/2002_IWU_DiefenbachEtAl_Energetische-Kenngr%C3%B6%C3%9Fen-f%C3%BCr-Heizungsanlagen-im_Bestand.pdf
- Q4: the decade row follows the request's installation_year when given; the 1990s row is the default for an existing boiler.
- Q3: hydrogen uses the gas condensing row, as a stated estimate (no published curve).
- Pellets and wood chips keep the draft's EN 303-5 / 2015/1189 datasheet points (Froeling PE1, Hargassner Eco-HK), since IWU's solid-fuel row describes 1990s log boilers.
- Legal floor as a test: Council Directive 92/42/EEC Art. 5 (NCV, Pn in kW): standard >= 84 + 2 log Pn at full load / >= 80 + 3 log Pn at 30 %; low-temperature >= 87.5 + 1.5 log Pn / >= 87.5 + 1.5 log Pn; gas condensing >= 91 + log Pn / >= 97 + log Pn (30 C supply).
- Condensing return-temperature gain stays as drafted (BRE SAP 10 S10TP-12).

Owner decisions 2026-10-20 (answers to the questions the implementation raised; C supersedes the 1990s default of Q4):
- A: the 92/42 floor test checks only the 1990s rows (and current products), with a stated tolerance of 0.005 (IWU prints two decimals; 92/42 Art. 5(2) demands appropriate tolerances). Source values stay untouched.
- B: scaling to a stated eta_s adds back only F(1) = 3 points; F(2)-F(4) are left out because HiSim models none of those losses; the resulting bias is stated in the spec.
- C: a boiler with no installation year, or one from 2000 on, uses current Ecodesign datasheet values (Vitodens for condensing gas, the same row on the GCV for hydrogen; a condensing-oil and a low-temperature datasheet sourced the same way). IWU's decade rows apply only to a stated installation year before 2000.
close_reason: Implemented on branch boiler-part-load-efficiency-curve (spec roadmap/boiler_part_load_efficiency_spec.md): one optional seasonal_efficiency (Ecodesign eta_s, GCV) and an optional installation_year replace eff_th_min/eff_th_max; the curve per type and vintage comes from IWU 2002 Tab. 2/3 with eq. 2-1 (before 2000) or current product data (Vitodens 200-W, Logano plus GB125-22, Logano G125-21, Froeling PE1, Hargassner Eco-HK), with the BRE condensing gain. Measured, full year 2021: gas and hydrogen fuel -20.3 % at 60 s and -12.8 % at 900 s (space heating 0.728 -> 0.977 at 60 s), oil -20.0 % / -11.8 %, pellets -4.8 % / -4.9 %, wood chips -4.3 % / -4.1 %; the 900 s against 60 s fuel gap of gas went from -8.0 % to +0.8 %. One RenoVisor request (condensing gas, 90 % stated): gas -9.5 %. tests/test_generic_boiler.py::test_a_condensing_gas_boiler_burns_at_its_ecodesign_test_points_not_on_the_old_linear_law fails on main (0.667 instead of 0.978). The boiler goldens are re-blessed by the coordinator.

title: Two outputs declare a unit that does not match their values: DHWStorage StandbyTemperatureLoss is a temperature drop in °C (should be K), Building OpenWindow is a 0/1 state in timesteps (should be binary)
description: Found by the time-series chart review (2026-10-15). The charts label their axes from the declared unit (Temperature [°C], Timesteps [timesteps]), so the wrong unit reaches every plot, the CSV headers and the report. StandbyTemperatureLoss values are 0.01-0.036, a difference; OpenWindow values are 0 or 1. Check the other outputs of both classes for the same mix-up.

title: Investigate whether the boiler controller's minimum run and idle times should be fixed or deleted: they never act after the first steps, and the boiler's BurnerTimes already protect the burner
description:
Found 2026-10-23 while reviewing #1100. GenericBoilerController.enforce_minimum_run_and_idle_times (hisim/components/generic_boiler.py) keeps the start-of-step mode while self.state.activation_time_step + minimum_runtime_in_timesteps > timestep (minimum run time) and forces OFF while self.state.deactivation_time_step + minimum_resting_time_in_timesteps > timestep (minimum idle time). Nothing in the controller ever calls self.state.activate() or self.state.deactivate() (GenericBoilerControllerState), so both time steps stay 0 and the minimum run and idle times act only in the first minimum_runtime / minimum_resting_time steps of a simulation, never afterwards. Every boiler twin that sets minimum run or idle times runs without them. Fix: record the switch-on and switch-off steps when the committed mode changes (in a way that keeps the save/restore contract: the record is state, saved in i_save_state and restored in i_restore_state), then measure the boiler twins at 60 / 900 s (cycles, gas, comfort) and re-bless. Compare with BurnerTimes in the boiler itself (pellets/wood chips minimum firing time and pause), which works and may make the controller's times redundant for some fuels: decide which of the two owns short-cycling protection.

Update 2026-10-25 (owner, Noah): P2, investigate whether to fix or delete. Found again while prototyping the explicit controller state (#1142), which keeps the bug unchanged. What is known: (a) the boiler itself keeps a minimum firing time and pause per fuel (BurnerTimes, hisim-75mt: pellets 30/15 min, wood chips 60/30 min, gas/oil/hydrogen none), committed per step, and that works; (b) the controller's GenericBoilerControllerConfig.minimum_runtime_in_seconds / minimum_resting_time_in_seconds default to 1800 s, which the modulating preset (gas, oil) keeps, while preset_on_off sets both to 0 although its docstring says the minimum times are what makes a switching burner tolerable; (c) the owner decided on 2026-10-10 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.40) that minimum run and idle times are device protection that belongs in the device, not the controller. Fixing the controller's times would give every modulating gas and oil boiler 30-minute minimum on and off times on the controller's mode, a large behaviour change nobody chose; deleting them changes no golden after the first minimum period of a run (the start-up lockout of hisim-component-physics-4g9.17 point 2 would go with them). Wanted: measure both on the gas, oil, pellet and wood-chip twins (60 s and 900 s: starts per day, fuel, comfort, forced steps), check every twin and preset that sets the fields, and give the owner the comparison; the likely outcome is deleting the controller's fields, activate()/deactivate() and enforce_minimum_run_and_idle_times. This bead now also holds the remaining part of hisim-component-physics-4g9.40, closed as its duplicate.

title: electrolyzer_with_renewables: the transformer delivers 95 % of all wind power regardless of its 1 MW rating, and the 46 % the electrolyzer cannot take vanishes
description:
Found 2026-10-24 while checking #1096 (owner asked why electrolyzer_with_renewables reports 168,588 kWh for the July week). The setup: a wind CSV in kW (hisim/inputs/wind_generated_power_1_min.csv, peak 5,000 kW, mean 1,238 kW, about 10.8 GWh/yr: a 5 MW turbine) feeds a StandardTransformerAndRectifier (95 %, rated in the setup to the electrolyzer's max load, 1,028 kW) which feeds an H-TEC ME450 PEM electrolyzer (nominal 987 kW, max 1,028 kW, 4.7 kWh/Nm3).

Defects:
1. The transformer ignores its rating: Transformer.i_simulate is output = input * efficiency (transformer_rectifier.py:201-206); rated_power_in_kilowatt only scales its investment cost. At the turbine's peak it 'delivers' 4,750 kW through a 1 MW unit. Its delivered energy is 95 % of all wind power: 168,589 kWh in the July week (1,003 kW mean), 10.3 GWh over the year.
2. The electrolyzer takes only what it can: 91,576 kWh in that week (1,682 kg H2, 54 kWh/kg). The other 77,000 kWh (46 %) reach no component: the energy balance does not close, and without an electricity meter the general KPI 'Grid injection of electricity' counts the whole production as fed in (related: hisim-meter-bought-carriers-lyfl).
#1096 (the KPI unit conversion, hisim-50kh) is correct as it is: the KPI now equals the transformer's own delivered energy; this bead is the physics behind that number.

Owner decision needed, recommendation first: (a) the transformer delivers only what its load draws, capped at its rating: min(input * efficiency, rating, the electrolyzer's demand); the rest is published as a curtailment output, so the balance closes and the Sankey shows it (an off-grid electrolyzer plant fed directly by the turbine); (b) it delivers up to its rating and the surplus beyond the electrolyzer's demand goes to a grid connection through a meter (the grid-connected variant; needs the meter of lyfl). Either way the goldens of electrolyzer_with_renewables move. Owner 2026-10-24: P2; nobody uses the wind turbine setup currently.

title: Make solar thermal an optional, sizeable flag rather than two dedicated setups
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 10

`household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` and
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` are the only solar-thermal setups, so an
oil- or electric-heated house with (or adding) solar thermal cannot be simulated with solar
thermal; the translator drops it with a report note. Collector area and storage volume are also
fixed by the setup rather than configurable (`solarThermal.collectorAreaM2`, `storageLiters` are
ignored).

Suggested fix: either add solar-thermal variants for the remaining heating systems or -- cleaner
long-term -- make solar thermal an optional flag handled inside each setup, with optional
collector area / storage volume fields. Under the declarative path the natural spelling is a
variant group on the recorded twins.

Related: challenges.md F10 records that the solar-thermal files wire the collector to DHW only,
so `DHW_ONLY` is the one supported supply mode; the other two catalogue values are refusals.

Testing: marker test per new combination; assert DHW energy from the boiler decreases when solar
thermal is enabled.

title: Model electric vehicles in every building-sizer setup, not only the one with a car
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 11

`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py` is the only building-sizer setup with a car; none of
the others model vehicles. RenoVisor models all vehicles (fuel cost and CO2 of the status quo, EV
charging load interacting with PV/battery/tariff) and the translator ignores the whole `vehicles`
array. An EV can shift several MWh/a onto the household meter, so PV/battery sizing conclusions
are skewed for EV owners.

Suggested fix: add an optional `electric_vehicles` list (annual km, kWh/km) and instantiate the
existing car / car-battery components when present, following
`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py`.

Blocked in part by `roadmap/p3_random_findings.md` F-9: `Car.__init__` requires
`data_dict_with_car_information` computed from the occupancy instance at setup time, so `Car`
cannot be built from configuration alone and the car setup is unrecordable (EF-33). Owner
decision 2026-08-30: leave unrecorded and name it a class-conversion gap.

Testing: setup test asserting total electricity consumption grows by about km x kWh/km; check the
EMS still converges.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23 (from hisim-cost-data-l07.12): before a RenoVisor request can run the car twin, generic_car.Car and advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery need a cost facts source (Irish device rows with sources plus adapter entries), and the owner has to decide whether the car is priced at all or treated as the household's own. tests/renovisor/test_twin_cost_declarations.py fails until then if the car twin is added to BaseFiles.

title: Represent an east-west PV split instead of approximating it as one east-facing array
description:
Source: roadmap/simulation_issues.md 12

`ArcheTypeConfig` has a single `pv_azimuth` and the setups build one PV array. RenoVisor offers
`east_west` roof orientation, common for terraced houses; the translator approximates it as a
single east-facing array (azimuth 90 degrees), which underestimates evening generation and
distorts self-consumption.

Suggested fix: allow a list of (azimuth, share) tuples -- or a simple `pv_split_east_west: bool`
-- and build two `PVSystem` instances with half the capacity each.

Related: challenges.md Q16 decided PV sizing reads roof form and orientation from new inventory
fields with TABULA roof geometry as the fallback, and that the rule is the existing `rooftop` law
with an added input.

Testing: compare annual generation profiles; the east/west split should flatten the midday peak
against a south array of equal kWp.

title: The electric-heating and district-heating controllers restore their mode to the start of the step on every pass, so after a forced step their committed mode can differ from the mode they held
description:
Source: found 2026-10-21 by the subagent fixing hisim-component-physics-4g9.28 (PR #1100). The heat pump's space-heating controller and the gas boiler's controller now keep a start-of-step and an end-of-step mode (the pattern of the energy manager and the heat-distribution controller): an unforced pass writes the end mode, restore leaves it, save makes it the next start, so after a forced step the committed mode equals the held output. The electric-heating controller (hisim/components/generic_electric_heating.py ~:1044-1057) and the district-heating controller (hisim/components/generic_district_heating.py ~:1189-1202) still restore their mode to the start of the step on every pass, the pattern that made the heat pump skip its hysteresis band after 185 forced steps a year.

Do: measure their mismatches first (forced steps where the committed mode differs from the published state; the electric and district-heating twins, full year at 900 s and a week at 60 s), then apply the same start/end-of-step pattern with a unit test, if any mismatch exists.

Done when: both controllers commit the mode they held after a forced step, pinned by a test, or the measurement shows they cannot mismatch (and the bead says why).

title: Cost module data and sources
Move the meters' >1 maintenance rates into fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 1

The legacy capex dict has meter maintenance rates above 1: `ELECTRICITY_METER: 2.4` and
`GAS_METER: 1.8` in DE/2024, i.e. 240 % and 180 % of investment per year. They encode absolute
yearly fees, not rates. They were migrated 1:1 into `devices_DE.json` for parity, but they
violate the sanity range a maintenance rate should have.

The new schema has `fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year` for exactly this. A data PR should
move 240 EUR/a resp. 360 EUR/a there and zero the rate -- a deliberate, visible KPI delta.

The AT entries (0.2 / 0.15) look like the same confusion with different magnitudes (a
"20 EUR/month" comment against a 0.2 rate).

Item 25 records that the new AI-estimate entries for 2026/2035 already put the metering fee in
the right field, so this closes the pre-2026 rows.

Done when: the meter rows carry the fee in `fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year`, the rate is
zero, and the KPI delta is blessed deliberately.

title: Replace the rough per-m2 AI estimates for envelope embodied CO2
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 12, "Still open"; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md section 11 F5

The envelope embodied CO2 values of the thirteen envelope `ComponentType`s are rough per-m2 AI
estimates.

Related open question from the RenoVisor side (challenges.md F5): embodied CO2 of the Irish
example is negative (-2 224 kg) because the materials dump gives wood fibre -174.8 kg CO2-eq./m3
with biogenic storage netted in at A1-A3. The question to the materials team -- does
`embodied_co2_in_kg` want storage netted in or reported separately (the dump has both columns)? --
has to be answered before the numbers mean anything.

Done when: the thirteen envelope classes carry sourced embodied-CO2 values and the biogenic-
storage convention is stated.

title: Set energy_related_cost_share from reviewed data instead of shipping 1.0 everywhere
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 12 decision (a), and item 32 note (a)

`energy_related_cost_share` is implemented as the coupled-cost (Ohnehin-Kosten) mechanism but
shipped as 1.0 everywhere -- user-acknowledged as "a bit of a hack, but good enough to start".
The credit logic is tested via scenario overlays and activates the moment reviewed shares land in
the data.

Why it matters, from item 32: with the interim 1.0, a like-for-like envelope credit equals nearly
the full measure cost, so the "vs doing nothing" frame is only as honest as that share. In the
German worked example this produces the year-2 spike of 58 kEUR of ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT.

Done when: reviewed shares per envelope measure land in the data and the 1.0 default is gone or
documented as the fallback for unreviewed entries.

title: Close the fourteen PRICED component classes that no cost facts source can price
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 34 (2026-09-08, stack part 8/8 review)

Fourteen component classes declare `cost_relevance = CostRelevance.PRICED` while nothing can
produce `ComponentCostFacts` for them -- no `get_cost_facts()` of their own and no entry in
`adapter.FactsExtractors.BY_CLASS_NAME`. Each fails `Simulator.check_cost_declarations` before
the first timestep of any run that asks for lifecycle costs, and would fail the postprocessing D7
check if it got that far. Closing one means two things: a `devices_<COUNTRY>.json` row with real
sources in `sources.json` for the device type it is priced against, and an adapter entry (or a
hook) mapping its config to that asset class and a size.

Grouped by the device type the cost database lacks:

* CHP -- `advanced_fuel_cell.CHP`, `generic_chp.SimpleCHP`. No CHP device type exists at all.
  This is why `system_setups/dynamic_components.py` fails fast under all options: it wires two
  CHPs and the run is refused before the first timestep.
* Fuel cell -- `generic_fuel_cell.FuelCell` (the reversible cell moved to `obsolete/components/`
  under D-25 on 2026-09-11).
* Electrolyzers other than the migrated one -- `generic_electrolyzer.GenericElectrolyzer`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.AdvancedElectrolyzer`. The `ELECTROLYZER` device type now
  exists, so these two need an adapter entry each -- but only after someone checks that their
  configs state a rating in kW and that an industrial PEM price is the right one.
* Hydrogen storage -- `generic_hydrogen_storage.GenericHydrogenStorage`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.HydrogenStorage`. No hydrogen-storage device type.
* Mobility -- `generic_car.Car`, `advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery`. No car or car-battery
  device type; the stationary `BATTERY` entry is not a vehicle pack.
* Wind -- `generic_windturbine.Windturbine`. No wind device type.
* Air conditioning -- `air_conditioner.AirConditioner`, `simple_air_conditioner.SimpleAirConditioner`.
  No air-conditioner device type.
* `simple_heat_source.SimpleHeatSource` -- a case of its own. Its config declares its own
  `investment_costs_in_euro`, `lifetime_in_years` and `device_co2_footprint_in_kg`, so it needs
  no database row; what it lacks is an asset class, because `SimpleHeatSourceType` says how the
  source behaves (constant power / constant temperature / brine) and never which fuel it burns.
  Deliberately left without an adapter entry rather than mapped by guess.

A class scan finds a fifteenth, `simple_water_storage.SimpleWaterStorage`, excluded because it is
an abstract base that is never instantiated.

Done when: every PRICED class has a facts source, or its declaration changes.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: MVP scope (2026-09-20): only the mobility pair matters for RenoVisor — household_heatpump_car_building_sizer wires generic_car.Car and advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery, so a request with an electric_vehicle block cannot run COMPUTE_LIFECYCLE_COSTS today. Close those two first (car and car-battery device rows for IE with sources, adapter entries); the CHP, fuel cell, electrolyzer, hydrogen, wind and air-conditioner classes are outside the MVP.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23, decided with Noah: out of the MVP. RenoVisor never selects a twin with an unpriceable class: the car twin and the air-conditioner twin are the only ones, and an EV and an air conditioner are not_implemented_yet (D-C). tests/renovisor/test_twin_cost_declarations.py now fails when a twin BaseFiles can select has a class check_cost_declarations would refuse, and fails once the car pair or the air conditioner gains a facts source. The car pair's pricing moves to hisim-component-physics-4g9.8 as a question.

title: Settle who curates the subsidy catalogues and the localized question texts
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11, Phase 4 questions Q8, Q31, Q32 and Q33

Q8 -- catalogue curation process: who verifies scheme files and how often? Schemes change
quarterly. Proposal: `catalog_snapshot_date` per file, a CI check that warns when older than 12
months, and scheme files carrying `legal_basis` + `url` for auditability. Scope v1 to DE + AT,
add FR/IT on demand. (IE has since been added as an AI placeholder -- see the IE.json review
issue.)

Q31 -- question catalog curation (section 5.7): who writes and reviews the localized question
texts? The wording is user-facing and legally sensitive ("Denkmalschutz" vs "erhaltenswerte
Bausubstanz" are different legal categories a layperson may conflate). Which languages ship in
v1? Proposal: de + en.

Q32 -- questionnaire default posture (section 5.7): start with zero questions and progressively
disclose via the optimistic upper bound (proposal), or ask the full computed question set upfront
in the RenoVisor flow? Affects the frontend UX contract, not the engine.

Q33 -- heritage scope: is `heritage_status` plus condition-level relaxations enough (proposal),
or do v1 studies need dedicated heritage programs (e.g. section 7i EStG monument depreciation) as
their own benefit kind? The tax-credit payout profile already exists, so this is likely catalog
data, not engine work.

title: Replace the placeholder Irish factors in the legacy emission and price table
description:
Source: roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md section 11 F2 and its revision of 2026-09-19;
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H1 (decided `[-]`: keep the placeholders)

The legacy KPI path has emission and price factors for DE and AT only
(`hisim/components/configuration.py`, `EmissionFactorsAndCostsForFuelsConfig`). Rather than
leaving `SimulationParameters.country` at DE -- a shim that would be rediscovered in three months
as "the country setting does nothing" -- Ireland is registered as a placeholder with every number
set to -1 000 000 000 (`PlaceholderCountryFactors`). A run with `country = "IE"` completes, and
every legacy cost or CO2 KPI of an Irish run is visibly absurd until sourced Irish rows replace
the block. Verified: the KPI path ran, "Costs of grid electricity" = -1.2e10 EUR for one January
day.

The owner's H1 decision of 2026-09-19 was (a) -- keep the placeholders, correct the spec text --
with the closing line: "Sourced Irish rows in `hisim/components/configuration.py` replace the
placeholder block when they exist." The payload reads none of those KPIs: emissions come from the
lifecycle engine's Irish factors, and energy demand and self-sufficiency do not depend on the
tables.

Done when: sourced Irish emission and price factors (SEAI / CRU) replace `PlaceholderCountryFactors`
and `mapping_report.translator.legacy_factors` stops saying "placeholder".

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-19 (shared todos H1): keep the -1e9 sentinel placeholders on purpose; money for RenoVisor comes from the lifecycle engine, so the legacy table is only what all_kpis.json shows. Priority lowered to P3; the item is data sourcing, not a blocker.

title: Price the air conditioner by the capacity it is sized to, not by the catalogue unit's fixed price
description:
Source: owner request 2026-10-12, after the sizing fix of hisim-h84t (#950).

Since #950, AirConditionerConfig.for_building_load scales the selected catalogue unit to 0.8 of the building's design heating load (scale_factor = 0.8 x load / fitted capacity). The costs do not follow that size:

- Legacy capex (AirConditioner.get_cost_capex): the investment is the selected row's price plus the installation cost of its type, maintenance is 5 % of that and the CO2 figure is the class constant 165.84 kg. None of them depends on scale_factor.
- Lifecycle cost engine: it cannot price an air conditioner at all. There is no air-conditioner device type in devices_<COUNTRY>.json and no adapter entry (one item of hisim-cost-data-l07.12).

The catalogue has four units, 4.9 to 13.8 kW heating at 5.7 C (Daikin, Mitsubishi, Panasonic, Samsung), with investments of 4,080 / 4,528 / 4,899 / 6,800 EUR. Any load is priced as one of these four, whatever it is scaled to:
- A 30 kW load selects the Samsung and runs it at scale factor 1.74, i.e. 24 kW, for 6,800 EUR.
- A 2 kW load selects the Daikin and runs it at 0.33 for 4,080 EUR.
In the air-conditioned house twin the scale factor is 0.95, so the error is small there (see hisim-component-physics-4g9.59 for the selection's part).

Proper fix: price the capacity that is simulated.
- Add an air-conditioner device type with a sourced price law: a fixed part plus a specific price per kW, or a scaling exponent. The engine already supports both (catalog_entries.py).
- Add an adapter entry whose size is the simulated heating capacity (scale_factor x the fitted capacity at the reference temperature).
- Make the legacy capex, maintenance and CO2 follow the same size, or retire them in favour of the engine.
- Decide whether the catalogue price stays as the price at scale factor 1.0.

Done when the investment grows with the load also between loads that select the same unit (a test like tests/test_air_conditioner_sizing.py), both cost paths agree, and the air_conditioned_house goldens are re-blessed. SimpleAirConditioner (hisim-cost-data-l07.12) is out of scope unless the same law fits it.

title: A door_replacement measure fails every RenoVisor run: the cost database prices EXTERIOR_DOOR per door, the translator sizes the door in m2
description:
Source: renovisorissues #74 (production since 2026-09-28; the backend suite keeps the reproducer 74-door-replacement.json); loop-design/contract_update_2026-10-14.md section 2.3, owner Noah 2026-10-14: fix it now.

Every request with door_replacement ends in exit 5: "door_replacement: declared size_unit 'm2' does not match the database entry's per_unit (None)." hisim/cost_database/devices_IE.json and devices_DE.json price EXTERIOR_DOOR per door (per_unit null, IE 2300/3400/5200 EUR in 2026), while the measure's cost subject (EconomicContextBuilder._envelope_subject) and the existing-asset register row declare m2 of door, and the kept-door subject was one door (Units.ANY). EconomicEvaluator.resolve_check skips the database only when both the investment and the lifetime are overridden; a request cost block overrides only the investment, so the check fails with and without one. The check is right to stop it: the service life, the maintenance share, embodied CO2 and any like-for-like replacement come from the entry and scale with the subject's size. HiSim's 2026-09-28 answer on #74 ("HiSim changes nothing") was wrong; the contract's new EUR/m2 door row does not reach HiSim's cost database.
close_reason: Branch door-price-per-m2: EXTERIOR_DOOR priced per m2 of door in IE and DE, 2026 and 2035 (IE from the contract's 500-1500 EUR/m2 band, DE from IWU 2015's 1433 EUR/m2 indexed to August 2026 with Destatis 61261-0002 joinery (owner decision 2026-10-14), the embodied CO2 from the per-door estimate over IWU's mean front-door area of 2.79 m2), the kept door sized in m2 like every other element; tests pin the unit of every envelope class and a door plan with and without a cost block.

title: Review the ENERGY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM investment migrated as an absolute euro amount
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 2

The legacy `ENERGY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM` investment comment says "EUR/kW" but the key is absolute
EUR (`investment_costs_in_euro: 3500`). It was migrated as absolute (`per_unit = null`).

Done when: someone decides which the 3500 is and the row says so, with a source.

title: Correct the DE/2018 diesel price of 128.90 EUR per litre in the migrated data
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 3

`opex_techno_economic_parameters` mixes carriers and units (oil in EUR/l, pellets in EUR/t) and
prices diesel at `128.90` EUR/l for DE/2018 -- an obvious typo for 1.2890. It was migrated 1:1
for parity; the DE/2018 diesel price should be corrected in a data PR.

Done when: the row reads 1.2890 EUR/l with its source, and whatever KPI it moves is blessed.

title: Reclassify every migrated price as net and set its true VAT handling
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions (section 11)" Q5 and "New issues" 4;
roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11 Q5 (Phase 3)

Device entries migrated from `configuration.py` carry `vat_rate: 0.19` (DE) / `0.20` (AT) and are
stored as-is from the legacy dicts. The legacy numbers' VAT status is undocumented -- parity
requires using them unchanged -- so the migrated entries are flagged `"price_basis": "AS_LEGACY"`
and the gross-up for FINANCIAL accounting is a no-op for them.

Consequence recorded in item 4: all migrated energy prices and device costs are treated as
household-final prices; `tax_and_levy_share` is filled only where a source exists, otherwise 0
with an EXPERT_ESTIMATE source, so macroeconomic results for migrated data are approximate.

cost_spec section 11 Q5's proposal: store net + `vat_rate` per entry; household perspectives
gross up, macroeconomic uses net directly, VAT-reduction subsidies override the rate. Requires
touching every price entry once during data migration.

Done when: each entry is classified as net or gross with a source, `price_basis: AS_LEGACY` is
gone, and `tax_and_levy_share` is sourced.

title: Fix the pellet and wood-chip emission factors quoted per kWh against per-ton prices
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 24

The legacy dicts price pellets and wood chips per ton but state their emission factors per kWh.
The migration kept both as-is, so for these two carriers the engine multiplies tons by a per-kWh
factor -- understating CO2 by a factor of a few thousand.

The new AI-estimate entries (2026/2035) carry per-ton factors (pellets ~175 kg/t, wood chips
~80 kg/t); the migrated pre-2026 entries should be corrected in the same data-review PR as
issue 21 (the energy-price unit conversion, which resolved on 2026-08-18).

Note item 33: the prices themselves were converted to EUR/kWh at migration using the heating
values from `PhysicsConfig` (pellets 4.9 kWh/kg, wood chips from 17.3 GJ/m3 at 250 kg/m3), with
the factors recorded in the entry notes -- so the emission factors are the half left behind.

Done when: the two carriers' emission factors are in the same unit as the quantity they multiply,
and a test pins the CO2 of a pellet run against a hand figure.
close_reason: Restored the legacy wood-fuel emission factors to their as-published per-kWh figures (DE pellets 0.036, DE chips 0.0313, AT pellets 0.026, AT chips 0.019; 20 rows incl. the two zero 2050 rows' notes) - the migration had wrongly divided them by the heating value like the per-ton prices, understating CO2 by a factor of a few thousand. Notes corrected. Hand-figure test pins one burned ton of pellets at 180 kg CO2 (cross-checked vs the AI estimate's 175 kg/t) plus a bug-band scan over every shipped entry

title: Review the escalation defaults and CO2 price paths shipped as EXPERT_ESTIMATE
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions" Q2; roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11 Q2 (Phase 1)

`escalation_defaults_DE.json` ships with a small, clearly-labelled EXPERT_ESTIMATE table
(electricity 2 %, gas 3 %, oil 3 %, others 2 %); the per-asset-class investment escalation table
ships empty per the spec proposal. The CO2 price paths for DE encode nEHS 2024-2026 fixed prices
and an ETS2 corridor estimate from 2027 -- values are EXPERT_ESTIMATE and need team review
against sources [33]-[35], which `hisim/components/configuration.py` already cites.

The same question applies per country: IE now has `escalation_defaults_IE.json` and its own
carbon-tax/ETS2 path (item 25).

Done when: each rate and each path carries a reviewed source, and the per-asset-class table is
either filled with learning curves or documented as deliberately empty.

title: Replace the src_ai_estimates placeholder rows for DE and IE with reviewed sources
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 25

Added 2026-07-07 for testing: all device classes and carriers have entries for DE and IE, 2026
and 2035, under source id `src_ai_estimates` ("AI Estimates", kind EXPERT_ESTIMATE) with real
min/best_estimate/max bands. All values are placeholders to be replaced by reviewed sources; the
bands are honest guesses of market spreads, not survey data.

Deliberate modelling differences against the migrated legacy entries, each exercising an engine
feature the legacy data cannot: fossil carriers carry `co2_price_exposure = 1.0` with working
prices excluding the explicit CO2 price (legacy entries embed it, exposure 0), so 2026+ basis
years price carbon via `co2_price_paths.json`; electricity/gas/district/hydrogen entries have
non-zero standing charges and gas a grid exit fee; meter entries put the metering fee into
`fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year`; `tax_and_levy_share` is filled with rough estimates.

Done when: the AI-estimate rows are replaced or confirmed against real sources and
`src_ai_estimates` no longer appears in shipped data.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP; every figure it touches is marked as an estimate in the provenance file. Labelled human: data sourcing by a person.

title: Legally review the CO2KostAufG tier table and the modernization levy parameters
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 10; roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11 Q12 (Phase 5)

The CO2KostAufG tier table and the modernization levy parameters are shipped as data
(`allocation_DE_2024.json`) with values per sections 559/559e BGB and CO2KostAufG as of 2024. The
spec itself requires a legal review pass before release (section 10 Phase 5), and section 11 Q12
repeats it for the levy parameters (559 at 8 % vs 559e at 10 % for the heating variant, caps,
duration) -- the spec deliberately keeps them as data.

Done when: a legal review has signed off each parameter, or the ones that could not be confirmed
are marked.

title: Legally verify the BEG EM catalogue values in subsidy_catalog/DE.json
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 11

`subsidy_catalog/DE.json` encodes the BEG EM catalogue from the Richtlinie as of 2024: base 30 %,
speed bonus 20 %, income bonus 30 % (income <= 40 000 EUR), efficiency bonus 5 %, combined cap
70 %, eligible-cost cap 30 000 EUR first unit / 15 000 EUR units 2-6 / 8 000 EUR further; section
35c EStG 20 % over three years (7/7/6 %) mutually exclusive with BEG. It needs legal
verification, as the spec demands.

Done when: each number is verified against the Richtlinie with a dated citation.

title: A run with a car writes a mobility Sankey: charged electricity or diesel through the car battery or tank to driving energy, with charging and storage losses
description:
Owner, 2026-10-18: besides the house's heat and electricity Sankeys (hisim-mzft), these carriers get a Sankey of their own, because the system they describe is not readable from heat and electricity alone.

Components: generic_car, generic_car_profile, lpg_car_information, the car battery and the EV charge controller (controller_l1_generic_ev_charge). Carriers: EnergyBalanceCarrier.ELECTRICITY for an electric car, DIESEL for a fuel car.

Wanted: per run with a car, charging electricity (from grid or PV, as the house's electricity Sankey shows it) -> charger losses -> car battery (stored change over the run) -> driving energy, and for a fuel car diesel -> driving. In the house's electricity Sankey the car is one consumer; this Sankey shows where that electricity goes and how much is lost on the way.

Needs: the car's and the charger's ports (hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.5).
Done when: household_heatpump_car_building_sizer writes the Sankey with a zero residual within tolerance, and the owner has reviewed it.

title: The space-heating buffer publishes its start-of-step temperature on its own port, WaterTemperatureAtStartOfStepInCelsius, and the generator controllers read it (two-mode buffer, T1)
description:
Spec: roadmap/two_mode_buffer_spec.md (merged with #1052; owner decisions Q1-Q9 in its section 9), sections 4.1, 5.1 and 8 (T1). Owner decisions Q1 (a new output, T0 in both modes) and Q4 (a small PR on top of #1035).

SimpleHotWaterStorage publishes WaterTemperatureAtStartOfStepInCelsius: T0 on the start-of-step path, the end temperature on the stratification path. The default connections of the generator controllers that decide on the buffer's temperature (boiler, heat pump, CHP) move from WaterTemperatureToHeatGenerator to it, so their on/off decision reads a value no pass moves, which the iterated buffer of T2 needs. No result change with the start-of-step buffer (the value is T0 either way); recorded energy-system files are re-recorded only if their wiring lists the port.

Done when: the port exists with a base test, the three controllers read it, the twins and composed files agree, and no golden moves.

title: The hplib heat pump's KPI 'Number of SH heat pump cycles' is always 0: the KPI loop overwrites the count for every output, and the last output is not TimeOff
description:
Found 2026-10-18 while folding stage D PR 8 into #1011 (0 in every 900 s and full-year run, at every step length).

MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib.get_component_kpi_entries calls get_heatpump_cycles(output=...) for every output of the component and assigns the result each time. get_heatpump_cycles counts TimeOff edges only for the TimeOff output and returns 0 for every other, so after the loop the KPI holds the value of the component's last output: 0.

Fix: count once, from the TimeOff column.
Done when: a test with a known TimeOff series gets its cycle count back from get_component_kpi_entries.

Also found by the aggregate chart review of #1019 (filed there as hisim-component-physics-4g9.68, dropped as a duplicate): in the full-year run of household_heatpump_building_sizer at 900 s the heat pump's CounterOnOff reaches 514 while the KPI reports 0.
close_reason: get_component_kpi_entries counts the starts once, from the TimeOff column and vectorised, instead of keeping the last output's 0, and get_heatpump_cycles refuses any other column. Per the owner decision on hisim-hp-cycles-kpi-name-xe9y the KPI 'Number of SH heat pump cycles' becomes two KPIs: 'Number of heat pump starts' (every off-to-on edge of TimeOff: space heating, hot water and cooling) and 'Number of space-heating starts' (off to space heating in OnOffStateHeatpump). test_more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py::test_the_start_kpis_count_every_start_and_the_space_heating_starts_whatever_output_comes_after_them gets 5 and 3 back from a known series (0 on main). Measured on household_heatpump_building_sizer, one week at 60 s: 56 heat pump starts, equal to the TimeOff edges and to the final CounterOnOff (56), and 43 space-heating starts. The goldens of the four heat-pump setups change in these KPI names and values and need a bless.

title: Declarative energy systems (P4 sweep, twins, recording)
Give KPI keys stable addresses so consumers stop rebuilding key strings by hand
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md, "Missing deliverables (code)"; spec
`roadmap/kpi_address_spec.md`

Related: `roadmap/p3_random_findings.md` F-28 -- the EMS builds
`KpiEntry(name=f"Priority for {input_sorted.field_name}")`, so an aggregator port name is
embedded in a KPI key, which is a second argument for renaming the legacy aggregator ports.

title: Give the parity rig a verdict that distinguishes an unrunnable environment from a disagreement
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-15 (reported, 2026-09-15)

`scripts/p3_parity_check.py` gives each of its two sides a private, empty cache directory and
deletes the whole work directory at the start of every triple (`p3_parity_check.py:159`,
`p3_parity_runs.py:324`), which is right for the question it asks: a shared cache would let one
side answer from the other side's result. The consequence is that every setup whose occupancy
comes from `USE_LOCAL_LPG` must actually run the LoadProfileGenerator binary, twice, on every
invocation. On a machine where that binary fails -- here the root filesystem was 98 % full and
the binary died with `System.IO.IOException: No space left on device`, leaving no results and no
log -- no such setup can be measured, and the rig reports a parity failure rather than an
unrunnable environment: three identical FAIL rows whose note is "the python run did not finish".
The golden gate has no such problem, since it uses the normal cache directory and a seeded entry
answers both modes.

Two things would help, neither a change to the isolation the rig needs: a verdict that
distinguishes "the run could not start" from "the two sides disagree" (the note already carries
the distinction, the verdict does not), and an opt-in read-only seed directory the private caches
are pre-filled from, so a profile that is an input to both sides rather than a result of either
can be supplied once.

title: Retire PVSystemConfig.location, a string nobody reads, with the PV conversion
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-7 (verified; logged 2026-09-03, re-verified 2026-09-12
against main)

`PVSystemConfig.location: str` (`hisim/components/generic_pv_system.py:116`) is passed by 23
setup call sites (`location=weather_location`) and written into all 27 PV blocks of the committed
energy-system YAMLs, and the PV component never reads it: inside the module it appears seven
times -- the module docstring, the dataclass field, a parameter of the two factory methods and
their two forwardings, and one docstring line -- and in no computation.

Its purpose was to make the PV cache key differ between sites, which worked only as long as every
setup copied the same variable into the weather and the PV -- a habit, not an invariant, and the
origin of `pylpg_flakiness.md` F7. F7 has since landed: the PV carries a `weather_identity` field
sized from the weather itself (`generic_pv_system.py:145`), so the key no longer needs `location`.
What remains is a field that can visibly disagree with its neighbour: a setup with Seville
weather and a PV built with the factories' default `location="Aachen"` records
`location: Aachen` beside `weather_identity: Sevilla/...`, and the first is wrong without
consequence.

The finding's own instruction: do not fix piecemeal. The field is in the config class, two
factory signatures, 23 setup call sites, one test and 27 energy-system YAML blocks, and the
conversion of `PVSystemConfig` is the point at which those are all rewritten anyway.

title: Move the car battery's charged and discharged totals off its configuration
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-20 (reported, 2026-09-16, left alone in batch B7)

Two fields of `CarBatteryConfig`, `total_charged_energy_in_kilowatthour` and
`total_discharged_energy_in_kilowatthour`, are not inputs at all: `CarBattery.get_cost_opex` and
`CarBattery.get_component_kpi_entries` each compute them from the post-processing results and
assign them back onto `self.battery_config`, so the configuration object a run started with is a
different object by the time the run ends. They carry a 0.0 default and the twin records them as
0.0, which is true of the configuration as written and untrue of the configuration as it ends up.

That a configuration is the author's statement of the system, read and never written, is what
lets the recorder diff a live config against a built preset and call the difference an override.
Here the difference is a result. Nothing is wrong today only because the two writes happen in
post-processing, after the last recording; a recorder that ran later, or a second post-processing
pass, would write two computed energies into a file as if an author had typed them.

Two honest ways out, per the finding. Move the accumulators onto the component -- they are
per-run state, which is what a component holds -- and let the two methods read and write
`self.total_charged_energy...`; the config loses two fields and the twin two lines. Or keep them
where they are and exclude them from recording, which needs a way to mark a field as
not-an-input that the recorder, `describe` and the schema all honour, and which would be the
first such mark in the repository. The first is smaller and says the true thing; it changes the
component's behaviour surface and the twin, which is why B7 (a behaviour-neutral batch) left it.

title: Decide what to do with the run-side description that nothing reads
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-24 (reported, 2026-09-18, found while retiring the
scenario JSON)

A run's one-line description travels a long way: the Python entry point takes it from the first
line of the setup file, a declarative run takes it from the energy-system file's `description`
field, `Simulator.description` carries it, `PostProcessingDataTransfer` carries it -- and its
single consumer was the `description` field of `scenario.json`, which no longer exists. Nothing
reads it now.

The description of the file is not in question: it documents the system for whoever opens the
file, the recorder writes it and the loader reads it back. What has no reader is the copy the run
object carries.

Three honest ways out: drop the run-side chain and leave the field to the file (smallest, and it
takes `hisim_main`'s docstring-scraping block with it); give it a consumer, the obvious one being
the PDF report, which today prints no description of the run it reports on; or leave it and say
so, which is what the entry does for now.

The scenario name is in a similar position but not the same one: its one remaining consumer, the
`scenario` column of the pyam export, is live -- see the pyam retirement question.

title: Decide whether the pyam scenario-evaluation export is still needed
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-25 (reported, 2026-09-18; logged rather than done on the
owner's instruction)

`pyam` is not a dependency and is imported nowhere. What exists is
`PREPARE_OUTPUTS_FOR_SCENARIO_EVALUATION`, which writes the run's results resampled to four
resolutions -- `hourly/daily/monthly/yearly_<n>_days.csv` in
`result_data_for_scenario_evaluation/` -- in the pyam long format, one row per variable carrying
`model, scenario, region, variable, unit, year, value`.

Its reader is already gone. `hisim/postprocessing/scenario_evaluation/` --
`result_data_collection.py`, `result_data_processing.py`, `result_data_plotting.py` and
`scenario_analysis_complete_with_config.py`, the tool that read those CSVs back and compared runs
-- was moved to `obsolete/` in #541 (2026-08-10) and left the repository entirely with the rest
of that tree in #590. The writer stayed. `hisim/postprocessing/__init__.py` still tells a reader
that results "can be compared and visualised with the `hisim.postprocessing.scenario_evaluation`
sub-package", which has not existed for six weeks.

Nothing else in the tree reads the CSVs: the building sizer reads `all_kpis.json` and
`*_kpi_config_for_building_sizer.json`, and neither RenoVisor nor the HPC harness touches the
directory. What is not known is whether anyone reads them outside the repository -- unlike the
scenario JSON, this artifact carries results rather than configuration, and the pyam long format
is the interchange format for cross-run comparison, so an analysis workflow living elsewhere is
plausible. That question is the whole of the decision, and it is the owner's.

What retiring it would take with it, about 300 lines and the last of the run metadata:
`prepare_results_for_scenario_evaluation` and its four helpers with the four
`self.model/scenario/region/year` attributes; `region_of`, whose only caller it is, and
`tests/test_postprocessing_region.py` entirely; the option in eleven building-sizer setups, three
legacy `*.simulation.json` parameter files and five test files. And the scenario name: the
`scenario` column of this export is its one remaining consumer since F-9, so
`Simulator.scenario_name`, the building sizers' hash strings, `EnergySystemFile.name` as a run
name and `scenario_name_of` for grouped runs would all become decoration. With F-24's description
that is the entire run-metadata layer.

At minimum, correct the stale pointer in `hisim/postprocessing/__init__.py` either way.

title: Repair or delete 2021_minutely_full.simulation.json, which names two dead options
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-26 (verified, 2026-09-18; left broken deliberately)

`system_setups/2021_minutely_full.simulation.json` -- the repository's only "full" parameter set,
the one a reader reaches for when they want everything -- lists `MAKE_RESULT_JSON_FOR_WEBTOOL`
and `MAKE_OPERATION_RESULTS_FOR_WEBTOOL` among its options. Both left `PostProcessingOptions` on
2026-06-26 (88869070, "more old webtool cleanup"). The Python entry point resolves option names
with `PostProcessingOptions[option]` (`hisim_main.py:148`), so loading that file raises a bare
`KeyError` naming the string, wherever it is loaded rather than where it is wrong. The
declarative reader refuses an unknown name properly, by name and location; the JSON path does
not.

The other six `system_setups/*.simulation.json` load cleanly, checked the same way. Nothing in
the repository references the broken one, which is why nothing noticed.

Left broken deliberately: it belongs to the imperative JSON parameter path, which retires with
the Python setups in P5/P6, and repairing it now would suggest the file is maintained. The YAML
library that replaces it holds every file to the rule this one broke: a test loads each one and
refuses an option name the enum does not have.

Two ways to close it: delete the file when the Python path goes, or -- if someone wants it before
then -- drop the two dead names, which makes it the one JSON parameter set with a live full
option list.

title: Settle what my_sim.my_module_config is allowed to hold across the eleven sizers
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

Nine sizers mutate `my_sim.my_module_config` to a dict on the fallback path; the two heat-pump
sizers do not, so downstream readers see a different type depending on the sibling. One behaviour
for all eleven.

`read_in_configs` is string-only by decision (review round of 2026-09-06: it refuses a non-string
with a `TypeError`), so this repair has to settle what the attribute is allowed to hold rather
than widening the reader to accept both.

Done when: the eleven sizers agree, the allowed type is stated, and a test pins it.

title: Make the four sizers that ignore weather_filepath and weather_datasource read or refuse them
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

Four sizers ignore `weather_filepath` / `weather_datasource`:
`household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer`, `household_heatpump_car_building_sizer`,
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer` and the hydrogen one. The same archetype config
therefore yields a different weather source across the fleet.

Either read them or refuse them.

Done when: the four agree with the rest of the fleet, and a test pins that an archetype config
naming a weather file reaches the weather component in every sizer.

title: Give air_conditioned_house one spelling of its location instead of two
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

`air_conditioned_house` duplicates its location: a `"Seville"` string for the PV beside
`LocationEnum.SEVILLE` for the weather. One edit without the other silently desynchronizes the
two. One spelling, one place.

Related: `roadmap/p4_random_findings.md` F-7 is the same class of defect at the config level --
`PVSystemConfig.location` is a string nobody reads that can disagree with `weather_identity`.

Done when: the setup names its location once.

title: Make ModularHouseholdConfig.get_hash() round-trip stable
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox (found 2026-09-06
while testing the reader)

`pv_azimuth: float = 180` and `pv_tilt: float = 30` hold ints in memory and come back as floats
from any JSON round trip, so a config built from defaults and the same config read from its own
file hash differently -- and the building sizer hashes configs.

Normalise in `get_hash()` (or make the defaults floats) and pin the round trip with a test.

title: Delete the json_v2 spike branch, locally and on origin
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md, "Operational, after the stack merges"

Delete the `json_v2` spike branch, local and origin -- the parity and templating halves are
ported. (#598 itself was closed 2026-09-07.)

title: Group automatic_default_connections and air_conditioned_house once their couplings are pinned
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, item 5 ("Still open, and
untouched by the 2026-09-07 pass")

`automatic_default_connections` and `air_conditioned_house` are small, but each carries one
environment coupling to pin first: the hplib database for the former, the reference-temperature
CSV plus the duplicated location for the latter. Neither reads a module configuration, so neither
has an axis a probe list could stand on until the coupling above it is pinned.

The worklist also names one axis shared by all twenty-two setups and belonging to no single one:
every `setup_function` invents its own parameters when `my_simulation_parameters is None`, so the
no-parameters-file path is a configuration of its own. The recorded twins all pin an explicit
parameters file, which is the right answer; the axis is named so nobody mistakes the twins for
covering it.

Depends on the air_conditioned_house location fix.

Done when: the couplings are pinned and both setups either carry a probe list and a grouped file
or are documented as deliberately flat.

title: P5: RenoVisor, building sizer and HPC harness all run from energy-system files
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, section P5 ("Consumer integration (outline;
document later)"), three unchecked items; epic.md EAC5

* RenoVisor: base file per heating system; `mapping.py` -> overrides + group flags;
  post-processing selection moves to the simulation-parameters file. (Largely delivered by the v2
  translator, which selects the recorded grouped twins through `translate.BaseFiles` -- confirm
  and tick.)
* Building sizer: same path; `ModularHouseholdConfig`, `EnergySystemConfig` and `ArcheTypeConfig`
  are deleted.
* HPC harness: payload = energy-system string + simulation parameters; the worker loads from the
  string.

EAC5 is the acceptance criterion: all three run from energy-system files and
`ModularHouseholdConfig` is deleted.

P5 also closes EQ1 (the name freeze): preset, field and fact names may change freely until P5 is
accepted; from then on a rename is a breaking change with a `schema_version` bump and a migration
note, no alias table, and a wire-format test pins every released name (EAC6).

A P5 requirements document is to be written; the list above is the outline.

title: P6: retire the parity rig and promote the setups its evidence earned into the gate
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, section P6, five unchecked items;
p3_recording_requirements.md R11.8/R11.9 (amended 2026-08-31) and AC-P3.20

Entry condition: P1, P2, P2.1, P3, P4 and P5 are all merged. Until then the rig is dispatched by
every batch that re-records, and its renaming tables are kept current.

* Confirm the whole stack is green with the rig still in place, over every runnable window (July
  is fenced pending `roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md`; R11.5 as amended 2026-09-06).
* Decide which setups earned a place in the permanent gate, on the rig's accumulated evidence --
  the six the 2026-08-28 scan cleared are the candidates, not the answer.
* Add those to `scripts/golden_config.json` and bless their references.
* Delete `.github/workflows/p3-parity.yml`, `scripts/p3_parity_*.py` and the renaming tables.
* Confirm the repository contains no reference to any of it (AC-P3.20).

Accumulated evidence so far: fleet-wide dispatches on 2026-09-18 (8f619e4a) and 2026-09-19
(dd6cb78b) were both green -- twenty-two triples each, January window, `rel_tol` and `abs_tol`
both zero, so every recorded setup reproduced its Python original at exact equality. The
candidates for the permanent gate are now every setup, which makes the question one of cost
rather than of trust.

`roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md`'s expectation of "seven KPI-broken setups" no longer holds: there
are none, and the baseline the rig leaves behind is full parity rather than a list of exceptions.

title: Implement the Many aggregator so a law can read several providers
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, parking lot row "Many-cardinality laws (epic
E3, P1 leaves the hook)"; epic.md EQ2 (open); p1_implementation_spec.md (E-07);
p4_component_sweep_requirements.md R2.2 under D-15 (b); p4_class_survey.md item 5

`Many(Size.PV_PEAK_POWER_IN_WATT)` is a `_ManyTerm` whose `facts_read()` returns
`(fact, Cardinality.MANY)` and whose `evaluate` raises E-07
`NotImplementedError("many-cardinality is declared but not implemented; see plan parking lot")`
(`hisim/config/laws.py:225-228`). `SizingContext` stays a frozen dataclass of typed scalars; the
tuple side-table was not added.

The named trigger: the first real consumer -- a buffer storage over a hybrid generator pair, or a
battery / price signal over several PVs. D-15 (b) names a second: the meter half of batch B2
wants `gas_loadtype` copied from the connected generator's energy carrier, which is
many-cardinality with a consistency aggregator, so the meters keep a plain field selected by the
preset instead.

EQ2 is the undecided question above it: is deferring until the first real consumer acceptable, or
must P1 ship it? The recommendation is (a) defer -- the inventory found zero readers that consume
several providers today, the file syntax (a list under `sizing_sources`) is fixed by E3
regardless, and implementing it means a `many` term, a tuple side-table, `sum`/`max`/`count`
aggregates, about 100 lines plus tests, validated on a fabricated use case. No `[decided]` marker
has been recorded, and the plan's parking lot already behaves as if (a) were taken.

Done when: the decision is recorded and, if (a) stands, this issue waits on its trigger.
close_reason: Decision (a) stood and its trigger came: the battery beside several PV arrays. Sum(Many(...)) was implemented in #894 (hisim-assemblies-lt0b.22): _ManyTerm binds every provider, SizingContext carries the tuple, the engine binds a sizing_sources list, and BatteryConfig's CAPACITY_LAW and INVERTER_POWER_LAW sum every array. Branch multi-pv-arrays proves it end to end on a two-array household (tests/test_multiple_pv_arrays.py: battery 6 kWh beside 4 + 2 kWp, flat and composed files) and lets the recorder leave a many-read field to its preset beside several providers instead of pinning it.

title: Give Sizable enum fields a name-based decoder so a wire value becomes the enum member
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] `Sizable[SomeEnum]`
fields bypass dataclasses_json's enum handling"; p4_component_sweep_requirements.md R2.2 under
D-15 (b)

The field-level decoder that `sized_field` injects replaces the library's default decoding, so a
JSON `"FLOORHEATING"` stays a string instead of becoming the enum member. It works today only
because config enums are `(str, Enum)` with value == member name, so equality comparisons still
hold -- but `is` comparisons would silently fail. `HeatDistributionConfig.heating_system` is the
live instance.

R2.2 names the same thing from the other direction and adds the concrete mismatch: `_sizable_decoder`
coerces by value, and `LoadTypes.GAS` is `"Gas"` while the twins write `GAS`. So the meter half of
batch B2 under D-15 (b) needs a name-based decoder before an enum-typed sizable field can carry a
carrier.

Done when: `sized_field` captures the field's concrete type (or the scenario codec handles
`Sizable` unions) so an enum-typed sizable field decodes to the member, and a test pins an `is`
comparison.
close_reason: Already mostly in place since #741: sized_field fields declared with an enum value_type, and enum-typed sizable fields completed at class creation, decode the member name first and the value second, so JSON "FLOORHEATING" is HeatDistributionSystemType.FLOORHEATING (identity) and LoadTypes GAS/Gas both reach LoadTypes.GAS. Branch sizable-enum-schema adds the missing refusal: a word naming no member raises ValueError naming <ConfigClass>.<field> and listing the member names and AUTO, also on the class's own from_dict/from_json path (the decoder for every enum-typed sizable field is now installed at class creation, where the field name is known). Tests in tests/test_sizing.py pin from_json identity, name and value spellings, the refusal, AUTO written and absent, and an encode-decode round trip over every member; every recorded twin unchanged.

description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[elegance] Setups now build
several small SizingContexts instead of one"

The pilot conversion constructs an inline context per component (boiler, HDS) because the spike
did not touch the setups' structure. The sweep should build one context per setup
(`SizingContext.for_building(...)` plus `.with_facts(...)` enrichment) and thread it -- that is

title: Correct the four config_defaults_spec statements the spike disproved
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, the four `[spec]` entries;
target document `roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/config_defaults_spec.md` section 4.1 and the design-B weakness note

1. One lazy import is unavoidable in the sizing module layout. Section 4.1 says `hisim/sizing.py`
   imports `building_config.py` directly, "no lazy imports needed" -- but `component.py` must
   import the sizing machinery and `building_config.py` imports `component.py`, so a module-level
   `sizing -> building_config` would close the cycle. The implemented resolution:
   `SizingContext.for_building` imports the building package locally.
2. Per-preset law variation exists in production after all. The weakness note claims "no such
   variation exists today", but `GenericBoilerConfig`'s scaled factories disagree on the minimal
   power law per fuel: gas/oil/hydrogen use a constant 0, pellet and wood chip use one twelfth of
   the sized maximal power. The escape hatch the spec sketched -- a preset assigning a
   `SizingLaw` as a field value -- is implemented, not hypothetical.
3. `sizing.concrete(value)`, the typed pass-through with a runtime assertion used at the pilot
   read sites, belongs in section 4.1; so does `Sizable` being widened to include `SizingLaw`,
   since the per-preset escape hatch makes law values legal field content pre-resolution.
4. The dataclass field-ordering constraint fires on every converted class (trailing capex fields
   need `None` defaults once sized fields above them are defaulted) -- worth stating so the sweep
   expects it.

Done when: section 4.1 and the weakness note say what the code does.

title: Decide whether contributed facts need a CONNECTED scope for multi-loop systems
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[spec] The HDS controller's
sizing facts are scope-GLOBAL, unlike the boiler's CONNECTED power band"

Surfaced by auditing a `ResolutionReport` of the heat-pump building-sizer chain:
`HeatDistributionControllerConfig.SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` declares `water_mass_flow_rate...` and
`heat_distribution_system_type` without a scope, i.e. GLOBAL -- two heat-distribution loops in
one scenario would hard-error on the double contribution rather than resolve per loop.
Defensible today (one HDS per building) and loud rather than wrong, but it is a modelling
decision the CONNECTED alternative would make differently.

The epic's decision register records that B11 ("Scope rule GLOBAL vs CONNECTED for contributed
facts") was superseded on 2026-08-25: no scopes exist any more; every fact is `<name>.<fact>` and
ambiguity is per consumer.

Worth an explicit look when multi-loop or multi-building scenarios reach the engine -- which is
the named trigger, the same one as the multi-zone `Building` row of the plan's parking lot.

A concrete near-miss is recorded as `roadmap/p4_random_findings.md` F-23: two sibling generator
controllers read the emitter circuit's contributed heating threshold while
`ElectricHeatingControllerConfig` re-derives it, because direct electric heating has no water
circuit and no provider exists -- so a system with both an emitter controller and an electric
heater would diverge the moment an author pins the emitter threshold by hand.

title: Build the multi-zone Building, per-unit facts and an aggregating occupancy input
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, parking lot rows "Multi-zone `Building`,

The template / repeat layer (a preprocessor to a flat file) is the second parking-lot row with

The plan names this as a separate epic. Recorded here so the trigger is findable.
