title: The golden history stitching does not know the fleet-wide KPI key suffix rename of the stable KPI addresses
description: scripts/golden_kpi_renames.py is the table scripts/golden_history.py stitches renamed golden keys with. The stable KPI addresses (hisim-declarative-systems-b3b.1, branch feat/kpi-addresses, roadmap/kpi_address_spec.md) key every component KPI as '<name> (<source.name>)' whether or not a collision exists, so the re-bless after that PR renames almost every component KPI key of every golden (e.g. BUI1.Building.Conditioned floor area -> BUI1.Building.Conditioned floor area (Building)), while keys already suffixed since #653 stay unchanged. Until the table carries this rename, every component KPI's history splits into two half-length series at the re-bless commit. The rename is fleet-wide in shape but not one literal pair per name (the suffix is the source component's runtime name, which differs per setup, and the flat goldens store no source), so the table needs either one entry per (pair, key) derived from the re-bless diff, as the module docstring prescribes, or a declared fleet-wide rule '<key>' -> '<key> (<suffix>)' restricted to the re-bless commit and to keys whose value is unchanged. Do it after the coordinator's golden-update re-bless, citing its commit and PR number; tests/test_golden_history.py checks the table against the real history.
close_reason: Covered by PR #882: the golden history walker identifies a leaf-form series by its address fields (building, tag, name, source import/instance/member) and stitches flat-form keys to it by dotted or bare key; the re-blessed leaf goldens (91c780cd) are in the walk.

title: KPI units are spelled inconsistently ('EUR' and 'Euro' side by side); settle one spelling per quantity
description: Seen 2026-10-03 when the golden references started storing units (PR #882): over the 30 goldens the unit set is ['%', '-', 'EUR', 'Euro', 'W', 'W/m2', 'h', 'kW', 'kWh', 'kWh/m2', 'kg', 'km', 'l', 'm2', '°C', '°C*h']; 'EUR' and 'Euro' both occur for money. The gate now fails distinctly on a unit change, so settling the spelling is one deliberate re-bless. Check which KPI producers write which spelling (kpi_preparation.py and the components' KpiEntry units), pick one (the Units enum value), and re-bless once. Done when: one spelling per quantity across all_kpis.json and the goldens.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Decided (owner, 2026-10-04): 'Euro' everywhere, the value of lt.Units.EURO; replace the stray 'EUR' strings in the producers and re-bless once (unit-only change, the gate reports it distinctly).

title: Make @constructor stamp provenance with the arguments it was called with
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-3 ("`@constructor` never stamps provenance", reported,
Open)

Only `@preset` writes the provenance attribute (`hisim/config/presets.py:_declare`), and the
stamp carries a builder name with no arguments. A recorder can therefore never emit a
`constructor:` entry, and P3's R2.2 and spec section 3.4 are preset-only in practice. Recording a
constructor entry needs the stamp to carry the arguments it was called with.

The finding places the work in P1's kernel, not in P3.

The constructors this blocks are the identifier-lookup ones of Q-P2.6: weather `for_location`,
occupancy `for_household`, building `for_tabula_code`.

Done when: a config built through a declared constructor records as `constructor: <name>` with
its arguments, and a twin using one re-records to itself.

title: Give golden_validate.py --scan-all a deterministic verdict or retire the flag
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-16 (reported, Open)

In a full 21-setup scan, `automatic_default_connections` and
`household_district_heating_building_sizer` were reported non-deterministic (12 and 16 differing
KPIs), yet both PASS when re-run in isolation with `--setup`. This is cross-run LPG/cache
interference inside one long scan session, not a property of the setups.

Consequence: `--scan-all` is unusable as a gate, and the eligibility table in
`roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/p3_setup_inventory.md` section 4f -- which came from one such
scan -- should be read as indicative, not authoritative. Per-setup runs are the reliable form.

Read together with F-21, the pattern is the same: this fleet's tooling is reliable per-setup and
flaky in bulk.

Done when: either each setup in a scan gets its own isolated cache so a scan equals the sum of
its per-setup runs, or `--scan-all` is removed and the inventory table is re-derived per setup.

title: Give the golden gate an absolute tolerance floor so a physically zero KPI is comparable
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-21 (verified, Open) and F-31; `golden_ref_spec.md`
section 7

A full-fleet `golden_check.py` run fails one pair of sixteen:
`household_electric_heating_building_sizer / one_week_60s`, on the KPI "Temperature deviation ...
below set temperature 20.0 Celsius" -- `ref = 1.216772342142273e-09`,
`got = 1.2167721052946946e-09`. The absolute difference is 2.4e-16, the relative difference is
1.95e-7, which exceeds `rel_tol = 1e-9` by a factor of about 195. The gate's report prints
"rel diff=0.000%", which rounds the number that decides the verdict out of view.

The cause is the tolerance regime, not the code: `golden_ref_spec.md` section 7 fixes
`rel_tol = 1e-9, abs_tol = 0` on the reasoning that it "absorbs sub-ULP platform noise". That
holds for KPIs of ordinary magnitude and fails exactly for KPIs that are physically zero -- here
a temperature deviation of 1.2e-9 degC.h -- where a relative comparison has nothing to be
relative to and one last-bit difference is an infinite relative error.

F-31 proved it is one ULP against `abs_tol = 0` and that which way it falls depends on cache
state, not on code: the pair passes in isolation on the documents branch and fails in isolation
on the implementation branch, bit-identically, and reverting the only two golden-path files
leaves the failure unchanged. Nothing was re-blessed.

Done when: an `abs_tol` floor (even 1e-12) makes near-zero KPIs comparable, the spec's section 7
states it, and the report prints the number that decides the verdict.
close_reason: ABS_TOL is 1e-12 (tolerances.py), golden_ref_spec.md section 7 and the README state it, and the report prints rel diff as the plain ratio. Found again on #956 (2026-10-12): the same pair and KPI, bless 1.39823909e-09 against check 1.39823904e-09.

title: Make the EMS refuse its two duplicate weight-2 electricity target outputs
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-25 ("a latent twin of F-24, deliberately left alone",
Open)

`L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.__init__` creates two `HEAT_PUMP_BUILDING` +
`ELECTRICITY_TARGET` weight-2 outputs, one for `HeatPumpHplib` and one for
`MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib`. It is harmless today only because pruning removes whichever class is
absent. A symmetric guard on the imperative path would fail every EMS setup at construction, so
it was left visible rather than hidden.

F-24 is the fixed sibling: two outputs answering one `(tags, weight)` search made the dispatch
list one entry too long and paired the battery's input with the heat-pump-DHW output, measured as
battery charging 32.09 -> 0.0 kWh and 62 of 108 KPIs moved. Guard `EF-2B` (ambiguous dispatch
signal) now refuses that shape on the declarative path.

Note that P4 F-1 (fixed 2026-09-12) removed the constructor's phantom target outputs entirely and
moved target creation into `connect_with_dynamic_connections_list`, so check whether this
duplicate still exists before doing the work.

Done when: the EMS declares one target per participant kind, and the imperative path refuses two
ports answering one signal as `EF-2B` does.

title: Enforce carrier and unit at imperative wiring time, as the declarative path already does
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-36 (reported, "To be fixed later, as its own change")

The two build paths share one participant vocabulary -- every aggregator's `CHANNELS` declaration
-- but only the declarative path enforces the whole declaration. A feed resolved from an
energy-system file passes `ChannelMatcher.match_and_validate`, which checks tags, carrier and
unit: a power output feeding an energy channel is refused with `EF-30`
(`tests/test_meter_channels.py::test_the_matcher_refuses_a_feed_in_the_wrong_unit` pins exactly
that -- a WATT feed into `FuelMeter`'s WATT_HOUR consumption channel). The imperative path checks
none of it: `add_component_input_and_connect` records tags and unit on the created port, and
`get_channel_inputs` selects participants by tag subset alone, so the byte-identical wiring the
declarative path refuses is silently accepted when a setup writes it by hand.

Concretely, using the repository's own pinned example: wire a heat source whose output is
HEAT_CONSUMPTION-tagged but denominated in WATT into the fuel meter imperatively, and
`i_simulate` sums watts as watt-hours -- at 60-second resolution the priced fuel energy is
overstated sixtyfold, a plausible-looking number that means nothing.

The finding names the seam: unit/carrier validation at imperative wiring time, where the matched
channel is known, not inside `get_channel_inputs` -- a lookup that silently drops mismatched
inputs would trade a wrong sum for a silently smaller one. The blast radius over existing setups
is unknown until tried, which is why it is a finding and not a patch.

title: Stop a failed recording leaving an uncommittable file in energy_systems/
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-34 (verified, Open)

`scripts/record_all_setups.py` writes the file and then verifies it builds, and on failure leaves
it "in place for inspection" -- so after a failed run an untracked
`energy_systems/<stem>.energy_system.yaml` sits there that must never be committed. Sensible for
debugging, hazardous next to `git add -A`.

Done when: a failed recording writes to a scratch path, or the file is named so `.gitignore`
catches it.

title: District heating and the electric heater get the maximum hot-water priority time the boiler and the heat pump have
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-21 (hot-water priority limit, branch dhw-priority-time-limit, bead hisim-room-air-dhw-dip-a5by): the boiler and heat-pump controllers interrupt a hot-water charge after a maximum time for a space-heating interval (default 15 / 15 min); district heating and the electric heater keep absolute priority. Measure their twins' room-air dips during hot-water charges first, then apply the same HotWaterPriorityLimit rule if the dips warrant it.

Done when: both are measured, and either use the rule with its config fields or the bead records why not.

title: Remove the mixed-season mid-year warning (hisim/january_readers.py) once every component follows the run's window, at the latest in PR7 (#1033)
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-16 (Noah), branch midyear-season-warning.

Since #988 (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.4) a run whose window starts after 1 January reads its own window for the weather, the PV system and the building's solar gains, while the LoadProfileGenerator occupancy (UtspLpgConnector), the cars (Car), the CHP controller's heating season (L1CHPController), the solar-thermal collector's own sun position (SolarThermalSystem) and the CSV loader (CSVLoader) still read January or a clock of their own. Such a run finishes and looks normal. Until the epic is done, `Simulator.run_all_timesteps` logs one warning at its start naming the ones the run contains, with the bead and PR that fix each; the list is `JanuaryReaders.CLASSES` in `hisim/january_readers.py`. Results do not change.

This warning is temporary. Each mid-year PR, when rebased onto main, removes the entry of the class it fixes: PR4+5 (#1031, hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.6) UtspLpgConnector, Car and L1CHPController; PR6 (#1032, hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.7) SolarThermalSystem; the CSV-loader PR (#1034, hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.14) CSVLoader. PR7 (#1033, hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.8) must remove the warning altogether once every component follows the window: `hisim/january_readers.py`, `Simulator.warn_of_january_readers` and its call, `tests/test_january_readers.py`, and the sentence in `SimulationParameters.one_week_july`'s docstring. If the CSV loader (#1034) has not landed when PR7 does, PR7 keeps only the CSVLoader entry and #1034 removes the rest.

Done when: no warning about January readers is left in hisim/ and every component follows a mid-year window.
close_reason: Branch midyear-csv-time-column (#1034), on its rebase onto main: every component follows a mid-year window, so hisim/january_readers.py, Simulator.warn_of_january_readers and its call, tests/test_january_readers.py and the sentence in SimulationParameters.one_week_july's docstring are gone. #1031 removed the entries of UtspLpgConnector, Car and L1CHPController, #1032 that of SolarThermalSystem, and #1033 kept only the CSVLoader entry because the CSV loader lands after it.

title: Staged ageing register dates stage purchases from the weather year, not the price basis year
description: hisim/economics/staged.py _staged_inputs dates an asset an earlier stage bought as installation_year = stage.inputs.simulation_year + from_year (spec economics-hisim-spec.md §1: installation_year = simulation_year + from_year_j). simulation_year is the WEATHER year (renovisorissues #57), while the engine ages every register asset against the price basis year (context_resolution.py age_in_years(price_basis_year)). For a RenoVisor plan (weather 2019, price basis 2026) an asset bought by a stage at year 3 is dated 2022 and is 4 years old at year 0 of the next stage's evaluation, so its replacement and residual value move ~7 years early. Anchor should be the plan's basis/start year (price_basis_year + from_year, or plan_start_year + from_year), with the spec line changed. Left out of #57 PR 1 (document only) on purpose; changes money in multi-stage plans with from_year > 0.
close_reason: plan year 0 = plan_start_year, else the price basis year: stage purchases dated year0 + from_year (feat/year-zero)

title: SolarThermalSystem.i_simulate costs ~7.5 ms per call (pvlib on one-element pandas Series): a full-year job with solar thermal takes 6-9 min instead of ~20 s
description: Found 2026-09-27 from the local backend's jobstats (jobs of houses with solar_thermal_system: 350-540 s CPU vs 15 s). Profile of request 584E73EA (IE 1988, gas + existing solar thermal dhw_only): 51.6 of 54.6 s in solar_thermal_system.py i_simulate (6870 calls). Since #619 (2026-09-02) the collector is computed per call with pd.Series + pvlib.irradiance.dni/get_total_irradiance. poa_global depends only on weather and sun (not the storage temperature), so it can be computed once per timestep or vectorised in prepare.
close_reason: fix/solar-thermal-speed: collector plane irradiance computed once per timestep on numpy scalars; bit-identical; slow.json full year 7:00 -> 17.6 s

title: HiSimCommit reports the commit of an enclosing git repository when HiSim is installed inside another working tree
description:
Source: evaluation of the review of #903, missed finding (2026-10-13), with R16/R17 of the same review. Owner decision 2026-10-13: bead it, no fix now.

Mechanism: HiSimCommit.ROOT is the directory that holds the hisim package (hisim/hisim_commit.py:51, Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]); for a non-editable install that is site-packages. HiSimCommit._git_at (hisim_commit.py:118-139) runs `git -C <ROOT> rev-parse --short HEAD` with no further check and no timeout. In a virtual environment that sits inside another git working tree (a project with its .venv in its own repository), git answers the enclosing repository's HEAD, and that hash goes into mapping_report.json, the capability document and economics_result.json as HiSim's commit. RunMetadata.git_commit (hisim/energy_system/metadata.py:88-108) guards exactly this: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must equal the package root, else None, and its git calls have a timeout (GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). Containers are unaffected, because they read the baked hisim/COMMIT file first.

Proposed fix: one guarded, timed lookup in hisim/hisim_commit.py (the toplevel check and the timeout), which RunMetadata.git_commit calls for the full hash and HiSimCommit shortens, so the two resolvers become one.

Done when: there is one git lookup, it answers None for a hisim package whose directory is not the toplevel of the repository git reports, and a test builds that case (a package directory inside an unrelated temporary git repository) and asserts that neither HiSimCommit nor RunMetadata reports the enclosing commit.

title: Lifecycle economics engine and staged plans
Attest the three staged-economics worked examples, which are still unreviewed
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H7; roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step10_staged_economics.md

title: Decide how *.simulation.json should carry EconomicParameters
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 5; roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11 Q3 (Phase 1)

`SimulationParameters` has a custom `__init__` and its JSONWizard field list does not include
e.g. `country`. To stay strictly additive (identical `*.simulation.json` round-trips),
`economic_parameters` is a plain attribute (default None) set via keyword argument or
`set_economic_parameters()`, not a dataclass field.

A follow-up decision is needed on how `*.simulation.json` should carry it. Spec Q3 proposes
serializing it there, for reproducibility -- which changes the JSON schema of simulation files.

Note: the declarative path has `*.simulation.yaml` files now, so the question is really about
both parameter formats.

Done when: the decision is taken and, if serialization wins, the two parameter formats carry the
block and round-trip.

title: Merge the namespaced lifecycle KPIs into all_kpis.json at cutover
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 6 and 7

Item 6: the new namespaced lifecycle KPIs are written to `lifecycle_kpis.json`, not merged into
`all_kpis.json`, so the legacy KPI JSON stays byte-identical during the parallel phase. The spec
(section 7.3) is ambiguous on whether new names should already appear in the existing KPI
collection; merging them in is a one-line change at cutover.

Item 7, the half that lands with it: `KpiEntry` gained optional `value_min`/`value_max` fields
(spec section 7.3), and dataclass-wizard emits `null` for unset optional fields, so
`all_kpis.json` gains two null keys per entry. This is the one visible (backward-compatible)
change to a legacy artifact; if the JSON golden parity check diffs byte-wise it must be
re-baselined once.

Done when: the cutover happens, the merge lands, and the golden re-baseline is one deliberate
commit.

title: Decide whether a capacity tariff at 3600 s timesteps should fail or be approximated
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 9

`BillingDeterminants` peaks are computed from the meter's power series in postprocessing. If
`seconds_per_timestep` does not divide the billing interval the pre-check fails per spec section
8.4. For setups with 3600 s timesteps and 15-minute intervals this means capacity tariffs simply
cannot be billed.

The source asks: acceptable? (Spec says fail; implemented as fail.)

Done when: the owner confirms the failure, or an approximation with a stated error is allowed.

title: Support simulations longer than a year in the lifecycle engine, or refuse them
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 15

Simulations shorter than a year are annualized by linear extrapolation with a warning (spec
section 3.6 rule 5). Simulations longer than a year are not supported by the lifecycle engine:
the first simulated year is used and a warning is emitted. The spec is silent on multi-year
simulations.

Done when: the spec says what a multi-year simulation means economically, and the engine either
implements it or refuses by name instead of silently using year one.

title: Give a meter a simulated_cost_in_euro hand-off so dynamic tariffs are integrated in-run
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 16 and 17, with the reporting consequence in 29

Item 16: dynamic-tariff in-simulation cost integration (spec section 8.4) is implemented in
postprocessing from the meter power series and the contract's spot series (native resolution).
The optional `simulated_cost_in_euro` hand-off from a meter that already integrated cost during
simulation is honored when present, but no meter currently computes it.

Item 17: the `TariffProvider` component publishes price signals per timestep; the price forecast
publication mirrors what `generic_price_signal.py` does today (24 h horizon). Whether MPC should
consume the new provider already in the parallel phase is a control-side decision (the spec keeps
EMS work out of scope).

Item 29 records the reporting cost: the section 8.5 dynamic-tariff decomposition
(volume/flexibility/capacity) has no report section because no shipped example runs a dynamic
contract yet. The synthetic contract exists; a meter-side cost-integration example is the missing
piece.

Done when: one meter computes `simulated_cost_in_euro` under a dynamic contract, a shipped
example runs it, and the section 8.5 report block exists.

title: Decide whether *_gross perspectives should exclude the anyway-cost credit
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 32, modelling note (b)

The anyway credit is currently booked in gross views too, while spec section 4.1 ties it to the
differential comparison. Worth a review whether `*_gross` perspectives should exclude it -- the
credit is separately reported either way.

Context from the same item: in the German worked example the year-2 "residual value" drop is
58 kEUR of ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT, because the old wall/windows/top-ceiling (1988/1993/1988) have
exactly two years of life left at the 2026 price basis, so section 4.1 books the avoided
like-for-like renovation at year 2.

Done when: the owner decides, the perspectives implement it, and the report goldens move once.

title: Decide whether a weather-year and price-basis-year mismatch gets a report header note
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 28, closing "Open question"

With the economic clock (2026-07-07), subsidy scheme validity, the CO2-price-path anchor and
existing-asset ages follow the price basis year (the economic "today") instead of the possibly
historical weather year -- a 2021 weather year with 2026 economics previously found no valid
2024+ schemes.

Open question: should `WEATHER_YEAR != PRICE_BASIS_YEAR` emit an advisory note in the report
header? It is currently only visible in the parameters line.

Done when: the owner decides and the report does or does not carry the note.

title: Wire or delete the REDUCED_VAT benefit kind, which has no consumer
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 7, discrepancy B7 ("Still open"), and section 8 decision
D1

`REDUCED_VAT` / `PayoutKind.VAT_REDUCTION` awards have no consumer anywhere. W2.2 (commit
d0f6ffe4) typed the payload as `ReducedVatBenefit(vat_rate)` and documented it as unwired at both
ends (the dataclass at `hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py:377` and the award branch at
`solver.py:337`), deliberately neither wiring nor deleting it. D1 says: leave typed, unwired;
wiring is a methodology question deferred until a real scheme needs it.

Decide: wire into `_eligible_cost_basis` VAT netting, or delete the kind.

Related: the VAT reclassification of the migrated price entries (cost_spec Q5) is the methodology
this depends on.

title: Make the subsidy solver and the financing module agree on the repayment-grant basis
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 7, discrepancy B3 ("Fix in W3.2")

The solver values a repayment grant on the gross measure cost
(`hisim/economics/subsidies/solver.py:427-429`, `value += gross * award.loan_repayment_grant_share`)
while financing applies `repayment_grant_share` to the principal
(`hisim/economics/calculators/financing_application.py`, whose own docstring at :26 says "section
7 B3 is preserved, unfixed"). The solver therefore overstates soft loans whenever
`financed_share < 1`; it is masked today because the shipped KfW rate is 0.0.

Done when: one basis is chosen, both sides use it, and a test with `financed_share < 1` pins the
agreement.

title: Settle the six remaining open questions of the cost engine implementation plan
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 6, "Open questions for review"

Six of the eight are still open (2 is resolved behaviourally, 8 is decided and implemented):

1. Package layout depth (section 2.5): sub-packages as proposed, or a flat module with enforced
   import-lint layers only? The import audit shrinks the question -- only `bridge.py`,
   `scenarios.py`, `__main__.py` and the tests import the evaluator. Recommendation: import-lint
   contracts from day 1, physical sub-packages once seam 3 has settled the calculator boundaries.
   Question 2 adds: the physical `data/` vs `engine/` move inside `subsidies.py` is the one thing
   left of seam 2, deferred so importers churn once.
3. Long-timeline examples (section 3.2): individual row labels vs a labelled two-column table
   convention -- decide when the first 40-year example appears.
4. Tolerance policy: a default `abs_tol` per unit (0.01 EUR for money, 1e-6 for rates),
   overridable per cell, or always explicit as currently specified?
5. Which existing tests migrate into the worked-example format vs stay as plain pytest. (The
   VDI-2067 hand examples in `test_economics_engine.py` are the natural first migrations.)
6. Tariff contracts in `economic_inputs.json` (W1.4): embed full contracts vs reference-by-id
   plus an explicit catalog version stamp?
7. Fix-or-freeze decisions for section 7 -- each needs an owner and a call before worked examples
   freeze the affected path. (B3 and B7 are the two still open; see their own issues.)

title: Examine the 48 AI-generated SEAI scheme entries in hisim/subsidy_catalog/IE.json
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H8; hisim/subsidy_catalog/README_IE.md;
roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step11_irish_subsidy_catalogue.md

Owner decision 2026-09-19 was option 1: the SEAI grants are transcribed from
https://www.seai.ie/grants/home-energy-grants (read 2026-09-19) into
`hisim/subsidy_catalog/IE.json` as placeholders a person verifies scheme by scheme. The files
exist (commit f12574ec): `IE.json` (48 schemes), `questions_IE.json` (8 questions, en + de), ten
`src_seai_*_2026` entries in `sources.json`, `README_IE.md` as the review checklist. The data
says so in three places -- every `display_name` ends with ` [AI draft -- needs examination]`,
every `legal_basis` starts with `AI-GENERATED PLACEHOLDER (2026-09-19), NEEDS TO BE EXAMINED --`,
every source note starts with `AI-generated transcription of the page text, not legally
verified` -- and the file carries `review_status: AI_GENERATED_NEEDS_EXAMINATION`.

Nobody has examined a single scheme. Approximations recorded, each a review item: dwelling type
bands the fixed amounts (an end-of-terrace house is paid more and cannot be told apart); cavity
fill and internal dry lining share `WALL_INTERNAL_INSULATION` and are told apart by a `placement`
attribute; the heat pump bundle is three schemes summing to 12 500 / 9 500 EUR; solar PV is pro
rata on the page and encoded as four fixed LUMP_SUM steps on `peak_power_in_kwp` (exact at 1, 2,
3 and 4 kWp, understated in between -- see the TIERED_PER_UNIT issue); the doors grant assumes
two doors; Warmer Homes is a 100 % share excluding every other scheme; the Home Energy Upgrade
Loan's 3 % rate comes from the landlord supports page because the loan page states no rate.

Not encoded, every line a review item: the One Stop Shop B2/uplift outcome, air-to-air heat
pumps, heating controls, the home energy assessment and project management, the expired landlord
tax deduction, MPRN "no previous grant" rules, the whole-surface wall rule, the second-wall-
measure rules, the windows "good insulation / HLI <= 2.3" prerequisite, the heat pump HLI
requirement for pre-2007 homes, approved-housing-body amounts, the traditional-homes pilot,
de minimis / GBER for landlords, and the loan's 75 % rule, 20 % uplift and provider rates.

Done when: a person has examined every scheme, the three placeholder markers and
`review_status` are removed from the entries that pass, and `README_IE.md`'s checklist is closed.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: not part of the MVP; the MVP ships with the data marked as AI draft / to be reviewed. Labelled human: a person does this, implementation agents skip it.

title: Decide the uncertainty-band curation and whether bands reach service lives and emissions
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11, Phase 1 uncertainty questions Q23, Q24, Q25, Q26;
roadmap/cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions" Q25 (bands beyond money -- service lives and emission
factors stay exact in v1)

Q23 -- sources and curation of the min/max bands: who defines the ranges per component type and
energy carrier, and are they maintained as explicit values (proposal, seeded from the spread of
the already-cited sources) or as symmetric +/- x % rules? Entries without a reviewed band stay
degenerate (min = best_estimate = max) rather than getting an invented one.

Q24 -- is the envelope semantics (full correlation toward cheap/expensive, section 3.9)
sufficient for the intended studies, or do some need statistical quantiles? Quantiles would
require distributions plus sampling via the scenario layer -- currently a non-goal.

Q25 -- extending bands beyond money: service lives and emission factors carry at least as much
uncertainty as prices. Proposal (taken provisionally in code): keep them exact in v1, because a
lifetime band changes the replacement structure of the timeline, not just amounts. Revisit after
phase 3.

Q26 -- KPI surface for bands: are the optional `value_min`/`value_max` fields on `KpiEntry`
(section 7.3) enough for the webtool and the RenoVisor frontend, or do bounds need to be separate
KPI entries for the existing plotting pipeline?

Related: `UncertainValue.__sub__` semantics changed while building the comparison view
(roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 26) -- the delta band is the envelope of the three slot deltas, so
"minimum" reads "best-case delta", not "LOW-world delta".

title: Decide the remaining phase 3b to 5 cost-spec questions on tariffs, allocation and scenarios
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_spec.md section 11, the questions not covered by a provisional default in
roadmap/cost_module_issues.md

Q9 (Phase 4) -- income data in RenoVisor requests, needed for income-dependent schemes: privacy
handling. Accept an income band enum rather than an amount?

Q11 (Phase 5) -- which allocation rulesets in v1 beyond `DE_2024`? AT has no modernization-levy
analogue (much simpler ruleset); is a generic `EU_SIMPLE` ruleset -- landlord pays
capex/maintenance, tenant pays energy -- the right fallback for other countries? Ireland now has
data and no ruleset.

Q13 (Phase 5) -- tenant-electricity models (Mieterstrom) for PV in rented buildings: v1 assigns
feed-in revenue to the landlord. Is that acceptable for the intended studies?

Q16 (Phase 3b) -- spot price data: which series ship in the cost database (EPEX day-ahead DE/AT
per simulation year)? Check redistribution licensing. The provisional answer taken in code: no
licensed EPEX data is shipped; a synthetic reference profile generator is provided for tests plus
a documented CSV loader for user-supplied series.

Q20 (Phase 3c) -- default shipped scenario set: which axes and levels constitute the standard
low/central/high bundle (interest, per-carrier escalations, CO2 path), and from which sources?
This is the public face of every study.

Q22 (Phase 3c) -- should the RenoVisor response include the full scenario cube or only the
robustness summary plus tornado data? Proposal: summary by default, full cube behind a request
flag, because of payload size.

Q29 (Phase 1 provenance) -- does the RenoVisor/webtool response need embedded provenance for end
users, or is the stored ledger plus the `explain` CLI sufficient? Proposal: sufficient.

title: Decide what happens to scenario_cube.csv now that scenario_evaluation is gone
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 22; cross-read with roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-25

roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 22 says `scenario_cube.csv` is written in the long format the spec
prescribes so the existing `scenario_evaluation` aggregation can consume it, but no ingestion
code was added on the `scenario_evaluation` side -- "that module aggregates across runs and should
adopt the cube in its own PR".

needs-triage: that module no longer exists. P4 F-25 records that
`hisim/postprocessing/scenario_evaluation/` was moved to `obsolete/` in #541 (2026-08-10) and
left the repository entirely with the rest of that tree in #590. So the cube's intended consumer
is gone and the note in roadmap/cost_module_issues.md is stale.

Decide: give the cube a consumer, keep it as an export for outside tooling, or retire it with the
pyam export question (F-25).

title: Tighten the deliberately generous plausibility thresholds as experience accumulates
description:
Source: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md 26 (report layer, 2026-07-07)

Plausibility thresholds live in `cost_database/plausibility_checks.json` and are deliberately
generous -- they catch unit mix-ups, not modelling disagreements. The source says to tighten them
as experience accumulates.

Done when: the thresholds have been revisited against the runs since 2026-07-07 and either
tightened or confirmed with a dated note.

title: Refactor the economics package for size and maintainability, without losing functionality
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Refactor the economics package so it is smaller and easier to change, without losing any
functionality. Performance is not a goal (the engine runs in milliseconds). Rough target:
code ~19.6k -> 12-13k lines, docstrings ~19k -> 9k, package ~47k -> 22-25k lines.

Phases (children of this epic):
- A, no behaviour change: tests/goldens/cost_summary.md and lifecycle_report.html must stay
  byte-identical, and the invariant tests stay green.
- B, declarative formats: serialization and the staged parameter reader.
- D, deeper structure: the timeline-build calculators, retiring the adapter, a time-aware
  evaluator in place of the staged splice.

Phase C (one chart backend instead of both the SVG and matplotlib layers) is deliberately not
filed yet; it waits for the owner's decision on the PNG set.

The safety net for every child is test_economics_report_goldens.py plus the
test_economics_invariants*.py files. Run targeted test files only, not the full suite.

title: A: Trim the economics docstrings to plain what/example/why/Args form and drop history and review codes
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase A, no behaviour change. Do this first: it touches every file, and the other A items would
conflict with it.

hisim/economics has 1,263 docstrings, median 12 lines; 259 are 20 lines or longer. 136 tell
history ("used to", "review finding 14", "owner decision", "PR #...", "before W4.3"), and the
code carries about 700 internal review codes (W4.3, Q26 F4, R7, V9, D27). That is the essayistic
style the house docstring rule excludes.

Trim each docstring to: what it is -> an example where useful -> a short why -> Args/Returns/Raises.
Keep the § references to cost_spec.md. Drop history, review codes and restated rationale (git and
beads keep them). Also shorten the module docstrings (the package README keeps the tour).

Done when: no docstring recounts history, internal review codes are gone, pure comment/docstring
diff (the AST without docstrings is unchanged), flake8/mypy clean, goldens byte-identical.
Expected: roughly -8k to -10k lines.
close_reason: Done in PR #901 (merged)

title: D: Turn build_timeline into an ordered list of calculators that write into one build record
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase D, deeper structure. Depends on the AnywayCredit record.

EconomicEvaluator.build_timeline (evaluator.py:708) is a ~260-line procedural loop with about 12
accumulators: sunk cost, modernization cost, anyway credits, three anyway dicts, levy asset
classes/costs/credits, replacement flows for the reserve and by subject, decisions, CO2.

Introduce a small calculator interface: each calculator (investment schedule, replaced asset,
maintenance, subsidies, energy, reserve, CO2 damage, financing) takes the per-subject costing and
the evaluation context, returns entries, and records its side outputs into one build record
(CO2, levy basis, anyway credits, decisions, sunk cost). build_timeline becomes an ordered list
of calculators. Entry order must stay exactly as today (CashFlowTimeline.npv accumulates in
entry order; the goldens pin it).

Done when: build_timeline is a short orchestration over the calculator list, TimelineBuildResult
is the build record, goldens byte-identical.

title: D: Move the cost adapter's class-name extractors onto the components and delete the adapter tables
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase D, deeper structure.

adapter.py (1,013 lines) maps component classes to cost facts and meter specs through
class-name-keyed tables (FactsExtractors at adapter.py:166 with 14 extractors,
MeterOutputContracts, DeviceEnergySpecs, UsefulHeatSources), while only 5 component modules
implement get_cost_facts(). The adapter is documented as shrinking "as adoption grows".

Move each extractor into its component as get_cost_facts() / get_energy_flow_facts() (and the
energy-balance / useful-heat declarations as class attributes), then delete the corresponding
adapter tables. Related: hisim-economics-engine-cyc.8 (adapter coverage of district heating and EMS-as-meter) and
hisim-cost-data-l07.12 (PRICED classes no facts source can price) should land on the component side instead
of the adapter. Whether this waits for the phase-7 cutover is the owner decision this issue
depends on; the legacy parity harness (audit.write_parity_report) and hisim-orsv go with it.

Done when: adapter.py holds no class-name tables (or is gone),
test_economics_adapter_contract.py and test_economics_extraction.py pass against the components.

title: D: Write the design note for a time-aware evaluator that prices staged plans without splicing
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase D, deeper structure. Design note first; the implementation is a separate issue.

StagedEvaluator (staged.py, a 1,413-line class) prices a staged plan by evaluating every stage
over the whole horizon and then splicing the timelines. The splice has to recompute engine
mechanisms after the fact: re-dated replacements, residual values from the plan's last
installation (_residual_entries), the re-levelized replacement reserve
(_staged_reserve_flows), the CO2 splice (_splice_co2) and an equivalent annual heat demand
(_equivalent_annual_heat), and it hand-builds a LifecycleCostResult (_aggregate).

Alternative: make the core evaluator time-aware. Each subject carries its install year; billing
determinants carry the years in which they are active; a normal run is a one-stage plan. The
residual, reserve, CO2 and heat-cost mechanics then run once, in the engine.

Write a design note (roadmap/economics/) that covers: the input model (per-subject install year,
per-stage billing and active years, register ageing), subsidies per stage year and the price basis
per stage, what changes in EvaluationInputs/economic_inputs.json, which E-spec §1.3 invariants
carry over (one-stage plan == plain evaluation, entry for entry), and a migration path that keeps
tests/economics/test_staged*.py and tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py as the oracle.
Answers the owner question on replacing the splice.

title: Decide whether the staged splice is replaced by a time-aware evaluator
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Owner decision: replace the staged splice with a time-aware evaluator?

staged.py prices a plan by splicing per-stage evaluations and recomputing residuals, reserve, CO2
and heat demand after the fact. A time-aware core evaluator (install year per subject, billing
active per year range) would do this once, in the engine, and delete most of the splice
machinery, but it changes EvaluationInputs and economic_inputs.json and is the riskiest item of
the refactor. The design-note issue lays out the details; this question records the go/no-go.

title: D: Replace the staged splice with the time-aware evaluator
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase D, deeper structure. Implements the time-aware evaluator design note; blocked on it and on
the derived-aggregates result.

Replace the splice in staged.py with the time-aware evaluator: StagedEvaluator shrinks to
building the time-indexed inputs from the stages and calling the engine once; _splice,
_assemble, _residual_entries, _staged_reserve_flows, _splice_co2, _equivalent_annual_heat and
_aggregate go away. StagedResult and the economics_result.json document keep their contract.

Done when: tests/economics/test_staged*.py, tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py and the
worked examples reproduce, economics_result.schema.json unchanged, staged.py substantially
smaller (the splice machinery is roughly 1k lines).

title: D: Remove the renovisor imports from hisim.economics so the engine no longer depends on the translator above it
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document).

Layering inversion: hisim.economics is a lower layer than hisim.renovisor (the translator calls
the engine), but economics imports renovisor. The only imports of hisim.renovisor outside
hisim/renovisor are:
- hisim/economics/__main__.py:161-163: MainSubjectError, MainSubjects, MeasureSubjects
  (renovisor/economics.py), MappingReport (renovisor/report.py) and CatalogueTable
  (renovisor/request.py), all used by the 600-line StagedCli class of the `staged` subcommand,
  which reads each stage's RenoVisor mapping report and measure list.
- hisim/economics/staged_document.py:626: a function-local import of renovisor.report.HiSimCommit
  for the document's engine/commit block.
As a side effect, importing the economics CLI pulls in renovisor and, through its vocabulary,
component modules (import hisim.economics.__main__ takes about 1.3 s).

Fix the direction:
- Move the RenoVisor-specific half of `staged` (reading mapping reports, measure subjects, main
  subjects, the catalogue table) into hisim/renovisor, and let economics take a neutral per-stage
  record (stage directory, year, label, measures as plain data). Whether the command stays
  reachable as `python -m hisim.economics staged` or moves to `python -m hisim.renovisor staged`
  is an owner decision to take in the PR (the backend calls it; check before renaming).
- Move HiSimCommit (or the part staged_document needs) to a neutral module below both, e.g. under
  hisim/ utilities, and import it from there in both packages.
- Put StagedCli in its own module (economics/staged/cli.py or the renovisor side) instead of
  __main__.py.

Done when: grep finds no hisim.renovisor import under hisim/ outside hisim/renovisor,
tests/economics/test_staged_cli.py and tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py pass, and the
staged command's behaviour and exit codes are unchanged.
close_reason: Done in PR #903 (merged)

title: A: Declare every CostCategory property once, in one CategorySpec table, replacing the ten scattered category tables
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase A, no behaviour change.

The CostCategory taxonomy is declared in about ten separate per-category tables:
timeline.CategoryRules, calculators/categories.py, views.ViewCategories,
views.FlowCounterparties.BY_CATEGORY, views.LandlordStatementCategories.LABELS,
views.StatementPartitions, views.BurdenCategories, staged.StagedCategories (staged.py:127),
staged_document.CostGroups (staged_document.py:112), presentation_style.PresentationStyle groups,
plausibility.PlausibilityCategories. Adding a category means editing all of them, and several
carry runtime "not declared" checks only because of that.

Replace them with one CategorySpec per CostCategory member (frozen dataclass in the timeline
kernel): sign, band mirroring (revenue-type), investment-caused, subsidy flow, bill part, display
group, document cost group, actor-flow counterparty, cash vs. accounting credit, statement label,

title: Add a TIERED_PER_UNIT benefit kind so the SEAI solar PV grant is paid pro rata
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H16

Observed: the engine's benefit kinds are `SHARE_OF_ELIGIBLE_COST | BONUS_SHARE | LUMP_SUM |
PER_UNIT | TAX_CREDIT | REDUCED_VAT | SOFT_LOAN | OPERATIONAL`. None expresses "an amount per
unit that changes by tier and is capped": `PER_UNIT` has no cap and no tiers, `LUMP_SUM` does not
scale. SEAI's solar PV grant is exactly that shape -- 700 EUR/kWp up to 2 kWp, 200 EUR/kWp up to
4 kWp, capped at 1 800 EUR, paid pro rata -- so `IE.json` approximates it with four `LUMP_SUM`
steps on `measure.technical_attributes.peak_power_in_kwp`. The steps are exact at 1, 2, 3 and
4 kWp and understate everything between them (a 2.5 kWp array is paid 1 400 EUR instead of
1 500 EUR).

Done when: a `TIERED_PER_UNIT` benefit kind exists in `hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py`
with a tier list and an overall cap, the solver values it, and the four `IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_*`
schemes collapse into one that reproduces the page's own example (2.5 kWp -> 1 500 EUR).

This is a HiSim engine change, not a contract one.
close_reason: Done: BenefitKind.TIERED_PER_UNIT with TieredPerUnitBenefit {tiers[{up_to|null, amount_per_unit}], cap_in_euro|null}, validated at load (non-empty, ascending, only the last open, no negative amount or cap, cap not below the first tier's full value); the solver values it on ComponentCostFacts.size (kWp for PV, confirmed: PVSystem power_in_watt * 1e-3, the same number as the peak_power_in_kwp attribute) and clamps it to the eligible basis. IE.json: the four IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_* steps are one IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV (Warmer Homes' exclusions repointed); README_IE.md and the source note updated. 1->700, 2->1400, 2.5->1500, 3->1600, 4+->1800; validate exits 0; the end-to-end staged run passes.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-09-20: MVP. Specification:
1. hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py: BenefitKind.TIERED_PER_UNIT with payload TieredPerUnitBenefit {tiers: [{up_to: number|null, amount_per_unit: number}], cap_in_euro: number|null}; tiers ascending by up_to, the last may be open (null). Value for size s: sum over tiers of amount_per_unit * (min(s, up_to_i) - up_to_{i-1}) for the covered range, capped at cap_in_euro; unit is ComponentCostFacts.size's unit (kW for PV — confirm the PV facts' size is kWp and that the translator's peak_power_in_kwp attribute agrees).

3. IE.json: the four IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_* schemes collapse into one IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV with tiers [{up_to: 2, amount_per_unit: 700}, {up_to: 4, amount_per_unit: 200}], cap 1800, same eligibility; README_IE.md and the sources note drop the step approximation; questions file unchanged.

title: Above 600 s a part-loaded device splits its part-load ratio into run time and power: it runs the whole step at the ratio's power down to its minimal power and cycles only below it
description:
Owner, 2026-10-18: the part-load ratio r is the share of time a machine runs times its share of power; 25 % can be 25 % of the time at full power or 50 % of the time at half power.

Model: a modulating machine runs at p = max(r, p_min) for tau = r / p of the step (p_min = minimal power / full power). The buffer, the part-load rules, the energy, the step-mean flows and temperatures stay as they are (at a fixed lift the flow scales with the power, so the mean flow is r times the full-load flow either way).

What changes:
- Published run time grows by tau * dt; a step with r >= p_min is continuous running, no start. In the cycling range (r < p_min) the starts per step follow from the minimum times: dt / max(t_run_min / tau, t_idle_min / (1 - tau)), so the cycle KPI becomes an estimate comparable with 60 s.
- The boiler burns at the efficiency of the part-load power, eta(p * P_max). Do this after the P1 bead on the boiler efficiency rising with burner power, or fuel moves the wrong way.
- The hplib heat pump's COP depends only on temperatures, so its electricity does not move; only run time and cycles do.

State before this bead: #1011 (the fold of stage D PRs 5 to 8) fixed only the bookkeeping: a space-heating step at ratio 0 publishes the heat pump as off, the control timers that the minimum times read are unchanged.
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-19: part 1 covers only the hplib heat pump first (it has minimum run and idle times and already publishes run time and starts on its bookkeeping track): run time grows by tau*dt, starts are estimated from its own minimum times. Devices without minimum times (gas, oil, hydrogen burners, the collector pump, a heat pump with cycling off) and run-time/start KPIs for the boiler and the collector moved to a separate bead. Part 2 (boiler efficiency at p) still waits for hisim-component-physics-4g9.66.

title: Pick the weather station from the postcode rather than one station per country
description:
Source: hisim-bc02 (owner request 2026-09-26): every entry of hisim/renovisor/not_implemented_yet.yaml names the bead that would let it be deleted.

Entry: path location.postcode (note: One weather station per country; the postcode is recorded and has no target). Germany alone has 15 DWD TRY regions; a postcode-to-station lookup would make the climate local. Needs the lookup table and the stations in the image.

title: Every component's energy balance closes, and a Sankey per energy carrier shows where the energy goes
description: Owner (cmf, 2026-09-28), prompted by the storage energy gap (hisim-component-physics-4g9.16, PR #864): introduce energy balances in HiSim and Sankeys per energy carrier across all devices, to find other devices that create or lose energy. Today only 6 of 46 component modules set ComponentOutput.sankey_flow_direction, and PostProcessor.export_sankeys is an empty stub.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decisions (cmf, 2026-09-29): (1) contract = annotate outputs: each energy-carrying ComponentOutput gets an explicit role IN/OUT/LOSS/STORED_CHANGE replacing sankey_flow_direction; a component adds outputs for losses/storage changes that are not outputs yet. (2) check in post-processing, vectorised over the result arrays. (3) report by default (balance_report.json + WARNING), a strict mode fails the run (tests/CI). (4) explicit environment nodes: ambient heat, solar, outdoors. (5) heat carriers: SH heat, DHW heat, cooling; a water flow counts by m*c*dT. (8) PR 1 = .1 .2 .9 + storages/HDS (.3); PR 2 = heat generators (.4).

description: Carriers: electricity, gas, oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen, district heat, heat SH, heat DHW, ambient heat, solar. Build on ComponentOutput.sankey_flow_direction but make carrier and role explicit (in/out/loss/stored) instead of a boolean. Epic hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.

title: Sweep every system setup with the balance report and Sankeys and open a bug for each imbalance
