title: Without a buffer vessel, district heating bills the space heat its controller asks for, not what the distribution system delivers
description: generic_district_heating.py:707-719 computes m*c*dT_needed while heat_distribution_system.py:563 books its own exchange with the building: 30.8 kWh/yr sent but never received (7.8 kW at the first step, ~130 W per step while the HDS controller is off). Found by the energy-balance hunt (hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo PR 2, feat/energy-balance-generators 56454425, 2026-09-29); analysis in /home/cmf/eb2_work/analysis.txt.
close_reason: Superseded by hisim-pnw7 (owner, 2026-10-20). Investigation on main 49b04e38c (report /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/9uoo12/report.md): the filed defect (7.8 kW first step, ~130 W per valve-off step, +30.8 kWh/yr) is gone since #1007. What remains has the opposite sign and sits in the heat distribution system: without a buffer it publishes the previous step's return and delivered heat and has no pipe-water store, so the substation (whose bill m c (T_sup - T_ret_pub) is right by the black-box rule) bills -6.0 / -17.6 / -44.7 kWh/yr (-0.05 / -0.16 / -0.41 %) less than the building receives at 60 / 900 / 3600 s. pnw7's pipe-water node closes it exactly per step (measured at 60 and 900 s); that is pnw7's acceptance criterion.

title: A heat pump cooling through a buffer vessel books its cooling: the vessel accepts negative heat, and the cooling and its electricity reach a meter
description: Since PR #864 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.16) a water storage accepts no heat from a flow colder than itself, so a MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib in cooling mode (mode 2, floor heating) into a buffer booked zero cooling and zero electricity; #864 makes that configuration fail loudly instead (owner decision 2026-09-30). Wanted: the storage booking rule gets a cooling branch (cold water lowers the vessel temperature; accepted negative heat bounded like the heating side), the heat pump books cooling and its electricity by the accepted share, and cooling electricity and brine-pump electricity reach the electricity meter (see hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.15). Then remove the refusal. No setup or RenoVisor path uses mode 2 today. The passive brine-cooling branch of MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib.i_simulate (passive_cooling_with_brine, on_off == -1) has no test; cover it when cooling is enabled (hydronic stage F).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10 (hydronic-stage-c): the passive brine-cooling branch now has a unit test, tests/test_heat_pump_flow_booking.py::test_passive_cooling_books_the_heat_its_flow_draws_and_only_the_brine_pump_s_electricity.

title: The Sankeys draw every link in one grey and the heat pump's electricity as coming from the energy manager
description: Found by the aggregate chart review (2026-10-15; loop-design/chart_review_aggregates.md S3, S4, S6). In overall.html every link is grey, so electricity and heat cannot be told apart: colour links by carrier (a colour-blind-safe palette such as Okabe-Ito)? The heat pump's electricity input is wired to L2EMSElectricityController's dispatch output, so its peer node is the energy manager, not the grid, PV or battery the energy comes from: draw a controller peer through to the physical source, or wait for the meter, PV and battery to declare ports? And should the Sankeys also be written as PNG/SVG (kaleido) for the PDF report?
notes:
Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md): D1 - controllers and meters are not nodes of the energy Sankey; electricity flows between physical devices through a house electricity bus (a node formed from the declared electricity ports, not a component), and the grid is a boundary node taken from the bus's per-step residual, with the meter only as a cross-check. D2 - one connected all-carrier diagram in which energy changes carrier along the chain (appliance electricity becomes internal gains in the building, heat-pump electricity plus ambient heat becomes heat through buffer, tank and distribution into the building, losses branch off at every node, storages show charge, discharge and stored change); per-carrier views stay only as filters of that graph. Built by PR 1 of the spec, links coloured by carrier.

Owner decision Q-J 2026-10-20 revises D1 (roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md §2, §4.3, §4.4, §8): no bus. "HiSim explicitly does not use buses as a concept"; the house electricity bus closed by construction, so electricity a declared port got wrong or missed vanished into grid import or export. Removed with its derived residual from code, spec, report schema and tests. Every meter that declares what it meters (Component.metered_exchanges) is a node under its own name between its boundary node (grid import/export, <carrier> supply) and the devices whose metered ports it reads through explicit connections, traced through exempt controllers (the energy manager's sum reaches the ElectricityMeter, so each device links to the meter). Grid import and export are the meter's published outputs. Controllers stay exempt and are never nodes. Built in PR 1 (#1086).
close_reason: Built by PR 1 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md as decided by D1 (revised by Q-J), D2 and D4: controllers are exempt and never nodes; there is no bus; every meter is a node under its own name between its boundary node and the devices whose metered ports it reads, directly or through exempt controllers; grid import and export are the meter's published outputs; per step a meter's published exchange must equal what it reads, and a gap beyond the tolerance is a red unaccounted flow at the meter; every bought carrier's flow passes a meter, else it is an unmetered finding; overall.html is the one connected all-carrier graph with per-carrier views as its filters; links are coloured by carrier (Okabe-Ito). The PNG/SVG export question of this bead was not part of D1, D2 or D4; it is bead hisim-4hed (Q-I).

title: The energy Sankey can also be drawn with arrows, losses branching off at the side of each device, sources on the left and sinks on the right
description:
Owner decision D4 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md (2026-10-19): the complete Sankey starts with plotly, the interactive HTML of today; the owner prefers arrows in the style of his data-center picture (matplotlib.sankey-like, losses as side branches), whose automatic layout is involved, so it is a later step. The graph model of the spec does not depend on the drawing; this bead adds a second renderer of the same graph.

What it needs: orientation rules per node kind (component, bus, boundary, loss, storage change, unaccounted): a loss leaves its device sideways as a branch, a storage change goes up or down; sources (grid import, fuel and district-heat supply, sun, ambient heat, residents' body heat) are ordered on the left and sinks (grid export, outdoors, hot water drawn) on the right, the chain in between ordered by its longest path from a source; matplotlib.sankey needs each flow's orientation and the order of diagrams joined with prior/connect, which this layout has to derive from the graph; a static image (PNG/SVG) for the PDF report.

Done when: one twin per heating system draws the arrow diagram from the same energy_sankey.json as the plotly one, every flow above a threshold labelled, and the owner has reviewed it. After PR 6 of the spec.

title: Check every component's energy balance per timestep after convergence and report the residuals
description: Residual = in - out - losses - delta U per component, carrier and timestep, checked after convergence (like the storages' i_doublecheck). A tolerance, a collect mode that lists every residual at the end (like HISIM_WRITE_GUARD=collect), and balance_report.json in the results.
close_reason: Confirmed built (spec §9): hisim/postprocessing/energy_balance/check.py computes the residual per component and step with the owner's tolerance, runs in every simulation, lists every failing component and link in one error and writes balance_report.json; #870. PR 1 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md re-points the generators' fuel and electricity ports to the meter that reads them (owner decision Q-J, no bus): the fuel through its gas or fuel meter from '<carrier> supply', the electricity through the ElectricityMeter, directly or through the exempt energy manager; grid import and export are the meter's published outputs, and a meter's gap between what it publishes and what it reads is an unaccounted flow.

title: The build refuses a water circuit whose pumping end publishes a flow nobody reads while another component reads its supply temperature (one pump owner per circuit)
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-22, from the circuit audit (/home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/circuits/report.md, main 9b092df16). hydronic_coupling_spec.md §3.1 (one pump owner per circuit; the other end reads its flow) and component_design_principles B4 are written down but enforced nowhere: gas_boiler_household wired a boiler and a heat distribution system that each pump their own flow on one circuit, and the boiler booked 33 % more heat than was delivered (hisim-boiler-circuit-flow-gap-g2mx). The energy-balance check could not see it, because the distribution system declares no ports without a buffer.

Rule: refuse, before step 1, an OUT circuit end whose mass flow is its own output when another energy-moving component reads its supply temperature but nobody reads its flow. Where: Wiring.circuits / refuse_a_broken_wiring of #1109 (hisim/postprocessing/energy_balance/ports.py), run in Simulator.run_all_timesteps, so both the YAML and the Python modes are covered. It does not need the distribution system to declare ports, so district heating is not affected. Derived from the wiring dump, it refuses exactly gas_boiler_household, the mockup energy_system_mockup_minimal.yaml and tests/energy_systems/uc1.realized.energy_system.yaml, which the a2 fix of g2mx repairs first. Idle circuits whose temperature nobody reads (the boiler's hot-water side in gas_boiler_household and basic_household_only_heating) are not hit. Mind the two dead mandatory flow inputs (DistrictHeating and ElectricHeating WaterInputMassFlowRateFromWarmWaterStorage), unless R2 has removed them.

Done when: the rule refuses a test that wires boiler -> distribution system without reading the boiler's flow, names both ends, and every recorded energy system still builds.

title: Declare the energy ports of the water storages and the heat distribution system
description: The pattern PR #864 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.16) established for SimpleHotWaterStorage, SimpleDHWStorage and HeatDistribution.

title: Declare the energy ports of the heat generators: boilers, heat pump, district heating, electric heating, solar thermal
description: GenericBoiler (all fuels), MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib (ambient heat as its own inflow), DistrictHeating, ElectricHeating, SolarThermalSystem.
close_reason: Confirmed built (spec §9): boiler, heat pump, district heating, electric heating and solar thermal declare their ports and close, tests/test_energy_balance_generators.py; #871. PR 1 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md re-points the generators' fuel and electricity ports to the meter that reads them (owner decision Q-J, no bus): the fuel through its gas or fuel meter from '<carrier> supply', the electricity through the ElectricityMeter, directly or through the exempt energy manager; grid import and export are the meter's published outputs, and a meter's gap between what it publishes and what it reads is an unaccounted flow.

title: Declare the energy ports of the electricity devices: PV, battery, EMS, meters, cars and chargers, appliance loads, air conditioners
description: Battery charge/discharge losses explicit; the LPG/appliance load as a sink.
notes: PR 2 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md (2026-10-20, branch sankey-pr2-electricity) declared the ports of section 5.3: PVSystem (AC electricity out, read by the energy manager and through it by the ElectricityMeter; new SolarPowerOnModulesInWatt, the plane-of-array irradiance times the module area, solar in from the sun; new ModuleAndInverterLossInWatt, solar loss to outdoors, Q-D), Battery (ChargingPower in and DischargingPower out, both naming AcBatteryPowerUsed, the signed output the energy manager reads, as their peer output, so they link to the meter; StoredEnergyIncreaseInWattHour stored; new InverterLossInWatt = AC - DC and CellLossInWatt = DC - stored increase per second as losses) and UtspLpgConnector (electricity in from the meter, body heat in from the residents, device heat and new BodyHeatToBuildingInWatt as room heat out to the building, new ApplianceElectricityNotReleasedIndoorsInWatt as electricity loss). All three close in every step of the heat-pump and gas twins over 2021 at 900 s; no KPI moved. The energy manager is exempt, the meter is a node (Q-J). Still open here: the car and its battery and charger (PR 5b), the air conditioners (PR 5a); this bead closes with PR 5b.

title: Declare the energy ports of the building: gains against losses and the thermal mass
description: Internal, solar and HDS gains vs transmission and ventilation losses plus delta U of the thermal mass. The building closes in its own model, so this checks the wiring, not the physics.

title: Declare the energy ports of the remaining components, or exempt each one with a reason
description: Gas/fuel/heating meters, hydrogen, CHP and everything else, so every component is declared or explicitly exempt.

title: Check the system-level balance per carrier: what enters the house equals what is used, lost or stored
description: Meters, sun and ambient heat in = consumption + losses + delta U of all storages, per carrier. Catches energy lost between components (a wiring bug) that per-component balances miss.
notes:
Owner decision Q-J 2026-10-20 (spec §4.4, §8) defines the system balance per carrier: no derived bus; every meter is a node, and per step what it publishes (import minus export) must equal what it reads (the IN minus OUT ports of the devices linked to it), within the balance's tolerance; a gap is a red unaccounted flow at the meter and a failing 'meters' entry, never absorbed. Every metered port (electricity or a bought carrier, IN/OUT) must pass a meter, else it is an 'unmetered' finding. Both are built in PR 1 (#1086) and enforced per Q-H once no component is undeclared (PR 6). Known unmetered ports today: the heat pump's ElectricalInputPowerForCooling and ElectricalInputPowerBrinePump, which nothing reads (hisim-component-physics-4g9.39).

Electricity part measured with PR 2 (2026-10-20, Q-J): with PV, battery and occupancy declared, the ElectricityMeter publishes what it reads in all 35,040 steps of 2021 at 900 s: heat-pump twin import 1,792.2 and export 18,709.7 kWh against the devices' 11,938.7 kWh taken and 28,856.2 kWh given, largest per-step residual 5.9e-9 kWh; gas twin 511.4 / 21,425.4 against 7,329.1 / 28,243.2, largest 8.9e-16 kWh. The GasMeter publishes exactly what the boiler burns (17,384.8 kWh, largest per-step residual 4.4e-16 kWh). Reported, not enforced, while a component is undeclared (Q-H). Unmetered in the heat-pump twin: the heat pump's ElectricalInputPowerForCooling and ElectricalInputPowerBrinePump (0 kWh there; hisim-component-physics-4g9.39).

title: Write a Sankey per energy carrier from the declared ports, with residuals as an unaccounted node
description: Implement PostProcessor.export_sankeys (plotly is a dependency): one diagram per carrier plus all carriers, yearly totals, residuals as a red 'unaccounted' node and undeclared components as 'undeclared' (a coverage view). Written to the results under a new post-processing option.
close_reason: Confirmed built (spec §9): sankey.py wrote one diagram per carrier plus overall with the unaccounted and undeclared nodes under EXPORT_ENERGY_BALANCE; #870, numbers on the nodes since #1019. PR 1 replaces the per-carrier diagrams by the connected graph and its filters (D2, hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.18). PR 1 of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md re-points the generators' fuel and electricity ports to the meter that reads them (owner decision Q-J, no bus): the fuel through its gas or fuel meter from '<carrier> supply', the electricity through the ElectricityMeter, directly or through the exempt energy manager; grid import and export are the meter's published outputs, and a meter's gap between what it publishes and what it reads is an unaccounted flow.

title: Check the comfort grades through a real full-year run
description:
Every test of the comfort grades (PR #815, hisim-sska) feeds synthetic KPI values or a stand-in
Building: tests/test_building_comfort_kpis.py calls the degree-hour functions and the Building's KPI
method on a stand-in, tests/renovisor/test_kpis.py builds the kpis block from a hand-made
all_kpis.json. Nothing runs the chain Building -> all_kpis.json -> KpiBuilder -> result.json end to
end. A full-year check belongs in a slow job (HPC harness or nightly), not the base tier (owner
decision: no new slow test now): run one RenoVisor request over a full year and assert that
result.json carries graded comfort.heating, comfort.cooling and summer_heat_protection with
SIMULATED provenance, and that the degree-hours in their source strings match the two Building KPIs
in all_kpis.json, rounded to one decimal (a full-year period is graded unscaled, owner decision
2026-09-25).

title: The DWD 10- and 15-minute weather readers swap latitude and longitude, so their sun position is computed near 6°N / 50.8°E
description:
Source: the analysis of hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.4 (2026-10-14). `get_coordinates` reads the coordinates of the DWD_10MIN and DWD_15MIN files as `row[1]` = latitude, but their header is `location,longitude,latitude`; for the shipped Düsseldorf file the sun position is computed at about 6°N / 50.8°E. ERA5 is probably affected too (no ERA5 file is shipped to check). No energy system or golden uses these sources today.

Fix: read the coordinates by header name; a test pins latitude/longitude for each source format with a shipped file.

Done when: every weather reader returns the file's latitude and longitude, pinned by a test.
close_reason: get_coordinates now reads the station header by its labels (calculation.StationHeader): the CSV formats by column name (NSRDB_15MIN 'Location ID'/'Latitude'/'Longitude'; DWD_10MIN, DWD_15MIN and ERA5 'location'/'latitude'/'longitude'), the .dat files of DWD_TRY and NSRDB by 'Ort'/'Breitengrad'/'Längengrad'; a missing label raises ValueError naming it. DWD 10/15-minute and ERA5 now yield the station's latitude and longitude instead of the swapped pair; all 45 catalogue locations (DWD_TRY, NSRDB, NSRDB_15MIN) read identically to before, so no golden moves. tests/test_weather_coordinates.py pins name, latitude and longitude for every format with a shipped file, ERA5 with a tmp_path fixture, a reordered header, and the refusals.

title: The generic heat pump's controller becomes an explicit state machine (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (generic heat pump): GenericHeatPumpController (generic_heat_pump.py): heating, cooling, off, the mode hysteresis and minimum times. The hplib heat pump is covered by hisim-component-physics-4g9.41.

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Calibrate the hplib heat pump from a stated seasonal efficiency in percent (SPF)
description: Source: owner decision 2026-09-26 (not_implemented_yet review). house.heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent is a boiler's figure, but the schema admits up to 400 %, which reads like a heat pump's seasonal performance factor. On an air-source heat pump HiSim ignores it (not_implemented_yet). If the frontend means the SPF (asked on renovisorissues), calibrate hplib from it like the EN 14825 SCOP pair does (hisim-component-physics-4g9.15 machinery), or refuse the combination.

title: The Building warns that HeatingByResidents/HeatingByDevices are not connected although they are
description: Source: renovisorissues #35 (backend, 2026-09-23), checked 2026-09-25. Every RenoVisor run (and the household_heatpump_building_sizer twin) logs 'the HeatingByResidents input is not connected. Internal heat gains from occupants default to 0 W' (and the same for HeatingByDevices), yet component_connections.json carries both links from UTSPConnector and Building_InternalHeatGainsFromOccupancy equals the connector's residents + devices (511 W mean on a January run). The warning is emitted before the energy system's connections are resolved. Fix: log it only when the input is still unconnected after wiring (find where the Building emits it, and where the energy-system loader resolves default connections). Answer #35 with the PR.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/building-gains-warning (uncommitted): the check ran in i_prepare_simulation, but Simulator.run_all_timesteps resolves source_output in connect_all_components after preparing every component, so it warned on every run. Moved to a once-only check on the first simulated timestep (Building.warn_about_unconnected_internal_heat_gains). New tests/test_building_internal_heat_gains_warning.py (wired: no warning; unwired: one warning per input, 0 W). One-day household_heatpump_building_sizer run: warning gone, 142 result files byte-identical. occupancy_identity note is correct (only generic_car reads it). Answer renovisorissues #35 with the PR.

title: RenoVisor baseline stage is awarded the IE heat-pump central-heating grant for its existing radiators
description:
Surfaced by the renovisorissues #50 fix (existing_heating now in the RenoVisor subsidy context).

Staged run of the vendored IE mockup (gas boiler -> air-source HP), baseline (no measures) and package, both year 0:
IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE is now AWARDED -2000 EUR in stage 0 (baseline) as well as in stage 1, both rows with measure_id None.
Before the fix both rows were UNDETERMINED (asking building.existing_heating.asset_class), which masked this.

Causes (pre-existing, not introduced by #50):
1. The heat distribution system is not in the RenoVisor existing-asset register (DeviceAssets.ALL has only pv_system and battery), so the simulated radiators are measure_kind INSTALL in every stage (calculators/subsidy_application.py: REPLACE iff replaced_asset), including the do-nothing baseline.
2. IE.json's central-heating scheme applies_to heat-distribution asset classes and conditions only on actor, year, dwelling type and existing_heating.asset_class != HeatPump; nothing requires that a heat pump is installed in the same stage.
3. The stage-1 distribution row carries measure_id None although the package's heating_installation measure installs it (result.subjects has no entry for the distribution component).

Effect: the baseline is credited a grant it would never get; the package-minus-baseline delta for this scheme nets to 0 instead of -2000.
close_reason: Resolved by registering the existing equipment (renovisorissues #48, owner decisions 2026-09-26): the heat distribution system, buffer, hot-water cylinder and meters are ExistingAssets of every stage, so the do-nothing baseline keeps its radiators, books no investment and no longer meets IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE at all; heating_system keeps the radiators, so an oil/gas plan without heating_installation gets no central-heating row either; a heating_installation measure replaces the emitters (REPLACE) and the grant is awarded once, on stage 1, with measure_id heating_installation. Left for the owner, catalogue unchanged: the scheme still has no condition that a heat pump is installed with the emitters (cause 2).

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Follow-up (owner decisions 2026-09-26, same worktree): cause 2 is now fixed in the catalogue too. IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE/_APARTMENT require package.installed_asset_classes contains HeatPump (new computed condition root package.*, filled per evaluation by EconomicEvaluator from the §4.1 installation verdict); IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_UNIT_HOUSE/_APARTMENT require building.existing_heating.asset_class != HeatPump. heating_installation alone on an oil/gas house: central-heating row ineligible; with heating_system in the same stage: awarded once.

title: The solar-thermal collector reads the direct normal irradiance the weather publishes, like the PV system and the building, instead of computing its own
description:
Source: second LLM review round of #1032 (2026-10-19), owner decision the same day: own PR after the mid-year chain.

The collector (hisim/components/solar_thermal_system.py) computes its own direct normal irradiance from the weather's global and diffuse irradiance with pvlib. The PV system and the building read the DNI the weather publishes, which clamps the sun's zenith at 87 degrees, so near sunrise and sunset the collector sees a different sky than the other solar components. #1032 already made the collector read the weather's sun position.

Wanted: the collector reads the weather's published DNI (one source of DNI for every solar component). Moves the three solar-thermal goldens once (expected small: the clamp matters only at a very low sun); bless on the PR.

Done when: the collector reads the weather's DNI, a test shows PV, building gains and collector see the same DNI for one step, the solar-thermal goldens are re-blessed.

title: A stated maximal power of the boiler, the electric heating or district heating, or a stated buffer volume, that is not finite or not above 0 builds: refuse it as the heat pump and the battery do
description:
Source: review of PR #1017 (size guards), findings R15 and R19 (review-evals/review1017_evaluation.md).

#1017 made the hplib heat pump and the bslib battery refuse a stated size that is not finite or not above 0, because a number in a config: block switches the sizing law off and nothing else checks it. The sibling heat generators have the same gap: GenericBoilerConfig.maximal_thermal_power_in_watt, ElectricHeatingConfig.maximum_electric_power_w and DistrictHeatingConfig.connected_load_in_w are sized fields, and a stated 0, -8000 or NaN builds. Each publishes the value unchecked as the sizing fact maximal_thermal_power_in_watt (sizing_facts in generic_boiler.py, generic_electric_heating.py, generic_district_heating.py), and the buffer vessel's volume law (simple_water_storage.py, VOLUME_LAW) turns it into a volume of 0 l, a negative volume or NaN. The buffer itself (SimpleHotWaterStorage) does not refuse such a volume either; only SimpleDHWStorage does (refuse_a_tank_without_water).

Done when: the boiler, the electric heating and district heating refuse a stated maximal power that is not finite or not above 0 when they are built and in their sizing facts, and SimpleHotWaterStorage refuses a volume that is not finite or not above 0 when it is built, each with a ValueError naming the component, the field, the unit and the value; tests fail without each guard; no shipped energy system changes. If the predicate is written a fifth time, consider one shared helper for 'finite and above a bound' (review 1017 R3/R4).

title: A storage reads the flow of every circuit whose temperature it reads: the buffer's flows are mandatory, a secondary coil is wired whole or not at all
description:
Source: hydronic circuit audit of origin/main 9b092df16 (2026-10-22), section 2, option R2; owner decision 2026-10-22.

Several receivers took a circuit's supply temperature as a mandatory input and its mass flow as an optional one. An unwired input reads 0, so a file wiring the temperature without the flow made the generator book heat the store never saw. Default connections wire both, but an explicit input list of an energy-system file can wire one.

Do: (1) SimpleHotWaterStorage.WaterMassFlowRateFromHeatGenerator and WaterMassFlowRateFromHeatDistributionSystem become mandatory wherever their temperature input is mandatory. (2) The secondary circuits of the buffer and of SimpleDHWStorage are refused at build when only one of flow and temperature is wired, with a message naming the component, both inputs and what to wire. (3) Remove the mandatory, never-read inputs DistrictHeating.WaterInputMassFlowRateFromWarmWaterStorage and ElectricHeating.WaterInputMassFlowRateFromWarmWaterStorage with their default connections.

Done when: the three refusals have tests, and household_district_heating_building_sizer.grouped, household_electric_heating_building_sizer.grouped and household_gas_building_sizer.grouped give bit-identical results before and after (January week, 900 s).

The three grouped twins are bit-identical over the January week at 900 s (DataFrame.equals, same columns, KPIs and pass counts); all 44 energy_systems files build, prepare and connect.

title: The assemblies' isolation test systems never deliver the tested heater's heat to the building, so the room cools to 9 C and the expected consumptions measure an unheated house
description:
Source: found 2026-10-20 while PR #1079 (hisim-b5u7, the building's thermal mass) failed 13 assembly expectations in tests/assemblies/test_library_contracts.py.

The isolation system of every heating assembly (hisim/energy_system/assemblies/testing/isolation.py with the partners of energy_systems/assemblies/test_partners.yaml) wires the Building to Weather and UTSPConnector only: the Building partner 'reads no heat distribution' by design. The heater, boiler or district-heating substation under test reads the building's demand and delivers, but its heat never reaches the building. Measured on the one test day (1 January 2021, Aachen, 900 s, defaults): heating/electric_resistive's room air falls from 20.4 to 9.1 C over the day while the heater delivers 172.9 kWh into nothing; heating/gas_condensing_boiler's room air falls the same way (20.4 to 9.1 C). The demand rises as the room cools, so the 'measured' consumptions the expect: entries check (98.9 kWh electric, 129.7 kWh gas, 101.0 kWh district heat before #1079; 181.8 / 160.3 / 145.6 kWh after) are the demand of an unheated, cooling house, not the consumption of a heated one. #1079 rescaled the 13 ranges to the new values; they still describe the unheated house.

Do: the isolation system of an assembly that heats the building delivers that heat to the Building (the direct heater's thermal output, the heat distribution system's ThermalPowerDelivered), e.g. a Building partner variant that reads the heat the assembly brings, so the room stays near its set temperature; then re-measure every expect: entry and the monotone/bounds comments that quote measured values.

Done when: in every heating assembly's isolation day the room air stays within about 1 K of its set temperature, and the expect: ranges are re-measured on that heated house.
close_reason: Fixed: the test partner Building reads the space heating of its system through an optional 'heating' port (partner HeatDistribution or ElectricHeating), which the harness binds per isolation system to the one candidate, the subject's heater or the partner distribution, as a composed file's Building reads its HeatDistributionSystem or its ElectricHeating. Two new contract checks fail loudly when heat is lost again: 'heat delivered' (no heat input a component of the system serves by its default connections is left unconnected, every sample) and 'room heated' (at the defaults a heated building's room air averages within 1 K of its set heating temperature). Measured on the test day (1 January 2021, Aachen, 900 s, defaults): the room air averages 19.97 to 20.02 C in every heating and supply assembly (before 13.84 C, falling to 8.93 C); the expected consumptions fall to the heated house's: electric 181.8 -> 80.9 kWh, gas/oil/hydrogen 160.3 -> 100.7 kWh, pellets/wood chips 161.1 -> 93.3/93.4 kWh, district heat 145.6 -> 80.1 kWh; heat pump SPF 4.06 -> 3.84 (space-heating only 3.95 -> 3.75). The 13 expect ranges and the measured comments are re-measured.
notes: Owner decision 2026-10-20: P1, fixed in its own PR right after #1079 (the thermal-mass fix), so the assembly contract tests check a heated house again.

description:
Source: found 2026-10-21 while closing hisim-grouped-recorder-ef-r10-4fy0. `hisim energy-system record --grouping energy_systems/household_gas_solar_thermal.grouping.yaml` (and therefore `scripts/record_all_setups.py --check`, which now covers the grouped twins) fails at probe two_dwellings: EF-R13 SolarThermalSystem.area_m2 '4.0 * Size.NUMBER_OF_APARTMENTS' computed 8.0 in the Python run, but the recorded file resolves it to 4.0. The sibling sizer setups (household_gas_building_sizer.py:220, household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py:197) set it. Failing since #745 (2026-09-14), when EF-R13 arrived.

Options: (A) set my_building_config.number_of_apartments = number_of_apartments as the siblings do; the twin and the grouped twin gain `number_of_apartments: 1.0` on Building, and two_dwellings becomes a real knob, so the grouping decision needs a re-probe and new override rows (Building, DHWStorage, SolarThermalSystem, boiler). (B) size the collector and boiler from my_building_information.number_of_apartments like the DHW storage; no twin moves, but the setup then ignores the dwelling count and the two_dwellings probe is vacuous and should be dropped. Recommendation: A, because the probe list describes exactly that behaviour.

Done when: `scripts/record_all_setups.py --check --only household_gas_solar_thermal` passes.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-21: option A. household_gas_solar_thermal.py sets my_building_config.number_of_apartments from number_of_dwellings_per_building as its sizer siblings do. The grouping overview is regenerated. scripts/record_all_setups.py --check is clean over all setups.

title: A one-day run with every post-processing option exceeds 5 GB of memory
description: Source: write-guard survey, 2026-09-26. A one-day run with all post-processing options (PDF report, network charts, ...) peaked above 5 GB and was OOM-killed on the 22 GB agent box (it took the Claude processes down with it); the moderate option set peaks at 1.7 GB. Profile which option allocates the memory (likely plots/PDF/network charts over the full result frame) and bound it; CI's 16 GB runners hide it.
close_reason: The PDF report held the decoded bitmap of every embedded plot until the report build ended, about 75 MB per 3600 x 2400 plot; its figures are now ReportLab Image flowables with lazy=2, which drop the bitmap after drawing (branch postprocessing-memory). gas_boiler_household, one day at 900 s, every option but OPEN_DIRECTORY_IN_EXPLORER (216 plots in the report): peak RSS above 12 GB (OOM-killed at the 12 GB cap; 14.4 GB at the earlier uncapped kill) -> 0.80 GB, the same as the run without report images (0.80 GB). The report build alone with all 216 plots: OOM at 12 GB after 39 s -> 0.32 GB in 131 s. Every output file except the PDF is identical; the PDF renders identically page by page except its timestamp. Not addressed: each report section rebuilds the whole PDF, six builds of about 135 s each in the all-options run.

title: The envelope elements' installation_year is reported used but changes nothing at the anchor
description: Source: tier-1 path verification findings (no effect), 2026-09-26. house.building.{roof,floor,window,door}.installation_year are reported used by the economic context, yet the economic context (and energy system) is identical for two values at the anchor (no envelope measure). title: The generic heat pump's controller decides within a step on the same step's building temperature, so the warm start moved its demo setups' week by up to 65 %
description:
Source: evaluation of the review of #914, missed finding M1 (2026-10-13). Owner decision 2026-10-13: bead it beside hisim-component-physics-4g9.58, no fix now.

Mechanism: GenericHeatPumpController.i_simulate (hisim/components/generic_heat_pump.py:852-873) reads TemperatureMean (the building's thermal-mass temperature) on every pass and, in smart mode, the electricity balance, which includes the heat pump's own draw. Both move within the step, so the mode can change between passes. On force_convergence it skips the decision and republishes the mode it holds, while the plant keeps the state of the last free pass (the hisim-component-physics-4g9.28 pattern). This is the defect #948 removed from AirConditionerController and hisim-component-physics-4g9.58 records for SimpleAirConditionerController.

Evidence that it matters: #914's warm start changed only where each step's iteration starts, yet it moved default_connections' January week by up to 65 % (self-consumption 10.66 -> 17.60 kWh, grid injection 26.36 -> 19.43 kWh, degree-hours above 25 °C 0.13 -> 1.09) and basic_household's week by up to 24 % (heating demand -13 %, degree-hours more than 1 K below the set point -24.5 %). Both setups use only the generic heat pump among the controlled devices. A result that moves this much with the start vector depends on the pass history, so neither the old nor the new number is the controller's answer to its inputs.

Scope: the demo setups basic_household and default_connections (the only system_setups that use generic_heat_pump); not RenoVisor.

Fix: the one #948 gave AirConditionerController: sample the building temperature (and the electricity balance) once per step and decide each step on the state committed at the end of the previous step, so every pass sends the same signal. Changes both setups' goldens.

Done when: the controller decides on the committed state only, a cold-started and a warm-started week of both setups agree within the simulator's tolerance, and their goldens are re-blessed with the change.

title: Decide whether the air conditioner's building-load sizing is inverted (effective capacity falls as the load rises)
description:
Source: the #816 bless (#821, 2026-09-24) and the history of hisim/components/air_conditioner.py.

AirConditionerConfig.for_building_load picks the catalogue unit whose heating capacity (at the reference temperature) is nearest the building's heating load and sets scale_factor = capacity * CAPACITY_SHARE_FOR_BUILDING_LOAD (0.6) / heating_load. The component multiplies every heating/cooling capacity and power by scale_factor, so the capacity it runs with is capacity^2 * 0.6 / load: the larger the building's load, the SMALLER the effective unit. The docstring's intent ('sizes it down to' the load, 'run below its rating') suggests scale_factor = 0.6 * load / capacity (running at 60 % of the load) or 0.6 alone.

Evidence (#821, air_conditioned_house, one week): a door on the doorless TABULA row raised the heating load 9619 -> 9780 W (+1.7 %); scale_factor fell 0.5364 -> 0.5276; heat delivered fell 768.5 -> 758.1 kWh while the theoretical demand rose 600 -> 661 kWh; K*h below setpoint 45 -> 63 (+40 %), minimum room temperature 17.27 -> 16.93 degC.

History: introduced 2025-06-05 by efca6bcf (#392, 'Update air conditioner'; before it there was no scaling); unchanged through e2033174 (#547, 2026-08-07) and c7ce8f65 (#757, 2026-09-16, factory -> for_building_load). The 0.6 is 'determined heuristically based on manually experimenting', possibly against this formula. The effect is small while the nearest unit's capacity is close to the load (factor ~0.6 either way); it grows when it is not. Scope: hisim/components/air_conditioner.py and the air_conditioned_house setup (RenoVisor does not use air conditioners, not_implemented_yet).

Decide with the component's owner: the intended law (0.6 * load / capacity, or fixed 0.6, or other), then re-check the 0.6, re-record the air_conditioned_house twin and re-bless its golden (without force_rewrite).
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-12: fix the sizing in its own PR before #948 (branch ac-sizing). The law is now scale_factor = share x load / capacity, with the capacity from the component's own straight-line fit at the heating reference temperature, so the simulated unit delivers share x the design heating load there and grows with the load (the inverse is pinned by tests/test_air_conditioner_sizing.py). Share 0.6 -> 0.8, chosen on air_conditioned_house, full year 2021 at 60 s with #948's controller: inverted law 651/645 K*h below 20 / above 24 degC (84/89 % of it at full power), 5070 kWh; share 0.6 164/195 K*h (38/64 %), 5245 kWh; 0.8 84/72 K*h (1/10 %), 5302 kWh, scale_factor 0.95; 1.0 73/56 K*h, 5323 kWh, scale 1.19; 1.2 66/50 K*h, 5343 kWh. Capex is the selected unit's price (4899 EUR) at every share. Twin re-recorded: scale_factor 0.5276 -> 0.9522.

title: The hydrogen, CHP and fuel-cell controllers become explicit state machines (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (hydrogen, CHP and fuel cell): L1CHPController (generic_chp/controller.py), FuelCellController (controller_l1_fuel_cell.py), ElectrolyzerController (controller_l1_electrolyzer_h2.py), PTXController (controller_l2_ptx_energy_management_system.py) and XTPController (controller_l2_xtp_fuel_cell_ems.py): start-up, standby, minimum run and idle times, load following.

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Upgrade pyloadprofilegenerator from the pinned 0.1.1 to 0.2.0: its release broke mypy, the LPG release detection and the UTSP connector
description:
Source: CI on 2026-10-15. requirements.txt listed pyloadprofilegenerator (the pylpg package) unpinned; release 0.2.0 came out on 2026-10-13, and the CI test image rebuilt at 10:57 that day (triggered by #1004's README change) installed it instead of 0.1.1. Everything that reads it broke: mypy (hisim/components/loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py:1454-1475, utspclient.helpers.lpgpythonbindings types no longer match pylpg.lpgpythonbindings), PylpgWorkspace.lpg_release (RELEASE_IN_DOWNLOAD_URL finds no LoadProfileGenerator release in LPGExecutor.retrieve_lpg_binaries' URLs), every test using the local LPG (extendedbase participant canaries), and the assembly nightly tier (EF-33 wiring errors at the UTSPConnector). requirements.txt now pins pyloadprofilegenerator==0.1.1.

Fix: upgrade to 0.2.0 deliberately: adapt the UTSP connector's types, PylpgWorkspace's release detection, the LPG release it downloads, and whatever the assemblies' UTSPConnector wiring needs; run the LPG tests, the nightly tier and a golden check (the occupancy profiles may change, which moves goldens). Done when: requirements.txt pins 0.2.0 (or a later release), CI is green, and any golden moves are explained.

title: Carry a stated heat-generator power in the calculation request, so a user-chosen or existing heat-pump size reaches HiSim
description:
Source: the analysis of 2026-10-14 (loop-design/contract_update_2026-10-14.md, decision D13) and PR #978 (hisim-component-physics-4g9.2). The calculation request carries no generator power, before and after the contract update to 36af54a: `house.heating` refuses one as `key.unknown`, and the `heating_system` measure has only `type_of_system`, `installation_year` and `condition`. The frontend's home inventory does have `energy_system_config.heating_system.power_in_watt` (existing generator, nullable, undocumented). title: The heat pump model gets a Carnot-efficiency COP shape and defrosting, after research into other heat pump models: hplib's Generic air/water curve misses real units by -33 % at A-7/W52 and has no defrost
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-21, after the hisim-x2mu evidence: "the entire heat pump model needs major work. hplib is missing any sort of defrosting for example, which can really mess with hp results."

Evidence (hisim-x2mu, 2026-10-21; data and scripts in /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/x2mu/): against ~1,930 Keymark-certified units (1,743 air/water, 176 brine/water; hplib's own raw exports), datasheets (Vaillant aroTHERM plus, Viessmann Vitocal 250-A, alpha innotec Hybrox 8) and Fraunhofer ISE 'WP-QS im Bestand', hplib's Generic air/water curve with the SCOP calibration is off where it matters: A-7/W52 -33 % (median), A7/W55 +16 %, A-7/W65 falls to the heating rod (COP 1) where real units reach ~2.0-2.4; hot water too optimistic (calibrated 3.29 at A7/W55 vs 2.81 certified, field hot-water JAZ 2.8). The required correction depends on the outdoor temperature, not the outlet, so no outlet-only calibration factor or cap can fix it (the mean-outlet SCOP anchors themselves are confirmed: x2mu). Part-load (cycling, inverter) effects are not represented: brine on/off units +17 to +28 % too high at the A12/W30 bin, air -17 % at A12/W24.

Scope (three parts, may be split into child beads):
1. Carnot-efficiency COP shape for air/water (and check brine/water): COP = eta * T_out[K] / (T_out - T_source + d), eta and d fitted to the Keymark population (prototype: air eta 0.451, d 4.45 K; air error 12.2 % -> 7.7 %, A-7/W52 -33 % -> +12 %, A7/W55 +16 % -> 0 %, aroTHERM A7/W65 2.49 vs datasheet 2.30), with the two-anchor SCOP calibration kept on top and hplib (or the replacement) supplying thermal power. Field data's stable Carnot efficiency (0.32-0.44 air, 0.44-0.52 ground) supports the shape.
2. Defrosting for air/water units: hplib has none. Model the defrost penalty (capacity and COP loss, typically around 0-7 degC outdoor and high humidity, reverse-cycle defrost energy taken from the circuit/buffer) from sourced data (EN 14511/14825 test points already include defrost at A2 and A-7; literature on defrost losses, e.g. frosting maps by temperature and relative humidity; the weather provides humidity?), so the heat pump's capacity and electricity at 0-5 degC are realistic and the buffer sees the defrost draw.
3. Research other heat-pump models: survey and compare alternatives to hplib (e.g. EnergyPlus/ Modelica Buildings heat pump models, VDI 4650 / DIN V 18599-5 methods, PySimHP/other open-source fits, manufacturer-map based models, the hplib maintainers' newer versions) on accuracy against the Keymark data, part load and cycling, defrost, hot water at 55-65 degC, input needs (what a RenoVisor request can state: SCOP W35/W55, type) and run time; recommend keep-and-extend hplib vs replace.

Related: hisim-x2mu (closed with the evidence), hisim-f79l (calibrate from SPF), hisim-g0dp (heating-rod switch, fixed on an unmerged branch), hisim-z0v4 (compressor below COP 1 next to the switch), hisim-ztt7 (ground source runs the air/water model), hisim-hydronics-fxix.12 (hot-water electricity vs step length).

Done when: the research recommendation is decided by the owner, the chosen model reproduces the Keymark population (median error at A-7/W52, A7/W55 and the hot-water COP within an agreed band) and has a sourced defrost penalty, goldens re-blessed, RenoVisor heads-up posted.
notes:
Owner decision 2026-10-21: a P1 epic with child beads (.1 research into other heat pump models, started now; .2 Carnot-efficiency COP shape; .3 defrosting; .4 part-load / cycling penalty, folded in from the brine/water finding of hisim-x2mu).

Owner decisions 2026-10-21 on the research (summary /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/hp-research/report_summary.md; full report with a verified 2020-2026 literature review in the coordinator's session): (1) hybrid then replace: own COP layer now with hplib's thermal power kept, then replace hplib's capacity surface with a sourced law and drop hplib; (2) COP = eta*T_out[K]/(T_out - T_src + d), pooled Keymark fit per source type (air 0.451 / 4.45 K, brine 0.568 / 4.50 K) with the two-anchor SCOP calibration on top and a minimum-lift guard; (3) defrost two-mode like the buffer: at steps <= 600 s a dynamic ice-mass model (Zanetti 2025 / AixLib style: one ice-mass state, discrete reverse-cycle defrost events drawing heat from the buffer), above 600 s the EnergyPlus/DOE-2 defrost-time fraction from the humidity ratio without its constant derate; both calibrated to the same targets (A2 about x0.90, field defrost heat share about 4-7 %) so 60 s and 900 s agree over a year; certified COPs treated as defrost-free (SCOP rated without defrost); (4) outdoor humidity for ALL weather sources (TRY keeps RF/x; NSRDB and DWD minute sources fetch it), no fixed fallback as the plan; (5) cycling: no Cd on simulated steps (HiSim cycles explicitly); EN 14825 Cdh (0.9, or 1.0 for an inverter) only inside StandardizedSeasonalCop below minimum output; an explicit start-up loss per start; default machine type air/water = inverter, brine/water = on/off, configurable; (6) hot water: no separate model, the same curve at the hot-water outlet (EN 16147 as a check); (7) capacity: replace hplib's inverted capacity surface (+49 % at the bivalent point) in the last step.

title: Compute the buffer-less distribution loop quasi-steady above its turnover criterion, so generator and pipe water need no fixed point
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §6.3, §7, §11 part 4 (owner, 2026-10-09). Replaces the circuit laws (hisim-component-physics-4g9.22) as the planned remedy for the buffer-less loop (hydronic spec D3).

Without a buffer the distribution system's pipe water turns over in minutes, so at 900 s generator and pipe water need about 16-24 iterations to agree (about 60 at 3600 s) and the result is biased by about 0.5 K. Above the turnover criterion (a = m_design dt / M_pipe > 1, and dt above part_load_above_seconds) the loop is computed quasi-steady within the step: the radiators deliver the building's demand, the generator covers it plus the pipe water's change of stored heat (a lift-holding generator by its part-load fraction, a district-heating substation directly), and the temperatures follow algebraically, with no fixed point between generator and pipe water. Below the criterion the loop keeps its dynamic behaviour, the reference.

Done when: 60 s results unchanged; the district-heating twin over a full year at 900 s and 3600 s agrees with 60 s within 1 % on delivered heat and the district-heating bill (bill = delivered heat + the pipe water's change of stored heat, hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.12), with no forced steps at 900 s.
close_reason: Not needed on the kind order (owner, 2026-10-12: #918's loop code is dropped). Measured 2026-10-12, full year 2021, predefined occupancy, district-heating twin against the 60 s run of the same head, with #922 below: the dynamic, one-step-lagged loop (no quasi-steady path) gives heat drawn (the bill) -0.03 % at 900 s and +0.03 % at 3600 s, heat delivered to the building -0.08 % / -0.21 %, no step flagged at force_convergence, 3.16 / 3.24 passes per step (3.13 at 60 s). The 16 to 24 passes per step at 900 s this bead was written against no longer occur, and the criterion (delivered heat and bill within 1 %, no forced step at 900 s, 60 s unchanged) holds without the quasi-steady path. #918's path gave -0.35 % / -0.31 %, -0.09 % / -0.24 %, 0 / 23 flagged steps and 5.42 / 7.03 passes. The code stays on branch part-load-hds. Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md sections 8 and 11.

title: An unpriced envelope measure books the cost database's embodied CO2 over its area, while a kept element's renewal books none: decide one rule
description:
Source: the review of PR #986 (door priced per m2), path-tracer finding, 2026-10-15. Pre-existing for every envelope measure; reachable for the door since #986.

EconomicContextBuilder._envelope_subject (hisim/renovisor/economics.py) gives an envelope measure without a cost block an investment of zero, flags it unpriced (UNPRICED_NOTE) and sets no embodied_co2_override_in_kg, so the engine (context_resolution.resolve_device) books entry.embodied_co2_for_size(area): a door_replacement without a cost block on 2.7 m2 shows 0 EUR and 116.1 kg (43.0 kg/m2). A kept element's renewal (_kept_element_facts, hisim-ryw1) sets the CO2 override to 0 and its note says its cost and embodied CO2 are "unknown, not zero, and are left out of every total". UNPRICED_NOTE says nothing about the carbon, so a reader cannot tell that the money is missing and the carbon is not.

Options: A) keep the carbon (it depends on the area and the material, not on a price) and extend UNPRICED_NOTE to say the embodied CO2 is the cost database's estimate over the area; B) treat it like a kept element: CO2 override 0 and the note says the carbon is unknown and left out; C) leave both as they are. Recommendation: A (no number moves, the note tells the truth; the carbon of a measure the plan does carry out belongs in its total). A or B changes the result notes, B also the CO2 totals of every plan with an unpriced envelope measure.

Done when: the owner chose, the rule is applied to every unpriced envelope measure, and a test pins the carbon and the note of an unpriced measure.
close_reason: Owner decision of 2026-10-15: option B. An envelope measure without a price books no embodied CO2: EconomicContextBuilder._envelope_subject sets embodied_co2_override_in_kg to 0 for an unpriced measure, as _kept_element_facts does for a kept element's renewal, and UNPRICED_NOTE says that its cost and embodied CO2 are unknown, not zero, and left out of every total. A reader's quote prices the money only: the quoted row's note adds StagedDocument.QUOTED_UNKNOWN_CARBON_NOTE. A door_replacement without a cost block on 2.7 m2 now books 0 kg instead of 116.1 kg; with a cost block it still books 116.1 kg. Pinned by TestAnUnpricedMeasuresCarbonIsUnknown in tests/renovisor/test_economics_context.py, which fails on the old rule.

description: Source: owner decision Q3 of 2026-10-20 on hisim-component-physics-4g9.66. Physics points both ways: hydrogen's latent share is larger (15.4 % of its GCV against 9.9 % for natural gas), so a hot return loses more on the gross basis, and its flue-gas dew point is higher (about 72 °C against 55 °C), so a cool return recovers more. title: Hydronic coupling in the temperature domain: pure (mass flow, temperature) ports, an exact mixed-node step, generators within their own limits (roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md)
description: Owner decisions 2026-10-01: no interim fix (PR #864's accepted-heat back-channel is not merged and is replaced by this work); everything in the temperature domain with pure (m, T) ports, energy only derived as m c dT, for composability (tanks in series, coils, mixing valves, generator -> HDS without a buffer); circuit laws deferred (hisim-component-physics-4g9.22, P4). Live RenoVisor results are wrong until this lands (renovisorissues #76: pellet boiler ~2.5x gas). Design and open decisions D1-D8: roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md.

title: A stratified water storage of N mixed layers replaces the dt/3600 mixing factor of heat_exchanger_is_present=False
description:
D5 (owner 2026-10-01): the stratification path is kept unchanged for now, documented as not energy-consistent, outside the balance guarantee and flagged by the energy-balance check. Replace it later by a tank of N coupled mixed nodes (each a MixedNode of hydronics.py), then drop the mixing factor. See roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §9.5.

Design with the start-of-step node (2026-10-17, owner asked for it to be recorded here): a stratified tank is N layers, each one StartOfStepNode (hisim/hydronics.py, #1009) with its own start temperature T0_k; everything in a step is computed from the start temperatures of all layers. The generator's return port is the bottom layer's T0 and the load's supply the top layer's T0, both constant for the step, so no circuit iterates against the tank. A charging flow m entering at the top reaches layer k as an Inflow from the layer above at T0_(k-1); the node books it as m c (T0_(k-1) - T0_k) dt, which is the upwind transport term, so no new physics function is needed. The transport terms cancel pairwise, and the tank gains m c (T_in - T0_bottom) dt, the heat the generator's circuit books, so the tank closes per step at any step length. Conduction and mixing between neighbours, UA_k (T0_(k+1) - T0_k), enter each layer as the signed heat_drawn_w argument; the loss to the room as ua_w_per_k. Stability: the explicit transport needs m dt <= one layer's mass (a 200 l tank in 10 layers charged at 0.3 kg/s: 18 kg per step at 60 s is fine, 270 kg at 900 s is not). Recommended remedy: the tank sub-steps internally, n = ceil(m dt / layer mass), publishing the start-of-step port values and booking the sums over its sub-steps, which keeps the balance exact and the tank a black box. Alternatives: a plug-flow shift model (exact, stable, but its own model) or fewer layers at coarse steps (result then depends on the step length). Controllers read a configured sensor layer's start temperature; the part-load fraction is found by stopping the charge in the sub-step where the sensor layer reaches its target.

title: The solar collector's hot-water circuit carries twice the heat it books, and its controller's switch-on test needs a collector temperature that is not the circuit's supply
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.3, §5.5, D4; hisim/components/solar_thermal_system.py (SolarThermalSystem.i_simulate, SolarThermalSystemController.get_controller_state).

The collector books Q_coll(T_in) but pumps m = Q/(c dT_n) at T_out = T_in + 2 dT_n, so its water carries 2 Q into the tank (dT_n = 10 K is the collector's inlet-to-mean difference). With the tank a mixed node (stage C), the tank books what the water carries: over 2021 at 900 s the gas solar twin's collector books 227.7 kWh and the tank receives 455.4 kWh from it. Stage C leaves the collector unconverted.

Spec §5.3 says: pump owner at the flow sized for dT_n, T_sup = T_ret + Q(T_ret)/(m c) (so T_out = T_in + dT_n), controller keeps start values. Two things the spec leaves open: (1) the efficiency law evaluates the collector at its mean T_in + dT_n, which for a linear profile means T_out = T_in + 2 dT_n, so the spec's outlet halves the lift the efficiency law assumes; (2) the controller switches the pump on when CollectorTemperature - T0 > 10 K and reads CollectorTemperature from the collector's outlet. With T_out = T_in + dT_n = T_in + 10 K the test becomes T_bar > T0 and the pump would almost never start; an idle circuit (T_sup = T_ret) never starts it.

Options: (a) spec as written for the circuit (m = Q/(c dT_n), T_sup = T_bar + dT_n) plus a separate collector-temperature output for the controller, evaluated at T0 (T0 + 2 dT_n while Q(T0) > 0, the value the controller reads today); (b) keep the outlet T_in + 2 dT_n and size the flow for it, m = Q/(2 c dT_n), with the controller-facing outputs evaluated at T0 as in (a) (the controller's 0.01 kg/s minimum flow then switches at twice today's collector heat unless restated); (c) as (a) but compare the collector's heat at T0 instead of a temperature. Recommendation: (b), consistent with the efficiency law, plus T0-evaluated controller inputs (D4). Blocks hisim-assemblies-lt0b.23.
close_reason: Decided by the owner 2026-10-09: the collector's outlet stays T_in + 2 dT_n and its flow is sized for 2 dT_n, so its water carries exactly the booked heat; its controller reads T0-evaluated inputs (spec §5.3 corrected). Done in 31ec2ee3 on hydronic-stage-c; the solar twins close per step and both circuit ends agree (tests/test_dhw_chain_twins.py).

The code merged in stage C has the controller read the collector's outputs evaluated at the tank's step mean, with only the full-tank stop on T0 (spec §5.3). On 2026-10-10 the owner removed the switch-on comparison and the collector-temperature output (finding F4): the controller now reads the flow the collector heat at the step mean needs (minimum-flow stop) and the tank's start-of-step temperature (full-tank stop).

title: Let the solar pump run only the part of a step it can deliver, so collector yield and the backup's fuel or electricity agree across step lengths
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.3 and §9.5 C (owner, 2026-10-09). Due before RenoVisor's solar thermal results are relied on: RenoVisor runs at 900 s.

The solar pump decides once per step: it switches on at the tank's step mean when the collector has heat there and runs the whole step, and it stops for the whole step once the tank started above 60 °C (the stop stays on the start temperature T0, owner 2026-10-09, because on the step mean it has no fixed point). The DHW chain otherwise agrees across step lengths, but the houses with a solar collector do not: at coarse steps the tank sits hotter for longer (whole-step charges of the backup generator, whole-step pump decisions), so the collector runs at a hotter inlet and less often, and the backup makes up the difference.

Evidence, full year 2021, predefined occupancy profile, 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s:
- household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer: collector yield -7.0 % / -23.5 %, the boiler's hot-water gas +1.3 % / +4.3 %, the tank's net heat +0.18 % / +0.50 %.
- household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer: collector yield -15.2 % / -15.1 %, the heat pump's hot-water electricity +9.2 % / +43 %, net heat +0.16 % / +0.58 %.

Task: let the solar pump run only the part of a step it can deliver (for example the fraction of the step until the tank reaches its 60 °C stop, or until the collector heat at the rising tank temperature falls below the minimum flow), so the collector yield and the backup's fuel or electricity agree within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s, without steps ending at force_convergence. Done when: the two solar twins meet that over a full year, the strict per-step closure test (tests/test_dhw_chain_twins.py) still passes, goldens re-blessed, and tests/test_part_load_twins.py runs the collector at part load: a solar twin case with the collector at 20 m² over January to March 2021, because the default 4 m² pump first runs on 20 January, so the suite's first-week window never starts it, and windows later in the year read January weather (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2). That case costs about as much as the extendedbase2 tests (review of #917, findings R9 and R27).

Approach (owner, 2026-10-09): the part-load run fraction above the step-length threshold, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md, prototype part 3; builds on hisim-naze.

With the pump running whole steps on the same base (#916): collector +1.28 % / +4.31 %, hot-water gas -0.18 % / -0.66 %, 123 / 56 flagged steps; without any part load (#922): collector -6.19 % / -24.01 %, hot-water gas +1.17 % / +4.35 %. Heat pump + solar: collector +1.57 % / +0.76 %, hot-water electricity +1.22 % / +13.64 %, 1310 / 719 flagged steps (#916, pump whole steps: +5.00 % / +1.29 % and +0.92 % / +12.99 %). Done-when not met: the gas + solar collector misses 1 % at 900 s, the heat pump + solar hot-water electricity misses it at both steps, and both twins have steps at force_convergence. Stays open. Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md section 11 (#918).

2026-10-12, parked (owner): the collector's part load (#917) waits as a draft branch until the energy manager's raise cycle (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28) and a fix of the car's controller under #922 are in, then it is measured again; the solar pump's hysteresis (#941) and 80 °C maximum (#942) move onto #915 without it. Measured on the kind order, full year 2021 against 60 s: gas + solar collector -1.75 % at 900 s and -1.00 % at 3600 s with the rule, +1.28 % / +4.31 % with whole-step pump runs (#915), flagged steps 165 / 223 against 123 / 56; heat pump + solar hot-water electricity +1.22 % / +13.64 %. Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md section 11.

Narrowed to the solar collector (owner decisions of 2026-10-19 (interview on review-evals/fxix_triage_2026-10-19.md)): what is left is a summer-week collector case in tests/test_part_load_twins.py (mid-year windows allow it now); the heat pump's hot-water electricity moves to hisim-hydronics-fxix.12, the forced steps to hisim-hydronics-fxix.25/4g9.28. title: The heat pump's hot-water electricity depends on step length: whole-step charges into hplib's near-COP-1 range
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §9.5 C (owner, 2026-10-09). RenoVisor runs at 900 s, where the residual is +1.73 %.

With the hot-water supply capped at the controller's set temperature (t_max plus the energy manager's raise) and the charge ending within 0.5 K of it, the heat pump's hot-water heat agrees across step lengths, but its electricity does not. household_heatpump_building_sizer, full year 2021, predefined occupancy profile, against 60 s: hot-water heat +0.09 % at 900 s and +0.27 % at 3600 s (net of stored heat +0.10 % / +0.38 %), hot-water electricity +1.73 % at 900 s and +18.1 % at 3600 s.

Cause: the controller decides on the tank's start temperature for a whole step (D4), so at 3600 s a charge runs an hour, often to the raised 70 °C target, and the cylinder sits hot. 62 % of the hot-water heat at 3600 s is made with a return above 63 °C, where hplib runs near COP 1 (its heating-rod mode), against 20 % at 60 s; the hot-water COP is 2.44 at 3600 s against 2.87 at 60 s. The energy manager's raise also switches inside a step (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28, hisim-component-physics-4g9.31), and under force_convergence the controller holds a raised set temperature.

Same whole-step cause as hisim-hydronics-fxix.11 (the solar pump): letting the heat pump run only the part of a step its charge needs may solve both. Done when: the heat pump's hot-water electricity agrees within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s over a full year, the strict per-step closure test still passes, goldens re-blessed.

Approach (owner, 2026-10-09): the part-load run fraction above the step-length threshold, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md, prototype part 2; builds on hisim-naze.
notes:
2026-10-12, parked (owner): the heat pump's and the electric heater's part load (#916) wait as a draft branch until the energy manager's raise cycle (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28) and a fix of the car's controller under #922 are in, then they are measured again. Measured on the kind order, full year 2021 against 60 s: hot-water electricity +0.96 % at 900 s and +8.89 % at 3600 s with the rule, +0.59 % / +9.36 % with whole-step charges (#915); flagged steps 1784 / 887 against 1601 / 618, 1383 of the 1784 at 900 s whole-step steps of the energy manager's loop. Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md section 11.

Lowered to P2 (owner decisions of 2026-10-19 (interview on review-evals/fxix_triage_2026-10-19.md)): at 900 s the heat pump's hot-water electricity already meets the 1 % target (+0.36 %), 3600 s is +9.7 %. PR #916 stays parked until hisim-component-physics-4g9.28 is settled; when it returns, the hot-water cylinder publishes its end temperature without each circuit, as the space-heating buffer does, so its part-load rule is exact.

title: The heat-pump-and-solar twin aborts at 3600 s: the capped heat pump and the tank's step mean form a 2-cycle the 0.5 under-relaxation cannot damp
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), owner decision 2026-10-09.

household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 3600 s (predefined occupancy profile), aborts with "More than 100 tries in time step 4426" (July). The heat pump's hot-water supply is capped at its controller's set temperature, so its heat is m c (T_set - T̄): with the heat pump on and the collector charging, the tank's step mean flips between 45.6 °C and 61.9 °C, a 2-cycle of the node's fixed-point map with a slope of about -3.5. The node's acceleration (hisim.hydronics.accelerated_node_mean) under-relaxes a residual that changes sign with weight 0.5 (owner-pinned, 2026-10-04), which damps only slopes above -3 (error factor 1 + 0.5 (F' - 1) = -1.25 here), and force_convergence freezes the controllers but not the node.

Tested in a scratch copy only: a secant step between the two bracketing iterates (x - r (x - x_prev) / (r - r_prev) when r r_prev < 0) makes the year complete (484 forced steps; hot-water electricity +14.2 % and collector yield +0.02 % against 60 s). The owner kept 0.5 for now (2026-10-09). 60 s and 900 s complete; no CI test runs this twin at 3600 s over July (the resolution test runs January). Done when: the twin's year at 3600 s completes without lifting the pinned parameter unilaterally, or with the owner's decision on the oscillation branch.
close_reason: The heat-pump-and-solar twin's year at 3600 s completes on main. Measured 2026-10-19 on origin/main 4ae6eb82: household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 3600 s, local LoadProfileGenerator occupancy: 8760 steps, mean 8.6 passes, max 88, 597 forced steps; step 4426 (July), where the year aborted, takes 10 passes. The 2-cycle came from the node acceleration's pinned 0.5 under-relaxation, which the owner removed with every other output acceleration on 2026-10-11 (#927, 6c95e544; hisim.hydronics.accelerated_node_mean is gone), so the done-when's second branch holds: the year completes by the owner's decision on the oscillation, not by lifting the parameter unilaterally. Since #1050 the pass limit at 3600 s is 6000. The hot-water electricity gap at 3600 s stays with hisim-hydronics-fxix.12.

title: HeatDistribution publishes the previous step's heat and temperatures, keeps pumping with the valve shut, and books differently from the buffer that feeds it
description: Component review of 2026-10-10 against system_docs/component_design_principles.md, on afd231a9 (PR #914). Finding F2, P1 by owner decision; the full fix is hydronic stage D (spec 4.6, hisim-hydronics-fxix.5). Outputs come from self.state, i.e. the previous step (heat_distribution_system.py:470-491, written :498-501). With the controller off, PARALLEL still pumps the design flow (:417-425) and returns T_in + 0.01 (T_room - T_in) per step (:460-467), booking 0 delivered while the buffer books m c (T0 - T_ret) into it (simple_water_storage.py:1089-1093): heat nobody receives, and a leak whose size depends on the step length.
