title: Design how a component learns its hydraulic topology, replacing the three PositionHotWaterStorageInSystemSetup enums that must agree
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10: needs its own bead with a proper design; a blanket rule 'a component carries no setting about what it is connected to' was rejected as doing more harm than good. Today three enums describe the same layout and must agree: heat_distribution_system.py:54-75 (PARALLEL, SERIES, NO_STORAGE_MASS_FLOW_FROM_HEAT_GENERATOR, NO_STORAGE_MASS_FLOW_FIX), simple_water_storage.py:63-75 (PARALLEL_TO_HEAT_SOURCE, SERIES_TO_HEAT_SOURCE), more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:74-97 (PARALLEL, SERIES, NO_STORAGE). Spec decision D25 (roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md) already removes the heat-distribution one. Design question: which parts of the topology a component legitimately needs to know (e.g. whether it owns the circuit's pump, whether its return comes from a store), how it learns them (wiring, a sizing fact, one shared enum, the energy-system file), and how a mismatch fails at build time. Write the design (with the owner) before implementing.

title: Above the part-load threshold the memoryless rule does not settle where a device is evaluated between its controller and the tank (boiler and collector twins)
description:
Source: the memoryless part-load rule (roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §4.3, branch hydronic-part-load, #915 to #918; agent measurement 2026-10-10).

The L1 controller pairs the ratio its device reports it ran (PartLoadRatioRunDhw) with the tank's end temperature it reads in the same pass. The two belong to the same run only in the cyclic evaluation order controller -> device -> tank. The boiler twins (gas, oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen, gas + solar) and the collector in both solar twins list the device before its controller and the tank after both (device -> controller -> tank): there the device has already run the controller's newer ratio when the controller reads the tank's answer to the older one. In x = ln r the iteration is then x_k = x_{k-1} - x_{k-2} + c, whose roots lie on the unit circle: the ratio circles its fixed point with a period of six passes and settles only by chance.

Measured, full year 2021 (spec §11), twin order / every part-load controller moved before its device: gas twin 1013 / 46 forced steps at 900 s and 679 / 50 at 3600 s, hot-water gas against 60 s +0.27 % / -0.00 % and +0.18 % / -0.01 %, mean passes 4.26 / 3.42; 5 of 739 partial boiler steps converge at 900 s in the twin's order, 718 of 759 with the controller first. Gas + solar: collector -11.9 % / -1.7 % at 900 s and -9.6 % / +0.4 % at 3600 s, forced steps 1193 / 121 and 839 / 212. The gas twin at 60 s with the controller moved: every column within 1e-12 relative, but not bit-identical. The DHW chain test expects the failure of a file whose forced steps all run a part-load ratio, and the part-load twin test expects the gas twin to have no converged partial step.

Options (owner decision):
(a) Order: every L1 controller before its device in the setups, the recorded and grouped twins and the assemblies' member order. Simple; moves 60 s results by about 1e-12 (below the golden tolerance of 1e-9, but not bit-identical) and needs a re-record.
(b) A port that tells the controller which flow the tank's reading answers: the tank republishes the mass flow it integrated per charging circuit (as it already republishes the inflow temperature), and the controller pairs T_end with r_run * m_tank / m_device. Order-independent and 60 s bit-identical, but every part-load controller reads two more ports, wired per circuit.
(c) Accept the forced steps.

Recommendation: (a), since a controller commanding before its device is the natural order and the change at 60 s is float noise; (b) if bit-identity at 60 s must hold.
close_reason: The simulator now evaluates every L1 controller before its device: each component class inherits one kind base class (DataSourceComponent, L2ControllerComponent, L1ControllerComponent, PhysicsComponent, MeterComponent; owner decision 2026-10-12, no KIND constant), a pass runs data sources, L2 controllers, L1 controllers, physics, meters, and within the physics each L1 controller's device goes before the other physics the controller reads (hisim/evaluation_order.py). Branch kind-classes, which replaces #922 and moves under the part-load stack; the part-load PRs on top (#915 to #918, #941, #942) are measured on this order.

title: The memoryless part-load rule alternates where the draw takes more than the rise the step still needs (electric heater beside space heating)
description:
Source: the memoryless part-load rule (roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §4.3, §11; branches hydronic-part-load to part-load-hds, #915 to #918; agent measurement 2026-10-10).

The rule takes the store's start temperature T_start as its end temperature at ratio 0. With a draw, the end temperature at ratio 0 lies below T_start by d, and the plain iteration's error is multiplied by -d / (T_aim - T_start) per pass: it alternates, and it diverges into a two-cycle between 1 and a small ratio (whose end temperature falls below T_start, which the rule answers with 1) once the draw takes more than the rise the step still needs. This is independent of the evaluation order (hisim-hydronics-fxix.16).

Measured, full year 2021: the electric-heating twin (controller evaluated before its heater) tops the tank up beside space heating at 45 °C in a third of its winter steps; 730 of its 900 s steps and 883 of its 3600 s steps need a forced pass (the pass-counting search: 212 and 200), and its hot-water electricity against 60 s moves from +0.01 % / -0.07 % to +0.12 % / +0.74 %. Traced example, 10 January 17:30 at 900 s: T_start 44.99 °C, target 45 °C, the ratio alternates 1 / 0.024 until the forced passes.

Options (owner decision): (a) accept; (b) a convergence aid on the ratio, which decision 13 of the spec rules out today; (c) a better stand-in for the end temperature at ratio 0 that the store can publish as a port quantity without a model behind it (none is known).

Q9 of roadmap/two_mode_buffer_spec.md, measured 2026-10-18 on the two-mode buffer (T2, branch two-mode-t2-mixed-node): household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 900 s, local LoadProfileGenerator occupancy. In every recorded twin the collector charges the hot-water cylinder (SimpleDHWStorage, a step-mean store with decision 11's rule), not the space-heating buffer, so the two-mode buffer does not touch its circuit, and the exact rule against the buffer's WaterTemperatureAtEndOfStepWithoutSecondaryHeatGeneratorInCelsius (Q9 option b) has no collector circuit on a buffer to apply to. The year: 35,040 steps, mean 5.86 passes, max 27; 1,650 forced steps, 138 of them while the collector's pump runs (7,038 steps). The collector ran a fraction of the step in 44 steps (March to September). Its ratio alternated within the step in a two-cycle (at least three reversals) in 8 steps, all forced, and the forced passes kept the small ratio: 1 June 13:30 to 14:45 (1 / 0.017 to 0.036, six steps), 23 August 14:15 (1 / 0.128), 27 August 13:45 (1 / 0.479). So the alternation of this bead occurs, rarely, on the cylinder; the remedy stays the owner's decision among this bead's options, since the cylinder has no exact stand-in.

Owner, 2026-10-18: Q9 measured on the two-mode buffer (8 of 7,038 running collector steps alternate on the cylinder, all forced); accepted (option a). The bead stays open for the electric heater's case it was filed for.

Their end temperature is exactly linear in each circuit's ratio, so the store can publish, beside its end temperature, its end temperature without each circuit as port quantities, with no model behind them; the rules of part_load.StartOfStepPartLoadRule then land in one pass under a draw. title: The cluster house's time-resolution test fails from #928 on: the battery's net power is a near-zero sum, and at 60 min the heat pump's hot-water controller misses the evening draw

title: The solar pump switches with a hysteresis held in the controller's saved state, so a running pump no longer flips off on its own heat
description:
Source: the kind-order diagnosis of 2026-10-11 (/home/noah/hisim/loop-design/kind_order_cycles.md, section 2, step 1871) and the owner's decision of 2026-10-11.

SolarThermalSystemController.pump_runs ran the solar pump while the flow the collector heat at the storage's step mean needs was at least MINIMUM_MASS_FLOW_IN_KG_PER_S (0.005 kg/s, about 420 W of collector heat). The pump's own heat lifts the step mean, so a step at the edge had no consistent on/off state. household_gas_solar_thermal at 900 s, step 1871 of 1-21 January: pump off -> 420.4 W -> 0.00502 kg/s -> on; pump on -> mean rises -> 416.8 W -> 0.00498 kg/s -> off; the step was forced.

Owner decision: a realistic hysteresis, as differential solar controllers have (on at a collector-to-tank difference of about 7 K, off at about 3 K).

Done (branch solar-pump-hysteresis, on part-load-hds): the controller's saved state is whether the pump ran in the previous step (set in i_save_state from the step's last pass, restored before every pass). A pump that stood switches on at SWITCH_ON_MASS_FLOW_IN_KG_PER_S = 0.005 kg/s (unchanged); a pump that ran switches off only below SWITCH_OFF_MASS_FLOW_IN_KG_PER_S = 0.0025 kg/s (half, about 210 W; the 7 K / 3 K ratio is 3/7). The 60 °C full-tank stop on the start-of-step temperature is unchanged. No pass memory is left. On part-load-hds a forced pass kept the pump as the collector reported it ran (PartLoadRatioRun > 0); since 2026-10-13 the branch sits on #915, without the collector's part load, and a forced pass decides as every other pass, because since hisim-hydronics-fxix.21 every input of the decision is a start-of-step quantity no pass moves.

Measured at 900 s on the part-load-hds order (before -> after; forced steps, collector heat, pump-on steps):
- household_gas_solar_thermal, 1-21 Jan: 68 -> 65 forced, 0.48 -> 0.70 kWh, 5 -> 7 steps.
- household_gas_solar_thermal, year: 1312 -> 1343 forced, 377.6 -> 390.8 kWh (+3.5 %), 1807 -> 1986 steps; unmet DHW 0.071 -> 0.003 kWh.
- household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer, year: 1248 -> 1291 forced, 359.5 -> 376.1 kWh (+4.6 %).
- household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, 1-21 Jan: 89 -> 89 forced, 3.51 -> 3.58 kWh; year: 1682 -> 1674 forced, 610.3 -> 642.8 kWh (+5.3 %), unmet DHW 17.8 -> 15.8 kWh.
Golden check one_week_60s, python mode, the three solar setups: unchanged (the pump does not run in the first week of January).

What the hysteresis does not reach: of the forced steps whose pump signal still flips between passes (year: 141 gas + solar sizer, 156 heat pump + solar), all but 4 and 3 are switch-on steps, where the pump stood in the previous step and the switch-on flow is crossed by the pump's own heat within the step. A hysteresis on the saved state leaves those without a fixed point; an open follow-up bead under hisim-hydronics-fxix records them and the options.
notes: 2026-10-13, restacked onto #915 (the collector's part load, #917, is parked and no longer below) and measured again: full year 2021, predefined occupancy, household_gas_solar_thermal and household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, #915 -> this branch. At 900 s: forced steps whose pump signal changes between passes 17 -> 1 and 31 -> 8; pump switch-ons 518 -> 216 and 502 -> 335; steps flagged at force_convergence 123 -> 99 and 1225 -> 1222; collector heat 424.2 -> 352.0 kWh and 612.8 -> 591.3 kWh. At 60 s: flagged steps 14 -> 0 and 216 -> 194, pump-signal flips 14 -> 0 and 26 -> 0, switch-ons 1855 -> 253 and 1677 -> 353. A forced pass decides as every other pass, since every input of the decision is a start-of-step quantity.

title: The solar pump's switch-on step has no fixed point when the pump's own heat moves the flow back below the switch-on flow
description:
Source: the solar pump hysteresis (hisim-hydronics-fxix.19) and the physics order (hisim-hydronics-fxix.20), measured 2026-10-11.

The solar pump's switch-on decision has no fixed point in some steps. A pump that stood in the previous step switches on when the flow the collector heat at the storage's step mean needs reaches 0.005 kg/s. Once it runs, its heat lifts the step mean, the collector heat at that mean falls, and the flow drops back below 0.005 kg/s, so the next pass switches it off again. The hysteresis of hisim-hydronics-fxix.19 is held in the saved state (the previous step), so it removes this for a running pump but cannot reach the step in which the pump starts.

Measured, full year at 900 s, forced steps whose pump signal changes between passes / of them switch-on steps: on #918's order 141/137 (gas + solar sizer) and 156/153 (heat pump + solar); with #922's physics order 55/52 (gas + solar) and 51/47 (heat pump + solar). In the 1-21 January window none remains in gas + solar.

Options for the owner:
1. Decide the switch-on on a quantity the pump's own run does not move: the collector heat at the storage's start-of-step temperature (the full-tank stop already decides on the start-of-step temperature). Needs a second collector output (the flow at the start-of-step temperature), a port quantity. Recommended.
2. Leave it: the forced step ends with the pump as it ran in the last unforced pass; about 50 steps a year.
3. A switch-on hysteresis within the step would need pass memory, which principle 5 forbids.
notes: 2026-10-13, restacked onto #915 (the collector's part load, #917, is parked and no longer below) and measured again: full year 2021, predefined occupancy, household_gas_solar_thermal and household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, #915 -> this branch. Forced steps whose pump signal changes between passes, year at 900 s: 17 -> 1 (gas + solar) and 31 -> 8 (heat pump + solar); at 60 s 14 -> 0 and 26 -> 0.
close_reason: The solar pump switches on the collector's heat at the tank's start-of-step temperature (branch solar-pump-hysteresis); no forced step flips the pump between passes any more on #941 (gas + solar 7 -> 0, heat pump + solar 156 -> 1 a year at 900 s).

title: The solar full-tank restart band moves 9 to 20 % of the collector heat to the backup, because the solar maximum is the same 60 °C as the hot-water aim
description:
Source: the solar pump changes of #941 (hisim-hydronics-fxix.21), measured 2026-10-11.

The solar controller stops the pump once the tank starts a step above its 60 °C aim and, since the owner decision of 2026-10-11, restarts it only once the tank starts a step at least 3 K below (SolarThermalSystemController.FULL_STORAGE_RESTART_BELOW_AIM_IN_KELVIN). The restart band removes the switching every second step (gas + solar on the stack top: 1625 -> 219 pump switch-ons a year at 900 s), but it costs collector heat, because the solar maximum is the same 60 °C as the hot-water aim: on a sunny day the tank waits between 57 and 60 °C instead of being topped up by the sun, evening draws then take it below the backup's switch-on point sooner, and the backup supplies the difference.

Measured, year 2021, collector heat / backup hot-water heat, without -> with the 3 K band:
- gas + solar, 900 s, #941's order: 392.1 / 2737.1 -> 314.4 / 2814.2 kWh (collector -20 %)
- gas + solar, 60 s: 423.9 / 2697.3 -> 358.7 / 2761.5 kWh (-15 %)
- heat pump + solar sizer, 900 s: 647.2 / 2423.9 -> 586.3 / 2483.6 kWh (-9 %)
- stack top (#922's order), 900 s: gas + solar 426.4 -> 341.3 kWh; heat pump + solar 618.3 -> 584.1 kWh (before = without either change of #941)
Unmet hot water does not change materially.

Options for the owner:
1. Keep it: the 3 K band at a 60 °C maximum is a valid controller setting; the yield is what such a setting gives.
2. Give the solar controller its own maximum storage temperature above the 60 °C hot-water aim (solar controllers let the storage maximum be set above the hot-water set temperature), with the 3 K restart below that maximum and the part-load rule aiming at it. The tank then stores solar heat above 60 °C; a mixing valve on the hot-water outlet would be implied. Recommended if the yield matters, but it changes the tank's temperature range and the part-load target, so it needs its own measurement.
3. A narrower band: below the 3 to 5 K of real controllers, so not recommended.
notes: 2026-10-13, restacked onto #915 (the collector's part load, #917, is parked and no longer below) and measured again: full year 2021, predefined occupancy, #941 -> the 80 degC maximum. household_gas_solar_thermal at 900 s: collector heat 352.0 -> 973.1 kWh, the boiler's hot-water heat 2767.8 -> 2170.5 kWh, standby loss 267.4 -> 291.2 kWh, unmet hot water 0.00 -> 0.00 kWh, flagged steps 99 -> 65, pump switch-ons 216 -> 267, highest tank temperature 61.5 -> 81.4 degC; at 60 s collector heat 358.7 -> 971.1 kWh. household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer at 900 s: collector heat 591.3 -> 1102.8 kWh, the heat pump's hot-water heat 2477.6 -> 1992.6 kWh, standby loss 235.9 -> 262.8 kWh, unmet 15.9 -> 16.3 kWh, flagged steps 1222 -> 994; at 60 s collector heat 584.6 -> 1099.8 kWh. Collector heat at 900 s against 60 s: +0.2 % and +0.3 %. The figures in the close reason were measured on the part-load stack with #917 below.

title: The boiler publishes its full-load hot-water supply temperature with no flow when its controller signals it on at part-load ratio 0
description:
Source: the review of #917 (findings R1, R2, R4, R15), 2026-10-14. #917 fixed the same fault for the solar collector: CircuitStep.at_part_load (hisim/hydronics.py) now returns CircuitStep.idle at a ratio of 0, so the collector's outlet is its inlet. The boiler of #915 was left as it is on purpose, so #917 stays about the collector.

Fault: GenericBoiler.part_loaded_firing (hisim/components/generic_boiler.py) scales the hot-water flow, heat and fuel by the part-load ratio but keeps the full-load supply temperature. At a ratio of 0 with the burner signal on, the boiler publishes flow 0, heat 0 and fuel 0 at the full-load supply. Probe (tests/part_load_rigs.py BoilerRig.charge(900, ratio=0.0): signal 1, 55 °C return, 15 K lift, 70 °C set): WaterOutputTemperatureDhw 70.0 °C at mass flow 0, against the rule of CircuitStep that an idle circuit has no flow and supplies its return (55 °C). The ratio is 0 above the part-load threshold when the tank already ends the step in or above the controller's band (hisim/part_load.py, PartLoadRule). Energy and the KPIs are unaffected, because the tank weights a generator's supply by its mass flow (hisim/components/simple_water_storage.py); what is wrong is the published outlet temperature column.

Fix: at a ratio of 0 return an idle firing with the supply at the return. Optionally build part_loaded_firing on CircuitStep.at_part_load, which since #917 scales the heat by the ratio (review finding R3), and add only the fuel. Done when: part_loaded_firing at a ratio of 0 publishes the return as supply with no flow, a ratio-0 row in tests/test_part_load_dhw.py pins it, and the golden KPIs do not move.

title: The solar collector gets a heat capacity and a temperature state, so its sensor reads a continuous temperature instead of stagnation or outlet
description:
Source: the differential solar controller of #941 (owner decisions of 2026-10-14) and its review.

The flat-plate collector has no heat capacity and no temperature of its own. Its sensor reads one of two quasi-steady temperatures at the start of a step: the stagnation temperature (the efficiency curve at zero heat) after a step its pump stood, and the outlet at the tank's start-of-step temperature after a step it ran. A real collector holds about 5 to 10 kJ/(m2 K) of metal, glass and fluid (datasheets state the effective thermal capacity C of EN ISO 9806), so its outlet stays warm for minutes after the pump starts and it warms up gradually after the pump stops.

Without it the model jumps between the two quasi-steady temperatures from one step to the next, so a pump switched on at 7 K would read a much cooler outlet in the next step. Two choices of #941, accepted by the owner on 2026-10-14, exist only to keep that jump above the 3 K switch-off difference: the efficiency curve is evaluated at the inlet plus half the lift (not the fixed 10 K inlet-to-mean difference), and the pump's minimum flow is 5 kg/(m2 h) (not 10). With the fixed 10 K difference the pump switched about 26 times a day at 60 s against 2 at 900 s; at 10 kg/(m2 h) 6.8 against 1.0 (probe on a 45 C tank, 2021 Aachen weather).

Wanted: a collector temperature state with a heat capacity per m2 (a config field from the datasheet, about 5 to 10 kJ/(m2 K)), integrated over the step from the absorbed irradiance, the curve's loss and the heat the flow carries away, saved and restored with the collector's state. The sensor then reads that continuous temperature. Done when the collector has the state, its sensor reads it, the switch-ons a day agree within 20 % between 60 s and 900 s with a minimum flow of 10 kg/(m2 h), and the twins' collector heat at 900 s stays within 1 % of 60 s.

title: Every pumping device runs one shared CirculationPump subcomponent (constant, temperature-sensor, controller lift, external signal), bit-identical to today
description:
Owner decisions 2026-10-23 (Noah): a separate Pump component is out ('separate device right now is definitely out'); the pump law lives inside the device that owns the loop as a shared subcomponent (option C of /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/pumps/report.md: no extra passes, results identical to 5e-10; a separate component measured +11-13 % step-loop time and up to x6.6 forced steps).

CirculationPump (hisim/subcomponents/pumps.py, rules of hisim-repo-cleanup-o6a.28): modes CONSTANT_FLOW (m = m_design; the HDS design flow), FLOW_MATCHES_FIXED_LIFT ('temperature-sensor pump': m = Q / (c dT_target); hplib's 5 K, the solar pump's 20 K), FLOW_MATCHES_CONTROLLER_LIFT (renamed from FLOW_MATCHES_TARGET_SUPPLY_TEMPERATURE / 'controller lift', owner 2026-10-25: 'controller lift' is misleading; m = Q / (c (T_set - T_ret)); the boiler, the hot-water charges of district heating and the electric heater), EXTERNAL_SIGNAL (m = signal * m_max, PWM / 0-10 V decided by a controller). Controlled modes clamp to [m_min, m_max]; clamped, the outlet follows T_ret + Q/(c m) and the result says flow_is_clamped (reported, not refused). Construction fields: mode, bounds, design flow, target lift; the supply set temperature is a call argument (it changes every step). A device whose heat depends on its own temperature (the collector) re-evaluates its heat when clamped; the pump never needs the device's physics. A device without a pump on a loop (the #1117 boiler behind the HDS) holds no CirculationPump for it and reads its flow input - not a mode. Result: a NamedTuple PumpOperatingPoint(mass_flow_in_kg_per_second, supply_temperature_in_celsius, flow_is_clamped).

Scope: replace BoilerPump, SpeedControlledSolarPump and the hand-written m = P/(c dT) in the hplib heat pump, district heating, the electric heater and the HDS. title: Try the TargetSupplyTemperaturePump in the boiler, the electric heater and district heating's hot-water charge, and switch to it
description:
Owner, 2026-10-25 (#1141): hisim/subcomponents/pumps.py has the pump class TargetSupplyTemperaturePump (one class per flow law since the owner's decision of 2026-10-25 on #1141, replacing CirculationPump and its modes): m = Q / (c (T_set - T_ret)) with the device's own return in the pass and the supply set temperature as a call argument; unclamped it supplies exactly T_set, at a flow bound the flow is exactly the bound and the supply follows the heat. No device uses it yet. In the solar-thermal literature this is what 'matched flow' strictly means (collector outlet held at a target temperature); the term itself stays out of the code because it is also used loosely for constant-dT control.

Today: the boiler and the electric heater run a ControllerLiftPump: their controller computes a lift (supply set temperature minus the tank temperature it read at the start of the step) and sends it on the TemperatureDelta port; the device's return is the step mean, so the supply is T_ret,mean + lift and can miss T_set. District heating's hot-water charge runs a FixedLiftPump at 100 K (m = P/(c 100 K), then throttled at the set temperature), a value with no physical source (substation secondary lifts are typically 10-30 K).

Work: (1) on a branch, switch each of the three to a TargetSupplyTemperaturePump: the controller sends the supply set temperature instead of the lift (port change), the device passes its own return; the boiler keeps its largest flow (P_max eta_100 / (c 5 K)). (2) Compare against main on the gas, electric-heater and district-heating twins (winter and summer week at 900 s, a 60 s day): delivered heat, supply temperatures against T_set, flows, passes and forced steps, step time, KPIs. (3) Report to the owner; if the results are physically better and convergence does not get worse, switch, remove ControllerLiftPump if nothing uses it any more, and re-bless. If they are not, record why and keep ControllerLiftPump.

title: The requested and the actual part-load ratio have their own names everywhere, so no port, variable or method carries one under the other's name
description:
Owner, 2026-10-25 (discussion of #1142): 'we are conflating requested_ratio and actual_ratio here? they probably shouldn't be the same variable.'

Today the controller commands a part-load ratio (port PartLoadRatioDhw/Sh) and the device reports the ratio it ran (PartLoadRatioRunDhw/Sh). The two differ when the device overrides its controller (the pellet and wood-chip BurnerTimes: held lit runs 1, held out runs 0) or does not fire the circuit (0). They are mixed in three places: (1) under force_convergence the controller writes the actual ratio into its requested output (PartLoadControl.publish_held, StartOfStepPartLoadControl.publish_held), so that port means 'requested' in free passes and 'actual' in forced ones; (2) GenericBoiler.commanded_firing reads the request into a variable named ratio_run, which becomes the actual ratio only because i_simulate overwrites it later; (3) the names differ only by 'Run', and PartLoadCommand.ratio() returns the request while PartLoadControl.ratio_run() returns the actual one.

Work (pure rename, no number moves): ports RequestedPartLoadRatioDhw/Sh and ActualPartLoadRatioDhw/Sh on every device and controller that has them; helpers and variables requested_part_load_ratio / actual_part_load_ratio (PartLoadCommand, PartLoadControl, StartOfStepPartLoadControl, PartLoadRule arguments); the boiler turns its requested ratio into the actual one in one visible step. Golden column headers change, values do not.

Not in this bead: whether a forced pass should publish the requested ratio of its committed state instead of the actual one (changes results in forced steps where burner times overrode the request); that follows separately and is measured.
close_reason: The requested and the actual part-load ratio now have their own ports (RequestedPartLoadRatio*, ActualPartLoadRatio*), methods and variables everywhere, and a one-week pellet run at 900 s gives bit-identical results.

comments.text: Found in the evaluation of the review of #908 (2026-10-13): passive brine cooling can heat. MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib.passive_cooling (hisim/components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:1615-1617 on review-guards) sets delta_t = min(return - space-heating set temperature, 5 K). A return below the set temperature gives a negative delta_t, a positive 'drawn' heat and an outlet above the return: with an 18 °C return, a 20 °C set temperature and the nominal 0.333 kg/s, the cooling step heats the circuit by 2 K, about 2.8 kW. Part of this stage's cooling work: a max(..., 0) floor on the lift, or an idle step when the return is at or below the set temperature, with a test that such a return books no heat. title: A whole-step full-power hot-water charge overheats the energy-conserving DHW tank past 90 °C: at 3600 s, and at 900 s for a small tank or a large generator
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.1, §5.2, §7, D1, D2, D4.

With the DHW tank a mixed node (stage C), a generator's hot-water heat is no longer lost in the tank's mass mixing. Controllers decide on the tank's start-of-step temperature T0 (D4), so a charge runs the whole step. A full-power charge then overshoots whenever the step is long against the tank and the generator is large: the boiler holds its lift (D1: T_sup = T_ret + dT, P_th fixed), the hplib heat pump holds its 5 K lift (D2), and the tank leaves the 0..90 °C plausibility range, which fails the run.

Measured:
- tests/test_water_storage_temperature_check.py::test_the_gas_house_keeps_its_storages_in_range_for_a_winter_week[3600] (Irish 1960 gas house via RenoVisor, first January week 2019) reaches 102.6 °C (marked a strict xfail on the branch); household_heatpump_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 3600 s, reaches 96.0 °C. 900 s and 1800 s stay in range for the recorded twins and that RenoVisor house.
- At 900 s the assembly test contracts (pytest -m assemblies, tests/assemblies/test_library_contracts.py) fail on the samples at the edge of their parameter boxes: dhw/indirect_cylinder at its minimum 100 l beside the 40 kW partner heat pump (90.4 °C), heating/wood_chip_boiler at its largest power (96.1 °C, and the power sweep), heating/air_source_heat_pump s002 (hot-water electricity 20.3 kW above its 20 kW bound, and a buffer sweep at 92.3 °C): 61 failures, all of this kind. The assemblies CI job fails on the branch until this is decided.
- At 3600 s the generators' hot-water heat (net of the tank's stored heat) is 1.2-1.6 % above 60 s, mostly the standby loss of the hotter tank; the stage C done-when asks for 1 %.

Options: (a) a maximum supply temperature per generator (a boiler's high limit, the heat pump's maximum outlet; e.g. the controller's 70 °C hot-water flow set point), the generator throttling to T_sup = min(T_ret + dT, T_max) like the district-heating substation (§5.4); for the boiler this needs the fuel for the booked heat, the inverse law D1 dropped; (b) declare the overshooting cases outside the supported envelope: keep the 3600 s test xfail and narrow the assembly parameter boxes (smallest cylinder, largest boiler) to what stays in range at 900 s; (c) circuit laws (hisim-component-physics-4g9.22). Recommendation: (a) for every generator with a fixed lift (boiler, electric heater, heat pump), since it is a physical limit the spec's "within its limits" (§5) already names; it reopens D1's fuel law for the throttled steps only.
close_reason: Decided by the owner 2026-10-09: every fixed-lift generator throttles at a maximum supply temperature (GenericBoiler 80 °C, ElectricHeating's hot-water side 80 °C, the hplib heat pump's hot-water side 75 °C), the throttled heat is m c (T_max - T_ret) and its fuel or electricity follows through the generator's own law (spec §5, D1 amended). Done in 29cf73a4 on hydronic-stage-c: the 3600 s gas house and heat-pump twin stay in range, pytest -m assemblies passes (2807 passed).

title: Estimate an energy label per house from its simulated energy demand per m2 and year, on the country's scale
description:
Source: owner request 2026-09-25. result.json's kpis.energy_label is always null today (decision in hisim/renovisor/kpis.py: 'no BER/DEAP procedure in HiSim; no letter is invented'). The owner now wants an ESTIMATED label: the simulated annual energy demand per square metre of reference area, placed on the dwelling country's label scale.

Scope:
- One scale table per country the request schema admits (at least IE and DE, then ES and NL), each with its source, its basis and its bands. The bases differ and must be matched, not mixed: IE BER grades primary energy in kWh/m2a (A1..G), DE's Energieausweis grades final (or primary) energy in kWh/m2a (A+..H), ES's CEE grades non-renewable primary energy and CO2 by climate zone (A..G), NL's label grades primary fossil energy per NTA 8800 (A++++..G). Every threshold must be taken from the official source and cited, not from memory.
- The quantity: which simulated figure feeds each scale (final energy from all_kpis.json, or primary energy via the country's primary-energy factors), per m2 of which area (the scale's reference area vs HiSim's conditioned floor area / the request's living_area_in_m2), and annualised only from a full-year run (like the comfort grades: absent with a reason otherwise).
- Provenance: the label is an estimate from HiSim's simulation under its own weather, occupancy and control assumptions, not the certified procedure (DEAP, GEG, CE3X, NTA 8800). Publish it as approximated/estimated with that note and the figure it was derived from in the source string; never present it as an official rating.
- Reference and plan both get one, so the label change of a package is visible.
- Update the capability document's result row (KpiSchema), the translation map, and tell the frontend (renovisorissues heads-up) that energy_label stops being null; check the contract's Kpis.energy_label type (string) still fits.
Relates to hisim-kuna (the other placeholder KPIs) and hisim-ofqy (output unification: the label's source figure should come from the one place that owns it).

title: The simulator counts a NaN output as converged, so a NaN passes the iteration silently, seeds the next step and lands in the results
description:
Source: evaluation of the review of #927, missed finding M1 (2026-10-13); the same hole is review 929 R13, review 948 R40 and review 914 R3. Owner decision 2026-10-13: bead it, no fix now.

Mechanism: SingleTimeStepValues.is_close_enough_to_previous (hisim/component.py:206-212) returns False only when abs(previous - current) > 0.0001 (:210). For a NaN that comparison is False, so a NaN output counts as converged; get_differences_for_error_msg (:214-221) skips it the same way. Since #914 every step's first pass starts from the values the previous step converged to, so the NaN also seeds the next step.

Cases it hides:
- review 929 R13: #929 removed the battery's realized power from the energy manager's share and with it that argument's finiteness check, so a NaN realized battery power now goes into the published grid balance without an error;
- review 948 R40: one NaN indoor-air sample makes AirConditionerController's power fraction NaN, the accumulating ramp keeps it NaN for good, and the unit delivers 0 W silently;
- review 914 R3: any NaN output seeds the next step's first pass.
Components with their own guard (hydronics.MixedNode.step refuses non-finite arguments and results, hisim/hydronics.py:600-670) are safe; every other output is not.

Fix (the owner's fail-loud rule): in the convergence check, `if not abs(previous - current) <= tolerance: return False`, and refuse a non-finite output there with an error that names the component and the output and gives the time step. One guard covers all three cases, so no local guards are needed.

Done when: a simulation in which a component publishes NaN or inf fails at that step with an error naming the component, the output and the step; a test pins that; and every golden still runs unchanged (no shipped energy system publishes a non-finite output).

title: Upsampled NSRDB 15-min weather is two or one values short at 300 s and 600 s timesteps
description: Found while measuring hisim-component-physics-4g9.16 (2026-09-27). The RenoVisor energy system of the vendored mockup request (IE, Dublin NSRDB_15MIN 2019, baseline) fails before the first timestep at sub-15-min resolutions: at 300 s 'The yearly weather arrays in this simulation's sim repository hold 105118 values but the simulation needs 105120'; at 600 s 52559 vs 52560. 105118 = (35040 - 1) * 3 + 1, i.e. the 15-min series is interpolated between its first and last sample without extending the last interval to the year end. So no IE (NSRDB 15-min) RenoVisor case can run below 900 s. title: CI keeps one inputs cache per job and ref (11.6 GB, above the 10 GB limit) and downloads the LoadProfileGenerator binaries on every cache miss
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-18 (options #1 and #3), after the GitHub Actions caches of the repository were measured at 149 entries and 11.6 GB, above the 10 GB limit, so entries are evicted (LRU), and two jobs failed the same day because loadprofilegenerator.de refused connections while they downloaded the LoadProfileGenerator binaries after a cache miss.

Every job that uses .github/actions/hisim-cache restores and saves its own scope (about 45: golden-year python/composed per setup, golden-check shards, pytest shards, quality basic-execution, energy-system freshness), and every ref (main and each PR merge ref) stores its own copy of each, so the same content appears many times. Each entry holds hisim/inputs/cache, including pylpg/LPG10.10.0/ (152 MB unpacked, about 60 MB compressed).

PR A (branch ci-lpg-in-test-image): Dockerfile.test installs the release pylpg downloads (pinned LPG10.10.0, the build fails if pylpg downloads another) read-only below /opt/hisim/pylpg and sets HISIM_LPG_BINARY_ROOT; PylpgWorkspace copies the binaries from there when the release matches, and falls back to installing into the cache directory, logging why, otherwise.

PR B (branch ci-shared-inputs-cache): one shared inputs-cache lineage instead of one per job: every job restores the most recent shared entry, uploads only the files it added as a short-lived artifact, and one merge job per workflow run saves one entry with the merged content.

Done when: both PRs are merged, the test image is rebuilt with the binaries, and the cache list shows about one entry per workflow and ref instead of one per job.
close_reason: Done: #1060 (the LoadProfileGenerator binaries ship in the CI test image, read through HISIM_LPG_BINARY_ROOT) and #1062 (one shared inputs cache, one merge job per workflow run) are merged; the weekly cold-cache run follows in #1064.

title: Retry a local LoadProfileGenerator run whose locked-database error reached only the binary's stderr
description:
Source: CI jobs 116953498394 (runner cn29-8, 2026-10-16) and 116598187813 (cn29-3), reported on renovisorissues #120.

PylpgWorkspace.execute_and_verify retries a run that died on `SQLiteException ... database is locked`, but recognised it only by text in the generator's log Log.CommandlineCalculation.txt, quoted by verify_results_were_produced. On the runners the binary died in its post-processing before writing that log; the error and its ~45-line .NET stack trace (through CalcPostProcessor.Postprocessor.RunPostProcessing) went only to stderr, which pylpg 0.1.1's execute_lpg_binaries does not capture. So no retry, and the message wrongly said "No log was found ... so the binary failed early."

Done when: HiSim runs the binary itself with stdout and stderr captured, the failure message quotes the exit code and the output tail, and a locked database anywhere in the output is retried.
close_reason: Branch lpg-stderr-retry: PylpgWorkspace.run_generator runs pylpg's command with stdout and stderr merged and captured and returns a GeneratorRun (exit code, output); success is still decided by the result files. verify_results_were_produced quotes the exit code and the last OUTPUT_LINES_TO_QUOTE lines of output, and says the binary printed nothing only when it did. execute_and_verify retries when a RETRY_SIGNATURE is in the error text or anywhere in the output. Pinned in tests/test_pylpg_workspace.py.

title: Refuse an empty HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES and treat a single cache_directories string as one directory

From the PR #795 review (findings about the cache-directory code of #792, merged on main). Owner decision 2026-09-24: a separate small PR against main.

Not in scope (review noise or refactors): duplicated HISIM_CACHE_DIR override logic, the second environment variable, os.access as root, the skipped read-only-seed tests under root, the manifest test name.
close_reason: SimulationSetup.parameters refuses a HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES that names no directory (':' or '::') by name instead of an IndexError, and a relative explicit cache_directory like a relative entry of the variable. SimulationParameters.validated_cache_directories takes a single string as one directory and refuses a relative entry (CacheDirectoriesError). title: The pellet burner starts about 3,700 times a year, above the field range of 3,000: the on/off boiler controller relights at its set temperature with no firing hysteresis
description:
Source: PR #997 (burner-firing-times, hisim-75mt), measured 2026-10-14; owner (Noah) asked for this bead on 2026-10-15.

With the burner's minimum firing time and pause in the boiler (hisim-75mt), the pellet twin's burner starts about 3,700 times a year (year 2021 at 60 s, 10.1 starts a day), above the field range of 480 to 3,000 starts a year, about 1,300 typically, for automatically stoked biomass boilers (Schmidl et al., 'Real-life emission of automatically stoked biomass boilers', IEA Bioenergy Task 32, 2016). Nearly every pellet burn lasts exactly its 30-minute minimum (median 30 min, 90th percentile 34 min): the boiler controller's on/off law relights the burner as soon as the buffer drops below its set temperature, so it has no firing hysteresis. The wood-chip twin (about 2,100 starts a year) is inside the range only because its minimum firing time is 60 min.

Fix: give the on/off boiler controller a hysteresis band on the buffer temperature (fire below set minus a lower band, stop above set plus an upper band, with sourced default widths), so a burn lasts longer than the minimum and the burner starts less often. Keep the device protection (minimum firing time and pause) in the boiler. Measure starts a year, mean burn length, fuel and delivered heat on the pellet and wood-chip twins at 60 s and 900 s before and after; the gas twin (modulating) must not change.

Done when: the pellet twin starts inside the field range, a test pins the band, and the golden moves are explained.

title: Every setup that buys a carrier meters it
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-20 (Q-J of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md): every bought carrier's flow passes a meter, and a metered port that no meter reads is an 'unmetered' finding in balance_report.json, reported while components are undeclared and failing the run from PR 6 on. Four setups buy a carrier and have no meter for it (found by the twin sweep of #1086/#1092, 2026-10-20):
- gas_boiler_household: a GenericBoiler burning natural gas, no GasMeter (add a gas meter).
- dynamic_components: PV, two batteries, occupancy, CHPs and an energy manager, no meter (add an electricity meter).
- simple_air_conditioner_household_building_sizer and its .grouped twin: an air conditioner, no meter (add an electricity meter).
- electrolyzer_with_renewables: transformer and electrolyzer fed from a CSV series, no meter (add an electricity meter).
Each Python setup (system_setups/) and its recorded twin (energy_systems/*.energy_system.yaml) get the meter, wired so that it reads the devices' metered ports, so the metering check passes before PR 6 enforces it. title: Mid-year simulation windows: start_date is ignored by every profile
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md

Mid-year simulation windows are January in disguise. Every profile-driven component indexes its
year-long profile from timestep 0 as if that were 1 January, whatever `start_date` says: weather
(all six data sources), PV, building solar gains, LPG occupancy, cars, smart devices, the CSV
loader, and the heating-season gates of the heat-pump and CHP controllers. Measured: a July week
in Aachen yields 37 kWh of PV where the true July offset yields 426 kWh (11.5x), written to disk
under a July-stamped index. The parity rig's July window is fenced pending this epic.

This epic collects the PR plan (PR1..PR8+), the window contract, the cache epoch, the split
oracle and the independent repairs the analyses surfaced.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10, re-verified on the hydronic stack (simulator-warm-start, #914) while benchmarking part load: household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer at 900 s from 2021-06-01 to 2021-06-08 gets January's weather (outside temperature mean 1.3 °C, GHI 16 W/m2), 10.8 W mean irradiance on the collector and 0 kWh of collector heat; the same week inside a full-year run gets 1051 W and 19.0 kWh. The collector's own sun position follows start_date, so it combines a June sun with January irradiance (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.7). No new bead: this epic and its PR plan cover it. Part-load and solar benchmarks therefore run full years from 1 January.

title: Warn when the simulation year does not match the weather file's data year
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 13

`hisim/components/weather.py`'s `LocationEnum` carries NSRDB 2019 files for IE/GB/... and DWD/TRY
files for German locations; setups default to `year=2021`. The weather file's year and the
`SimulationParameters` year are independent, so simulating year X with weather of year Y silently
misaligns weekdays and (for leap years) day counts. The RenoVisor translator hard-codes 2019 for
this reason, but nothing in HiSim checks or documents the constraint.

Suggested fix: `Weather.i_prepare_simulation` should log a warning (or raise, behind a flag) when
the requested simulation year does not match the data year of the selected weather file; expose
the data year on `LocationEnum` entries instead of parsing it from filenames.

This sits next to the mid-year window epic: the same "which calendar does this profile speak"
question, from the year side rather than the offset side. The epic's leap-year refusal (PR2) is
the decidable half.

Testing: unit test that a mismatched year triggers the warning; no behaviour change otherwise.
close_reason: PR A+B of the #57 step 2 epic (feat/weather-year-ab)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Absorbed by hisim-weather-year-wps1.2 (PR B of the #57 step 2 epic, cmf 2026-09-27): INFO log + record note, not a WARNING; close with it.

title: A local LoadProfileGenerator request names its days day-first, which the generator reads month-first
description:
Source: found while building PR4+5 of roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.6), 2026-10-15.

UtspLpgConnector._execute_local_lpg_single_household wrote the requested days as %d-%m-%Y. The LoadProfileGenerator reads them month-first: a one-day request (01-01-2021 to 02-01-2021) delivered 32 days, to 1 February, and a one-week run from 1 January was simulated from 1 January to 1 August. Measured: the first two days of CHR01 differ between the day-first request and the ISO request of the same days (max 12 kW in a minute), because the generator household behaviour depends on how many days it simulates. A full year (01-01-2021 to 01-01-2022) reads the same either way. A mid-year window (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.6) cannot be requested at all: 01-07-2021 is read as 7 January.

Fix: request the days in ISO 8601 (the UTSP request already does), and name the requested days in the occupancy cache key. Moves the January week goldens of the local-LPG setups (the building sizers), not the full-year ones; ships alone so the golden diff has one cause.

Owner decision of 2026-10-19: the LoadProfileGenerator always simulates the run's whole calendar year (local and UTSP alike), and the run's window is cut from that year, because the household it simulates depends on how many days it simulates.
close_reason: Branch midyear-pr3b-lpg-request-dates: UtspLpgConnector.LPG_DATE_FORMAT (ISO 8601) for both requests; lpg_request_days() asks a local LoadProfileGenerator and the UTSP alike for the run's calendar year (1 January to 1 January of the next year, the end day the full-year request always had), whatever the run's length or start; request_key_material() names those days in the occupancy cache key, the same for every window of one year. tests/test_lpg_request_days.py (base: a day, a week, a July week and a year all request 2021-01-01..2022-01-01 and name the same key material; utsp: a one-week and a full-year local run give the same first week). Week goldens move for the eleven local-LPG setups only (household_*_building_sizer); full-year goldens do not.

title: Decide whether the solar-thermal collector's unread coordinates field leaves the energy-system format
description:
Source: PR6 of roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.7), 2026-10-15.

Since hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.7 the collector reads the sun the weather publishes (ApparentZenith and Azimuth inputs) and no longer computes its own, so SolarThermalSystemConfig.coordinates is read by nothing. The field is a format change to remove: an energy-system file that sets it would then be refused. No committed file, twin, assembly or RenoVisor translation sets it. It is also the only nested-dataclass config field of HiSim, and four tests of the energy-system config codec in tests/test_energy_system_configure.py use it as their real example (a complete config block keeps its rebuilt nested object, a sparse override rebuilds it, a mapping that does not fit is refused, a block entry's origin is not the configuration the run mutates).

Options:
(A) Remove the field (recommended): the config states nothing that has no effect, as coding_style.md (YAGNI, no unread config field) asks. The codec tests move onto a test-only config class with a nested dataclass. RenoVisor heads-up: the field leaves the schema.
(B) Keep the field, documented as not read (the state hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.7 leaves): no format change, but a field a user can set to no effect.
(C) Keep it and give it a meaning: the collector would compute the sun at its own location again, which reintroduces the duplicate sun the epic removed and its clock problem.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-16, option (A): the collector's unread coordinates field left the configuration and the energy-system schema; the four codec tests moved onto a test-only nested config (PR #1032, midyear-pr6-solar-thermal-sun).

title: Decide how the CSV loader finds a mid-year window in its profile; today a July run reads January
description:
Source: PR7 of roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md (hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.8), 2026-10-15; the plan lists the shipped wind CSV under "slice a kept year" but assigns it no PR.

CSVLoader (hisim/components/csvloader.py) reads column_values_in_loaded_unit[timestep], so timestep 0 is the file's first row whatever start_date says. The only shipped user is electrolyzer_with_renewables (hisim/inputs/wind_generated_power_1_min.csv, a 2021 minute series with a naive time column, 2021-01-01 00:00 to 2021-12-31 23:59). Its July week therefore runs on January wind; PR7 keeps it out of the july_week golden pairs (horizons [week, year] in scripts/golden_config.json, CANNOT_RUN_JULY in tests/test_golden_matrix.py). CSVLoaderConfig names a value column but no time column, so the loader cannot look the window up without a format change.

Options:
(A) Recommended: CSVLoaderConfig gains an optional time column (index or name) whose labels are read in the run's standard time; the loader resolves the window with hisim.window_offset.WindowOffset.resolve against them and refuses a window the file does not cover. A loader without a time column refuses any window not starting on 1 January (fail loudly). Format change: one optional field, RenoVisor does not use the loader.
(B) Only the refusal of (A), no new field: a mid-year run with a CSV loader fails until a file states its clock. No format change.
(C) Compute the offset from the file's resolution as if its first row were 1 January 00:00. Rejected by the plan's rule: never skip N rows from 1 January.
Once fixed, electrolyzer_with_renewables joins the July pairs and leaves CANNOT_RUN_JULY.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-16, option (A): CSVLoaderConfig.time_column (optional); with it the loader resolves the window with WindowOffset and reads the window's rows, without it a run not starting on 1 January is refused. The electrolyzer setup's July pairs follow in hisim-xgzf (branch midyear-csv-time-column).

title: Settle the contradictory initial-state defaults for storages, the EV and hydrogen
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses" (out of scope there, trigger: when the
season-aware storage seed lands)

Measured contradictions recorded by the analyses: the buffer storage starts at a hard-coded
35 degC while its dataclass default is 25 degC; the EV state of charge is 0 in one place and 0.5
in another; the hydrogen storage is 80 % full in one package and empty in the other -- arbitrary
twice over. DHW storage at 60 degC is season-neutral and correct; battery SOC 0 settles in a PV
day; about 25 controllers start "off" with their minimum idle time blocking the first 15-60
minutes, which is a season-neutral start artefact.

The epic's decision: keep the defaults and document the measured per-component transient, plus
exactly one season-aware change -- the buffer / space-heating storage seeds from the
heating-season gate, so outside the season it starts at ambient 20 degC instead of 35 degC (a
buffer nobody has charged sits at room temperature, the one derivation defensible in a sentence).
Warm-up prefixes are rejected on the measured evidence.

Done when: each component's initial value has one definition, the contradictions are gone, and
the season-aware buffer seed lands with its goldens.
notes: 2026-10-14: the storage part is done in branch storage-start-half (hisim-component-physics-4g9.64): every storage states one start value as a class constant, the 25 vs 35 °C buffer default and the EV 0 vs 0.5 contradiction are gone, the hydrogen start is 50 % (the 0 kg figure lived in obsolete/ and in the two hydrogen tests, which set starting_fill = 0 until this branch removed the field). The buffer's season-aware seed of this bead is superseded by 4g9.64: the owner kept the buffer at 35 °C (2026-10-15). Left here: the thermal mass and the controllers.

title: PR1: one window contract, YEARLYFORECAST renames and the dead smart device deleted
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR1, "The window contract (one chokepoint)"
and "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

First PR of the mid-year epic: establish the single window chokepoint, rename the
`YEARLYFORECAST`-shaped names to window names, fix the plot labels, and delete the dead
`generic_smart_device` (zero references, raises `KeyError` on first call -- deleting it also
retires the independently broken `convert_lpg_timestep_to_utc` and the test that pins its wrong
output).

Blast-radius rule for the whole epic: PR2 and PR4+5 must not move a single January golden (offset
0 on 1 January is each PR's own cheapest proof).

Done when: there is exactly one place that decides a run's window, and the renames and deletion
are in with no golden movement.
close_reason: PR1 is in (branch window-contract, on #981): SimulationParameters.validated_window refuses a window that does not start at midnight, cover whole days, lie in one year and divide into whole timesteps (SimulationWindowError); Weather.YEARLY_* became Weather.RUN_WINDOW_* and the Weather publishes exactly the run's window; the carpet and single-day plots label the run's own dates; utils.convert_lpg_timestep_to_utc and the test pinning its wrong output are deleted (the smart device stays archived in obsolete/ under D-30). No golden, twin, schema or cache key moves.

title: PR2: an offset primitive the weather adopts, plus the leap refusal and the four anchors
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR2, "The design: B' -- the profile owner
resolves one offset against its own frame", "Caches: the epoch" and "Independent repairs"

The offset primitive plus the weather adopting it; the leap-year refusal (the offset lookup is
where "this source cannot serve this date" is decidable); the DWD_15MIN reader, which sizes its
index from the run's duration instead of the file and is the one reader that cannot be sliced
until anchored; deleting the dead building solar-gain cache (delete, do not fix the `hasattr`
typo -- repairing it would serve stale entries past every check and add a sixth window-sensitive
cache); the four unit anchors; and building the oracle harness. Bumps the cache epoch.

The four unit anchors, in `tests/`: first-timestep identity against the source's own labels; the
DST phase pins (260 550 / 260 610 / 260 640 and a December mirror); each weather reader's
`index[0]` pinned (the six sources use three different anchors -- Berlin 00:30, Berlin 00:00
after the padding row `Weather.interpolate` prepends, and UTC 00:00, which is exactly why
"resolve against the delivered frame" is the rule); and the cold-then-warm cache equality
assertion.

The harness is `scripts/midyear_oracle.py`, modelled on the parity rig (per-run empty cache
directory, one process, one printed verdict table, a tolerance flag that shouts when nonzero),
reusing `ResultComparison` verbatim -- its index check refuses a misaligned slice for free.

Done when: PR2 moves no January golden and the oracle runs.
close_reason: Branch window-offset: hisim/window_offset.py resolves the run's start among a profile's own labels in standard time (owner decision 2026-10-14), refusing uncovered windows with a leap-year note; the Weather keeps its year, carries standard_time labels through its cache and reads row offset + timestep; DWD_15MIN is sized from its file and the hourly padding no longer invents 31 December of a leap year; window_start is key material of the PV, solar-gain and car producers (solar thermal had it), no epoch; the solar-gain cache is kept. tests/test_window_offset.py holds the four anchors (1 July = row 260640 of the delivered Aachen frame). scripts/midyear_oracle.py runs: July and December weeks of basic_household reproduce all weather columns and the solar gains bit-exactly, cold == warm, occupancy still January until PR4+5. No January-start or full-year golden moves (the 3 pairs that diverge do so identically on the base branch).

title: PR3: rewrite convert_lpg_data_to_utc as localize, convert, slice
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR3

`convert_lpg_data_to_utc` is rewritten as localize -> convert -> slice. This changes January
numbers too: the current code starts every window at source row 60 and fabricates the final hour.
It is therefore the deliberate January re-bless of the epic and ships alone, so the golden diff
has exactly one cause. Bumps the cache epoch.

Depends on PR2 (the offset primitive).

Done when: the conversion is date-correct, the January goldens are re-blessed in one commit whose
message names this as the single cause, and nothing else is in the PR.

The LoadProfileGenerator connector's cache still keys legacy-style (`utils.get_cache_file` / `build_cache_key_string` on the household configuration and the simulation parameters), and what it files is the profiles after `convert_lpg_data_to_utc`. Its key does not see `hisim/components/lpg_local_time.py`, so the rewrite here would be served from entries the old conversion wrote, while the car's producer key (hisim-caching-hi1.4) does follow it. This PR has to make the connector's key follow the conversion: extract the transform as a producer whose closure contains `lpg_local_time`, or put the conversion's fingerprint into the legacy key material (hisim-caching-hi1.4 close reason; review of #987, R13/R36).
close_reason: Branch midyear-pr3-lpg-utc: hisim/components/lpg_local_time.py puts the LoadProfileGenerator's wall-clock minutes onto the run's standard-time clock (owner decision 1 of 2026-10-14) by localize (spring hour dropped, autumn hour taken twice), convert and slice (WindowOffset.resolve); the occupancy and the car producer use it. A January run reads the profile's row 0 at timestep 0 instead of row 60, the year's last hour is the profile's own, a run from 1 January ending between the clock changes is served (the oracle's reference no longer runs to the year's end). The occupancy cache key carries the conversion's code fingerprint. Every January week golden with an occupancy moves (one cause: the one-hour shift); the four setups without one (electrolyzer_with_renewables, simple_air_conditioner_household_building_sizer, simple_system_setup_one/two) are unchanged. Mid-year windows still read January until hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.6.

title: PR4+5: the LPG connector owns occupancy and cars in all three modes, gates go day-of-year
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR4+5 -- MUST SHIP TOGETHER

The LPG connector owns the window offset for occupancy and for the cars, in all three data
acquisition modes, and the seasonal gates (the heat-pump and CHP controllers' heating-season
checks) go day-of-year. These must ship together, or a July window heats the house. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR3.

Blast-radius rule: must not move a single January golden -- offset 0 on 1 January is the PR's own
cheapest proof.
close_reason: Branch midyear-pr4-lpg-window: the occupancy reads the run's window in all three modes. Every profile is looked up from the StartTime its activity files state, laid onto the run's year (a shipped profile like the weather); a local LoadProfileGenerator run and a UTSP request both ask for the run's whole calendar year (lpg_request_days of #1030, owner decision of 2026-10-19), so a computed profile starts on 1 January too; the whole delivered profile is put onto the run's clock and sliced at start_date (LpgLocalTime). The cars read the profile's StartTime, which the occupancy now publishes, and their producer slices at the window start. The CHP controller's heating season counts timesteps from 1 January (the only seasonal gate left; the heat pumps follow the heating curve, which reads the weather). Evidence: before the rebase onto #1030, all 22 January week pairs bit-identical to PR3b; after it, household_gas_building_sizer / one_week_60s passes the golden check; scripts/midyear_oracle.py on basic_household (1 July, 7 days, 900 s) passes with the occupancy's 6 columns exact (they were January before); a local-LPG July week equals the full-year run's July days (test_lpg_request_days.py); tests in test_lpg_local_time.py, test_car_profile_producer.py, test_generic_chp.py fail without the change.

title: PR6: the solar thermal collector consumes the weather's window instead of its own sun
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR6 and "Independent repairs surfaced by
the analyses"

The solar-thermal collector drops its naive-UTC duplicate sun position and consumes the weather's
published window. This is one of the two places that honour the date today, which is what makes a
mid-year run incoherent rather than correct -- the collector sees a genuine July sun (apparent
zenith 27.7 degrees) wired to January irradiance. Three solar-thermal goldens move. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR2.

Done when: there is one sun position per run, and the three goldens are re-blessed.
close_reason: Branch midyear-pr6-solar-thermal-sun: the collector reads ApparentZenith and Azimuth from its weather inputs every timestep, so there is one sun per run, on the weather's clock (the window PR2 resolves); the sun-position producer (hisim/components/solar_thermal_sun_position.py), its cache and its test are deleted. The three solar-thermal week pairs move (collector heat 0.2->0.3 and 0.4->0.6 kWh in the January week), every other week pair is bit-identical to PR4; household_gas_solar_thermal full year: collector heat 1047.2 -> 1042.0 kWh, boiler gas +0.03 %. The collector's coordinates field is now unread: whether it leaves the format is hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.13 (owner decision).

title: PR7: lift the July fence in its five sites and bless the first true July goldens
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR7; the fence is recorded in
`scripts/p3_parity_matrix.py` and R11.5 as amended 2026-09-06

Lift the fence in its five sites -- the parity workflow's hand-kept window options among them,
which nothing derives from the code -- invert the fence test into "July differs from January",
add the `july_week` parameter set to `scripts/golden_config.json` and bless the first true July
references.

This is what unfences the parity rig's July window, which P6 of the declarative plan needs to
confirm the stack green "over every runnable window".

Depends on PR4+5 and PR6.
close_reason: Branch midyear-pr7-july-fence: the fence is lifted in its five sites (scripts/p3_parity_matrix.py, p3_parity_runs.py, p3_parity_check.py, .github/workflows/p3-parity.yml with july offered, and the golden gate's vocabulary: scripts/golden_horizons.py + golden_matrix.py gain the july_week horizon, one_week_july); the fence test became test_the_july_window_reads_july_not_january; scripts/golden_config.json gains july_week_60s for 22 of 23 setups (electrolyzer_with_renewables kept out until hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.14, CANNOT_RUN_JULY in tests/test_golden_matrix.py); golden-check offers july_week by dispatch. All 22 July pairs ran locally (scripts/golden_update.py into a scratch directory, nothing committed): PV 37 -> 426 kWh (basic_household) and 82.5 -> 949.7 kWh (building sizers), heating demand ~0, collector 53-67 kWh/week, max indoor 25-30 C. Parity rig July: basic_household and household_heatpump_car_building_sizer reach parity. The July goldens are blessed through golden-update.yml when this PR reaches the bottom of the stack.

title: PR8+: every stateful component expresses its complete state as startup configuration
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR8+ and "Validation: the split oracle"

A series, one component per PR. Run the full year once, read every stateful component's state at
the window start (the battery's SOC on 1 July, the storage temperatures, the thermal-mass
temperature, the controllers' modes and timers), hand those to the window run as startup values,
and the whole comparison becomes an exact gate: with its complete mid-cycle state handed over,
even a bang-bang controller continues on the very limit cycle the year run was on, so the one
column no warm-up could ever buy back (`WaterMassFlowHDS`, permanently 16.7 % out) joins the gate
too.

What it costs is completeness -- a partially seeded component just re-imports its transient --
and not every component can express its state as configuration today (controller idle timers, the
meters' cumulative sums, the EMS's internals are not config fields). So the seeded tier grows
component by component: a column moves from the oracle's report tier to the exact gate the moment
its component's full state is expressible as startup configuration. The cumulative meter columns
move immediately, gated on first differences instead of levels.

This is checkpoint handover at the configuration level, which is why it shares its prerequisites
with the two `i_save_state` repairs (the EMS reference restore and the HDS self-assignment).

The series moves no golden at all: startup values default to today's constants, and each PR's
proof is its component's columns going exactly to zero in the seeded oracle.

Depends on PR7.

title: The cost database loader checks neither embodied_co2.per_unit nor the field_sources keys, and embodied CO2 has no provenance record
description:
Source: the review of PR #986, type-invariants, config-footgun and wiring findings, 2026-10-15. Pre-existing; every shipped row is consistent today.

1. CostDatabase._load_devices (hisim/economics/database.py) validates specific_investment.per_unit against DeviceEntry.PER_UNIT_TO_SIZE_UNIT, but not embodied_co2.per_unit, and nothing requires the two to agree. DeviceEntry.embodied_co2_for_size branches only on None, so a row priced per m2 with its carbon per unit (or the reverse) books a wrong carbon without a word, and resolve_check compares only the price unit.
2. field_sources keys are not checked against the row's fields, so a misspelt key silently falls back to source_ids.
3. resolve_device writes provenance records for specific_investment, maintenance_rate_per_year and service_life_in_years only; embodied CO2 gets none, so a field_sources entry for embodied_co2 (the four EXTERIOR_DOOR rows since #986) is read by nobody, and the carbon cannot be traced with `python -m hisim.economics explain`.

Fix: the loader refuses an unknown embodied_co2.per_unit, one that differs from per_unit, and a field_sources key that names no field of the row; the engine records the provenance of the embodied CO2 it books (keyed `embodied_co2`, as the JSON names it).

Done when: the three checks and the record exist, each with a test, and `python -m hisim.economics validate` passes on the shipped data.

title: A full-year run of every recorded twin writes heat and electricity Sankeys across all devices of the house, from sources to end uses and losses, with no undeclared node
