title: Part-load run fraction above a step-length threshold: the threshold, the memoryless part-load rule and the boiler
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §2, §4, §5 (owner, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10).

Above a step-length threshold (SimulationParameters.part_load_above_seconds, default 600 s), a device its controller has switched on runs only the fraction of the step (PLR) that ends its store at the controller's target. The averaged flow enters the store's node as a constant inflow; the controllers' on/off and mode decisions and MixedNode.step are unchanged; at and below the threshold the ratio is exactly 1 while running and 0 while off, so 60 s results and goldens stay bit-identical.

Design (owner, 2026-10-10, replacing the pass-counting search): hisim/part_load.py holds a pure memoryless rule, PartLoadRule.next_part_load_ratio: r_next = r_run (T_aim - T_start) / (T_end - T_start), clamped to [0, 1], T_aim the middle of the 0.05 K band above the target; inside the band r_run is kept; a store at or above its target gives 0, an end at or below the start (draw dominates) gives 1, a device that ran nothing below the target gives 1. Each device publishes the ratio it ran with (Units.FRACTION) and its controller reads it; the simulator's plain iteration solves the rule, with no acceleration and no controller state; under force_convergence the controller publishes the ratio run. PartLoadControl (controller part) and PartLoadCommand (device part) are stateless. GenericBoilerController commands the boiler's hot-water fraction (every fuel) and publishes its target; GenericBoiler books the fraction and reports it. SimpleDHWStorage publishes nothing new.

Done when: 60 s golden checks pass unchanged; the gas twin's hot-water heat and gas agree within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s over a full year; forced steps and run time reported.

Resolved 2026-10-12: the evaluation-order problem (in the boiler twins the boiler was evaluated between its controller and the tank, so the rule paired a ratio with the tank's answer to the one before and did not settle) is solved by the simulator's kind order, #922, below this branch (hisim-hydronics-fxix.16, closed).
close_reason: Done-when met, measured 2026-10-12 on hydronic-part-load (#915) with the simulator's kind order (#922) below it; full year 2021, predefined occupancy, against the 60 s run of the same head. Gas twin: hot-water heat and gas -0.002 % at 900 s and -0.012 % at 3600 s (whole-step charges in the kind order without the rule: +0.17 % / +0.63 %). Steps flagged at force_convergence (12 passes or more) 94 / 47, of which 59 / 45 ran a forced pass (without the rule 38 / 0); 718 of 759 / 614 of 643 partial hot-water steps converge and end 0.032 / 0.037 K above the target on average, at most 0.050 K; mean passes 3.29 / 3.67 (3.18 at 60 s). Wall time 12-16 s at 900 s, 6-9 s at 3600 s, 124-158 s at 60 s (two runs on six cores). The oil, pellet, wood-chip and hydrogen twins give the same hot-water results and step counts. 60 s: the full year of the gas, gas + solar and pellet twins is bit-identical to #922 in every common column, with the same passes. Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md section 11 (part-load-hds, #918). hisim-hydronics-fxix.17 (a draw larger than the rise a partial step still needs) stays open on its own.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10, memoryless rule (branches hydronic-part-load to part-load-hds), full year 2021 against 60 s of the same head: gas twin hot-water gas +0.27 % at 900 s and +0.18 % at 3600 s with 1013 and 679 forced steps in the twin's order (the controller pairs a ratio with the tank's answer to the one before, hisim-hydronics-fxix.16); with the controller moved before the boiler -0.00 % and -0.01 % with 46 and 50 forced steps and 3.42 / 3.89 passes per step. 60 s bit-identical to #914 (gas and gas + solar). Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §11.

title: Staged document: kept-asset replacement years count from the price basis year, calendar_year from the simulation year
description:
Source: renovisorissues #58 work (worktree agent-e58), 2026-09-26.

The staged document labels year index y as calendar_year = simulation_year + y (2019 + y for the
mockup), but the engine ages every kept register asset at the price basis year
(calculators/context_resolution.py: first_replacement_year = max(1, round(life - (price_basis_year -
installation_year)))). The relative replacement year therefore counts from price_basis_year while
the document says it counts from simulation_year.

Mockup (IE, simulation_year 2019, price_basis_year 2026): the hot-water cylinder is installed 2008
(request) with a 20-year life from the cost database. It is due in 2028, the engine books it at
year index 2 = 2008 + 20 - 2026, and annual[2].calendar_year says 2021. Every kept asset of the
mockup is shifted the same 7 years (boiler 2008+18 -> year 1 = "2020", meters 2018+16 -> year 8 =
"2027").

The same mismatch reaches the staged ageing: StagedEvaluator._staged_inputs registers a subject an
earlier stage bought as installed in simulation_year + from_year_j, and the next stage ages it at
price_basis_year, so it is (price_basis_year - simulation_year) years older than the plan says.

Related: hisim-economics-engine-cyc.16 (whether a weather/price-basis mismatch gets a report note) - this one is a
figure, not a note. Decide which year is the plan's year 0 (price_basis_year, or simulation_year
with ages anchored there) and make calendar_year, the register ages and the staged ageing agree.
Done when the mockup cylinder's replacement year satisfies installation_year + service_life_years -
(year-0 calendar year) on the published document.
close_reason: kept assets age against plan year 0, so calendar_year and replacement years agree (feat/year-zero)

title: An unpriced envelope measure on an element with no area is sized 1.0 m2, so it books the cost database's carbon of a phantom square metre
description:
Source: the review of PR #986, silent-failure and config-footgun findings, 2026-10-15. Pre-existing code, not changed by #986.

EconomicContextBuilder._envelope_subject (hisim/renovisor/economics.py) refuses a priced measure whose element has no area (TranslatorError, ELEMENT_AREA_MESSAGE), but an unpriced one is built with `size=float(area) if area else 1.0`, size_unit m2. _element_area returns None only when the Building's area for the element is zero (a TABULA row without windows, say). The engine then books entry.embodied_co2_for_size(1.0), e.g. 43 kg for a door, and the subject claims 1 m2 of an element the house does not have. For the door the reviewer found the TABULA area always positive (3.28 m2 on the mockup's archetype), so the window is the likelier case.

Fix: refuse an envelope measure on an element without area whether priced or not (as the priced branch does), or record it with size 0 and a note; decide together with hisim-hq4z.

Done when: no envelope subject is sized with a surrogate area, and a test covers a measure on an element of zero area.
close_reason: Owner decision of 2026-10-18: an envelope measure on an element the house does not have is refused whether priced or not. EconomicContextBuilder._envelope_subject now raises the TranslatorError ELEMENT_AREA_MESSAGE (reworded: names the measure, the element and that the house has none of it) for every measure whose element has no area, before anything is booked; the surrogate size of 1.0 m2 is gone. A RenoVisor run with such a measure exits 3 with translator_error.json. test_economics_context covers the priced and the unpriced case.

title: The post-processing charts take the step length once, as seconds_per_timestep
description:
Owner plan 2026-10-18. Every chart took time_correction_factor_in_hours, the step length in hours, and Chart.__init__ stored it and never read it: tests/test_charts.py passed 3600 where one hour is 1.0 and nothing noticed. PostProcessingDataTransfer.time_correction_factor_in_hours_per_timestep existed only to feed it. The single-day chart also took timesteps_per_day (#982), a second spelling of the same step length.

Done when: the parameter and the attribute are gone from the chart base class, the line, carpet, bar and single-day charts, postprocessing_main.py and the tests; the single-day chart takes seconds_per_timestep and derives its rows per day through SimulationDay.timesteps_per_day, keeping the exact whole-day slicing of #982 (2 h and 45 min steps) and refusing a non-positive step.
close_reason: The charts take the step length once, as seconds_per_timestep: time_correction_factor_in_hours (stored, never read) and timesteps_per_day are removed

title: Clean up and unify the output files of a run: result.json, all_kpis.json and the rest
description:
Source: owner request 2026-09-25 ('result.json vs all_kpis.json is a mess').

A RenoVisor job writes several overlapping files, each with its own naming, units and provenance rules:
- all_kpis.json (postprocessing): flat KPI names with values baked into the names (setpoints, '1.0 K', '26.0 Celsius'), units such as °C*h, and legacy cost leaves that must not be read (renovisorissues #16).
- result.json (hisim/renovisor/result.py, kpis.py): the payload, with its own field names (energy_demand_in_kilowatt_hour_per_year, comfort ratings), each value wrapped with provenance/source strings that quote all_kpis.json names.
- economics_result.json (staged document) and economic_inputs.json (bridge), plus the lifecycle exports.
- mapping_report.json, problems.json, translator_error.json, and the capability document's results rows (KpiSchema, CostSchema) that describe the payload.
The same figure can appear in two files under two names and units (e.g. degree-hours K*h vs °C*h; energy in kWh vs Wh), and a reader cannot tell which file owns it.

Goal: one documented output layout. Decide which file owns each figure (simulation KPIs vs the RenoVisor payload vs economics), give every figure one name and one unit convention (_in_<unit>, as the contract now uses), stop duplicating values across files (reference instead), drop or quarantine the legacy cost leaves of all_kpis.json, and keep the capability document's result rows generated from that single description. Include a migration note for the backend and frontend (renovisorissues heads-up) and the golden references (all_kpis.json keys are what the golden check compares).

Start with an inventory: every file a RenoVisor run writes, its writer, its readers (backend, frontend, goldens, tests), and every figure it carries.

title: basic_household_only_heating's building reads no heat from its distribution system, so the house is never heated
description:
Found by hydronic stage E (branch sankey-pr3-storages): with the distribution system declaring its ports, its ThermalPowerDelivered port is unlinked in basic_household_only_heating, because nothing that moves energy reads it. The building there is wired with connect_only_predefined_connections(my_weather, my_occupancy) (system_setups/basic_household_only_heating.py) and its twin lists only Weather and UTSPConnector as the building's inputs (energy_systems/basic_household_only_heating.energy_system.yaml), so the building's ThermalPowerDelivered input is not connected and reads 0 W, while the gas boiler, the buffer and the distribution system run: 269.2 kWh delivered over 10-12 January 2021 at 900 s go into no building. The balance itself closes (the heat leaves the declared distribution system to an unlinked node).

It is a golden setup (golden_references/basic_household_only_heating__*.json), so the fix moves its KPIs: the building gets its heat, the boiler burns to a heated house.

Done when: the building reads the distribution system's heat in the setup and in its recorded twin, the port links to the building in the balance report, and the goldens are re-blessed with the KPI deltas in the PR.
close_reason: branch only-heating-house-heated: the building reads the distribution system's heat in the setup and its twin (Building inputs list HeatDistributionSystem). No build-time guard (owner, 2026-10-24): lost heat fails every run generically once the complete energy balance enforces unlinked ports (complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md, PR 6); a special-case check or test would break with multi-zone and multi-family systems. Golden week (first January week, 60 s): room air min 0.68 -> 20.00 C, mean 5.87 -> 20.00 C; degree-hours more than 1 K below the set temperature 2207.8 -> 0.0; heat delivered by the distribution system 1718.9 -> 548.5 kWh (before: into a 0.7 C house that never warmed); gas 1929.7 -> 806.4 kWh. Goldens of the setup move; re-bless.

title: Window opening ventilates the building at an adjustable air-exchange rate and books the heat it removes, instead of overwriting the indoor air temperature
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-19, on Q-E of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md: "the window opening needs to be quite a bit more sophisticated with an adjustable ventilation rate to model that even if you open all the windows, the indoor air temperature doesn't magically equal the outside air temperature, unless you have pretty strong winds or a lot of fans".

Today: when the occupants open the windows (building.py, occupants_open_the_windows), the building overwrites its published indoor air temperature (up to 7.96 K lower, in 1,986 steps a year of the heat-pump twin at 900 s) and books no heat leaving the building, so the cooling has no energy flow behind it and the building's balance cannot show it.

Wanted: open windows add a ventilation heat transfer H_ve,win = rho*c*q_win (q_win an adjustable air-exchange rate, a sourced default for tilted/open windows, optionally wind-dependent) to the 5R1C network for the steps they are open; the indoor temperature follows from the network, and the removed heat is a ventilation loss of the building (ROOM_HEAT out, see the Sankey spec). Related: hisim-29qd (window opening as an option of the energy system and of a RenoVisor request).

Done when: open windows cool the building through the ventilation term only, the heat removed is booked and appears in the building's balance and Sankey, the rate is configurable with a sourced default, and the summer comfort KPIs are re-blessed.

title: Remove the retired legacy_flat_subsidy_share field from the device tables, loader, validation and reports
description: Follow-up of the PR #799 review (owner decision 2026-09-24): the §10.1 flat subsidy shim is retired in behaviour -- with no catalogue nothing is booked on any path -- but the legacy_flat_subsidy_share field was kept in hisim/cost_database/devices_{DE,IE,AT}.json (about 150 lines) and in the loader, validation and catalog_entries, documented as retired. Remove it everywhere in its own PR (not in the bottom of the stack), with the data files, the dataclass field, validation, and any report text.

title: An omitted applicant.role defaults to owner_occupier without a defaulted line in the mapping report
description: Found by the tier-1 path verifier after hisim-qzyv (probe field:applicant.role=owner_occupier: no_effect against the anchor, 'applicant.role: no line there'). The request schema says an omitted role defaults to owner_occupier, and EconomicContextBuilder._subsidy_context leaves the profile's owner-occupier default standing, but EconomicContextBuilder.stated_leaves only reports applicant keys the request states, so the anchor's mapping report carries no line for applicant.role at all. The contract's rule is that the backend reports every default: a request without a role should get a 'defaulted' line for applicant.role (owner_occupier). The other applicant keys stay undetermined when omitted (a question, not a default), so no line is right for them.
close_reason: An omitted applicant.role now yields a defaulted line (owner_occupier, the profile's own actor, with a note citing the schema default) from EconomicContextBuilder._subsidy_context. No other applicant key has an engine default (main_residence is schema-required; the rest stay None = undetermined), so none gets a line. Tested in test_economics_context and test_translate.

title: CI rule: no Python file over 500 lines of source code (comments excluded); split larger files
description:
Owner request (cmf, 2026-09-27): a CI rule that no Python file may hold more than 500 lines of actual source code; anything larger is split into several files (modules / a package).

**Counting.** A line counts when it carries a code token. Comment-only lines and blank lines don't count. Count with `tokenize`, not a regex, so a `#` inside a string still counts as code. Open question for the owner: do docstrings count as code? (Tokenize treats them as strings, so today they count.)

**Today (2026-09-27, main e51dfca3, docstrings counted):** 145 of 662 files are over the limit (hisim 80, tests 52, scripts 8, obsolete 5). The worst:
- `hisim/economics/views.py`: 5051
- `hisim/components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py`: 2798
- `hisim/economics/staged.py`: 2371
- `report_prose.py`: 2125
- `renovisor/capabilities.py`: 2074
- `renovisor/translate.py`: 2046

**Rollout (proposal):** a ratchet, so CI stays green from day one.
- `scripts/check_file_size.py` (or a flake8 plugin) plus an allowlist file, e.g. `.github/file_size_allowlist.txt`, holding each current offender and its count.
- CI fails on:
  - a new file over 500;
  - an allowlisted file that grows;
  - a stale allowlist entry (the file is now ≤500 or was deleted, so it must leave the list).
- Wire it into `quality.yml` as a new job (it's cheap).
- Decide the scope: `hisim/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `system_setups/`. Exclude `obsolete/`? Generated files?
- Then split the offenders, one bead per file or per package, starting with the economics and renovisor giants. Each split keeps imports stable: re-export from the old module, or update the call sites.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decisions (cmf, 2026-09-27): docstrings do NOT count as code (module/class/function docstrings excluded, like comments and blank lines); obsolete/ is out of scope. Recount on main with that rule: 74 of 628 files over 500 (hisim 44, tests 27, scripts 3). Largest: economics/views.py 2727, more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py 2381, economics/report_prose.py 1920, loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py 1671, kpi_preparation.py 1629, building/building.py 1569.

title: The hydrogen tank and the example storage withdraw below their floor, down to 0, though their floor is documented as the fill that always stays
description: Source: review of PR #1000 (storage-start-half), findings on generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.py:604 and example_storage.py withdraw, 2026-10-15. HydrogenStorageSimulation.withdraw (hisim/components/generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.py) takes the whole request whenever fill > request, even when that leaves the fill below min_capacity, and its partial branch sets fill = 0; ElectrolyzerWithHydrogenStorageConfig.min_capacity is documented as 'Hydrogen that always stays in the tank, in kg; withdrawal stops here'. Reproduce: a tank with min_capacity 100 kg starts at 300 kg (initial_fill_in_kg) and, drained long enough, reports 0 kg. ExampleStorageState.withdraw (hisim/components/example_storage.py) has the same two branches against min_val_in_kwh. No setup uses either storage with a non-zero floor (the hydrogen tank is used in tests only, both with an empty floor), so no result moves today. Done when: both withdraw only down to the floor (the released amount is fill minus floor), with a test on a non-zero floor that fails on the old code. Second review round of PR #1000 (2026-10-16): both withdraw also raise 'forgotten case' when the request equals the fill exactly and the fill lies above the floor, because none of their three branches matches; reproduce: ExampleStorageState(min_val_in_kwh=0, max_val_in_kwh=50, fill_in_kwh=25).withdraw(25) and a 250 kg tank asked for 250 kg in one step. The rewritten branches cover that case too, with a test.

title: Standing water in a heat distribution system gives its heat to the rooms by free convection while the pump stands
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-20, split out of hisim-pnw7: not wanted now.

On main the standing pipe water of a chain without a buffer keeps its temperature for months and gives the rooms nothing; physically radiators keep emitting after the pump stops. The decay is already modelled in heat_distribution_system.py (determine_water_temperature_input_output_effective_thermal_power_without_mass_flow) but unused in these chains. Measured in the 9uoo.12 investigation: with it as the pipe-water node's draw while the pump stands, the district-heating twin got 13 forced steps in the shoulder season at 900 s (the valve flips between heating, cooling and shut within a step); those must be solved too.

Done when: the standing water's heat reaches the rooms through a booked port, the balance closes per step, and the forced steps stay at main's count.

title: Hydronic chain without a buffer: the pipe water as a start-of-step node, D25's flow ownership and district heating's bill (split out of stage D)
description:
Source: the review of #1006 (hydronic stage D, PR 0; review1006_evaluation.md M-A) and the owner's decision of 2026-10-16 (Noah): the no-buffer half of stage D is split out of stage D, which closes with the buffer chain (roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §9.5 D and §12).

What is left, from the first scope of §9.5 D and from §4.6, for every chain without a buffer (district heating; gas_boiler_household, NO_STORAGE_MASS_FLOW_FIX):

- The pipe water of the heat distribution system as a start-of-step node, as stage D made the buffer: HeatDistribution still publishes the previous step's heat and temperatures when no buffer sits in front of it (heat_distribution_system.py; the remainder of hisim-hydronics-fxix.14 without a buffer). The pipe water's mass (mass_of_water_in_hds) and its free-convection decay are already there; the generator then sees the pipe water's start temperature as its return.
- D25 (design summary S10, owner 2026-10-04): who pumps a circuit without a buffer follows from the circuit. The distribution system reads the flow of the component at the other end of its space-heating circuit if that component publishes one, and pumps with its design flow otherwise; the position enum PositionHotWaterStorageInSystemSetup is removed.
- District heating's bill (hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.12): the substation bills the heat that entered the pipe water, so the bill equals the pipe water's change of energy plus the heat delivered to the building, instead of the heat its controller asks for.

Stage D's part-load mode acts only where a buffer sits, so in this chain every ratio is 1; the district-heating twin forces no steps at 900 s and its results did not move in stage D.

Done when: the pipe water and the distribution system close per step in the district-heating twin and gas_boiler_household at 60, 900 and 3600 s; the district-heating bill equals the pipe water's change of energy plus the delivered heat (hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.12 closed); the position enum is gone and the affected twins are re-recorded; the delivered heat at 900 s is within 1 % of the 60 s run; the goldens are re-blessed through golden-update.yml and the result change is announced on renovisorissues.
notes:
2026-10-19 (fxix triage): hisim-hydronics-fxix.14 is closed for the chains with a buffer; its remainder, the distribution system's one-step lag without a buffer, is this bead's first item.

Owner decisions 2026-10-20 (from the hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.12 investigation, report /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/9uoo12/report.md):
- Acceptance (from 9uoo.12, closed into this bead): the district-heating bill equals the pipe water's change of energy plus the heat delivered, per step; measured with a prototype start-of-step pipe-water node (hydronics.StartOfStepNode, C = 0.89 MJ/K, substation unchanged): exact at 60 and 900 s, 0 forced steps, comfort 215 -> 3 degC h below 20 degC at 900 s.
- Long steps: 'every ratio is 1 in this chain' holds only at 60 and 900 s. At 3600 s the explicit node swings 10-52 degC (a = m c dt / C = 4.6) and comfort collapses (447 -> 1976 degC h). The chain without a buffer gets the part-load mode above 600 s, as the buffer has (spec section 12): the node publishes end-temperature-without-circuit ports, the substation and the boiler get a part-load circuit.
- Control: whether the circuit flows is decided by the room thermostat in the heat-distribution L1 controller (hisim-component-physics-4g9.37, which this bead now depends on), never by the standing pipe water's temperature; the generator decides only how hot (the curve's supply set point). D25 is reworded accordingly. A prototype that let the boiler controller decide on the pipe water's start temperature deadlocked (the boiler waits for the standing water to cool, the water only cools if it flows, it only flows when the boiler fires; 14170 degC h below 20 degC).
- Free convection of the standing pipe water is out of this bead (owner): hisim-pipe-water-free-convection-6vdp (P3).
- The gas boiler chain's flow mismatch is filed as hisim-boiler-circuit-flow-gap-g2mx (P1), which this bead's D25 item fixes.

Owner decision 2026-10-20 (option b): D25 is split out of this bead into hisim-boiler-circuit-flow-gap-g2mx (P1), together with the gas boiler's flow gap. This bead keeps the pipe water as a start-of-step node, the district-heating bill (the acceptance criterion from 9uoo.12) and the part-load mode above 600 s, at P3.

title: The rooftop sizing law reads each PV module's peak power from its database, so sizing and simulation use one source
description:
Source: the LLM review of PR #1092 (Sankey PR 2, electricity ports), evaluated in review-evals/review1092_evaluation.md; owner decision on 2026-10-21: option (c), the rooftop law reads the peak power from the database.

The problem. `PVSystemConfig.MODULES` (hisim/components/generic_pv_system/config.py, about lines 109-110) lists the Sandia module "Hanwha HSL60P6-PA-4-250T [2013]" at 1.65 m2 and 250 W, its nameplate. The performance model divides the AC power by the database's Impo times Vmpo, 8.0822 A x 29.2011 V = 236.0 W (hisim/inputs/photovoltaic/data_processed/sandia_modules_new.csv, line 519), and since #1092 the solar power on the modules is divided by the same 236.0 W. The rooftop sizing law counts the modules that fit on the roof and multiplies by 250 W, so a rooftop-sized Sandia array is simulated as 250/236 = 1.059 times the modules on the roof: 5.9 % more AC power and 5.9 % more sun than the roof holds. The ratio of AC power to sun is right. The CEC row ("Trina Solar TSM-435NE09RC.05", 1.98 m2, 435.16 W = I_mp_ref x V_mp_ref) has no gap. Today only the air_conditioned_house twin uses the Sandia module, with a pinned 4000 W, so no recorded result moves. The gap exists before #1092.

The purpose (owner, 2026-10-21). Once the rooftop law and the PV system both read the module's area and peak power from the module database (`calculation.module_area_and_peak_power`), any CEC or Sandia module name works without a hand-kept row in `PVSystemConfig.MODULES`. A run can then compare module efficiencies: the CEC database holds modules from about 17 % to 23 %; the default Trina Solar TSM-435NE09RC.05 is 22.0 %, the Sandia Hanwha HSL60P6-PA-4-250T [2013] about 15 %. The owner wants this to show the impact of higher-efficiency modules graphically in the energy Sankey, where PV starts at the sun (Q-D of roadmap/complete_energy_sankeys_spec.md): a narrower loss band per kWh of electricity and, on a fixed roof, more electricity from the same sun.

To do: the rooftop sizing law takes the module's area and peak power from the module database row the simulation reads (one source), and `PVSystemConfig.MODULES` goes (or keeps nothing the database states).

Done when: a rooftop-sized Sandia array's peak power is the number of modules on the roof times 236.01 W; a module given only by its name and database runs and sizes correctly, with a test for a CEC module that has no row in `MODULES`; the twins' KPIs are unchanged (CEC default module).

title: Review the wood-fuel emission factors against one stated accounting
description: From the PR #794 review (owner decision 2026-09-24: a bead, not in #794). With the corrected wood-chip heating value (4333.3 kWh/t, hisim-cost-data-l07.15) the shipped wood-chip CO2 factors disagree per tonne: the legacy DE 2018-2024 series 0.0313 kg/kWh (src_opex_14/15, kept as published by #791) is 136 kg/t, the AI-placeholder DE/IE 2026/2035 rows derive from 80 kg/t (0.0185 kg/kWh), AT 2025/2040 is 82 kg/t. UBA's factsheet (2024, table 3) states 88.1 g CO2-eq/MJ (0.317 kg/kWh) for wood chips, counting biogenic carbon -- a different accounting. Decide one accounting (biogenic counted or not, GEG vs UBA vs legacy source), then re-derive the wood-fuel factors (pellets too) and replace the AI placeholders.

title: Stop the heat pump's space-heating controller from staying off below a low flow setpoint
description:
Found 2026-09-23 while computing comfort grades (hisim-sska) on the RenoVisor mockup package, full year 2019, IE: air/water hplib + floor heating + insulation.

MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2658-2686) switches on only when the buffer water is below set_heating_flow_temperature - lower_temperature_offset_for_state_conditions_in_celsius (5.0) and off above flow + upper offset (5.0). With floor heating in mild weather the HeatDistributionController asks for a flow of ~23.4 C, so the switch-on point is ~18.4 C; the buffer sits at room temperature (~18.6 C) and never gets there. The pump stays off while the distribution is on and the room sits at 18.6-19.5 C against a 21 C setpoint.

Evidence: June-August 4516 quarter-hours with room < 20.5 C, of which 4223 with SH controller off, HDS state on, window closed. 1944 of the year's 2503 K*h below setpoint fall in June-September at outdoor > 10 C. Heat delivered 26 233 kWh vs 29 425 kWh theoretical demand (-11%). The gas-boiler baseline of the same house: 331 K*h.

Consequence: every heat-pump plan with a low flow setpoint under-delivers heat, so its electricity, bills, CO2 and LCOH are too low -- the economics comparison favours the heat pump by roughly that much. Owner interview on the fix pending.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/heat-pump-switch-on-floor (decided with Noah 2026-09-23: never switch on below the room setpoint, component-wide). RenoVisor mockup package, full year IE: heat delivered 26 233 -> 26 877 kWh against 29 425 -> 27 530 kWh demand (-11% -> -2.4%), K*h below 21 C 2503 -> 729 (the rest is on/off ripple: 57 K*h beyond 1 K), grid electricity 8 490 -> 8 619 kWh. HiSim's heat-pump twin (Aachen, 2021, predefined profile): 230.5 -> 228.3 K*h, 2 253 -> 2 255 kWh.

title: Staged splice: a later stage's anyway-cost credit is neither shifted to its stage nor kept when another stage is active in its year
description: Found while fixing hisim-4uv9 (PR #841 review fixes, 2026-09-27). resolve_replaced_asset books the ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT at credit_year = round(remaining life), a year of the stage's own evaluation. StagedCategories.STAGE_START lists ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT but the splice takes STAGE_START entries only when entry.year == 0 (_spliced_entry), so a credit at year r > 0 falls to the operating branch: kept only if the replacing stage is active in plan year r, unshifted by from_year_k. Probe: stage 1 (f=3) buys a heat pump, stage 3 (f=8) replaces it with a same-class subject, anyway_threshold_years 5 -> stage 3's own evaluation books the credit at year 5 (age 5, remaining 5; hisim-4uv9), and the plan timeline drops it (stage 1 is active in year 5). economics-hisim-spec §1 item 2 says the credit is booked in from_year_k. The same applies to a register asset a later stage replaces (its age is measured at plan year 0, so its credit year is in plan years and survives only when that stage is active then). Decide: book the credit at from_year_k + r (the year the avoided replacement would have fallen) or at from_year_k, and pin with a hand-computed test.
close_reason: Obsolete since #855: the staged engine books no anyway-cost credit (book_anyway_credit=False), and the levy basis takes the credit amount, not its timeline year; tests/economics/test_staged.py pins no ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT flow

title: The KPI 'Total electricity consumption' is rounded to 0.1 kWh while 'Total energy from grid' is not, so the grid import can exceed the consumption
description:
KpiPreparation.compute_electricity_consumption_and_production_and_battery_kpis (hisim/postprocessing/kpi_computation/kpi_preparation.py, around :234) rounds the total consumption, the building consumption and every production total to 0.1 kWh; the ElectricityMeter reports 'Total energy from grid' unrounded. A household that draws everything from the grid then reports more import than consumption.

Measured on midyear-pr3-lpg-utc (#1029), household_gas_solar_thermal, one day at 60 s: the residents consume 10.824 kWh, the grid supplies 10.824 kWh, and 'Total electricity consumption' is 10.8 kWh. tests/test_system_setups_household_gas_solar_thermal.py compared the two and failed; it now allows half the rounding step (CONSUMPTION_ROUNDING_IN_KILOWATT_HOUR = 0.05). The relative grid demand (around :553) rounds both to 0.1 kWh before dividing.

Fix: keep the KPI values unrounded and round only for display, as the meters do. Moves the general KPIs in the goldens by up to 0.05 kWh, so it needs a re-bless; then the test's allowance can go.

title: The PDF report is built once per report section instead of once per run, six builds of about 135 s in the all-options run
description:
Source: hisim-gehf (its close reason lists this as not addressed) and the LLM review of #981 (its performance findings).

ReportGenerator.close() builds the whole story into report.pdf with multiBuild, and PostProcessor calls report.open() and report.close() around every report section (postprocessing_main.py: the component chapters, the network charts, every text chapter and every table chapter), and the constructor builds once more. Each build rebuilds every page written so far and overwrites the file, so only the last build is kept. In the one-day gas_boiler_household run with every post-processing option (216 plots) that is six builds of about 135 s each.

Since #981 every plot is an Image flowable with lazy=2, which keeps the memory at 0.32 GB for the build but decodes each plot again in each multiBuild pass (at least two passes, for the table of contents); repeated builds multiply that cost.

Wanted: build the report once, after its last section, so report.pdf is the same document (except its timestamp) and the run spends one build instead of six. Check that nothing reads report.pdf between sections before removing the intermediate builds.

title: An existing solar thermal collector is simulated in a heat-pump plan but not in the gas/LPG/oil reference, so the comparison credits the plan with the collector's gain
description: renovisorissues #77 point 2 (2026-09-28). The boiler twins have no solar-thermal wiring: house.solar_thermal_system is not_implemented_yet ('collector left out') in the gas/LPG reference, while the heat-pump plan twin wires the kept collector (register asset SOLAR_THERMAL_SYSTEM, EUR 0). Reference and plan are then not the same house (solar gain, upkeep, renewal). Also: an unstated area_m2 is registered as 1 m2. Fix: wire the collector into the boiler twins, or leave it out of the plan too until then.

title: Coal and peat as a fuel carrier, so a solid-fuel house can be simulated and its replacement priced (renovisorissues #76)
description:
Since PR #865 a request whose house.heating.type_of_system is solid_fuel_heating is refused by name (heating.type_of_system.unsupported), also when a heating_system measure replaces the boiler (owner decision 2026-09-29). Before, it ran on the pellet twin and was priced as wood chips, so fuel, cost and CO2 were a wood boiler's; coal/peat CO2 per kWh is many times wood's, which understated exactly the saving these houses are interesting for.

Needed: a coal/peat carrier (fuel price, CO2 factor, sources) in the economics data, a boiler twin that burns it (or the pellet/wood-chip boiler parametrised with the carrier), a solid-fuel boiler asset class (price, lifetime) for the existing-asset register, then remove SOLID_FUEL_HEATING from SemanticChecks.UNSUPPORTED_GENERATORS and put it back into BaseFiles.BY_GENERATOR and GeneratorAssets.BY_GENERATOR.

title: RenoVisor translation layer and contract
Post-MVP: write LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR as the emitter and price it approximated
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H3

Observed: a package run sending `heat_distribution.type_of_system: low_temperature_radiator`
produces `HeatDistributionController.config.heating_system: FLOORHEATING`, and the option is
reported `not_implemented_yet` with the note "No cost row for a low-temperature radiator in the
cost database yet; modelled as surface heating".

H3's argument: the physics target exists (`LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR`,
`heat_distribution_system.py:38-50`) and drives the heat pump's COP, so the physics must be
written regardless of pricing; the missing cost row is an economics-side `approximated`, not a
translation gap.

HiSim agent's finding (2026-09-19): the current behaviour is the project owner's explicit
decision of the same day ("put it as not-implemented"), because
`hisim/economics/adapter.py::_hds_facts` returns `None` for `LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR` on purpose
(its own test asserts it) and cost-spec D7 then aborts the whole evaluation: writing the physics
target makes every heat-pump package with that emitter exit 5 with no `lifecycle_costs.json`.
Accepting H3 needs an economics-side change first -- the adapter must degrade to an
`approximated` price for that emitter instead of aborting.

Also confirmed en route: a heat pump on `conventional_radiator` runs the buffer to 90 degC.

Needs the owner's decision. Until then the substitution stands and
`TestTheLowTemperatureRadiatorBlocker` fails the day a cost row exists.

Done when: `LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR` is written for every generator; the option's status is
`used` (physics) with the cost gap surfaced by the economics engine; T-CAP and the mapping report
agree; the probe `heating_installation.type_of_system=low_temperature_radiator` in a heat-pump
house asserts the target.

title: Land the capability-document determinism change (translator.generated_at dropped)
description:
Source: /home/contract-proposals/todos.md H18 (marked `[-]`: decided, PR pending)

Observed: two builds of the same commit (5a6a4ef) with cache-identical final layers produced
capability documents of 61 982 and 81 311 bytes, same 32 measures, same version fields. It
matters because the backend stores the document per version and serves
`GET /{version}/measures` with a strong ETag that is the hash of the file plus
`Cache-Control: immutable`, so re-registering the same commit yields a different ETag for
equivalent content.

Decision taken (2026-09-19): `translator.generated_at` is dropped from the document, the CLI
(`--generated-at` is gone) and the shared specs (`measure-capabilities.md`, `.openapi.yaml`,
`calculation-request.md`, `translator-implementation-spec.md` section 10.2); a test compares two
builds byte for byte. The work sits on branch `renovisor-staged-economics` on top of the
staged-economics work, PR pending.

What could not be reproduced, recorded so nobody re-chases it: locally two runs differ in nothing
but the timestamp (82 629 bytes each with it neutralised), so the 61 982 vs 81 311 bytes the
backend saw was not the clock. The likely cause is two different code states behind one reported
commit, or a probe run that behaved differently in the image.

Done when: the determinism PR is merged and the byte-for-byte test runs in CI.
close_reason: Completed: translator.generated_at was dropped in PR #779 (commit 536dc265, merged to main as b0c2f043); the capability document is byte-identical across builds, pinned by tests/renovisor/test_capabilities.py::test_two_builds_of_one_state_are_byte_identical

title: Carry measures[i].cost, installation_year, applicant and scop into the request schema
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md F7 and F10 (frontend section, HiSim's half), and the
step-10 / step-12 notes under H7

HiSim reads four additive request fields that the vendored
`hisim/renovisor/contract/calculation-request.schema.json` still rejects, so they are implemented
and unreachable:

* `measures[i].cost {min_in_euro_per_m2, max_in_euro_per_m2, source}` -- without it every
  envelope subject of every real request is `unpriced: true` and
  `result.json.costs.investment_breakdown.envelope_material` is absent with the reason "the
  request carries no material price". The frontend copies `materials.yaml` `measure_costs` into
  it. HiSim already refuses a band with `min > max`, a negative price or a non-finite one as
  `measure.cost.band_invalid`, a code minted HiSim-side because section 7 of the contract does
  not carry the block yet.
* `house.<block>.installation_year` -- without it every existing asset is dated to
  `construction_year` and reported `defaulted`.
* an `applicant` block -- read when present; it carries `receives_means_tested_benefit`,
  `first_time_buyer` and `managed_full_retrofit`, without which every welfare, first-time-buyer,
  One-Stop-Shop-only and loan row of the Irish catalogue comes out `undetermined`.
* `house.heating.scop` -- the engine's subsidy conditions read a heat pump's seasonal performance
  factor as a technical attribute and neither the schema nor the recorded twins state one, so any
  scheme keyed on SCOP stays undetermined for every RenoVisor calculation. Alternative: a
  decision that no Irish scheme uses it.

Done when: the shared `calculation-request.schema.json` carries the four, HiSim re-vendors it,
and the end-to-end test shows a priced envelope subject and a dated existing asset.
close_reason: Done: the shared calculation-request.schema.json carries measures[i].cost, the ten installation_year leaves, living_area_in_m2 and applicant (renovisorissues !8), HiSim re-vendors it (specs at 93b7d70) and #789's readers are carried onto it; the end-to-end staged run prices the facade subject and dates the boiler. house.heating.scop left out: the SCOP is the W35/W55 pair of hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.27.

comments.text:
Specification (2026-09-20) of the schema additions, to be written into /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/calculation-request.schema.json and calculation-request.md section 3 together with the frontend agent (F7/F10); HiSim's readers already exist. All optional, additive:
- measures[i].cost: {min_in_euro_per_m2: number >= 0, max_in_euro_per_m2: number >= min, source: string}; the frontend copies materials.yaml measure_costs; HiSim refuses min > max or negatives (measure.cost.band_invalid, exit 2).
- house.heating.installation_year, house.pv_system.installation_year, house.battery.installation_year, house.solar_thermal_system.installation_year, house.building.<facade|roof|floor|window|door>.installation_year: integer 1900..2100; default construction_year, reported defaulted.
- house.building.living_area_in_m2: number > 0; default the conditioned floor area.
- applicant: {role: owner_occupier|landlord|tenant|condominium_association, receives_means_tested_benefit: boolean, first_time_buyer: boolean, managed_full_retrofit: boolean, taxable_household_income_in_euro: number, household_size: integer, main_residence: boolean}, every key optional; absent = undetermined for the subsidy conditions that read it.

title: Patch the TABULA IE band-05 row's zero door and window areas so a 1975 house lands on band 05
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md C4 ("box stays open for the row decision");
simulation_issues.md items 1 and 2; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md Q19 and C20

Observed: the mockup comments `construction_year: 1975` as "-> TABULA IE.N.SFH.05.Gen.ReEx.001.001",
but the translator emits `IE.N.SFH.06...` with `status: approximated` and the note "band 05
(1967-1977) covers construction year 1975 but its TABULA row has no door or window area, which
crashes the Building component; the nearest usable band 06 (1978-1982) is used instead". The
comment half was corrected in the shared mockup on 2026-09-19; the row decision is open.

State of the code (checked 2026-09-20): `Building` no longer divides by a zero door area --
`hisim/components/building/information.py` carries `keep_u_value_when_reference_area_is_zero` for
the door element -- but the window element has two area columns and no such guard, so a row with
both window areas zero still divides by zero (simulation_issues.md item 2, a latent crash).
`hisim/renovisor/tabula.py::_is_usable` still requires `door > 0 and window > 0`.

The physics owner decides: give the band-05 row the missing areas in the TABULA IE table, or keep
the fallback as documented behaviour. 22 of the 124 Irish rows and 146 German rows list no
separate door.

Done when: the decision is taken; if the row is repaired, the excluded bands are re-enabled and
`tests/renovisor/` expectations go back to the exact bands.
close_reason: Superseded by #816 (merged 2026-09-24): the Building gives every doorless TABULA row its own A_Estim_Door with the country's mean door U-value per variant (IE band 05: 2.7 m2, U 2.87/2.04/2.03), and every row is selectable, so the mockup's 1975 house lands on band 05 without a data patch. PR #811 (the CSV patch) closed unmerged by owner decision 2026-09-24; hisim/inputs stays untouched.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-09-20: MVP. Specification:
1. SimulationParameters gains cache_directories: List[str] (default: the package's current cache location, so nothing changes for existing callers). A CacheLocations helper (class-scope constants, in the module that owns the cache path today) answers read(path_relative) = first directory holding the file, in order, and write_directory() = the first entry; every caching component goes through it — survey the six caching components hisim-caching-hi1.2 names (building/TABULA, weather, PV, solar thermal, car, LPG/UTSP) and any other hisim/inputs/cache writer.
2. The RenoVisor run (hisim/renovisor/simulation.py) fills it from the environment variable HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES (os.pathsep-separated, absolute paths) when set; the realized simulation record and calculation.json state the directories used. Cache directories are exempt from the output-location cleanliness rule (R13.4) and from the 'no artefacts outside results/' test rule — document that in AGENTS.md.
3. Tests (base): two directories, a file present only in the second is read, a new file is written to the first; unset variable = today's behaviour. End-to-end (system_setups): the mockup baseline run twice with a temporary cache directory, the second run finds the cache (assert by file mtime or a log line), results identical.
4. Backend side (file as a B item in specs/todos.md): mount a persistent volume and pass HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES; hisim-caching-hi1.8 (move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs) becomes the natural default location and depends on this.

title: Confirm translator.commit is filled once the backend writes hisim/COMMIT into the image
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H6, H13 and H17 (one thing under three ids)

Observed: `mapping_report.json` carries `{"version": "2.0.0", "commit": null,
"hisim_commit": null}`, and `capabilities.py` validates the capability document against a schema
requiring `translator.commit` to be a string, so a null was fatal: the probe exited 1 and the
backend registered the version `broken`. The cause was `HiSimCommit.of()` shelling out to
`git -C /app rev-parse --short HEAD` in an image whose Containerfile fetches shallow and deletes
`.git`, which forced the backend to ship the `git` binary (~100 MB) plus an 8 KB fabricated
`.git` holding only HEAD -- 1.65 GB instead of 1.55 GB purely for provenance.

HiSim's half is done. `HiSimCommit.of()` in `hisim/renovisor/report.py` now reads the file
`hisim/COMMIT` next to the package, then the `HISIM_COMMIT` environment variable, then git as the
last fallback, and it feeds the mapping report, the capability document and
`economics_result.json` alike; the repository's `Dockerfile` writes that file from a
`HISIM_COMMIT` build argument; and the capability document now emits `"unknown"` instead of
`null`, because the vendored contract schema types both commit fields as strings.

What is left is not HiSim's code. The backend does not build with HiSim's Dockerfile (it
generates its own Containerfile), so the `ARG HISIM_COMMIT` there is irrelevant to the released
images; the backend agent writes `hisim/COMMIT` in its build stage from the SHA it already
resolves. Once it does, the `.git` stub and the runtime git binary can go.

Done when: a released image's `mapping_report.json` and capability document both carry a real
commit, verified on a run, and the three shared-todo boxes are ticked.
close_reason: Backend confirmed on image v20260923-1 (HiSim 75877861): capability document, mapping_report.json and economics_result.json all carry commit 7587786 without git in the image (renovisorissues #10).

title: Carry heat pump SCOP and its W35/W55 application in the house inventory spec
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21 on heat pump efficiency; the maintainer of the RenoVisor house
inventory spec (calculation-request.schema.json and calculation-request.md in
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/) will carry the fields, HiSim does not write that spec.

Today the request has `house.heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` (1..400) and HiSim applies it to
boilers only. For a heat pump the translator lists it as not implemented and the twin's hplib
defaults stand. The field also does not say which number a heat pump user would enter: SCOP x 100
(about 300..500) or the ErP label's eta_s (about 120..200), which differ by a factor of about 2.5.

What HiSim needs the spec to carry for a heat pump (existing one in `house.heating`, and the same
shape on the `heating_system` measure options for a new one):
- `scop`: number > 1, the manufacturer's standardized seasonal COP per EN 14825, average climate.
- `scop_application`: enum `w35` | `w55`, the sink temperature the label refers to (low-temperature
  or medium-temperature application). Without it the number cannot be placed on the curve.
- Ground source: same two fields; the standard's brine bins apply. Nothing extra.
- The boiler keeps `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent`; the spec should say the percent field is not
  meant for heat pumps.

This also settles the `house.heating.scop` item in hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.14 (subsidy conditions read the SCOP as
a technical attribute): one field serves both the physics and the economics.

Done when: the shared schema and the request document carry the two fields with the meaning above,
and HiSim has re-vendored the schema (hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.14 covers the re-vendoring routine).
close_reason: Done: the request carries house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35/_w55 (renovisorissues !9, re-vendored at 93b7d70); HiSim refuses them on a heating that is not a heat pump (heating.scop.not_a_heat_pump) and a W55 above W35 (heating.scop.w55_above_w35), lists both as not_implemented_yet (tracked hisim-component-physics-4g9.15) and probes them on a heat pump. Physics only (decision 2026-09-23): nothing is published for subsidies, since no grant is ever decided for the pump already in the house.

So the pair replaces scop + scop_application, which is better for HiSim: two rating points place the unit at its design flow temperature. description: Remote backend 2026-09-29: base D2811327 -> package 728B0B70 (IE, ground-source HP, existing pv_system 8000 W; measures heating_system->ASHP + photovoltaic_system size_in_percent_of_roof_area 50): PV production 6178 -> 2804 kWh, self-consumption 2608 -> 1596, grid import 14284 -> 14319, so energy_demand rose. title: A stated boiler seasonal efficiency below 30 % maps to eff_th_min above eff_th_max, and the boiler config cannot refuse the inversion without breaking the translator
description: Found in the review of PR #909 (R33, 2026-10-10). The translator maps heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent (request schema 1-400) to eff_th_max = value/100 and eff_th_min = max(eff_th_max - 0.3, 0.3) (hisim/renovisor/constants.py BoilerEfficiency, from calculation-request.md section 3.6). Below 30 % that rule contradicts itself: 1 % gives eff_th_min 0.3 > eff_th_max 0.01. GenericBoilerConfig therefore only refuses non-finite or non-positive efficiencies (PR #909); a check eff_th_min <= eff_th_max (and any upper bound) breaks 75 RenoVisor tests whose capability probes build the boundary requests. An upper bound of 1 would also be wrong: condensing boilers on the lower heating value reach 105-109 %. Owner decision 2026-10-10: keep #909 at 'finite and > 0' and agree the mapping with the contract side first. Options: cap the floor at the maximum (eff_th_min = max(eff_th_max - 0.3, min(0.3, eff_th_max))) and state it in the contract; or narrow the boiler's allowed range in the request schema (e.g. 30-115 %); then enforce eff_th_min <= eff_th_max in the boiler config.
close_reason: Gone with hisim-component-physics-4g9.66 (owner decision 2026-10-20): the stated figure maps to one field, GenericBoiler.config.seasonal_efficiency = value/100, which scales the boiler's sourced curve, so no min/max pair can invert. GenericBoilerConfig refuses a seasonal efficiency not in (0, 0.97], and the request validation refuses a boiler house stating more than 97 % (range.exceeded). The contract row of calculation-request.md section 3.6 still has to change on renovisorissues (draft kept outside the repository, posted with the owner's go).

title: Have the physics owner review the fifteen TO BE REVIEWED constants of the translator
description:
Source: hisim/renovisor/constants.py (15 sites marked TO BE REVIEWED);
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H11; roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step8_reconciliation.md
and step10_staged_economics.md

`hisim/renovisor/constants.py` says in its own module docstring that every default it holds is
marked TO BE REVIEWED. The fifteen marked sites, by line, are: default insulation thicknesses per
build-up (:70), the country-pack U-value fallbacks (:88), the two conductivity defaults (:123,
:127), `NEW_WINDOW_U` (:164), `NEW_DOOR_U` (:173), the DHW-pipe insulation stand-in (:215), the
ventilation/heat-recovery defaults (:224), `DesignTemperatures.BY_COUNTRY` (:246-253; IE -3 degC
after I.S. EN 12831 / SEAI heat-pump sizing guidance, NL -10 degC after NEN 5060 / ISSO 51), the
heat-recovery interpolation bounds (:281), and the `AnywayShareByPlacement` shares (:357, :365).

H11 records why the design temperature in particular matters: HiSim #771 moved it to the weather
(`Weather.for_location` requires `heating_reference_temperature_in_celsius`; the building reads
it as a sizing fact), TABULA cannot supply it (`Theta_e_Base` is the 12 degC heating-degree-day
base for every country, `Theta_e` the annual mean), and a country without a reviewed constant is
a translator error rather than Aachen's -7 degC.

Done when: each constant is either confirmed with its source or replaced, and the TO BE REVIEWED
marker is removed from the ones that were reviewed.

(shared folder `/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/`):

   (computed once, cached), not `DAILY_ELECTRICITY_KWH_BY_RESIDENTS`; that table does not exist.
