title: Add a CI rule that no module under hisim/ outside hisim/renovisor imports hisim.renovisor
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document).

Add a quality gate so the rest of HiSim can never import hisim.renovisor again. RenoVisor is the
top layer (a request translator on top of the energy-system format and the economics engine);
nothing below it may depend on it. Today the rule is broken only by hisim/economics (see the
inversion bead this one depends on), and nothing stops it happening again.

Implement it as a base-marked test in the style of tests/test_economics_import_lint.py (parse
every .py file under hisim/ with ast, so function-local imports count like top-level ones), not
a grep:
- walk hisim/**/*.py excluding hisim/renovisor/;
- flag every Import/ImportFrom whose module is hisim.renovisor or starts with hisim.renovisor.,
  and relative imports that resolve into it;
- the failure names file, line and imported module, and says the rule: renovisor sits on top.
Optionally add a fresh-interpreter check like tests/test_energy_system_layering.py (import
hisim.economics.__main__, hisim.hisim_main, hisim.simulator and assert no hisim.renovisor module
was loaded), which also catches imports through importlib.
Tests, system_setups and scripts are out of scope (tests may use renovisor freely). Mention the
rule in the CLAUDE.md RenoVisor paragraph.

Done when: the test runs in the base CI job, passes after the inversion is fixed, and fails on a
deliberately added import.
close_reason: Done in PR #903 (merged)

title: No print() in hisim/ outside hisim/log.py: move the 76 remaining calls in 12 modules onto the logger and empty the temporary allowlist of .semgrep/no_print.yml
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10: the only place in the package that may print is the logger (hisim/log.py). PR #919 adds the semgrep rule .semgrep/no_print.yml (run by the CI job 'semgrep (file writes)'), with a temporary allowlist of the 12 modules that printed when it was introduced: hisim/cli.py (8), cli_grouping.py (4), cli_render.py (7), hisim_main.py (2), economics/__main__.py (19), economics/staged_cli.py (6), energy_system/assemblies/describe.py (18), energy_system/recording/probe_session.py (1), renovisor/run.py (4), renovisor/verify/__init__.py (4), renovisor/contract/refresh.py (1), components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py (2). Most are command-line output (describe, facts, economics CLI), so the logger probably needs a function for plain console output of a command's result (without prefix or log file), e.g. log.console(message); decide its name and behaviour first. Then move every call, remove each module's allowlist line, and delete the commented-out print lines in the fuel-cell, transformer and PtX modules (no todo or dead code, coding_style.md). Done when the temporary part of the allowlist is empty.

title: CI ratchet on code size: lines of code per function and file, arguments and branches may not grow beyond a baseline of today's offenders
description: Owner decisions 2026-10-10 (system_docs/coding_style.md, 'Code rules' 1 and 2). Limits: a function at most ~50 lines of code (hard 100), a file at most 750 lines of code, at most 6 arguments (else a parameter object), a bounded number of branches. Only code counts: comments, docstrings and blank lines do not, so agents are never pushed to cut documentation (owner, 2026-10-10). pylint's too-many-lines counts every line and therefore cannot be the check: the file and function limits need a small counter (ast for docstring ranges, tokenize for comments; a prototype counted 26 of 308 files in hisim/ over 750 code lines on 2026-10-10, largest economics/views.py 2728 code lines of 4729, more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py 2444 of 3419). Arguments and branches use pylint (too-many-arguments, too-many-branches). A committed baseline of today's offenders may only shrink: also measured 2026-10-10, 92 functions over 100 lines (16 over 200; longest more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py __init__ 607, kpi_preparation.read_opex_and_capex_costs_from_results 542, hplib i_simulate 468; all lines, to be re-measured as code lines), 32 functions with more than 8 arguments. A new violation fails CI; a fixed one leaves the baseline in the same PR.

title: CI ratchet on escape hatches: Any, type: ignore, pylint: disable and catch-all except may not grow, and each ignore or disable carries its reason
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (coding_style.md, 'Code rules' 2, 3 and 6). Baseline 2026-10-10 in hisim/: 543 uses of Any, 43 '# type: ignore', 154 'pylint: disable', 42 'except Exception' or bare 'except:'. A script counts them per file against a committed baseline that may only shrink; a new ignore or disable without a reason after it fails. Pick semgrep or a small checker script.

title: mypy gets stricter step by step: disallow_untyped_defs and no implicit Any, package by package
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (coding_style.md, 'Code rules' 3). Turn on disallow_untyped_defs (then disallow_any_generics, warn_return_any) per package in mypy.ini, starting with the packages that already pass, for all three CI mypy runs (hisim, system_setups, tests). Each step its own PR.

title: import-linter checks the layering in CI, and the importlib/getattr workarounds for circular imports are removed
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (coding_style.md, 'Code rules' 7). Declare the layers (config -> core -> components -> postprocessing -> renovisor; tests/test_renovisor_import_lint.py is the first such rule) as import-linter contracts and run them in CI. 8 component modules use importlib.import_module by string to dodge circular imports (default connections); each is a design error to fix (component principles review, M6), with a temporary allowlist that may only shrink.

title: CI reports diff coverage and requires about 90 % of the changed lines in hisim/ to be covered by tests
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (coding_style.md, 'Code rules' 8). Measure coverage in the base job (pytest-cov) and check the changed lines of a PR with diff-cover (or similar) against ~90 %. Decide how the stacked PRs (only the bottom one has CI) are handled.

title: A regular job finds functions with the same purpose by comparing their first docstring sentences, and files merge candidates as beads
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (coding_style.md, 'Design' DRY and purpose sentence, 'Code rules' 11). Extract the first docstring sentence of every function in hisim/ (AST), group candidates (embeddings or an LLM pass), have an LLM judge each candidate pair against the code, and file a bead per confirmed duplicate. Run it on demand or monthly, not per push. Decide where it runs and who pays the tokens.

title: One generic test checks every component for iteration safety: save, simulate several times, restore, simulate with X must equal save then simulate with X
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (system_docs/coding_style.md, 'Testing state machines'). The component review of 2026-10-10 found restore bugs by hand: HeatDistributionController.i_restore_state assigns the mode to itself (heat_distribution_system.py:1178-1180), the DHW controller writes its previous state inside i_simulate (hisim-component-physics-4g9.28), the boiler controller does not save its state. A generic parametrised test over every component class reachable from the recorded twins: build the component in a small rig, i_save_state, call i_simulate repeatedly with different (random) inputs, i_restore_state, call it with input X, and compare all outputs and the state with a fresh save followed by one call with X. Failures found become bugs under hisim-component-physics-4g9; until fixed they go on an expected-failure list that may only shrink.

title: Delete the SimRepository entries nobody reads: the per-step forecasts of weather, occupancy and PV, the dynamic-entries API, and weather_location
description: Component review 2026-10-10 (YAGNI: unused code is deleted). Written but never read since the MPC controller was retired: Weather.Weather_Temperature_Forecast_24h written every step in i_simulate (weather/weather.py:326-332), UtspLpgConnector.Electricity_Demand_Forecast_24h (loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py:601-606), the PV forecast through set_dynamic_entry (generic_pv_system/pv_system.py:425-439), all three behind predictive_control flags that default to off (remove the flags and config fields too); the whole dynamic-entries API of hisim/sim_repository.py (set/get/delete_dynamic_entry, get_dynamic_source_weights; only tests/test_sim_repository.py uses it); the 'weather_location' entry (weather.py:342). weather_year_effective stays (tests read it). No golden change expected.

title: Make self.config precisely typed per component so mypy sees the 300 masked findings
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/json_cleanup.md section 6, "Mypy visibility for config classes
(follow-up to sweep 1)"

Removing the dataclass-wizard's `Any` base revealed about 300 latent typing findings that sweep 1
deliberately re-masked to stay reviewable: LSP-violating `get_cost_capex(config: SpecificConfig)`
overrides (about 75), subclass-field reads and writes on `ConfigBase`-typed slots (about 280),
and a handful of genuine type lies (`my_module_config` holding a dict, the `List[int]` annotation
on `post_processing_options` that actually holds enum members).

The real fix is a generic `Component[TConfig]` so `self.config` is precisely typed per component,
then: delete the checking-only escape hatches on `ConfigBase` (the `__getattr__`/`__setattr__`
and serialization-API stubs), re-enable the `override` error code, and drop
`follow_imports = skip` for `dataclasses_json` -- which restores the injected-API stubs problem,
to be solved via a small typing shim or upstream stubs.

Related, and unblocked by the same change: the config-presets findings note that
`Catalog` attribute access is inherently `Any` because a `ClassVar` may not contain a type
variable, so `Catalog` cannot be generic over the config class it serves; a
`__class_getitem__`-based `Catalog[SomeConfig]` declared as a plain class attribute might work
once the `Component[TConfig]` generics sweep lands.

Also named there: `my_sim.my_module_config` holding a dict is one of the type lies -- see the
issue that settles what that attribute may hold.

title: Idea: components declare which SimRepository entries they publish and need, the simulator prepares them in dependency order, and CI refuses repository writes outside i_prepare_simulation
description: Owner decision 2026-10-10: kept as a P4 idea under YAGNI, since today's order rules work and fail loudly. Today prepare_calculation walks the components in the order the setup added them, so the Weather must be added before PVSystem and the occupancy before every car, and the Building postpones its solar-gain precomputation to its first i_simulate because 16 of 18 setups add it before the Weather (building.py:832-850). Idea: each component declares PUBLISHES/REQUIRES (the producers' key constants), prepare_calculation sorts topologically (the time-loop evaluation order stays unchanged, so results do not change), a missing producer fails at build time, describe/facts list the dependencies, and the Building moves its precomputation into i_prepare_simulation. Plus a CI rule (semgrep, like .semgrep/no_print.yml) that refuses SimRepository writes (set_entry) outside i_prepare_simulation; it needs the forecast deletion first. Do it when a real case appears: a second producer of the same data, or an ordering bug.

title: Every energy system has a full-year golden
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-11 (every energy system gets a yearly golden test); branch golden-full-year-all.

The golden gate's week is the first week of January, in which the solar collectors' pumps never run (they first run on 20 January), so no golden exercised the solar thermal systems and changes to them (a pump hysteresis, an 80 °C solar maximum) were invisible to the gate. Only the eight generator building sizers had a full-year golden; the other fourteen setups of scripts/golden_config.json were restricted to the week.

Done: every setup of golden_config.json runs the full year (21 of 22; household_heatpump_car_building_sizer cannot finish a year and stays week-only until hisim-component-physics-4g9.56 is fixed), each with a locally measured full_year_60s weight; golden-year.yml cuts the year tier into five shards instead of four; tests/test_golden_matrix.py holds every system_setups/*.py with a setup_function in the config and every config setup on the full year except the named exception. The first bless (golden-update.yml on the branch, force_rewrite false) writes the 13 new full-year golden files.
close_reason: golden-full-year-all: 21 of 22 setups run the full year; the heat pump with a car waits for hisim-component-physics-4g9.56

title: Check each component kind's contract automatically: wiring rules at build time and behaviour rules in a test sweep
description:
Source: owner request 2026-10-13, after #922 made the kind of a component its base class (DataSourceComponent, L2ControllerComponent, L1ControllerComponent, PhysicsComponent, MeterComponent).

The kind base classes state each kind's contract in prose only. Make the contracts checked automatically, so a component that breaks its kind fails a build or a test instead of producing order-dependent results.

## Wiring rules (checked when the simulator is built, before the first step; a violation is refused with both components' names)
- W1: a data source has no inputs.
- W2: nothing reads a meter: no input of a non-meter component is connected to a meter's output (a meter may read another meter).
- W3: an L1 controller commands exactly one device: its outputs feed exactly one physics component (meters and L2 controllers may also read them).
- W4: an L2 controller reaches devices only through their L1 controllers: no L2 output is connected to a physics input.
Known violators go on an allow-list in code, each entry naming its bead; the list may only shrink (a ratchet test):
- W1: UtspLpgConnector reads the hot-water mass flow and temperature (2 inputs) — split the profile (data source) from the hot-water heat it derives, or file a bead; TariffProvider reads the grid draw (see below).
- W2: TariffProvider reads ElectricityMeter.ElectricityFromGridInWatt for its peak tracker.
- W2: GenericHeatPumpController reads ElectricityMeter.ElectricityAvailable (default connection; basic_household).
- W4: the energy manager commands the battery directly (hisim-component-physics-4g9.38).
- W4: the energy manager raises the building's room set temperature directly (Building.BuildingTemperatureModifierInKelvin; hisim-component-physics-4g9.37, hisim-component-physics-4g9.38).
- W4: the energy manager sets the CHP's electricity target directly (dynamic_components, CHP.ElectricityFromCHPTarget).
No recorded energy system breaks W1 or W3 beyond the entries above (checked over all 44 energy systems, review of #968).

## Behaviour rules (a test sweep over every recorded energy system, at sampled time steps of a short run)
- B1: a pass depends only on its inputs and the committed state (component design principle 5): restore, run a pass, restore, run the same pass with the same inputs: identical outputs. Would have caught hisim-component-physics-4g9.24 and the car controller's replay (#965).
- B2: save/restore is exact: after i_restore_state the component's state equals what i_save_state saved, whatever the passes in between did.
- B3: a data source's outputs are identical in every pass of a step, whatever the other components output.
- B4: a forced pass decides like any other: under force_convergence a pass with the same inputs gives the same outputs as an unforced pass (no replay of state written inside i_simulate). Likely violator: the CHP controller's processed_state (generic_chp/controller.py).

## TariffProvider (owner, 2026-10-13: a tariff may legitimately depend on the current consumption)
Today it reads the electricity meter's grid draw and nothing reads its outputs (PricePurchase, PriceInjection, BillingPeriodPeakSoFar, CapacityChargeMarginal are only written to the results), so it behaves like a meter. Make it a MeterComponent: that satisfies W1 and W2 as written (meter reads meter). When a controller is to optimise against a consumption-dependent price, decide then between splitting it into a price data source plus a tariff meter, or letting a controller read a meter's committed (start-of-step) value as an explicit W2 exception.

Done when: W1–W4 are enforced at build with the allow-list and its ratchet test; B1–B4 run as a test over every recorded energy system; every violator found is either fixed or on the allow-list with a bead; TariffProvider is a MeterComponent.

title: Monthly values and run totals are aggregated by unit only, so running totals, stored energies and on/off flags are summed into nonsense
description:
Found by the aggregate chart review (2026-10-15, household_heatpump_building_sizer, 2021 at 900 s; loop-design/chart_review_aggregates.md B6/Q1). Simulator.get_std_results averages an output whose unit is in loadtypes.UNITS_USING_MEAN_AGGREGATION and sums every other one. Summed although a sum means nothing: Cumulative* outputs in Wh (CumulativeThermalEnergyTotal sums to 3.6e9 Wh in January), TimeOnHeating in s (cumulative too: the December bar reads 795,000 h), ThermalEnergyInStorage (a state, Wh), HeatingSeason (binary: 2,976 in January). This reaches the monthly bar charts, the monthly CSVs, the scenario-evaluation files and the result values on the network chart; KPIs read the time series and are not affected. Options: (a) a per-output aggregation declared on ComponentOutput (sum / mean / last value), clean but touching many components; (b) leave such outputs out of the bar charts and the monthly exports; (c) leave as is, the bar chart axis now says 'monthly sum'. Recommendation: (a).

Also summed today (owner review of #1018, 2026-10-18, where the bar charts started to say 'monthly sum'): tariff prices in EUR/kWh, whose monthly sum has no meaning, and 0/1 flags such as the heating curve's HeatingSeason. The label is truthful about what the simulator did; the aggregation itself is what this bead fixes.
close_reason: Done in branch output-aggregation (draft PR on report-300dpi-once), owner decision 2026-10-15. ComponentOutput.aggregation (loadtypes.OutputAggregation: SUM, MEAN, LAST, NONE) defaults to the old unit rule, so undeclared outputs aggregate as before; 46 outputs of the setup components declare it: 25 running totals and counters LAST, 2 stored energies and 2 on/off flags MEAN, 17 controller modes, restarting timers and sun angles NONE. get_std_results, the bar charts and the network-chart values follow it. NONE outputs and outputs constant over the run get no line, carpet, single-day or bar chart; the report lists both once with the reason (chapter Outputs Without Charts: "constant at <value>" or "no aggregate declared"). Full-year all-options run of household_heatpump_building_sizer, base -> branch: 658 -> 554 chart PNGs (158 -> 132 outputs charted, 17 constant, 9 NONE), report 539 -> 459 pages; UNITS_USING_MEAN_AGGREGATION became OutputAggregation.units_averaged_by_default(); remaining components in hisim-repo-cleanup-o6a.27; all 17 KPI JSON files and all_results.csv byte-identical; run value of CumulativeThermalEnergySH 2.27e11 Wh -> 11,926 kWh (= KPI), CounterOnOff 255 -> 514.

title: Two KPIs give different grid injections for the same run: 'Grid injection of electricity' 18,795.31 kWh against 'Total energy to grid (ElectricityMeter)' 18,791.53 kWh
description: Found by the aggregate chart review (2026-10-15, household_heatpump_building_sizer, 2021 at 900 s). ElectricityMeter ElectricityToGrid sums to 18,791.53 kWh in all_results.csv; the General KPI 'Grid injection of electricity' (kpi_preparation) is 3.78 kWh higher. Find which series the general KPI integrates and make both read the meter.

title: The option PLOT_SANKEY (3) does nothing: nothing reads it, the Sankeys come from EXPORT_ENERGY_BALANCE
description: Found by the aggregate chart review (2026-10-15). A simulation file that lists PLOT_SANKEY gets no Sankey. Options: (a) deprecate it with a warning when it is set; (b) make it imply EXPORT_ENERGY_BALANCE. Its number cannot be reused. Recommendation: (b), with a deprecation note.

title: The PDF report is rebuilt from page 1 after every chapter: 33 of the 46 minutes of a full-year run with all options, and 201 MB
description: Found by the aggregate chart review (2026-10-15, household_heatpump_building_sizer, 2021 at 900 s, every option). Each chapter calls ReportGenerator.open()/close(), and close() runs multiBuild over the whole story; seven builds took about 400 s each for 417 pages. The plots are 3600 x 2400 px PNGs (600 dpi), hence 201 MB. Options: build once at the end of PostProcessor.run (about 5 min instead of 33); save the plots at 300 dpi (half the size). Recommendation: both.
close_reason: Both done in branch report-300dpi-once (draft PR on charts-aggregates). Every chart is saved at 300 dpi from one constant, SavedChartResolution.DPI in chartbase.py (output charts were 600, lifecycle cost charts 130), and the report is built once, after the KPI chapter, instead of in the constructor and after each of six chapters. Same full-year all-options run of household_heatpump_building_sizer before -> after: wall clock 47:52 -> 5:37 min, report 2531 s in six builds -> 132 s in one, report.pdf 234 MB -> 102 MB (539 pages both, same text but the timestamp), time-series PNGs 135 MB -> 64 MB, monthly bars 31 MB -> 14 MB, lifecycle PNGs 1.4 MB -> 3.9 MB, peak memory 1.64 GB -> 1.01 GB; KPI JSON files identical.

title: Declare the aggregation of the outputs of the components no system setup uses (fuel cell, hydrogen storage, heating meter, tariff provider and others)
description:
Source: PR #1028 (branch output-aggregation, bead hisim-repo-cleanup-o6a.23); owner decision of 2026-10-15 on its open question 1.

#1028 lets every component output declare how its time steps are aggregated into monthly values and run totals (loadtypes.OutputAggregation: SUM, MEAN, LAST, NONE; ComponentOutput.aggregation, add_output(aggregation=...)). An output that declares nothing follows its unit (W averaged, Wh summed). #1028 declared the outputs of the component classes used by the 22 system setups and their energy-system twins, and nothing else. The component classes below are used by none of them and keep the unit rule for every output.

Task: review every output of these classes and declare an aggregation where the unit's rule is wrong, using the same rules as #1028 (its PR body has the table): a running total or a counter is LAST, a stored amount or a state of charge is MEAN, a 0/1 flag is MEAN (share of time on), a state with more than two values, a timer that restarts at every switch or an angle is NONE (no aggregate and no charts). Outputs whose unit already gives the right aggregate stay undeclared.

Classes and candidates found by reading the output names and units (verify against the code before declaring):
- generic_fuel_cell.FuelCell (16 outputs): TotalEnergyProduced (kWh), TotalRampUpTime, TotalRampDownTime (s), TotalHydrogenConsumed, TotalOxygenConsumed, TotalWaterProduced (kg), OperatingTime (h), NumberofCycles look like running totals or counters (LAST); FuelCellState looks like a mode (NONE).
- controller_l1_fuel_cell.FuelCellController (6): ShutdownCount, StandbyCount, OffCount (LAST?); CurrentMode (NONE?); PowerNotProvided (kWh, per step or total?).
- generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.HydrogenStorage (8): CurrentHydrogenFillLevelAbsolute (kg, a stored amount: MEAN, today summed); HydrogenNotStored, HydrogenNotReleased, HydrogenLosses (kg, per step or total?).
- generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.AdvancedElectrolyzer (8): flows, powers and an efficiency; probably nothing to declare.
- heating_meter.HeatingMeter (8): CumulativeConsumption, CumulativeProduction (Wh, LAST), as for the electricity, gas and fuel meters.
- example_storage.SimpleStorage (3): CurrentFillLevelAbsolute (unit from the config; a stored amount: MEAN).
- example_component.ExampleComponent (3): StoredEnergy (Wh, a stored energy: MEAN).
- generic_chp.chp.SimpleCHP (5), generic_chp.controller.L1CHPController (2: CHPControllerOnOffSignal, CHPControllerHeatingModeSignal, binary: MEAN as share of time on, or NONE if the mode signal has more than two meanings).
- controller_l2_ptx_energy_management_system.PTXController (3): EnergyToBattery (kWh, per step?).
- controller_l2_xtp_fuel_cell_ems.XTPController (2), controller_l1_example_controller.SimpleController (1), idealized_electric_heater.IdealizedElectricHeater (2) and IdealizedElectricHeaterController (1), night_setback_controller.NightSetbackController (1), simple_heat_source.SimpleHeatSource (3): powers, temperatures and set-points; probably nothing to declare.
- tariff_provider.TariffProvider (4): PricePurchase, PriceInjection (Euros per kWh, summed today: a price should be MEAN); BillingPeriodPeakSoFar (kW, a running maximum: LAST); CapacityChargeMarginal.
- sumbuilder.CalculateOperation and sumbuilder.SumBuilderForThreeInputs (1 each, unit from the config): follow their unit; probably nothing to declare.
- Dynamic outputs built in hisim/dynamic_component.py follow their unit; check whether any of them is a running total.

Done when: every output of these classes has been looked at, the wrong ones declare their aggregation, the PR lists the classification, and a full-year run of one setup that uses a changed class (or a unit test) shows that the KPIs are byte-identical.

title: Subcomponents are a named pattern: plain classes that model part of a device's behaviour, shareable as classes, marked and defined in the design principles
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-23 (Noah): the pattern of plain classes that model part of a device's behaviour, until now called 'laws' in conversation, is named 'subcomponent'. Sizing laws (hisim/config/laws.py SizingLaw, the *_LAW constants, RenoVisor's BatteryLaw/BatteryCapacityLaw) are a different concept and keep their name.

Definition, to go into system_docs/component_design_principles.md: a subcomponent is a plain class that models part of a device's behaviour. It is used inside one or more components' own code (built from their config, called in their i_simulate), has no ports and no lifecycle, is never seen by the simulator (so it costs no convergence passes), and is tested in isolation. Subcomponents are shareable across components as classes (owner, 2026-10-23): any component may use a subcomponent class (a future CirculationPump in the boiler, heat pump, collector and HDS). Instances are never shared (owner, 2026-10-23): each component builds its own subcomponents from its own config. Two components that must agree on a parameter do so through the same config value, a sizing rule or a port, never through a shared object. Today no instance is shared: DualCircuitHotWater is used through its class (static methods), and the HDS and the heating curve each build their own EmitterDesign from their config. Hierarchy: assembly -> component -> subcomponent.

Work: (1) the definition in component_design_principles.md (and a pointer in coding_style.md); (2) a marker base class Subcomponent (no behaviour; e.g. in hisim/component.py or its own module); (3) tag the existing ones: generic_boiler.py CombustionEfficiencyCurve, BurnerModulation, BoilerPump, BurnerTimes; dual_circuit_system.py DiverterValve, HotWaterPriorityLimit, DualCircuitHotWater; solar_thermal_system.py FlatPlateCollectorCurve, SpeedControlledSolarPump; more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib_model.py ScopCalibration, StandardizedSeasonalCop; heating_curve.py EmitterDesign; (4) a test that no Subcomponent is also a Component, and that no Subcomponent instance is reachable from two components. Not subcomponents: per-step records (BoilerFiring, CollectorOperatingPoint, HplibResult, HeatPumpOperation, DhwTankStep), state records (HotWaterPriorityTimer, HeatPumpRunTimers), input bundles/cache keys (PvSeriesInputs, WeatherSeriesInputs), channel groups (BoilerCircuitChannels), infrastructure (PylpgWorkspace). No behaviour change, no golden moves. Rename docstrings that call these classes a 'law' where the class is meant. Follow-up, separate: a shared CirculationPump subcomponent (option C of /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/pumps/report.md) once the owner has decided the pump questions.

2026-10-23, owner decisions on location, seam and performance:
- Location: a package hisim/subcomponents/. A subcomponent used by two or more components lives there (pumps.py, later valves.py, priority.py, ...); one used by a single component stays beside it and moves when a second user appears. The Subcomponent marker goes to hisim/subcomponents/base.py. hisim/hydronics.py stays: plain physics functions and constants that subcomponents use.
- Imports, enforced by a new tests/test_subcomponent_import_lint.py (modelled on test_renovisor_import_lint.py): a module under hisim/subcomponents/ imports only the standard library, numpy, hisim.config, hisim.hydronics, hisim.loadtypes, hisim.units and other subcomponents; never hisim.component, hisim.components, the simulator, postprocessing, hisim.energy_system or hisim.renovisor.
- Interface: plain values in (floats with units in their names, keyword-only), no SingleTimeStepValues, no ComponentInput/ComponentOutput, no simulation-parameters object. Built once by classmethod factories from values the component got from its config or a sizing rule; __post_init__ refuses invalid settings, so a bad subcomponent fails when its component is built. Stateless; state across steps stays in the component. Tested alone under tests/subcomponents/, marker base.
- Performance (measured 2026-10-23, Python 3.12, a three-field result of a pump-sized law at 179 ns): per-call cost of the result object over the bare law: tuple +28 ns, slots dataclass +110 ns, NamedTuple +152 ns, frozen dataclass +271 ns, frozen dataclass built with keywords +361 ns (its __init__ goes through object.__setattr__). Rules: (1) subcomponent instances are frozen dataclasses (built once, cost irrelevant); (2) per-call results in the hot path are NamedTuples (immutable, named, typed; half the cost), a single value is returned as a plain float with units in the method name; (3) no frozen dataclass is constructed per call in i_simulate paths - this rule goes into system_docs/coding_style.md next to the existing hot-path rule.
close_reason: Subcomponent marker in hisim/subcomponents/base.py, definition and rules in component_design_principles.md section C and coding_style.md, import lint, marker tests; 12 existing classes tagged, no behaviour change.

title: Inline the trivial wrappers that predate the coding style's 'a function of its own only for something worth testing' rule
description:
Owner, 2026-10-25 (#1145): subagents kept creating functions with docstrings ten times longer than their one-line body. The coding style now keeps glance-readable expressions inline and requires direct tests for every static function (system_docs/coding_style.md §1, anti-pattern 'Trivial wrapper' in §3). #1141 was revised to it; these wrappers predate it and were left alone there:
- SolarThermalSystemController.pump_ran_as_reported (solar_thermal_system.py): return ratio_run > 0.0, 12-line docstring, 1 caller.
- HeatDistribution.pump_stopped_by_the_valve (heat_distribution_system.py): return valve_state == 0, 12-line docstring, 1 caller.
- BurnerState.at_start (generic_boiler.py): one constructor call, 1 caller.
- MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating.space_heating_target_temperature_in_celsius: one sum, 25-line docstring, 1 caller.
- Borderline (2-3 callers, one-line body, 12-13 docstring lines): BurnerModulation.heat_power_in_watt, BurnerTimes.whole_steps / whole_steps_in_seconds, GenericBoiler.space_heating_runs_on_distribution_flow.

Work: inline the single-caller ones (a short comment where the reason is not obvious), test them through their user, and for the borderline ones decide per the rule (keep with a one-sentence docstring, or inline). Boy-scout: also when a PR touches a module anyway. Results bit-identical.

title: The goldens also run at 900 s, RenoVisor's step length, so a change to the part-load and start-of-step code that acts only above 600 s fails the golden check
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-26 (Noah): add 900 s goldens.

Problem: every golden runs at 60 s (scripts/golden_config.json: one_week_60s, july_week_60s, full_year_60s), but the part-load rules (hisim/part_load.py), the start-of-step node of the buffer and the DHW tank, and CircuitStep.at_part_load act only above 600 s, and RenoVisor runs every calculation at 900 s (hisim/renovisor/simulation.py, SECONDS_PER_TIMESTEP). What runs at 900 s today checks totals against tolerances only: tests/test_space_heating_time_resolution.py (heat to the building over a year within 1 % of the 60 s golden, four twins), tests/test_dhw_chain_time_resolution.py (hot-water heat within 1 %, six twins, four weeks), tests/test_time_resolution.py, the assembly isolation runs (one day at 900 s, mostly mock components) and tests/renovisor/test_run.py (qualitative). A change to the code that acts above 600 s passes CI unless it moves one of those totals by more than about 1 %; fuel and electricity at coarse steps are asserted nowhere. #1148 needed a manual 900 s comparison for this reason.

Done when: golden_config.json has a one-week 900 s parameter set checked per PR by golden-check, and a full-year 900 s set run by golden-year, for every golden setup (python and composed modes as for 60 s); the references are blessed through golden-update on current main; the shard durations ('seconds') are measured; golden_references/README.md and the testing documents name the new sets. The time-resolution tests stay: they check the physics across resolutions, the 900 s goldens catch any change of behaviour. A PR that changes 900 s behaviour on purpose then needs a re-bless, as one changing 60 s behaviour does now.
close_reason: Done: scripts/golden_config.json has two more parameter sets, one_week_900s (one_week_only, 900 s) and full_year_900s (full_year, 900 s), with the 60 s sets' post-processing options. The tiers pick sets by factory, so golden-check runs the 900 s January week beside the 60 s one and golden-year the 900 s year beside the 60 s one, python and composed modes as for 60 s, and golden-update blesses both; the scripts and workflows needed no change beyond their comments. Every setup carries 900 s weights, measured locally and scaled by each setup's CI-to-local ratio at 60 s. A pair without its golden fails its shard or job before anything runs (tests/test_golden_check.py pins it for a shard holding a 60 s and a 900 s pair). golden_references/README.md, system_docs/testing.md and system_docs/results_and_interfaces.md name the sets and why 900 s is there. The references themselves are written by the next golden-update run on current main.

title: Re-enable pylint's cyclic-import check by moving for_building into the building package
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] pylint's
`cyclic-import` cannot see the difference between a lazy import and a real one"

`SizingContext.for_building` imports the building package inside the method body, which is
invisible to Python's import system but fully visible to pylint's import graph, so prospector
reports the cycle anyway. Worse, it attributes the message to an arbitrary module outside the
cycle (a file under `hisim/inputs/`), so a `# pylint: disable=cyclic-import` at the actual site
does nothing. It is disabled in `.prospector.yml`, matching `pylintrc-critical-only`, which
already disables it.

If the check is ever wanted back, the honest fix is to move `for_building` into the building
package and leave `SizingContext` fact-agnostic.

Done when: either the check is back with the move done, or the disable carries a note saying this
is the reason and the fix.

title: Settle the five open questions of the HPC harness spec
description:
Source: roadmap/hpc_harness_spec.md section 17, "Open questions / future"

* Autoscaler: whole-node autoscaling and proactively cancelling running (not just Slurm-PENDING)
  surplus workers are the natural follow-ups.
* Priorities and fairness across multiple submitted batches -- the schema supports `priority` and
  `batch_id`; the policy is TBD.
* Richer output validation -- section 4.8 requires a single success file for `done`; a future
  extension could let a runner check multiple files, sizes or content hashes before the rename.
* Multiple runners per server -- the database is already runner-tagged; confirm whether one
  server should host mixed-runner queues or one runner per server instance.
* Database growth at very large scale -- a `worker_metrics` downsampling policy, and possibly
  moving long-term metrics to a separate rollup database.

Also relevant to the harness, from the declarative plan's P5: the payload becomes an
energy-system string plus simulation parameters and the worker loads from the string, which
changes what a job record has to carry.

title: Check autodoc member visibility for the building package when the Sphinx docs are next built
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/building_cleanup_findings.md, item 15

`docs/api/hisim.components.building.rst` uses `automodule` on the package, and the classes are
now imported names in `__init__` (listed in `__all__`). The docs build is not a CI gate, so this
was left unchanged -- worth a look whenever the Sphinx docs are next built, because `automodule`
on a package whose classes are re-exports can silently document nothing.

title: Explain the sporadic errors of test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code` errors sporadically when anything else runs in
the repo concurrently"

Three `pytest -m base` runs that overlapped with other work in the same checkout (a scenario-JSON
regeneration, a parallel pytest invocation, live source edits) each produced one or two
collection/setup ERRORs on random TABULA parametrizations of this test; the identical suite run
sequentially passes twice with zero errors, and every errored parametrization passes in
isolation. Plausibly contention around a shared file (`logs/`, `results/`, or the class-scope
TABULA CSV cache being rebuilt while another process imports).

Harmless for CI, which runs one suite per checkout, but worth knowing before blaming a branch for
a red local run -- and worth a look if it ever appears in CI.

needs-triage: no owner and a named reason not to chase it. It is the same class of hazard as the
stale-cache one and the `--scan-all` non-determinism; whoever does the cache-injection work
(Rust Tier 3) should check whether it disappears.

title: Add a syntax gate to any future mechanical call-site rewriting sweep
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] Mechanical call-site
rewriting needs a syntax gate, not a diff review" and "[bug] Import-insertion tooling corrupted
one setup"

Converting the 72 `get_default_german_single_family_home` call sites with a
keyword-args-to-field-assignments script silently produced one wrecked file: the setup whose last
keyword argument ended `...,)` on the same line ran the "read until the closing paren" loop past
the end of the call and rewrote nine following statements into attribute assignments.
`compileall` over the touched trees caught it instantly.

The same shape bit once before: inserting a `SizingContext` import after
"from hisim.simulator import SimulationParameters" broke
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py`, whose import line continued with
", Simulator". Textual import insertion needs full-line anchors.

Any future sweep of this shape should run a parse gate per file, not per tree.

Done when: the rule is written where a sweep author will read it (a script helper that does the
per-file `compileall`, or a line in the repository's own conventions).

title: Keep ConfigBase annotations importable at runtime from hisim/config/base.py
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` needed a home on `ConfigBase`" ("third occurrence of the pattern; worth a
rule"), with the two earlier occurrences in the same document

The pattern, hit three times from three directions: a name that is not importable at runtime from
`hisim/config/base.py` must not appear in a `ConfigBase` annotation, because `dataclasses_json`
evaluates those annotations from every subclass's module.

The three occurrences: `Sizable = Union[T, _AutoSize, "SizingLaw"]` as a string forward reference
above the class made `get_type_hints` fail with `NameError` in every config module that did not
itself import `SizingLaw`, fixed by defining the alias below the class with a real reference;
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` had to be declared on `ConfigBase` for mypy, with its element type kept as
`Any`, because naming `FactContribution` would either invert the package layering or leave a
`TYPE_CHECKING`-only forward reference; and the general lesson for shared aliases.

Done when: the rule is stated where a config author will read it -- the `hisim/config/` package
docstring is the natural place, since it is where the layering rule already lives.

title: The room air drops about 2 K within 15 minutes while the boiler or heat pump charges hot water with priority, far faster than a real house cools
description:
Source: owner decision 2026-10-20, after PR #1090 (hisim-fob3) measured a one-step room-air dip in the heated assembly test houses: "that seems indeed too large for 15 minutes, given how slow real systems are".

Observed: while a boiler or heat pump charges the hot-water cylinder with priority, the room air drops by about 2 K within one 15-minute step. Assemblies' isolation day (1 Jan 2021, 900 s, defaults): gas, oil and hydrogen boilers min 17.88 C, air-source heat pump 17.95 C, dhw/indirect_cylinder 17.80 C, district heating 19.55 C; electric, pellet and wood-chip boilers show none. The recorded gas twin (household_gas_building_sizer, January week at 900 s) has 12 steps with a drop of more than 1 K. Example, 1 Jan 2021: the DHW charge runs 17:00-17:45 (7.6 / 6.7 / 6.4 kW to the cylinder, 0 W to space heating); the space-heating buffer drains from 30.3 to 21.4 C, the radiators' heat falls from 3.58 kW to 1.13 kW, and the room air falls from 20.0 to 17.9 C in the 17:30 step, then recovers to 18.8 and 20.0 C.

Two causes, both to be examined: (1) the building's air node has no heat capacity (ISO 13790 5R1C): the air temperature is recomputed each step from the gains, so a 2.4 kW loss of radiator heat lowers it by about 0.82 K/kW at once (measured on the heat-pump twin), where a real room, its furniture and the radiators' own water would take tens of minutes; (2) the buffer is small against the length of the hot-water charge: it empties to room temperature within 30-45 minutes of priority charging. Related: the minute-scale air jumps from appliance gains (same cause 1), hisim-s9h7 (radiators without a size, no emitter inertia), hisim-6irf (summer radiator cooling).

Do: quantify how much of the dip each cause explains (e.g. a run with a larger buffer, and an estimate with an air-node capacity); then propose to the owner either an air-node heat capacity (5R2C; moves every golden) or emitter/buffer inertia, or both.

Done when: the dip during a hot-water charge is within what a real house shows (owner to agree a figure, e.g. well under 1 K per 15 minutes), with the goldens re-blessed once.
notes:
Owner decisions 2026-10-21 (Noah), after the investigation of 2026-10-21 (hot-water priority charges empty the small space-heating buffer after 20-25 min; the room air has no heat capacity): target: the room's shortfall below its set point grows at most 0.5 K per 15 minutes and at most 1 K per hot-water charge, at 900 s and at 60 s. Two control fixes now, physics (emitter mass, air capacity) later after hisim-component-physics-4g9.37: (A) the heat pump's hot-water charge ends 2 K below its target; (B) a maximum hot-water priority time in the boiler's and the heat pump's controllers, after which the charge yields to space heating for an interval and then resumes.

2026-10-21, (A) on branch hp-dhw-charge-ends-below-target: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHWConfig.charge_end_below_target_in_kelvin, 2 K by default, replaces the class constant SWITCH_OFF_TOLERANCE_IN_KELVIN (0.5 K), which was also the energy manager's surplus switch-on point; both keep sharing the one value. household_heatpump_building_sizer, main -> (A); quarter-hours counted when they or the one before hold hot water, set-point changes of the energy manager masked; a charge's drop is the largest growth of the shortfall from its start to 30 min after its end. Full year 2021 at 900 s: quarter-hours with a drop > 0.5 K / > 1 K 305 / 160 -> 164 / 101, largest 4.33 -> 4.34 K; charges with a drop below 20 °C of more than 1 K 50 -> 15, largest 2.67 -> 2.67 K; degree-hours below 20 °C 69.7 -> 36.4, more than 1 K below 9.7 -> 3.0; heat-pump electricity 3790 -> 3800 kWh (+0.3 %); hot water unmet 7.0 -> 7.7 kWh; forced steps 1860 -> 1973. January week (1-7 Jan 2021) at 60 s: quarter-hours > 0.5 / > 1 K 9 / 1 -> 3 / 0, largest 1.10 -> 0.70 K; largest drop per charge 2.34 -> 1.06 K; degree-hours below 20 °C 4.0 -> 1.2; electricity 183.6 -> 182.1 kWh; forced steps 53 -> 26. The target is not met by (A) alone; (B) follows on branch dhw-priority-time-limit.

2026-10-21, (B) on branch dhw-priority-time-limit (stacked on A): HotWaterPriorityLimit (dual_circuit_system), asked by GenericBoilerController and MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW (new optional input SpaceHeatingStateFromController from the space-heating controller's State_SH): a charge that has had priority for maximum_hot_water_priority_time_in_seconds while space heating asks for heat yields to space heating for space_heating_interval_after_hot_water_priority_in_seconds, then resumes until the tank reaches its target; never interrupted while space heating does not ask; defaults 15 / 15 min. Sources: Vaillant multiMATIC VRC 700 (max. cylinder charge time 45 min, anti-cycling 30 min), Mitsubishi Ecodan FTC3 (DHW max. operation time 60 min, DHW mode restriction 30 min), Siemens Albatros2 line 5030 (pause as long as the limit). Same metrics as (A). household_gas_building_sizer full year 900 s, main -> 15/15 (45/30, 60/30): quarter-hours > 0.5 / > 1 K during hot water 246 / 161 -> 16 / 10 (231 / 154, 243 / 161), largest 3.26 -> 3.03 K; charges > 1 K 160 -> 8, largest 4.21 -> 3.03 K; degree-hours below 20 °C 125.3 -> 8.3, more than 1 K below 45.3 -> 2.3; gas 17385 -> 17363 kWh; forced steps 90 -> 67. January week 60 s: quarter-hours 8 / 7 -> 0 / 0, largest 1.75 -> 0.33 K; largest per charge 2.47 -> 0.64 K. household_heatpump_building_sizer full year 900 s, main -> A -> B (45/30, 60/30 on A): quarter-hours 305 / 160 -> 164 / 101 -> 42 / 32 (115 / 61, 144 / 75), largest 4.33 -> 4.34 -> 3.25 K; charges > 1 K below 20 °C 50 -> 15 -> 2, largest 2.67 -> 2.67 -> 1.25 K; degree-hours below 20 °C 69.7 -> 36.4 -> 23.4, more than 1 K below 9.7 -> 3.0 -> 1.2; electricity 3790 -> 3800 -> 3806 kWh; hot water unmet 7.0 -> 7.7 -> 9.1 kWh; forced steps 1860 -> 1973 -> 2038. January week 60 s: quarter-hours 9 / 1 -> 3 / 0 -> 0 / 0, largest 1.10 -> 0.70 -> 0.37 K; largest per charge 2.34 -> 1.06 -> 0.08 K. Target: met in the January week at 60 s in both twins, not met at 900 s in either: at 900 s one hot-water step is the whole 15 minutes, the buffer cannot bridge it and the room air has no capacity (gas 2021-01-29 08:00: the buffer starts the step at 26.5 °C on the low phase of the boiler's step-by-step swing, hisim-6ehm, and the room falls 3.0 K; heat pump 2021-02-08 09:15-10:30: the energy manager's surplus raise lifts the set point to 22 °C and the hot-water target to 70 °C, and every charging step drops the room 1.6 to 3.3 K below the raised set point). Left open for the physics after hisim-component-physics-4g9.37; a control alternative at 900 s would split one step between hot water and space heating (no bead yet).

title: Make the golden-update workflow's force_rewrite checkbox say what it does and when not to tick it
description:
Source: owner, 2026-09-24, after bless PR #819 (for #816) was run with force_rewrite ticked by mistake.

The workflow_dispatch input of .github/workflows/golden-update.yml reads: "Overwrite every stored value with the fresh one, dropping KPIs the runs no longer produce." The owner read it as "write the new values for what changed" -- i.e. what a normal bless already does -- and ticked it. The forced run rewrote every golden verbatim, so 16 goldens that did not change got last-digit float noise (1e-16 .. 5e-10 relative) next to the one real change (air_conditioned_house), burying it and inviting conflicts; stale bless #817 looks the same.

Wanted: the input's description (the one line GitHub shows next to the checkbox) makes the default clear and the checkbox the exception, e.g.: "Leave UNTICKED for a normal bless: values within the gate's tolerance keep their stored value, so the PR shows only KPIs that really moved. Tick only to clear accumulated noise, retire a KPI or repair an unreadable golden: it rewrites EVERY value (float noise in every golden) and drops KPIs the runs no longer produce." Also consider renaming the input to something that reads as dangerous (e.g. force_rewrite_all_values), and make the bless PR body of a normal run say "only KPIs beyond tolerance were rewritten" and of a forced run warn at the top that every golden carries noise and that the reviewer should check the non-intended files. GitHub limits input descriptions in length -- keep the key sentence first. The file header comment (lines 6-12) already explains it; the checkbox text is what people actually read.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-24, second pitfall: bless #820 ran on main although the reason said building-door-estimate -- the 'Use workflow from' branch selector of the Run workflow dialog defaults to main, and the reason text does not choose the branch. The input description (or the reason's default text) should say to pick the PR's branch in 'Use workflow from'; the workflow could also refuse to run on main unless the reason says so, or print the branch it ran on at the top of the bless PR body.

title: Rust conversion ideas
Profile a representative run and publish the time breakdown
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Step 0 -- "Measure before
changing anything"

Two or three setups (one minutely full year, one 15-minute short run, one with MPC), broken into:
timestep loop, third-party library calls (pvlib/hplib/bslib/windpowerlib), input parsing,
postprocessing, external waiting (UTSP/LPG). This is a day of work and it is the gate on every
performance argument in the companion feasibility document -- including whether Tier 1 should be
reordered around whatever actually dominates.

Payoff now: it will almost certainly find optimizable Python nobody has looked at.
Payoff for a port: it converts "10-50x on the loop" into an Amdahl ceiling for the whole run.

title: Stop the byte surgery that appends to component_connections.json
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

`component.py:447` seeks to `st_size - 1` and overwrites the closing bracket of
`component_connections.json` to append an entry. Buffer the connections and write the file once
when wiring completes.

Payoff now: an interrupted run stops leaving a syntactically broken JSON file behind.

title: Make the convergence criterion explicit, configurable and unit-aware
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2; and
roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md option O8, "Per-output tolerance vector"

`component.py:194` compares every output against a hardcoded absolute 1e-4 -- watts, joules,
kelvin, euros and dimensionless ratios on one scale -- and the forced-convergence thresholds
(above 10 iterations forced, above 100 raises, `simulator.py:266-270`) are hardcoded next to it.
At minimum make all three configurable and document the choice; ideally scale per unit.

O8 states the targeted form: replace the single absolute 1e-4 with a per-output (or per-unit)
tolerance supplied at construction. It is the cheap fix for the real defect measurement M4 looks
for -- an absolute threshold applied across incommensurable units, where a counter at 1e9 needs
1e-13 relative and would fail on every iteration, silently forcing the 10-iteration cutoff on
every timestep.

Caution from O8: it changes iteration counts and therefore results. Needs a one-time golden
re-bless and a stated policy, per the parity-policy decision.

Payoff now: the tolerance becomes a modelling decision that can be justified, and the "runs
converge but nobody knows how tightly" question gets an answer.

Gated on measurement M4.

title: Give i_save_state and i_restore_state explicit state structs instead of deepcopy
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Five component modules `deepcopy` themselves or their state each iteration. An explicit small
state object is faster in Python and removes the "which attributes are state?" ambiguity.

Payoff now: measurable -- this runs once per component per convergence iteration per timestep.

Related: the two live `i_save_state` defects (the EMS restoring a reference and the
heat-distribution controller self-assigning) are exactly the ambiguity this removes, and the
mid-year epic names both as prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

title: Inject the cache backend, the clock and the RNG instead of monkeypatching them in tests
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

22 test files use `monkeypatch`, 8 of them around `utils.get_cache_file`; without that patching,
runs are order-dependent through the shared on-disk cache, and `conftest.py` scrubs
`HISIM_CACHE_*` around every test. Turn these into constructor parameters.

Payoff now: order-independent tests, less autouse machinery, and the stale-cache class of false
failures loses its main route in.

This also matches the AGENTS.md guideline that monkeypatching is to be avoided in shared
fixtures, and the seeded-RNG precedent of `RandomNumbers`, whose seed became a configuration
field in P3 so a system description can say what a run will do.

title: Write an owned, versioned cache-key serializer with a stable field order
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

The cache key is `sha256(dataclasses_json output + sim-params string)`, so field order, float repr
and enum spelling from a third-party library are load-bearing for about 319 MB of committed cache
and every cross-machine share. Write an owned key serializer with a stable field order, a schema
version in the key, and a test that pins the exact string for a fixture config.

Payoff now: upgrading `dataclasses_json` or `pyhumps` stops silently invalidating every cache
entry in the fleet.

Related: the producer-fingerprint keys of the cache service solve the other half (what code
produced the content); this one is about what identifies the request.

title: Audit the sixty exact float comparisons in component control flow
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Roughly 60 `== 0`-style comparisons sit in component control paths
(`water_mass_flow_rate == 0`, `control_signal == 0.0`, `delta_t == 0` patched to `1e-8`).
Replace with documented epsilons and re-bless the goldens once.

Do this in Python, where re-blessing is cheap and reviewable, rather than discovering it during a
port where the change is indistinguishable from a translation bug.

title: Move module_selection.py out of hisim/inputs and stop reading data at import time
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`hisim/inputs/photovoltaic/module_selection.py` is Python inside `hisim/inputs/`, and it reads PV
module databases at import. Relocate to `hisim/components/` and make the read lazy.

Payoff now: import time, and the data directory becomes purely data.

title: Prune requirements.txt of the three declared but unimported packages
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`seaborn`, `plotly` and `html2image` are declared but imported nowhere under `hisim/`, `tests/`,
`tools/`, `scripts/` or `system_setups/`; there are commented-out pins (`pvlib`,
`windpowerlib`, `wetterdienst`) and a migration TODO.

An accurate dependency list is a prerequisite for reasoning about the domain-library gap at all,
and the commented-out pvlib pin is named separately in the Tier 1 adapter item as a risk of its
own.

Note that `pyhumps` already left with the scenario-JSON writer (P4 F-9), so the list has drifted
since the survey.

title: Converge on the energy-system YAML as the only way to describe a system
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Converge on one
front end"

At the time of the survey there were three ways to describe a system: 23 setup functions in
`system_setups/*.py`, 22 `.scenario.json` twins and 28 `.energy_system.yaml` files, with
byte-identity freshness gates keeping the generated ones in sync. Per the declarative-energy-
systems plan the YAML is the intended survivor; finish that migration and retire the others.

The JSON third retired on 2026-09-12, so what is left is retiring the Python setups, which is
P5/P6 work in the declarative plan.

Payoff now: one loader to keep correct instead of three, and one place where a new component must
be registered.
Payoff for a port: the single largest reduction in porting surface available anywhere in this
list.

title: Decide what happens to MPC and casadi before any port is estimated
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4 -- "Decisions to take
before a port, not cleanups"

Reformulate MPC as a MILP (the feasibility document argues the dynamics are linear between
disjunctions), accept a permanent Python island, or declare MPC out of core scope.

This is the only red item in the whole analysis; leaving it open leaves the total open.

Note that `controller_mpc` moved to `obsolete/components/` under P4 decision D-16 (2026-09-10),
which is close to "out of core scope" already but was not taken as this decision.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Beads schema migration 2026-09-28: this looks obsolete or duplicate, left open for the owner to check. Answered: MPC retired to obsolete/ (#680), casadi is no dependency.

title: Give every physics library one HiSim-owned adapter module with no library types in signatures
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

Today `pvlib`, `hplib`, `bslib`, `windpowerlib`, `oemof.thermal` and `pygfunction` are called
inline from the components that need them -- `weather.py`, `generic_pv_system.py`,
`building/window.py`, `solar_thermal_system.py`, `more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py`,
`simple_heat_source.py` -- and library objects cross the boundary in both directions (HiSim
mutates `heatpump.delta_t` on an hplib object mid-simulation). Give each library one HiSim-owned
module with typed scalar/array inputs and outputs and no library type in its signatures.

Payoff now: upgrading or pinning pvlib stops being a repo-wide risk (the pin in
`requirements.txt` is commented out, which is its own finding); the calls become mockable, so
component tests stop needing real solar-position math; and one place can record reference
inputs and outputs per library call.
Payoff for a port: this boundary is the FFI seam, and it is the difference between a hybrid being
designable and not.

title: Decide whether charts and the PDF report are in core scope
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4

Docker mode already runs with every chart and the PDF disabled, which proves they are optional.
Decide whether they are in core scope; if not, formalize the JSON manifest that external tooling
would render.

(The container post-processing allow-list that made "Docker mode" a different option set was
removed on 2026-09-19 with HiSim #780 -- the simulation file is authoritative in a container too
-- so the evidence the item leans on is historical. The decision stands.)

title: Decide whether the core simulator may depend on the closed-source .NET LPG binary
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4

The forever-dependency is the closed-source .NET binary, not the Python wrapper. Decide whether
the core simulator may depend on a subprocess at all.

The operational evidence for how much that dependency costs is in
`roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md`: the shared sqlite database that was never found, the
whole-calculation lock that serialises local runs, and the ETXTBSY install race.

title: Decide the FFI direction before estimating a hybrid
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4 -- "the FFI direction
(review item R5)", one of "two decisions masquerading as engineering tasks"

Does Python call into Rust (an extension module inside the existing run) or does Rust drive and
call back into Python for the components not yet ported? The feasibility document's review item
R5 sets out the trade; `rust_simulator_spec.md` option O7 sketches the Rust
`process_one_timestep` under the second reading, including the mechanics that will bite (hold the
GIL across the timestep rather than re-acquiring per call; call `Python::check_signals()` once
per timestep or Ctrl-C stops working on long runs; decide how a `PyErr` from a component becomes
a Rust error and back with the traceback intact, including the existing raise at 100 iterations).

Gated on measurements M2 and M3.

title: M0: measure per-element container read and write costs on our CPython
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2 "Measurement program", M0

Read and write cost for `list`, `array.array('d')`, `memoryview` format `'d'`, and numpy scalar
indexing. Establishes where the boxing conversion is cheapest to pay.

Expected ordering, to be confirmed and not assumed: list fastest per element, every unboxed
buffer slower, numpy slowest -- which is why an unboxed buffer handed to Python is the wrong
shape. A prior team measurement already found converting the value store to numpy came out
slower: the vectorized compare gain is smaller than the loss on hundreds of individual scalar
stores.

title: M1: measure the four i_simulate call-site spellings on one representative component
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M1

One representative component, four `i_simulate` bodies: (a) the current
`stsv.set_output_value(self.channel, v)`; (b) `o[self.channel.local_index] = v`;
(c) `o[self.IDX_X] = v` with a class-level int; (d) `o[2] = v` with the index hoisted to a local.

Decides whether rewriting 717 call sites (484 `set_output_value` and 233 `get_input_value` under
`hisim/components/`) earns its churn, and which spelling to rewrite them to. It is also the gate
on options O3, O5 and O6 of the same document -- in particular whether the gap between spellings
(b)/(c) and (d) is worth a port-plumbing generator.

title: M2: measure the PyO3 boundary cost with a gather-and-scatter stub
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M2 -- the only measurement that
needs a Rust toolchain

One extension call that gathers 10 scattered f64 into a Python list and scatters 7 back. Yields
the real crossing cost and the real per-float boxing cost on our platform, which every estimate
in the options register depends on. It is also the cheapest available probe of the Rust build and
wheel story.

title: M3: split per-iteration time into component physics versus value plumbing
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M3

Per-iteration time split into component physics versus value plumbing (writes, reads, the
compare, and the copies), on two or three representative setups. Without this, every speedup
figure in the options register is unanchored.

The plumbing it measures: per iteration the engine does one full-array `copy_values_from_other`
(`component.py:171-179`) and two `clone()` per timestep (`simulator.py:239-241`), plus an
interpreted loop over every output at absolute 1e-4 (`component.py:191-197`).

title: M4: log which output fails the convergence test last, per timestep
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M4 -- "residual argmax"

Per timestep, log which output index fails `is_close_enough_to_previous` last. This answers two
questions at once: whether the outputs driving the iteration count are wired signals or
write-only diagnostics (on the measured 14-component setup, 141 outputs are registered and only
41 distinct ones are read, so about 71 % of outputs are read by no component), and whether any
output's magnitude makes the absolute 1e-4 threshold unsatisfiable -- a counter at 1e9 needs
about 1e-13 relative, so it would fail on every iteration and silently force the 10-iteration
cutoff on every timestep.

This is the gate on the per-output tolerance vector.

title: M5: measure the iteration histogram and the result-buffer memory high-water
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M5

The distribution of iterations per timestep, and the peak size of `all_result_lines`. A year at
1 min x 141 outputs is about 593 MB as raw f64 but roughly 2-3 GB as a Python list of lists of
boxed floats; at 500 outputs it is about 2 GB versus about 10 GB. Given the 16 GB runner ceiling
tracked by `ci-usage`, this may be worth more than any CPU figure in the register.

title: M6: assert that one forced extra convergence iteration leaves the outputs identical
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M6 -- "state-leak test
(correctness, not performance)"

Run a timestep, then force one extra iteration, and assert the outputs are identical. This checks
the premise that `i_restore_state` undoes everything `i_simulate` mutates. If it fails anywhere,
the loop is not a fixed-point iteration, iteration count changes results, and several arguments
in the options register and Appendix A do not hold.

Worth having regardless of the whole Rust programme -- which is why it is P3 among P4 siblings.

It will fail on at least two components today: the EMS restores a reference rather than a clone
(`controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:665`) and the heat-distribution controller
self-assigns (`heat_distribution_system.py:1180`). Both have their own issues.

title: Replace the string-keyed SimRepository with a typed simulation context
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

17 modules under `hisim/` still reach for the singleton, including the weather -> building
forecast handoff (11 yearly arrays), price signal -> MPC (about 20 forecast keys), the
air-conditioner fit coefficients and the PID thermal coefficients; `generic_car.py:293` reads its
repository through `getattr(self, "simulation_repository", None)`. Replace with an explicit typed
context constructed by the engine and passed to components.

(Counts are from the 2026-09-09 survey at f91c3eb1. `hisim/sim_repository_singleton.py` was
deleted on 2026-09-12 and the weather and occupancy forecasts moved into the per-simulation
`SimRepository` under writer-owned key names, so the singleton half is smaller than the survey
says; the string-keyed half is what remains.)

Payoff now: mypy sees these handoffs, a missing publisher fails at wiring time instead of as a
`KeyError` in timestep 0, test fixtures that reset a global disappear, and run isolation stops
depending on discipline.
Payoff for a port: removes the single largest piece of untyped shared mutable state.

title: Replace pd.DataFrame in the component cost and KPI hooks with a typed results view
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

92 signatures under `hisim/components/` take `postprocessing_results: pd.DataFrame`, so pandas is
part of the component API and every cost/KPI implementation depends on column-name conventions.
Introduce a narrow view type (a per-output series accessor plus the reductions actually used) and
migrate the hooks behind it.

Payoff now: KPI and cost code becomes unit-testable without constructing a DataFrame; the
column-name coupling that section 6.2 of the feasibility document describes as "positional
column-name parsing" becomes a compile-time-visible interface.
Payoff for a port: removes pandas from the component trait, which is otherwise a hard blocker for
porting any component before porting all of postprocessing.

title: Replace reflection-based component instantiation with a static registry
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

29 `importlib` call sites across 9 component modules exist purely to dodge circular imports in
default connections, and the energy-system YAML files name components by fully-qualified Python
path (`class: hisim.components.weather.Weather`). Add a name -> constructor table with a test that
pins its contents, keep the fully-qualified paths accepted as aliases, and let the declarative
loaders resolve through the table.

(The survey counted 22 `.scenario.json` files too; those were retired on 2026-09-12, so the 28
`.energy_system.yaml` files are the live half.)

Payoff now: a typo in a file fails at load with a suggestion instead of an `ImportError` from
deep inside `importlib`; the circular-import dodges can be deleted; the component inventory
becomes enumerable for docs, the webtool and `hisim energy-system describe`.
Payoff for a port: this is the inventory Rust cannot generate for itself, and building it in
Python proves the list is complete.

Related: this is also the fix for the two `Building` class spellings in the v3 schema.

title: Decide the numeric-parity policy and make the goldens implement it
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2 (first item) and
Tier 4 ("the parity policy ... a decision masquerading as an engineering task")

Today the regression corpus mixes byte comparison of CSV and markdown with `math.isclose` at
`rel_tol` 1e-9 and `pytest.approx` at its implicit 1e-6 default. Byte comparison pins pandas'
float formatting, which is why pandas is pinned to an exact version. Move comparisons to parsed-
value numeric comparison at declared per-domain tolerances, and keep byte identity only where
byte identity is the point (the `.energy_system.yaml` freshness gates).

Payoff now: goldens stop breaking on formatting changes in a dependency, and every tolerance
becomes a stated decision rather than a library default nobody chose.
Payoff for a port: this is the acceptance harness; review item R6 in the feasibility document
explains why the current contradiction blocks the estimate itself.

The document's explicit non-recommendation belongs with it: do not chase bit-exactness. It is
unattainable across languages and it also means faithfully reproducing known defects.

Related: the golden gate's `abs_tol = 0` floor, which makes a physically zero KPI incomparable,
is the first concrete instance.

title: Pass the OPEX cost values in memory instead of re-reading the CSVs it wrote
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2, "Kill the intra-run
file feedback loop in postprocessing"

KPI preparation re-reads the cost CSVs that the OPEX step wrote earlier in the same run, keyed by
magic row names such as "Total" (`kpi_preparation.py:732-776`). Pass the values in memory.

Payoff now: removes an ordering dependency between postprocessing options and a whole class of
"works alone, fails in the full run" bugs.

Related: roadmap/cost_module_issues.md item 27 records a second ordering hazard in the same area -- the
legacy `get_cost_capex` writes computed values back into component configs, which the lifecycle
engine then read as overrides until the engine was moved to run first.

title: Replace the pickle result export with parquet or CSV plus JSON
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

`postprocessing_main.py` pickles a DataFrame. Pickle has no cross-language reader and is a
security and version-compatibility liability in Python too.

This one has external consumers, so it needs an announcement and a deprecation window -- start it
early precisely because of that.

title: Split physics from cost and reporting boilerplate in the large component modules
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

Section 4.1 of the feasibility document estimates that 25-40 % of the big component files is
cost, KPI and report code. Split per component, one PR each, no behaviour change.

Payoff now: `building.py` at 2 099 lines and `more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py` at about 2 750
become reviewable, and the physics gets testable without the reporting stack.

(The building has since been split into a package, `hisim/components/building/` -- so it is an
example of the shape rather than a remaining case.)

title: The do-nothing reference renews the envelope at end of life, and plan rows name the part a measure replaces (renovisorissues #59)
description: Owner decision 2026-09-27 (renew fabric in the reference): reference.by_subject gets a row per existing envelope element (roof, facade, floor, window, door) with service_life_years, installation_year and the replacement_years in which doing nothing renews it like-for-like at end of life (the cost database's lifetime, dated from the element's installation_year), priced like any replacement; plan by_subject rows state replaces_subjects (the subjects a measure replaces, from the translator's own replaced_by_asset_classes table). Changes every reference total; spec MR (economics-hisim-spec) needed.
close_reason: reference renews the fabric (unpriced, due years), replaces_subjects, full-cost method, schema 7 (feat/reference-fabric)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Implemented uncommitted in worktree agent-fab (feat/reference-fabric): envelope_<element> kept subjects priced from the cost DB (IE/DE have all five classes, src_ai_estimates; NL none -> unpriced with engine fallback life), replaces_subjects via mapping report + fallback from stored registers, schema_version 7. Open owner questions: anyway credit now double counts vs a reference that renews; undated 1975 fabric all due in year 1; register classes are insulation classes (renewal priced as ETICS). Mockup gets 5 rows only after fix/envelope-area-pricing (c69653a2) merges.

title: One ground albedo for every plane-of-array computation: the solar thermal collector uses pvlib's default 0.25 while Window.ALBEDO and the PV system's ALBEDO are 0.2
description: Found reviewing PR #876 (2026-10-04). Three components compute irradiance on a tilted plane with pvlib.irradiance.get_total_irradiance: generic_pv_system/calculation.py passes ALBEDO = 0.2 (line ~113); building/window.py passes Window.ALBEDO = 0.2 (a class attribute since #876, with tests/test_building_window.py pinning it equal to the PV constant); solar_thermal_system.py (plane_of_array_irradiance_w_m2, around line 42) passes no albedo and therefore gets pvlib's default 0.25. One ground in front of the house, two values. Resolution: one shared constant in a core module below the components (as hisim/hydronics.py holds the water constants, cf. PR #890), passed explicitly by all three callers; the EN ISO 52010-1:2017 default 0.2 is the documented choice. Result change: solar thermal collector irradiance moves slightly (ground-reflected share 0.2 vs 0.25 of GHI times (1-cos tilt)/2), so one golden re-bless for the solar-thermal twins, announced. Done when: grep for get_total_irradiance shows every call passing the shared albedo, and the equality test becomes an identity.

title: The radiators and floor heating get a heat-transfer limit: the heat they deliver follows their size and the water's excess temperature (EN 442), not just the water flow
description:
Source: owner question 2026-10-20 after the July-week check (hisim-6irf).

Today: HeatDistribution.determine_water_temperature_output_after_heat_exchange_with_building_and_effective_thermal_power gives the room exactly the building's theoretical demand, limited only by the water: the outlet may fall to room temperature (heating) or rise to it (cooling), so the circuit can deliver up to m*cp*(T_supply - T_room). The emitter itself has no size. At this setup's 0.27 kg/s, water 5 K above the room delivers about 5.6 kW; a real radiator 5 K above the room delivers a few per cent of its rating.

Consequences: (1) cooling through the radiators is unlimited (hisim-6irf); (2) in heating, any supply temperature above the room meets the demand, so the supply temperature never has to rise because the radiators are too small, a house is never underheated by its emitters, and the heat pump's COP never pays for undersized radiators; (3) emitter measures (low-temperature radiators, hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.1; keeping old radiators after an envelope renovation) cannot change the result through the emitter.

Do: an emitter heat-transfer law, EN 442 style: Q = Q_design * (dT_lm / dT_lm,design)^n with dT_lm the log-mean excess of the water over the room, n about 1.3 for radiators and 1.1 for floor heating, a dead zone at zero excess. Q_design and the design temperatures (e.g. 55/45/20 C) are configuration; Q_design is a sized_field from the building's design heat load, so a preset needs no number. The circuit delivers min(demand, emitter law, what the flow can carry), and its outlet temperature follows from the delivered heat. The heating curve and the emitter must agree at the design point (a check, or the curve derived from the emitter).

Related: hisim-6irf (summer pump switch), hisim-component-physics-4g9.37 (room thermostat moves into the distribution controller), hisim-renovisor-translator-epc.1 (low-temperature radiator as an emitter).

Done when: the delivered heat follows the emitter law in heating and cooling, with an owner-agreed default sizing; a test shows an undersized emitter forcing a higher supply temperature or an underheated room; the goldens are re-blessed once (every setup with a heat distribution moves).
