title: The heating curve's season and the night setback become explicit state machines (hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 method)
description:
Source: owner request of 2026-10-15 (Noah): proper state machines for every controller, to find all logic errors and undefined state transitions; one bead per controller family beside the pilot hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (boiler), hisim-component-physics-4g9.41 (hplib heat pump) and the heat distribution controller named there.

Scope (heating curve and night setback): HeatingCurveController (heating_curve.py): the heating season switch on the daily mean outside temperature and its hysteresis. NightSetbackController (night_setback_controller.py): the setback window by time of day. Small, timer- and hysteresis-driven; good second examples after the pilot. Also make the component template (hisim/components/example_template.py, controller_l1_example_controller.py) teach the pattern.

Method: the one of hisim-component-physics-4g9.34 (the boiler pilot), reusing its helper once it exists: states as an Enum, transitions as a table of (state, condition) -> next state, a pure next_state(state, inputs, timers), the transitions taken recorded; tests from the table (every row, the boundary value of each condition), a coverage check that every declared transition is taken and no undeclared one, Hypothesis invariants, match plus assert_never for exhaustiveness, and the state diagram generated from the table. A transition the code takes that the table does not declare, or a state with no way out, is a finding: fix it in the same PR if no result moves; otherwise report it with options.

Done when: every controller of this family decides through a declared transition table with a pure next-state function, its tests cover every row and boundary, the coverage check shows no undeclared transition, and any change of results is explained in the PR (goldens re-blessed if needed).

title: Staged splice: a later stage's tax-credit and operational instalments are neither shifted nor escalated
description: hisim/economics/staged.py _spliced_entry treats SUBSIDY entries after year 0 (TAX_CREDIT_SCHEDULE instalments in the stage's own years 1..N, OPERATIONAL payments) as operating flows: kept only in plan years whose active stage is the entry's stage, at the stage's OWN year index, unescalated. So a stage starting in year 4 gets its tax-credit instalments of own years 1..3 dropped, and a stage-0 credit is cut off when the next stage starts. Owner principle (2026-09-27): a TAX_CREDIT is a share of cost and should follow that cost (escalated DB price, or the quote as stated) and be dated from the stage's start year (shift by from_year like the loan schedule, share x stage_start_factor); OPERATIONAL is a fixed nominal rate per kWh and should be shifted but not escalated. Changes money for any staged plan whose solver picks a tax credit (e.g. DE 35c) — list the goldens it moves.

title: A run with hydrogen or combined heat and power writes a hydrogen Sankey: electricity through the electrolyzer, the hydrogen storage and the fuel cell or CHP back to electricity and heat, with the conversion loss of every stage
description:
Owner, 2026-10-18: besides the house's heat and electricity Sankeys (hisim-mzft), these carriers get a Sankey of their own, because the system they describe is not readable from heat and electricity alone.

Components: generic_electrolyzer_h2 / generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage, the hydrogen storage, generic_fuel_cell / advanced_fuel_cell, generic_chp, and the controllers controller_l1_electrolyzer_h2, controller_l1_fuel_cell, controller_l2_ptx_energy_management_system, controller_l2_xtp_fuel_cell_ems. The carrier is EnergyBalanceCarrier.HYDROGEN (and NATURAL_GAS for a gas CHP).

Wanted: one Sankey per run that uses any of them: electricity in (grid, PV) -> electrolyzer -> hydrogen into storage, storage losses, hydrogen out -> fuel cell or CHP -> electricity and heat, with each component's conversion loss as its own node. The round-trip efficiency electricity -> hydrogen -> electricity is what decides whether such a system pays off, and it is spread over several components.

Needs: the energy ports of these components (part of hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.5 and hisim-energy-sankeys-9uoo.7) and a setup or twin that runs them for a full year.
Done when: one such setup writes the Sankey, its residual is zero within tolerance, and the owner has reviewed it.

description:

title: Refuse NaN and negative irradiance at the weather boundary once, for every consumer, instead of each consumer guarding (window returns 0 on NaN, nothing clamps negatives)
description: Found reviewing PR #876 (2026-10-04). building/window.py returns 0.0 when the plane-of-array irradiance is NaN (a silent zero gain; #876 is asked to raise instead), and no consumer clamps slightly negative GHI/DHI (night zero-offsets in some weather sources), which would give negative window gains, PV output or collector irradiance. hisim/components/weather/calculation.py handles only the horizon divisor (around lines 836-862), it does not validate the irradiance columns. Resolution per the fail-hard rule: the Weather component validates its irradiance series once after loading (DNI, DHI, GHI, extraterrestrial: finite and >= 0; small negative night offsets are a data defect to refuse by name with the source file and timestep, not to clamp silently — if a known source needs a tolerance, state it as a documented threshold), so every consumer (window, PV, solar thermal, air conditioner) can drop its own guard. Check every bundled weather source (DWD TRY, EPW readers, the IE data) for negatives/NaNs before enabling, and the UTSP/renovisor paths. Done when: the weather component refuses bad irradiance by name, the consumers' NaN guards are gone, and a test feeds a NaN and a negative value through the loader.

title: The hourly ci-usage report fails its whole run on one GitHub API error instead of retrying with backoff and reporting what it skipped
description:
Source: owner request 2026-10-15 ("it keeps failing"). The hourly `ci-usage` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci-usage.yml`, `scripts/ci_usage_report.py`) failed in 7 of its last 8 runs (2026-10-13 02:04 to 2026-10-14 18:41; one success at 13:47).

Both failures inspected die in the GitHub API client: run 38617254128 with `urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 500: Internal Server Error` raised from `_request` (`scripts/ci_usage_report.py` ~143) via `get` (~169) in `run` (~1180); run 38530194588 the same way via `paginate` (~183) in `sweep_resources` (~670). The client retries RETRYABLE_STATUS a few times without backoff, then re-raises, and nothing above catches it, so one bad page fails the whole job and no overview is written.

Fix: (1) retry transient errors (5xx, URLError, timeouts) with exponential backoff and jitter; (2) let one failed listing degrade the report instead of failing it: skip that page/run/artifact, count and name what was skipped in the job summary, and exit 0 when a usable overview was produced (the monitoring must never be red because GitHub hiccupped; per `.github/ci-monitoring.md` the probe never fails the job it measures); (3) a unit test with a fake client that returns 500 then 200, and one that fails a page permanently.

Done when: the workflow survives transient API errors, reports what it skipped, and runs green for a day of hourly runs.
close_reason: GitHubApi retries 5xx, connection errors and timeouts up to five attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (1-2, 2-4, 4-8, 8-16 s); a request that still fails raises ApiRequestFailed, and the collector skips only what it was for (the jobs of one run, one artifact, the rest of a listing), names each skipped part under Collection and exits 0. After ten failed requests the sweep stops as partial. Tests in tests/test_ci_usage.py (TestTransientApiErrors): 500 then 200, growing waits, a permanently failing job listing, the full ReportCommand with a failing run listing exiting 0, and the stop after ten failures. The 'green for a day of hourly runs' check is for after the merge.

title: The weather starts every hourly source at zero at midnight of 1 January, so the first 30 minutes ramp up from 0 Pa, 0 °C and 0 m/s, and the azimuth is averaged across 360°/0°
description: Found by the time-series chart review (2026-10-15, household_heatpump_building_sizer, 2021 at 900 s). hisim/components/weather/calculation.py interpolate() prepends a 0.0 sample at 00:00 of 1 January before interpolating the hourly source (labelled at mid-hour) to one minute; the end of the year repeats the last sample instead. Result at 15 min: Weather Pressure is 23 333 Pa at 00:00 and 73 333 Pa at 00:15 (then ~100 000 Pa), TemperatureOutside 0.30 °C then 0.95 °C, WindSpeed 0.37 m/s then 1.17 m/s; visible in Weather/Pressure line and single-day charts (y axis down to 20 kPa). Fix: pad the start by repeating the first sample, as the end does. Separately, Azimuth at 00:30 on 1 January is 239° between 351° and 6°: averaging/interpolating an angle across the 360°->0° wrap. Interpolate the azimuth on its sine and cosine, or compute it from the sun position at the step.

title: Weather year separate from the calendar year (renovisorissues #57 step 2)
description:
# Weather year separate from the calendar year (renovisorissues #57, step 2)

Status: **decided by cmf on 2026-09-27**. Base: origin/main @ faa88f3b.

## Today
`SimulationParameters.__init__` (hisim/simulationparameters.py) sets `self.year = start_date.year`, which serves as both the calendar and the weather year.

`Weather.build_calculation_inputs` hands `year=C` to `WeatherSeriesInputs`. Every reader in `hisim/components/weather/calculation.py` stamps the file's rows onto C **by position** (`pd.date_range(f"{year}-01-01 …", periods=N)`):

| source | reader | anchor | data year in file | shipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DWD_TRY | read_dwd_try_data | Berlin 00:30, 8760 h | none (MM/DD/HH, MEZ) | Aachen TRY, 15 regions |
| NSRDB | read_nsrdb_data | Berlin 00:30, 8760 h | Year 2019 | 9 cities |
| NSRDB_15MIN | read_nsrdb_15min_data | UTC 00:00, 35040 | Year 2019 | 20 countries (RenoVisor) |
| DWD_10MIN | read_dwd_10min_data | UTC 00:00, 52560 | year 2021 | Aachen |
| DWD_15MIN | read_dwd_15min_data | UTC 00:00, run duration | year 2024 (leap) | Düsseldorf |
| ERA5 | read_era5_data | UTC 00:00, 8760 | year column | none shipped |

Nothing reads the data year. Sun position (`produce_weather_series`: pvlib `get_solarposition`, `get_extra_radiation`) is computed on the C-stamped index, i.e. on the calendar, and PV, the building and solar thermal read it. When C is a leap year, dates after 28 Feb drift by position and `interpolate` pads 31 Dec flat.

## Decisions (cmf, 2026-09-27)
1. **The parameter is `SimulationParameters.weather_year: Optional[int] = None`.** It covers the whole run and is also a `*.simulation.json/.yaml` key, which the loaders already accept through `SimulationParameters(**data)`. `self.year` stays C. Valid range: int, 1900–2100.
2. **Unset = today, byte-identical:** positional stamping, no check, no remap. A mismatch between the file's declared year and C is logged at INFO and noted in the realized record (not a WARNING). This closes hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.1.
3. **When set:**
   - The file's rows of year W are selected. The run is refused if W is not in the file (the message names the years that are), and refused on a source with no data year (TRY: pick the file instead).
   - The direct normal irradiance is derived on the W-stamped frame.
   - The rows are then remapped W→C **by same date**, in the source's own fixed-offset clock (UTC, or MEZ = UTC+1 for the Berlin-anchored readers), never Berlin wall time.
   - A 365-day W onto a leap C: 29 Feb is a copy of 28 Feb. A leap W onto a 365-day C: 29 Feb is dropped. W = C is the identity.
   - `interpolate(…, C)` and the resampling are unchanged. The sun stays on C.
4. **Future climates are weather files** (a LocationEnum entry or `WeatherConfig.for_data_file`), never a weather_year value. Revisit a `climate_scenario` parameter when scenario files ship.
5. **Cache keys and records:**
   - `get_unique_key` gets `###weather=W` and `get_unique_key_as_list` a line, **only when set**.
   - `ParameterNormalisation.normalise` and `ParameterFileWriter` write `weather_year` only when set, and `ParameterFileName` gets a `_weatherW` suffix only when set.
   - `WeatherSeriesInputs` gets `weather_year: Optional[int]`.
   - The LPG, car and solar-thermal caches key on W when set.
   - Unset keys and records stay byte-identical.
6. **Economics (PR D):**
   - `EvaluationInputs.weather_year: Optional[int]` is serialized in economic_inputs.json (read with `.get`), filled from the repository value `weather_year_effective` that the weather component publishes: W if set; otherwise the file's single declared year; otherwise None.
   - The staged document echoes it when the stages carry it, else `simulation_year` as today (no change while unset).
   - The staged "same year across stages" check also covers weather_year.
7. **RenoVisor (PR E):** `renovisor/simulation.py` `SimulationSetup.YEAR` splits into `CALENDAR_YEAR = 2019` and `WEATHER_YEAR = 2019`. The numbers are identical; the records gain a `weather_year` line. There is no request key. Later we ask RenoVisor whether they want a calendar year (e.g. = plan_start_year) and a weather choice (typical / extreme / 2045).
8. **Order:** A and B now; C after hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.4 (reuse its "resolve a date against the delivered frame" helper and its reader anchor tests; 9g2.4's leap refusal stays for the unset case only); then D and E.

## PRs
- **A, the parameter:**
  - `weather_year` in SimulationParameters, with validation, keys and records only when set.
  - If set, the weather component refuses by name until PR C lands.
  - Tests: .simulation.yaml round trip with and without the key; `get_unique_key()` pinned identical when unset; the realized record is identical when unset.
- **B, declared data years:**
  - `WeatherSourceFiles.data_years(source, path) -> Optional[FrozenSet[int]]`, reading the year column, None for TRY, cached per content hash.
  - `Weather.i_prepare_simulation` publishes `weather_year_effective` and logs the INFO mismatch note, plus a note in the record.
  - Tests: the data_years of every shipped file (NSRDB_15MIN {2019}, DWD_10MIN {2021}, DWD_15MIN {2024}, TRY None); the note is emitted; the series are unchanged. Closes hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.1.
- **C, select and remap:**
  - Readers filter by year when W is set; `remap_to_calendar(raw, W, C, clock)`; the refusals.
  - Tests: W = C frame-equal to unset; 365→leap (29 Feb = 28 Feb, 31 Dec real); leap→365; no duplicate or missing hour around the DST dates of W and C; sun series equal for W ≠ C; cold and warm cache equal.
- **D, the economics echo:** as in decision 6.
- **E, RenoVisor internal 2019/2019:** as in decision 7.
- No golden moves while weather_year is unset.

## Side findings (to be filed as beads)
- `read_nsrdb_data` labels UTC NSRDB data as Europe/Berlin, probably a 1 h shift.
- `calculation.interpolate` pads 31 Dec 23:00 of the previous year with 0.0 in every column, a temperature of 0 °C included.
- `read_dwd_10min_data`: the file is named 2021-2022 but holds 365 days.
- `Weather.calc_sun_position` (weather.py ~458) looks unused.

title: The PDF report's wide tables break words in the middle: the 9-column investment table shows Investmen/t, CO2-f/ootprint, MoreAdvancedHeatPu/mpHPLib
description:
Found in the review of PR #1019 (finding #5, review-evals/review1019_evaluation.md, outside the repository); the owner accepted it for #1019 on 2026-10-18 and asked for this bead.

What happens: #1019 makes the report's tables fit the page and wrap between words, but the 9-column investment (CAPEX) table of a heat-pump house still breaks words in the middle. Headers: Investmen/t [EUR], CO2-f/ootprint, percen/tage of in/vestment, Rest-Investmen/t. Component names: MoreAdvancedHeatPu/mpHPLib, SimpleHotWaterStorag/e, Total_without_heatpu/mp. The numbers do not break, and no table is cut off any more (on main the table was wider than the page and cut off at both edges). The OPEX (5 columns) and KPI (4 columns) tables have no break.

Cause: ReportGenerator.table_column_widths shares the 453 pt figure width among the columns by character count, so the widths are the same at any font size. The component column gets about 83 pt, while MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib needs 99 pt at the 7 pt font of tables above six columns (still 78 pt against 77 pt available at 5.5 pt), because capital letters are wider than the average character. The nine longest words need about 494 pt at 7 pt with padding, more than the page width. The wide-table test uses 4 columns, so it cannot see this.

Evidence: review1019-probes/capex/page-3.png (/home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/review1019-probes/, outside the repository), rendered by capex_render.py; capex_fontsize.py shows which font sizes still break.

Options shown to the owner:
(a) weigh the columns by measured text width (reportlab.pdfbase.pdfmetrics.stringWidth in the cell's font) instead of character counts, and set tables above six columns at 6 pt; the nine words then need about 431 pt of the 453 pt. Recommended. Small change in reportgenerator.py plus a 9-column test.
(b) put wide tables on a landscape page; a larger change to the document template.
(c) shorten the headers in opex_and_capex_cost_calculation.py; the component names still break until hisim-9w3g gives components display names.

Done when: the investment table of a heat-pump house breaks no word in the middle, and a 9-column test pins it.

title: Check the SCOP calibration's mean-outlet anchors against measured heat pump data
description:
Source: decision with Noah, 2026-09-23, while implementing hisim-component-physics-4g9.15 ("go with the mean outlet
anchors, but make a bead that we need to check this against real data").

What was decided without data: when a heat pump's datasheet states both EN 14825 SCOPs (W35 and
W55), ScopCalibration scales hplib's COP by a factor that is linear in the outlet temperature
between two anchors and constant outside them. The anchors are the heat-weighted mean outlets of
the two EN 14825 rating lines (28.9 C for W35, 40.7 C for W55), and both factors are solved so the
calibrated fit rates exactly at the stated SCOPs. The alternative, anchors at the nominal 35 / 55 C,
was rejected because it is ill-conditioned: wide pairs (e.g. 5.5 / 3.0) drove the 55 C factor to
0.46 (air) and 0.19 (brine), which domestic hot water at 55 C would inherit. The comparison table
over nine realistic pairs is in the 2026-09-23 session and summarised in the commit that adds
ScopCalibration.

Nothing checks that the calibrated machine behaves like the real one away from the two ratings.
In particular: (1) the factor at 45-55 C outlets (radiator houses, DHW) is an extrapolation;
(2) hplib's Generic air/water fit gives COP 1.41 at A-7/W52 where real units reach about 2.5, a
curve-shape error a factor per outlet temperature cannot fix; (3) the Generic brine/water fit's
W35/W55 spread (4.85 vs 4.02) is narrower than real datasheets, so every realistic brine pair
lands in the regime where the anchor choice matters.

Wanted: take several real units with published EN 14825 data (both SCOPs plus COPs at the
standard rating points A7/W35, A2/W35, A-7/W35, A7/W55, A-7/W55, A-7/W52, ideally from the
hplib database's own rows or a Keymark / HP Keymark certificate), calibrate the Generic fit to
their two SCOPs, and compare the calibrated COP with the stated one at each rating point. Report
the error per point for both anchor schemes, and for "calibrate a matched hplib database row
instead of Generic".

Done when: the error table exists, and the anchor choice is either confirmed or changed with the
data behind it; if the A-7 shape error dominates, a follow-up for the fit shape is filed.
close_reason: Checked 2026-10-21 against ~1,930 Keymark-certified units (1,743 air/water, 176 brine/water), datasheets and Fraunhofer ISE WP-QS (data, scripts and tables in /home/noah/hisim/agent-tmp/x2mu/). The mean-outlet anchors are confirmed: air/water ties with the nominal 35/55 C anchors (12.2 % mean absolute error each), brine/water is clearly better (10.0 % vs 13.8 %; B0/W55 -15 % vs -30 %; nominal anchors worst for on/off brine units). The remaining error is the shape of hplib's Generic air/water curve (A-7/W52 -33 %, A7/W55 +16 %, A-7/W65 falls to the heating rod; the needed factor depends on outdoor temperature, so no outlet-only factor or cap helps), plus unmodelled part-load cycling. Follow-up (owner, 2026-10-21): hisim-heat-pump-model-rework-fpqz (Carnot-efficiency shape, defrosting, research into other heat pump models).

title: Under pytest-xdist a collection guard's refusal reaches CI only as INTERNALERROR 'no active workers', without the names of the offending tests
description:
Source: review of #1039 (finding R1, review-evals/review1039_evaluation.md), reproduced 2026-10-16 with pytest 9.1.1 and pytest-xdist 3.8.0.

Three collection guards refuse a bad collection by raising pytest.UsageError: the job-marker check (tests/job_markers.py, pytest_collection_finish), AssemblyTier (tests/assemblies/conftest.py, pytest_collection_modifyitems) and ProbeTier (tests/renovisor/conftest.py). Under pytest-xdist the controller collects nothing; every worker collects and raises. The worker dies without relaying the error, and the controller prints only `INTERNALERROR> RuntimeError: Unexpectedly no active workers available` (exit 3). The message naming the offending tests is gone. Every CI job of tests.yml but utsp, renovisor-probes and extendedbase2 runs with -n, so a marker fault on a pull request shows as an internal error; the names appear only in a local run without -n (exit 4).

Reproduce: a throwaway repository with tests/job_markers.py, a conftest registering JobMarkerCheck and one unmarked test; `pytest -m base` prints the names, `pytest -m base -n 2` prints the INTERNALERROR only.

Options:
1. Keep raising; document in system_docs/testing.md that an INTERNALERROR 'no active workers' at collection means a guard refused, to be read with a run without -n.
2. On an xdist worker (`hasattr(config, "workerinput")`), report the refusal as a failed collect report (`config.hook.pytest_collectreport(report=CollectReport(<guard module>, "failed", message, []))`) and empty `session.items` instead of raising; without xdist raise as today. xdist relays a failed collect report once (deduplicated over workers), and the run ends `ERROR tests/job_markers.py - <message>`, exit 1. Tried on the job-marker check in a scratch repository: the full message reaches the controller's summary.
3. Option 2 as one shared helper used by all three guards.

Recommendation: 3, so every guard's refusal names its tests in CI.

Done when: a refusal of each guard under -n names the offending tests in the CI log, and a test runs the throwaway repository under xdist (skipped where xdist is missing) or pins the worker branch with a stand-in config.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-16: document only. system_docs/testing.md §2 says that an INTERNALERROR 'no active workers' during collection under -n means a guard refused, and to rerun without -n to see the tests.

title: Decide how electrolyzer_with_renewables reads its minutely wind profile in a 15-minute run, so it can name the profile's time column and join the July golden pairs
description:
Source: hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.14 (CSV loader time column, branch midyear-csv-time-column), 2026-10-16.

Since hisim-midyear-windows-9g2.14 CSVLoaderConfig has an optional time_column: with it the loader looks the run's start_date up among the column's labels (hisim.window_offset.WindowOffset) and reads the window's rows; without it a run that does not start on 1 January is refused. The shipped wind profile of electrolyzer_with_renewables (hisim/inputs/wind_generated_power_1_min.csv) already has a time column (column 0, minutely, 2021-01-01 00:00 to 2021-12-31 23:59, gapless). But WindowOffset.resolve requires the file's rows to lie at the run's resolution, and scripts/record_all_setups.py records every setup under one_day_15min_export (900 s): with time_column=0 the setup's recording is refused ("does not run on an even grid of 900 s"). Without the time column a 900 s run reads 96 consecutive minutes as one day, silently, which is today's behaviour. So the setup keeps no time column for now, stays in CANNOT_RUN_JULY (tests/test_golden_matrix.py) and keeps horizons [week, year] in scripts/golden_config.json.

Options:
(A) Recommended: the loader, given a time column, aggregates a file finer than the run to the run's step (the mean of the rows inside each step, which is right for a power such as kW; an energy per row would need the sum, so the rule depends on the unit and needs a decision). The setup then names time_column=0, its twin records it, it joins the July pairs (add july_week_60s to its seconds, drop its horizons restriction) and leaves CANNOT_RUN_JULY; the July golden is blessed by the golden-update workflow. January 60 s numbers do not move.
(B) Record this one setup at 60 s (a per-setup parameters entry in record_all_setups.py). No loader change, but the setup still cannot run at any resolution but the file's.
(C) Leave it out of the July pairs.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-16, option (A): a CSV with a time column finer than the run is averaged over each timestep (keeps a power column's energy); coarser or non-dividing row steps are refused. electrolyzer_with_renewables names time_column=0 and joins the July golden pairs; CANNOT_RUN_JULY is gone (PR #1034, midyear-csv-time-column).

title: Staged splice: a fixed-amount grant of a stage starting after year 0 is clamped to its year-0 cost, not the stage-year cost
description: renovisorissues #65 fixed the year-0 shift (the solver now sees the cost in plan-year-0 money). The splice still books a LUMP_SUM/PER_UNIT award of a stage with from_year>0 unescalated (share only) while the cost it was clamped to is escalated (1+r)^from_year: a lump sum clamped at year-0 cost C is booked as C beside a stage-year cost C*(1+r)^F (and with a negative learning rate an unclamped lump sum can exceed the stage-year cost). Same for max_amount_in_euro via StagedResult.subsidy_scale. Fix needs the award's eligible basis in the splice (StagedCategories / _StageCharges.booked_factor) or valuing each stage's subsidies at its stage-year price level.
close_reason: fix/stage-grant-cap: each stage's subsidies valued at the price level its purchase is booked at

title: The HiSim repository gets a clear structure: every multi-file component in a folder of its own, and enforced seams (a layer map with one import lint) between the packages
description:
Source: owner, 2026-10-19: "we urgently need to create a better structure in the hisim repo and for example move all components that span multiple files into a folder for that component, and we need to introduce and enforce seams between packages to make them more independent."

State on 2026-10-19 (main):
- hisim/components holds 50 top-level modules and only four component folders (building, generic_chp, generic_pv_system, weather). Components that span several modules sit side by side as flat files, e.g. more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib + more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib_model, generic_car + generic_car_profile (+ lpg_car_information, controller_l1_generic_ev_charge), the electrolyzer and fuel-cell components with their controllers.
- hisim/ has 32 modules directly at its top level beside the packages building_sizer_utils, caching, components, config, cost_database, economics, energy_system, postprocessing, renovisor, subsidy_catalog.
- Seams enforced today: three import lints (tests/test_renovisor_import_lint.py: nothing outside hisim/renovisor imports it; tests/test_economics_import_lint.py; tests/test_energy_system_layering.py) and the config layer rule (hisim/config imports nothing from the rest). Everything else may import anything.

Wanted:
1. Every component that spans more than one module gets a folder of its own under hisim/components (its model, its controllers, its configuration and helpers), with the public names re-exported from the folder's __init__ only where callers need them; the module paths recorded in energy-system files, MAIN_CLASS entries, golden references and the RenoVisor bindings move with it (a migration with a recorded mapping, fail loudly on an old path except where written down).
2. A written layer map of the packages (which package may import which: config at the bottom, then the simulator core, components, energy_system, postprocessing, economics, renovisor on top, as today's lints imply), with one import-lint test that enforces the whole map instead of one test per package, and the top-level hisim modules sorted into the packages they belong to.
3. Seams between packages are explicit interfaces (a small public API per package); a package does not reach into another's internals.

Done when: no component spans loose top-level modules, the layer map is documented in system_docs and enforced by one base test, and every recorded energy system, golden and RenoVisor binding still resolves. Split into child beads per step before starting (spec first, see roadmap/templates/spec_template.md).

title: With a SCOP calibration factor below 1 the compressor runs next to hplib's heating-rod switch at a calibrated COP below 1, worse than the rod alone
description:
Source: evaluation of the review of #930, missed finding M1 (2026-10-13). Owner decision needed.

Mechanism: ScopCalibration.apply (hisim/components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib_model.py:412) scales a compressor result's COP by the calibration factor and leaves a rod-alone result at 1.0. hplib decides between compressor and rod on its raw COP: it switches to the rod alone where the raw COP reaches 1 (HplibResult.HEATING_ROD_ALONE_MAXIMAL_COP, :494). With a factor below 1 the compressor therefore still runs where its calibrated COP is below 1. Example (probe on main 737f7801, 8 kW generic air/water, stated W55 SCOP 3.0, factor 0.876, 0 °C, hot-water mode): at a 64.0 °C return the compressor runs at a calibrated COP of 0.879 (raw 1.0033), worse than the rod's 1.0, and the rod takes over only between 64.01 and 64.05 °C.

Options:
- (i) accept it: the stated rating describes the unit as a whole, and the region is narrow (returns just below hplib's switch, near 60 °C hot water);
- (ii) let the calibration also move the switch: below a calibrated COP of 1 the rod runs alone. This changes results of calibrated runs near 60 °C hot water, and it does not remove the need for hisim-g0dp (the straddle detection must follow whichever switch is used).
Recommendation: (i) until hisim-x2mu has checked the calibration's outlet anchors against measured data, because whether a real unit's COP falls below 1 there depends on those anchors (the factor above 55 °C outlet is an extrapolation).

Done when: the owner has decided. (i) closes this bead with the decision; (ii) retypes it to a bug with the switch on the calibrated COP and a test at W55 = 3.0.

title: The energy manager reads the electric car's draw through the charge controller's relay, two passes stale instead of one
description:
Source: evaluation of the review of #965, missed finding M1 (2026-10-14).

The energy manager (L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem) measures the electric car's draw through the charge controller's relay output L1Controller.BatteryChargingPowerToEMS (controller_l1_generic_ev_charge.py, the end of i_simulate), not from the car battery itself. In a pass the energy manager (L2) runs before the controller (L1), which runs before the car battery (physics). The energy manager therefore reads the relay of the pass before, which carries the battery's AC power of the pass before that: two passes of lag where one would do (the house battery's ports are read directly, one pass). Converged values are right; a step only needs more passes.

The relay also publishes a physics quantity (the battery's realized AC power) from a controller, which the components-are-black-boxes rule does not want: the published port quantity belongs to CarBattery.

Option: the energy manager reads CarBattery's AC power port (AcBatteryChargingPower, its charging part) directly, as it reads the house battery's ports, and the relay output is removed. The car's grid KPI (max(0, draw - max(0, offer))) then reads that port as the draw.

Measure first: mean passes and forced steps of household_heatpump_car_building_sizer, one_week_60s and full_year_60s, before and after; decide on the numbers.

Done when: the pass counts are measured and either the energy manager reads the battery's port with the relay removed (car goldens re-blessed), or the bead is closed with the numbers showing the lag costs nothing worth the change.

title: RenoVisor ground-source heat pumps run hplib's air/water model; wire a brine/water machine (hplib group 2, brine source temperature) so a ground-source SCOP calibrates a brine machine
description:
Source: review of PR #810 (feat/heat-pump-scop-calibration, hisim-component-physics-4g9.15), decision with Noah on 2026-09-24.

Every RenoVisor heat pump runs the same twin, `household_heatpump_building_sizer.grouped` (and its
solar-thermal sibling), whose `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib` is hplib's Generic air/water fit (group 1).
`hisim/renovisor/translate.py` `_standardized_scop` writes a ground-source heat pump's stated
EN 14825 SCOP pair (`house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35` / `_w55`) onto that machine, so a
rating the manufacturer measured with brine entering at 0 C is met by an air machine under air
conditions: the SCOP is kept, the temperature dependence across the season is the air fit's. The
report marks the pair `approximated` for ground_source_heat_pump (and hybrid_heat_pump) since PR #810.

To do: wire a brine/water machine for ground_source_heat_pump -- hplib group 2 on the twin (or a
brine twin), with a brine source temperature input rather than the outdoor air -- so a ground-source
SCOP calibrates a brine machine (StandardizedSeasonalCop already rates group 2 with brine at 0 C).
Then `_standardized_scop` reports `used` for it again, and the generator's own not_implemented_yet
note ("No brine/water heat-pump preset ...") shrinks accordingly.
